title: A credential that belongs to one box can't be handed to another
story: As an operator, I want a credential that structurally binds to a single box — a Telegram bot token, a bucket-scoped R2 token — stored as non-shareable and owned by that box, so that granting it elsewhere is refused and provisioning a new box from an existing one skips it with an explanation instead of breaking the box already using it.
evidence: `setAndGrantSecret` (core/secrets/lifecycle.ts) writes `owningBox` + `shareable: false` and stores-and-grants under one lock, reading ownership off the store so a caller can't claim another box's entry; `grantSecret` throws `SecretNotShareableError` for a non-owning box, and `copyBoxGrants` skips such entries with a per-name reason while still reporting `sourceHadGrants`.

verdict.note: core/secrets/store.ts defines `owningBox`/`shareable` on the entry schema; core/secrets/lifecycle.ts `setAndGrantSecret` runs inside one `mutateSecretStore` lock, reads the existing owner off the STORE (not opts) and throws `SecretNotShareableError` (core/secrets/errors.ts:211) if another box's slug claims it, then writes the value and the grant together. `grantSecret` (lifecycle.ts:165) throws the same error when `shareable === false` and the requester isn't the owner. Real callers exist: webapp/trpc/routers/admin.ts:113 stores the Telegram bot token + webhook secret with `shareable:false, owningBox`, and publish/connector-secret.ts:163 does the same for the bucket-scoped R2 token. `copyBoxGrants` (lifecycle.ts:283) skips `shareable === false` entries with a per-name reason string and reports `sourceHadGrants`; it is reachable via `cb secrets copy-grants` (cli/commands/secrets-migrate.ts:106/143), which deploy/add-box.sh:375 runs when provisioning a new box from an existing one.

title: Account for token usage per session and task
story: As an operator, I want Claude Code session logs aggregated per session, date and model into a queryable database, so that I can see what the box's agent work is costing and which task it belonged to.
evidence: syncUsage() joins store/usage/session-manifest.jsonl (task attribution written by createAgent) with the ~/.claude/projects session logs into .callback-box/usage.db; `cb usage` syncs and prints the aggregate table, and codex-usage.ts records the equivalent ledger at store/usage/codex-turns.jsonl.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/usage.ts defines a SQLite table `usage` keyed on (session_id, date, model) at .callback-box/usage.db; syncUsage() reads store/usage/session-manifest.jsonl for task attribution and parses ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-path>/<sessionId>.jsonl session logs, aggregating tokens per (date, model). core/agent/manifest.ts appendSessionManifest is called from core/agent/index.ts (createAgent path) with the task. src/cli/commands/usage.ts registers the `usage` command (added in src/cli/index.ts:137); with no flags it syncs then prints a task/model aggregate table, and --sql/--schema expose arbitrary queries. codex-usage.ts writes the parallel ledger at store/usage/codex-turns.jsonl (CODEX_USAGE_REL_PATH).

title: Ask for a credential you don't have
story: As the box's agent, I want to declare an empty, ungranted secret slot with the reasons I need it and to read my own box's secret status — what's granted, which granted slots are still empty, which grants point at nothing — so that I can tell the boxholder exactly what to fill in without ever being shown the machine's other secrets.
evidence: `declareSecret` writes a valueless entry (idempotent, `uses` appended not replaced, `declaredBy` stamped) and `boxSecretStatus(slug)` returns `granted`/`emptySlots`/`danglingGrants`/`declaredHere` for one box only — exposed as `cb secrets declare` ("the agent-facing surface") and `cb secrets status` in cli/commands/secrets.ts.

verdict.note: core/secrets/lifecycle.ts declareSecret() writes an entry with value preserved/undefined, appends uses via appendSecretUses, stamps declaredBy, and returns {created} (idempotent). boxSecretStatus(slug) reads only that slug's grants and returns granted/emptySlots/danglingGrants/declaredHere, deliberately never enumerating other boxes' secrets. cli/commands/secrets.ts registers `cb secrets declare` (described as "the agent-facing surface", with repeatable --use) and `cb secrets status <box>`; declare has no agent refusal, while `list` and cross-box `status` go through refuseIfUnconfirmedAgent / refuseIfAgentAskingAboutAnotherBox in cli/lib/secrets-guard.ts, which also refuses uniformly for out-of-scope or nonexistent names.

title: Authenticate Claude Code for the box
story: As a box operator, I want to see whether Claude Code is authenticated and to log in, log out or refresh from the admin page, so that background agents can run.
evidence: ClaudeCodeSection drives claudeAuthMachine (loading/starting/polling/loggingOut), showing the authenticated account email or the error, an Open Anthropic Login link while polling, and Authenticate/Log Out/Refresh buttons.

verdict.note: components/admin/ClaudeCodeSection.tsx is rendered by pages/AdminPage.tsx (line 37) and drives machines/claudeAuthMachine.ts via useMachine, matching states loading/starting/polling/loggingOut/idle. It shows 'Authenticated as {status.email}' or 'Not authenticated' with status.error, an ExternalLink 'Open Anthropic Login' to context.authUrl while polling, and Authenticate/Log Out/Refresh buttons sending LOGIN/LOGOUT/REFRESH. The machine's actors call trpcClient.admin.claudeStatus/claudeLogin/claudeLogout, which exist as ownerProcedures in webapp/trpc/routers/admin.ts (lines 257-278) delegating to services/claude-cli.ts authStatus/authLogin/authLogout (shelling to `claude auth ...`). The section's own copy states these creds enable background agents (scheduler, reactor).

title: Be protected from password guessing
story: As a box owner exposing my box to the internet, I want repeated failed logins to be slowed per IP, per email, and globally, so that a brute-force attempt cannot grind through my password or exhaust the server's memory.
evidence: LoginThrottle applies exponential (ip,email) backoff plus per-IP and per-email buckets and a 2-way scrypt concurrency cap; the login, setup, invite, and reset handlers all consult loginThrottle and answer 429 with retryAfterMs.

verdict.note: src/webapp/login-throttle.ts implements LoginThrottle with three maps — per-(ip,email) exponential backoff min(1s*2^(n-1),60s), a per-IP bucket, and a per-email bucket — plus MAX_CONCURRENT_HASHES = 2 acquireHashSlot/releaseHashSlot gating scrypt, with 1h TTL and a 4000-entry oldest-evicted cap (the memory-exhaustion half of the story). src/webapp/routes/auth-password-post.ts calls loginThrottle.check then acquireHashSlot on both the login handler (line ~224) and the setup handler (line ~343), returning 429 with retryAfterMs / CONCURRENCY_RETRY_MS; auth-password-change.ts, auth-password-reset.ts and auth-invite.ts also consult it (invite throttles first on a token-derived key, then on the email, returning 429 via genericFailure). Minor evidence imprecision — the invite/reset paths return 429 without a retryAfterMs body — but every claim in the story itself holds.

title: Be told plainly that an invite or reset link is dead
story: As someone who clicked an invite or password-reset link that has expired or already been used, I want the page to say so and tell me to ask the box owner for a new one, so that I am not left guessing at a login form that will never accept me.
evidence: renderInviteUnavailablePage emits "This invitation is invalid, expired, or already used. Ask the owner for a new link." and password-reset-page.ts's gone state emits the matching sentence; renderInvitePage also warns that accepting the invite replaces a session you are already signed into.

verdict.note: invite-page.ts renderInviteUnavailablePage emits exactly 'This invitation is invalid, expired, or already used. Ask the owner for a new link.' and password-reset-page.ts renderPasswordResetUnavailablePage emits 'This password reset link is invalid or has expired. Ask the box owner for a new link.' Both are reachable: routes/auth-invite.ts registers GET/POST /auth/invite and returns the unavailable page with 410 (or 503 storeUnavailable) on invalid/expired/consumed tokens (lines 113-190, 226-249); routes/auth-password-reset.ts registers GET/POST /auth/reset-password and returns 410 + the unavailable page (line 47). Both registrars are wired in routes/auth.ts (registerAuthInviteRoutes / registerAuthPasswordResetRoutes, lines 186-187). renderInvitePage also carries the 'accepting this invite replaces that browser session' hint as the evidence states.

browser.note: GET /auth/invite?token=bogus123 returns 410 Gone with a self-contained page titled 'Invite unavailable': 'This invitation is invalid, expired, or already used. Ask the owner for a new link.' GET /auth/reset-password?token=bogus123 returns 410 Gone, 'Reset link unavailable': 'This password reset link is invalid or has expired. Ask the box owner for a new link.' Both send cache-control: no-store and referrer-policy: no-referrer.

title: Box subprocesses get a fail-closed environment
story: As an operator, I want scripts, tricks and agents spawned inside a box to inherit only an explicit allowlist of environment variables plus the box's own identity, so that server-held secrets never leak into box-run code.
evidence: script-env.ts derives CB_BOX_NAME and CB_SERVER_URL from config/box.json's publicUrl for every box-spawned subprocess, and script-env-allowlist.ts is the fail-closed allowlist replacing the old `{...process.env}` spread, mirroring the hub's CHILD_ENV_ALLOWLIST one level up.

verdict.note: src/core/script-env-allowlist.ts does implement a fail-closed SCRIPT_ENV_ALLOWLIST and script-env.ts derives CB_SERVER_URL/CB_BOX_NAME from publicUrl plus CB_AGENT_TOKEN, so the mechanism exists. But the story's scope ('scripts, tricks and agents ... so that server-held secrets never leak into box-run code') over-claims: buildToolingScriptEnv adds CONNECTOR_ENV_ALLOWLIST (GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, CALLBACK_MISTRAL_API_KEY, THINKING_OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_KEY, CB_SECRETS_FILE, CALLBACK_DEEPGRAM_* prefix) to spawns of the box's own tooling, which includes scheduled scripts' `runs:` commands — and the file's own doc comment states this profile is agent-reachable by writing a script card and waiting for it to fire, with that path only closed by an unfinished Track 3. Server-held connector secrets therefore still reach some box-run code.

panel.note: Both cited files are real and live. script-env-allowlist.ts defines SCRIPT_ENV_ALLOWLIST plus a tooling-only CONNECTOR_ENV_ALLOWLIST/prefix list and exports pickBoxSubprocessEnv(sourceEnv, {connectorCreds}), which script-env.ts's buildEnv() calls instead of a process.env spread; buildEnv also derives CB_SERVER_URL/CB_BOX_NAME from ambient publicUrl (registered by src/webapp/server.ts:348 registerBoxPublicUrl) or config/box.json publicUrl, and injects CB_AGENT_TOKEN. The two exported profiles are imported and used at every box spawn site I followed: agents (src/core/agent/run.ts:198), tricks (src/cli/commands/trick.ts:124), chat sessions (core/chat/session/start.ts:124, thread.ts:156), procedure shell steps (core/procedure/shell.ts:51), scan-vision (services/scan-vision-claude.ts:307), and the tooling profile in core/commands/wakeup.ts:43, core/reactor/subprocess.ts:26, cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts:274, tick-utils.ts:141, webapp/trpc/routers/scheduler-run.ts:88. Nothing here is dead code; the earlier verdict's objection was about scope of the guarantee (connector creds still reach the tooling profile), not about existence or wiring, so my lens is satisfied.

The allowlist is unconditional on every box-spawn path, not behind a flag or opt-in config: pickBoxSubprocessEnv() in src/core/script-env-allowlist.ts copies only allowlisted names/prefixes with no env-gated branch, and buildEnv() in src/core/script-env.ts always starts from it. Real entry points reach it from ordinary operator/agent activity: chat sessions (src/core/chat/session/start.ts, thread.ts), agent runs (src/core/agent/run.ts), procedure shell steps (src/core/procedure/shell.ts), the `cb trick` CLI (src/cli/commands/trick.ts), and scheduled/tick + wakeup + reactor spawns and the scheduler-run tRPC procedure via buildToolingScriptEnv. CB_BOX_NAME/CB_SERVER_URL derive from box.json publicUrl or the live URL registered by src/webapp/server.ts, so a normally-run server supplies them without extra config. My lens (reachability) is satisfied; the earlier verifier's objection was about over-claimed scope of the connector-credential profile, which is another reviewer's call.

The allowlist half holds: script-env-allowlist.ts's pickBoxSubprocessEnv copies only named entries out of process.env, and script-env.ts's buildEnv adds CB_SERVER_URL/CB_BOX_NAME/CB_AGENT_TOKEN derived from publicUrl. But the story names 'scripts' alongside agents and promises 'server-held secrets never leak into box-run code', and the second profile buildToolingScriptEnv passes connectorCreds:true, adding CONNECTOR_ENV_ALLOWLIST (GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, CALLBACK_MISTRAL_API_KEY, THINKING_OPENAI_API_KEY, CALLBACK_OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_KEY, SKE_GEMINI_API_KEY, CB_SECRETS_FILE, CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE) plus the CALLBACK_DEEPGRAM_ prefix. That profile is what scheduled scripts' `runs:` commands spawn with (cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts:274, tick-utils.ts:141, webapp/trpc/routers/scheduler-run.ts:88), and script-env.ts's own doc comment concedes 'this profile is agent-*reachable* by writing a script card and waiting for it to fire... Track 3 closes this one.' So server-held connector secrets do reach box-run code today; the 'never' benefit clause claims an outcome the code does not yet produce.

triage.reasoning: The mechanism the story names is real and unconditional: pickBoxSubprocessEnv (callback-box/src/core/script-env-allowlist.ts) copies only allowlisted names/prefixes out of process.env, buildEnv (src/core/script-env.ts) always starts from it instead of a {...process.env} spread, and it adds CB_BOX_NAME/CB_SERVER_URL derived from publicUrl plus CB_AGENT_TOKEN. Two of three lenses cleared it on exactly that ground; only the wording lens refuted. What the wording lens caught is in the story's benefit clause, not the code: buildToolingScriptEnv passes connectorCreds:true, which adds CONNECTOR_ENV_ALLOWLIST (GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, CALLBACK_MISTRAL_API_KEY, THINKING_OPENAI_API_KEY, CALLBACK_OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_KEY, SKE_GEMINI_API_KEY, CB_SECRETS_FILE, CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE, CALLBACK_DEEPGRAM_*) for spawns of the box's own cb tooling — including scheduled `runs:` commands, which are agent-authorable. So 'server-held secrets never leak into box-run code' is stronger than what the code has ever provided. That scope limit is not a discovery: script-env.ts's own docblock states it ('agent-reachable by writing a script card and waiting for it to fire'), and docs/implemented-plans/secret-custody.md names retiring the env-var credential path as Track 3, with the remaining steps operational (run the data migration, then remove the fallbacks). Nothing in the product is missing, broken, or unreachable — the story needs its 'never' clause corrected to describe two allowlist profiles (agent-safe for agents/tricks/chat, a wider tooling profile for the box's own cb commands, which still carries connector credentials on an env-var-configured server).

title: Capture sessions belong to whoever started them
story: As a person sharing a box with others, I want uploads, finalize, and discard on a capture session restricted to the user who created it, so that another user's device cannot add to or destroy my in-flight capture.
evidence: resolveCaptureRequestOwner stamps createdBy on session creation and rejects ownerless legacy paired devices with a 403; authorizeCaptureSessionOwner guards the upload, finalize and delete routes, and selectResumableCaptures filters by requestingUser.

verdict.note: webapp/capture-request-owner.ts defines resolveCaptureRequestOwner (cookie/hub identity, else paired-device bearer identity whose createdBy becomes the owner; ownerless legacy paired devices return 'ownerless-mobile' → 403) and authorizeCaptureSessionOwner, which rejects with 401/503/403 and 403 'Capture belongs to another user' when owner.email !== session.createdBy. routes/capture.ts stamps createdBy at createStagingSession on POST /api/capture/sessions and calls authorizeCaptureSessionOwner on DELETE /api/capture/sessions/:id and POST /:id/finalize; routes/capture-upload.ts handleCaptureUpload calls it before accepting the upload. core/capture/pending.ts selectResumableCaptures filters `s.createdBy === requestingUser`, and the /resumable route passes owner.email.

title: Change my own password
story: As a signed-in box user with a local password account, I want to change my password from Settings by proving the current one, so that I can rotate a credential I think is exposed.
evidence: PasswordSection posts to /auth/password; handlePasswordChange re-resolves the cookie identity, verifies the current password via verifyPassword, calls setPassword, and re-issues the session cookie. The section reports 'signs in with Google' when the account has no password.

verdict.note: PasswordSection.tsx renders a 'Change password' card in SettingsPage.tsx (routed at router.tsx:170) with current/new/confirm fields and POSTs to /auth/password; when useCurrentUserQuery reports !hasPassword it shows 'This account signs in with Google; no local password is set.' The route is registered in src/webapp/routes/auth.ts:188 -> handlePasswordChange in auth-password-change.ts, which resolves the cookie identity (401 unless source==='cookie' with an email), throttles, verifyPassword() on the current password, setPassword() on the new one, resets the local-user cache, and re-issues the session cookie before 204. currentUserHasPassword/getLocalUser come from local-users.ts and feed auth.ts:227.

browser.note: The Password section exists on /settings but renders only 'Sign in to manage a local password.' — the browse-key identity is not a signed-in local-password account, and this box has no local users configured. No current/new password fields were reachable, so the change-password flow (and the 'signs in with Google' variant) could not be exercised.

title: Choose the agent engine
story: As a box owner, I want to choose Claude Code or Codex as the harness for new chats, wakeups and procedures, so that the box runs on the engine I want.
evidence: AgentEngineSection renders a card RadioGroup over admin.boxConfig.agentEngine and saves via admin.updateBoxConfig, showing optimistic pending value plus Saving…/Saved./error states.

verdict.note: components/admin/AgentEngineSection.tsx renders a Card with a cards-variant RadioGroup over ENGINE_OPTIONS ('claude' → Claude Code, 'codex' → Codex), reading trpc.admin.boxConfig and saving via trpc.admin.updateBoxConfig, showing update.variables.agentEngine optimistically while pending plus Saving…/Saved./role=alert error states. It is mounted on pages/AdminPage.tsx (line 36). Backend: webapp/trpc/routers/admin.ts updateBoxConfig (ownerProcedure, z.enum(['claude','codex'])) writes via webapp/box-config-write.ts; core/box/config.ts loadAgentEngine reads it (default 'claude') and is consumed by core/agent/index.ts, core/chat/session/reserve.ts and core/schedule/engine-wait.ts, so it does govern new chats, wakeups, and procedure agents.

title: Choose which transcription service the box uses
story: As a boxholder, I want to pick the realtime/batch transcription service and, separately, the high-quality pass, so that my box can stream with one provider and do accurate re-transcription with another.
evidence: `loadTranscriptionConfig`/`updateTranscriptionConfig` read and merge `config/transcription.json` (under `withCardLock`) holding `service` (whisper/voxtral/deepgram/openai-realtime/fake) and an independent `hqService`; `transcribeAudio` dispatches on the first, `transcribeAudioHq` on the second.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/transcription/index.ts defines TranscriptionConfig with an independent `service` (realtime/batch) and `hqService`; loadTranscriptionConfig reads config/transcription.json (defaults voxtral/whisper) and updateTranscriptionConfig merges partial updates under withCardLock. transcribeAudio dispatches on config.service (fake/voxtral/deepgram, else whisper) and transcribeAudioHq dispatches on hqService via dispatchHqTranscription. The web path exists: webapp/trpc/routers/transcription.ts exposes config (public query) plus ownerProcedure setService/setHqService, and frontend components/chat/VoiceChip.tsx calls trpc.transcription.setService/setHqService from the voice chip menu.

browser.note: Voice settings submenu has two independent sections: LIVE TRANSCRIPTION (Voxtral (Mistral), ✓ Deepgram, OpenAI Realtime Whisper) and HQ TRANSCRIPTION (✓ Whisper (OpenAI), Whisper LLM, Whisper LLM mini, Voxtral (Mistral), Voxtral + diarization) — a different provider selected in each.

title: Claim a new box with the boot-printed setup link
story: As an operator standing up a fresh box, I want the server to print a one-time setup link at startup that lets me create the owner account in the browser, so that the box is never claimable by whoever finds it first.
evidence: armSetupToken() mints a 15-minute in-memory token printed only to the console; GET /auth/setup serves SetupPage and POST /auth/setup (handleSetupPost) checks the token via checkSetupToken before calling createFirstUser.

verdict.note: maybeArmFirstRunSetup() in callback-box/src/webapp/setup-token.ts is called at listen time from src/webapp/server.ts:286 (and cli/commands/hub.ts:161); when auth is required and no owner/local store exists it calls armSetupToken() (32 random bytes, 15-minute TTL, in-memory only) and console.logs `First-run setup: <publicUrl>/auth/setup?token=…` — never rendered into any served page. GET /auth/setup (src/webapp/routes/auth.ts:154) serves renderSetupPage from src/webapp/login-page.ts:169, and the SPA route /auth/setup → SetupPage.tsx exists in src/frontend/src/router.tsx. POST /auth/setup (registered at auth.ts:185) runs handleSetupPost in src/webapp/routes/auth-password-post.ts:302, which rejects when the store is already initialized, throttles, calls checkSetupToken and refuses anything but 'valid' (403 mismatch / 410 expired-absent) before createFirstUser + clearSetupToken — so an unclaimed box is not claimable without the printed token.

title: Configure a box's access list and engine
story: As the box owner, I want to edit who may access this box, which Google services it uses, and which agent engine it runs, and to log Claude in or out, so that box-level settings live in the app instead of in config files.
evidence: `admin.boxConfig`/`updateBoxConfig` (ownerProcedure) read and write `allowedEmails`, `googleServices` and `agentEngine`; `localAccountStatus` annotates each allowed email via admin-user-details.ts, and `claudeStatus`/`claudeLogin`/`claudeLogout`/`tailscaleBaseUrl` round out box admin.

verdict.note: src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin.ts defines ownerProcedure `boxConfig` (reads agentEngine, allowedEmails, googleServices from the box config file, annotated with describeAllowedUsers from admin-user-details.ts) and `updateBoxConfig` (accepts allowedEmails/googleServices/agentEngine, writes via updateBoxConfigFields in src/webapp/box-config-write.ts), plus `localAccountStatus`, `claudeStatus`, `claudeLogin`, `claudeLogout`, and `tailscaleBaseUrl`. The frontend consumes them: AllowedEmailsSection.tsx/useAllowedEmails.ts, AgentEngineSection.tsx and useGoogleServices.ts call admin.boxConfig/admin.updateBoxConfig, and claudeAuthMachine.ts drives Claude login/logout — so these are editable in the app, not only in config files.

browser.note: All four surfaces exist on the page: an 'Agent Engine' region, a 'Claude Code' block showing 'Not authenticated' with Authenticate/Refresh buttons, an 'Allowed Users' region with an email field + Add, and 'Google Services' with a Connect button. Every one of them shows 'Owner access required' instead of live config, because the browse-key session is not an owner. Could not read or write allowedEmails / googleServices / agentEngine, and could not log Claude in or out.

title: Connect Google from whatever URL the box is served at
story: As an operator, I want the OAuth redirect built from the browser's own origin, falling back to the box's configured public URL, so that a box behind a proxy or on a shared host completes the Google grant instead of bouncing to localhost.
evidence: googleSetup resolves `input.origin || resolveBoxPublicUrl(boxRoot, { fallback: "http://localhost:3210" })`, strips any box path prefix via baseServerUrl, and builds `${base}/auth/google-services/callback` as the redirect_uri passed to createOAuth2Client — the same value the callback handler must be registered for in the Google app.

verdict.note: admin-google.ts:49-64 does accept an optional `origin` input and cascades `input.origin || resolveBoxPublicUrl(boxRoot, {fallback:'http://localhost:3210'})`, strips the box slug via baseServerUrl and builds `${base}/auth/google-services/callback` (route registered in webapp/routes/admin.ts:27). But no caller ever supplies `origin`: the only client, src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts:93, calls `trpcClient.admin.googleSetup.mutate({})`, and grep for googleSetup across src finds no other call site. So the story's headline claim — the redirect is built from the browser's own origin — is dead in practice; what actually runs is box.json#publicUrl -> CB_PUBLIC_URL/PUBLIC_URL -> localhost:3210 (src/lib/public-url.ts resolveBoxPublicUrl).

panel.note: The fallback half is fully wired: googleSetup (admin-google.ts:49-80) is spread into the admin router (trpc/routers/admin.ts:15,255), imports resolveBoxPublicUrl (src/lib/public-url.ts) and baseServerUrl (src/webapp/base-server-url.ts), builds `${baseServerUrl(publicUrl)}/auth/google-services/callback`, and the matching callback route is registered in webapp/routes/admin.ts:27 and hub/hub-server.ts:428. But the story's headline mechanism — redirect built from the browser's own origin — has no live wiring: `input.origin` is an optional zod field that no caller ever supplies. The sole call site, src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts:93, does `trpcClient.admin.googleSetup.mutate({})`, and a repo-wide grep for googleSetup (excluding node_modules) finds no other caller in src/, ios-app/, callback-clerk/, or the doctests. So the `input.origin ||` branch is dead code and only the publicUrl/env/localhost cascade actually runs.

There is a real operator entry point: AdminPage.tsx:40 renders GoogleServicesSection, whose "Connect Google Account" button (GoogleServicesSection.tsx:127-131) calls handleAuthorize -> trpcClient.admin.googleSetup.mutate({}) (useGoogleServices.ts:93), and googleSetup is a registered ownerProcedure (admin-google.ts:49) that builds `${baseServerUrl(publicUrl)}/auth/google-services/callback`; the matching callback route is registered at webapp/routes/admin.ts:27. No flag or unset config gates it. The one caveat is that the UI passes `{}`, so the `input.origin` branch is never exercised in practice and only the resolveBoxPublicUrl/env fallback runs — that is an accuracy question about the story's headline claim, which belongs to another lens, not to reachability of the flow itself.

Taking the code path as reachable per my lens, admin-google.ts:49-63 delivers exactly the story's wording: googleSetup accepts an optional `origin`, resolves `input.origin || await resolveBoxPublicUrl(ctx.boxRoot, {fallback:'http://localhost:3210'}) || 'http://localhost:3210'`, and builds `${baseServerUrl(publicUrl)}/auth/google-services/callback` as redirect_uri for createOAuth2Client. That matches 'browser's own origin, falling back to the box's configured public URL' precisely — public-url.ts resolveBoxPublicUrl is config/box.json#publicUrl -> CB_PUBLIC_URL/PUBLIC_URL -> fallback, and base-server-url.ts strips the box slug so a proxied/subpath deployment gets a correct non-localhost redirect rather than bouncing to localhost, which is the 'so that' clause. The one real defect I found is that the sole caller, src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts:93, calls `googleSetup.mutate({})` and no other call site passes `origin` (grep across src), so the browser-origin branch is dead in practice — but that is an unreached-parameter problem, i.e. the reachability lens, not mine. On scope/wording alone the code does the whole of what is claimed.

triage.reasoning: The story's headline mechanism (redirect built from the browser's own origin) is dead in practice and the project has explicitly decided against it. googleSetup (src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts:49-64) accepts an optional `origin`, but the sole caller — src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts:93 — calls `mutate({})`, and a repo-wide grep for `googleSetup` (src/, ios-app/, callback-clerk/, doctests) turns up no other caller. What actually runs is resolveBoxPublicUrl: config/box.json#publicUrl -> CB_PUBLIC_URL/PUBLIC_URL -> http://localhost:3210 (src/lib/public-url.ts), slug-stripped by baseServerUrl (src/webapp/base-server-url.ts). That is not a shortfall: issues/bugs/2026-07-28-google-oauth-pairing-broken.md (Update 2 + 'Latent smell') records the maintainer conclusion that deriving an OAuth redirect_uri from a client-supplied origin is a smell to remove, because every alternate origin (dev router, Tailscale URL, alternate subdomain) yields an unregistered redirect_uri Google rejects — the canonical configured URL is the wanted behavior, and it is what runs. The 'so that' clause is satisfied through box.json publicUrl / CB_PUBLIC_URL, not through the browser origin. So the code is fine and the story misdescribes it; the catalog entry should say the redirect is built from the box's configured public URL (box.json -> env -> localhost), slug-stripped. The dormant `origin` input is cruft already tracked in that issue, not a missing capability.

title: Connect the browser extension to my box using the session I already have
story: As someone who already signs in to a box in Chrome, I want to enable that box in the extension and have it call the box with my existing session, so that the extension works without holding a separate credential and reaches only the box origins I granted.
evidence: enableBox calls chrome.permissions.request({origins:[`${origin}/*`]}) from the popup click, clerk-api fetches with credentials:"include" so the browser's cb_session rides along, and registerChromeExtensionCors answers the preflight and echoes Access-Control-Allow-Origin for chrome-extension:// origins with credentials allowed; syncRelayRegistration scopes the relay content script to the enabled boxes' URLs.

verdict.note: callback-clerk/src/platform/enable-box.ts `enableBox` calls chrome.permissions.request({origins:[`${origin}/*`]}) and is invoked from popup-app.tsx's handleEnable click callback (comment notes it must stay in the gesture); it then persists the box and calls syncRelayRegistration, which registers the box-relay content script with match patterns derived from enabled boxUrls only. clerk-api.ts fetchOrThrow uses `fetch(url, {credentials:"include", ...})` with no token in EnabledBox (config.ts EnabledBox is just boxUrl/slug/title), so the browser's own cb_session cookie is the auth. callback-box/src/webapp/server-root.ts registerChromeExtensionCors (wired in server.ts:131) short-circuits OPTIONS from chrome-extension:// origins and echoes Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Allow-Credentials:true.

title: Control who may open this box
story: As a box owner, I want to edit the box's allowed-email list and see whether each entry actually has a local password account, so that I can tell an invited-and-ready person from an address that can never sign in.
evidence: admin.boxConfig returns allowedEmails plus describeAllowedUsers()'s per-email kind (local-member / local-owner / owner-entry / access-only) and resetEligible flag; AllowedEmailsSection renders those badges and writes the list back through normalizeAllowedEmails/updateBoxConfigFields.

verdict.note: admin.boxConfig (webapp/trpc/routers/admin.ts:180-206) normalizes allowedEmails and calls describeAllowedUsers() from admin-user-details.ts, which classifies each address as local-member/local-owner/owner-entry/access-only/unknown from listUsers() and sets resetEligible for local-member. AllowedEmailsSection.tsx renders AccountBadge per row — 'Local password account' for local-*, 'Owner', 'Password status unavailable', otherwise 'Google sign-in only'/'Needs account setup' — so an invited-but-no-account entry is visually distinct. Editing works: useAllowedEmails.ts saveEmails/addEmail call trpc.admin.updateBoxConfig (which writes via updateBoxConfigFields), and AdminPage renders the section at the /admin route registered in router.tsx.

browser.note: The 'Allowed users' region renders with the copy 'Email addresses that can access this box. Leave empty to keep the box owner-only.', the state line 'Owner-only — no additional users can access this box.', an 'Allowed email' textbox, a disabled Add button, and 'Owner access required'. The list is empty on this box and the section is owner-gated, so no per-email local-member/local-owner/access-only badges could be seen and no edit could be made.

title: Cut off sessions someone already holds
story: As a box owner, I want changing or resetting an account's password — or removing the account outright — to invalidate every browser session that account already has, so that a stolen laptop or a departing member loses access immediately instead of thirty days later.
evidence: Each user record carries a `gen` counter that setPasswordWithPasswordHash increments on every password write; signSession stamps the current gen into the cb_session cookie and resolveRequestIdentity rejects a cookie whose gen differs from the record's, or that carries a gen for a record that no longer exists (removeUser).

verdict.note: local-users.ts stores a positive-int `gen` on each UserRecord (schema line 56, seeded to 1 at creation) and setPasswordWithPasswordHash increments it on every password write (line 395); setPassword delegates to it, and it is reached from the web routes webapp/routes/auth-password-change.ts (line 59) and auth-password-reset.ts (line 154) plus the CLI set-password command in cli/commands/auth.ts (line 182). auth.ts signSession stamps currentGenForEmail into the cb_session payload (line 223-230) and classifyLocalRecord (called from resolveRequestIdentity) returns unauthenticated when `user.gen !== record.gen`, and also when no record exists but the cookie carries a gen — the documented mechanism by which removeUser (cli remove-user) kills that account's sessions. A corrupt store fails closed as source 'unavailable' (503), not open.

title: Fail closed when the credential file can't be read
story: As an operator, I want a corrupt or unreadable credential store to make the box answer 503 rather than treat every request as unauthenticated-but-harmless, so that a damaged auth file can never quietly widen access.
evidence: resolveRequestIdentity returns a distinct source "unavailable" when the store throws; the box auth preHandler answers 503 "Authentication temporarily unavailable" for it (never 401), the hub's box picker does the same before listing boxes, and resolveCaptureRequestOwner maps it to a 503 rejection.

verdict.note: webapp/auth.ts defines IdentitySource including "unavailable" and resolveRequestIdentity catches a throwing credential store while verifying the session cookie, logging 'failing closed (503)' and returning {email:null, source:'unavailable'} rather than a plain null/unauthenticated identity. webapp/server-box-scope.ts's box preHandler switches on identity.source and answers reply.status(503) {error:'Authentication temporarily unavailable'} for the unavailable case before any 401 path; the tRPC/WS context builder in the same file throws AuthStoreUnavailableAtContextError when source==='unavailable' and no bearer/mobile/browse key applies. hub/box-picker.ts line 84 returns the same 503 before listing boxes, and capture-request-owner.ts maps source 'unavailable' to {status:'auth-store-unavailable'} and then a rejected 503.

title: Fail closed when the paired-device store can't be read or locked
story: As a box operator, I want an unreadable or lock-contended mobile device store to reject device auth and refuse to be rewritten, so that a corrupted file can never silently erase every paired device or let a revoked one keep renewing.
evidence: `DeviceStoreUnreadableError` and `MobileDeviceStoreLockError` distinguish a corrupt/locked store from a genuinely absent one (ENOENT → empty first run); `isMobileDeviceActive` catches the unreadable case and returns false so cookie renewal stops, and `resolveCaptureRequestOwner` maps a `source: "unavailable"` identity store to a 503 'Authentication temporarily unavailable' rather than to an anonymous request.

verdict.note: core/mobile/pairing.ts defines DeviceStoreUnreadableError and MobileDeviceStoreLockError and wires them into the mobile TokenStore via unreadableError/lockError. core/token-store.ts read() returns [] only on ENOENT and otherwise throws unreadableError (IO error or bad JSON), and every mutation (append/revoke/verify) goes through withLock(), which re-reads inside the lock before write() — so an unreadable store aborts before overwriting, and exhausting the 50x100ms retry budget throws lockError instead of writing unsynchronized. isMobileDeviceActive catches DeviceStoreUnreadableError and returns false (fail-closed cookie renewal); webapp/capture-request-owner.ts's resolveCaptureRequestOwner returns status 'auth-store-unavailable' when resolveRequestIdentity reports source 'unavailable' (auth.ts:498), which authorizeCaptureSessionOwner maps to 503 'Authentication temporarily unavailable' rather than anonymous.

title: Fill the credential slots the box asked for
story: As a box owner, I want the Secrets section to list the empty slots this box's agent declared it needs and the grants that name secrets no longer on the machine, each with the one action that resolves it, so that I can answer the box's standing credential requests and clear its broken ones without knowing the store's layout.
evidence: BoxSecretsView renders a 'Requested by this box's agent' block over status.declaredHere, each DeclaredRow offering a 'Supply value' toggle that opens SecretValueForm with the slot's name fixed, and a 'Stale grants' block over status.danglingGrants where DanglingRow calls secrets.revoke to drop a grant naming a removed secret. SecretsSection feeds both from the secrets.boxStatus query and refreshes them on every mutation.

verdict.note: SecretsSection.tsx queries trpc.secrets.boxStatus and passes it plus a refresh() that invalidates it to BoxSecretsView. SecretsSection-box.tsx renders a "Requested by this box's agent" block over status.declaredHere with DeclaredRow ('Supply value' toggles SecretValueForm with fixedName=slot.name) and a 'Stale grants' block over status.danglingGrants with DanglingRow calling secrets.revoke. Backend core/secrets/lifecycle.ts boxSecretStatus fills declaredHere from secrets whose declaredBy===slug and are not yet granted (badged 'empty slot' / 'has a value, not granted'), and danglingGrants from grants whose secret entry is gone.

browser.note: Neither a 'Requested by this box's agent' block nor a 'Stale grants' block appears — but the whole secrets.boxStatus query is refused with the authenticated-owner error, so their absence is explained by the gate, not by the feature being missing.

title: Gate every box request behind the auth wall
story: As an operator, I want each box's routes to require a recognized credential — session cookie, hub identity header, mobile device token, agent bearer, or browse key — so that box content is not reachable by an anonymous caller.
evidence: `addBoxAuthHook` in server-box-scope.ts installs a preHandler that tries `verifyAgentBearer`, `verifyBrowseKey`, `resolveMobileRequestAuth`, then `resolveRequestIdentity`, 401s API URLs, redirects page navigations to login, and 403s an email that fails `canAccessBox`.

verdict.note: addBoxAuthHook (callback-box/src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts:67) installs a preHandler on the per-box scope that tries verifyAgentBearer, verifyBrowseKey, resolveMobileRequestAuth (device token or cb_mobile cookie), then resolveRequestIdentity from src/webapp/auth.ts (hub header or session cookie); missing email gives 401 for isApiUrl paths and loginRedirect for page navigations, and a known email failing canAccessBox (src/webapp/box-access.ts) gives 403. The only bypass is instance.openAccess, but src/webapp/server.ts refuses to listen when openAccess is true (decorate defaults to false and startServer throws), so it is a test-only seam, not a config a real deployment can be anonymous under; narrow exemptions are OPTIONS preflight, non-API static asset extensions, the diagnostic API key, and POST pairing-redeem.

title: Get a login page that works with no scripts and no gated assets
story: As someone logged out behind a proxy that gates the app's bundle, I want the sign-in and first-run pages served as self-contained HTML forms, so that I can still log in when the SPA's scripts cannot load or JavaScript is off.
evidence: login-page.ts renders the login and setup pages with one inline `<style>` and a plain `<form>` POST, referencing no script, stylesheet, or asset URL, and takes the form action, Google link, and `returnTo` from `readBasePrefix` so the pages work behind a prefix-stripping proxy.

verdict.note: src/webapp/login-page.ts pageShell emits one inline <style> and no script/stylesheet/asset URL; renderLoginPage and renderSetupPage build plain <form method=POST> targeting `${prefix}/auth/login` and `${prefix}/auth/setup`, with the Google link and hidden returnTo also prefixed. src/webapp/routes/auth.ts registerPasswordRoutes registers GET /auth/login and GET /auth/setup returning that HTML (text/html), with the prefix from readBasePrefix (src/webapp/base-prefix.ts, reading the trusted x-cb-base-prefix header); the form POSTs are handled in a scoped plugin with a urlencoded parser. Works with JS off as claimed.

browser.note: The login page is fully self-contained: in the live DOM document.scripts.length === 0 and document.querySelectorAll('link').length === 0, with one inline <style> block and a plain <form method=POST action=/user-stories-refresh/auth/login> holding email, password, and hidden returnTo. It rendered and submitted in a browser with no app bundle loaded, and the form action/returnTo both carry the router's base prefix. The invite/reset-unavailable pages are likewise script-free.

title: Get told plainly when the box has no agent login
story: As someone maintaining a box, I want a missing Claude login to surface as one actionable message before a run starts, so that I fix the login instead of debugging an opaque agent failure.
evidence: `checkClaudeAuth` shells out to `claude auth status` (10s timeout) and throws `ClaudeAuthError` with `CLAUDE_NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE`; `preflightChatBackend` runs it before a chat session's first SDK run, and a confirmed login is cached for `POSITIVE_TTL_MS` while a negative result is never cached.

verdict.note: core/agent/auth-preflight.ts exports CLAUDE_NOT_LOGGED_IN_MESSAGE ('Claude Code is not logged in — run `claude auth login` on this machine'), ClaudeAuthError, and checkClaudeAuth(), which calls claudeCli.authStatus(); services/claude-cli.ts implements that as execFile('claude', ['auth','status'], {timeout: 10000}) and treats non-JSON/error output as loggedIn:false. A positive result is cached in cachedOkAt for POSITIVE_TTL_MS (10 min) and a negative result is never cached. preflightChatBackend() is awaited before the first SDK run in core/chat/session/index.ts:179 and thread.ts:141, emitting 'error' on the session (skipped for engine 'codex' or backends without requiresClaudeAuth); core/agent/run.ts:230 does the same for agent runs.

title: Hold service credentials in a custody store instead of the box tree
story: As a box owner, I want to store a service credential once, grant it to specific boxes at a chosen access level, and see only its metadata afterwards, so that agent-authored integrations can use it at call time without the value ever being readable back through the UI.
evidence: The secrets router (authenticatedOwnerProcedure) exposes setSecret/grantSecret/revokeSecret/boxStatus/machineView and returns only metadata — never a value; agent code obtains a value at call time through POST /api/secrets/resolve, which requires the agent bearer.

verdict.note: src/webapp/trpc/routers/secrets.ts defines secretsRouter with authenticatedOwnerProcedure procedures setValue (store/rotate a value), grant/setAccess (per-box grant at a secretAccessLevelSchema level), revoke, remove, plus boxStatus/machineView/formatHints queries that return only metadata (name, note, updated, verified, lastUsed, probe) — no query or mutation returns a stored value. The UI is reachable: src/frontend/src/pages/AdminPage.tsx renders <SecretsSection />, and SecretsSection.tsx/-box/-forms/-machine call trpc.secrets.boxStatus/machineView/setValue/grant/setAccess/revoke/remove. Agent-side read-back is a separate raw route, POST /api/secrets/resolve in src/webapp/routes/secrets.ts calling resolveSecret from src/core/secrets/resolve.ts (documented with an Authorization: Bearer $CB_AGENT_TOKEN in src/core/agent-guide/secrets.ts). Lifecycle writes go through src/core/secrets/lifecycle.ts as cited.

browser.note: The Secrets region renders with the intended framing ('API keys live in one store outside every box, and each box holds a grant to the ones it may use. Values are never shown here — saving one replaces it.') and three controls: 'This box', 'Machine-wide', 'Add a new secret'. Both queries fail with 'secrets management requires an authenticated owner session — open-access does not qualify (the store is machine-level, spanning every box on this host)', so no secret metadata, grants or levels were visible. Clicking 'Add a new secret' produced no form.

title: Invite someone to the box with a link
story: As a box owner, I want to generate a short-lived invite link, optionally bound to one email, so that someone else can create their own account on my box and be added to its access list without me handling their password.
evidence: admin.createInvite (ownerProcedure) calls mintAuthInvite and returns /auth/invite?token=…; InviteSection renders the copyable URL, and routes/auth-invite.ts consumes the token, creates the member with addInvitedMemberWithPasswordHash, grants box access, and signs them in.

verdict.note: trpc/routers/admin-invites.ts exposes createInvite as an ownerProcedure taking an optional email, calling mintAuthInvite (auth-capabilities.ts, CAPABILITY_TTL_MS = 15 min, random token stored hashed) and returning /auth/invite?token=…; it is spread into the admin router (admin.ts line 46). InviteSection.tsx (rendered from pages/AdminPage.tsx) offers an 'Let invitee enter email' open-invite checkbox or a bound email field, shows the absolute URL and a Copy link button, and states the 15-minute expiry. routes/auth-invite.ts (registered via registerAuthInviteRoutes from routes/auth.ts) serves GET/POST /auth/invite, validates name/password/confirm, consumes the token, calls addInvitedMemberWithPasswordHash, grantBoxAccess on the box config, and setSessionCookie before redirecting to the box — the invitee sets their own password.

browser.note: The 'Create invite link' form is present and complete: copy 'The link creates one member account for this box and expires after 15 minutes.', a 'Let invitee enter email' checkbox, a required 'Invitee email' textbox, and the submit button. I filled invitee@example.com and submitted; POST admin.createInvite fired and the form rendered an alert reading 'Owner access required'. No link was produced, so the copyable URL and the /auth/invite consumption path are unverified.

title: Issue a dedicated upload credential for a scanner
story: As a box owner, I want to mint and revoke named scan-upload tokens shown once at creation, so that a document scanner can push files into my box without holding an account credential.
evidence: scanTokens.create/list/revoke are ownerProcedures over the box's own hashed scan-token store; makeScanAuthPreHandler accepts either that bearer or a full owner identity on /api/scan/… and 401s otherwise, and the hub's scan-gate refuses to proxy the bearer to any other path.

verdict.note: scan-tokens.ts exposes create/list/revoke as ownerProcedures (registered as scanTokens in webapp/trpc/router.ts:56) over core/scan/tokens.ts, a separate hashed TokenStore at .callback-box/scan-tokens.secret.json with name-uniqueness (DuplicateScanTokenNameError) and revokeScanToken. The UI is ScanUploaderSection.tsx, rendered from SettingsPage.tsx:33; it mints, shows the plaintext with 'This token is shown once — copy it now. It won't be shown again.' plus a Copy button, lists tokens with createdAt/lastUsedAt, and has a per-row Revoke button. webapp/scan-auth.ts's makeScanAuthPreHandler accepts either a scan-token bearer or a resolved owner identity and 401s otherwise; hub/scan-gate.ts restricts the bearer to SCAN_PATHS (/api/scan/check or /api/scan/files/<64-hex>) so it authorizes nothing else.

browser.note: The 'Scan uploaders' section is present with the described purpose text ('Mint a token for a machine running the scan uploader, then paste it into `configure`.'), a prefilled 'Token name' textbox (uploader-2026-08-21), a 'Mint token' button, an 'Uploaders' list, and a 'First-time setup on a new machine' disclosure. Clicking 'Mint token' produced 'Owner access required'; the Uploaders list shows the same. The show-once token and revoke flow could not be reached.

title: Keep each box's access separate on a shared host
story: As an operator running several boxes on one machine, I want a box to admit only its owner or the emails it explicitly lists, so that access to one box never implies access to another.
evidence: canAccessBox() returns true only for the configured owner or an email in the box's allowedEmails (missing/empty means owner-only); addBoxAuthHook calls it per request under /<slug> and answers 403, while filterAccessibleBoxes trims the /api/boxes listing to the same rule.

verdict.note: webapp/box-access.ts canAccessBox() returns true for the canonicalized owner email, else only if the box's own loadBoxConfig(boxRoot).allowedEmails (normalized) includes the email — missing/empty means owner-only, per-box config so one box's ACL never covers another. server-box-scope.ts addBoxAuthHook adds a preHandler on the /<slug> scope that ends in canAccessBox(...) → 403 'Not authorized for this box'; server-root.ts's /api/boxes handler runs the same rule through filterAccessibleBoxes. (openAccess standalone mode skips the hook, but that's an explicit operator opt-out, not the configured multi-box case.)

title: Keep transcribed audio out of the provider's model-training pool
story: As a boxholder, I want the audio the box sends for transcription excluded from the provider's model-improvement program, so that private recordings aren't retained as training data by a third party.
evidence: `transcribeAudioDeepgram` sets `mip_opt_out=true` on the `/v1/listen` request URL alongside the formatting params, so every prerecorded Deepgram transcription this box makes opts out of Deepgram's Model Improvement Program.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/transcription/deepgram.ts:112 transcribeAudioDeepgram builds the URL from DEEPGRAM_ENDPOINT (https://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen) and sets model/smart_format/paragraphs/punctuate/detect_language plus url.searchParams.set("mip_opt_out", "true") (line 130) before the ky.post. It is the only Deepgram prerecorded call path, reached from transcription/index.ts:239, so every Deepgram transcription the box makes carries the Model Improvement Program opt-out.

title: Know whether a stored credential still works
story: As a box owner, I want a stored API credential checked against its provider when I save it, and flagged afterwards when a real use is rejected, so that I find out a key expired from the admin page rather than from a silently failing transcription.
evidence: secrets.setValue awaits probeSecret(), which calls a server-owned read-only endpoint per known name (OpenAI/Gemini/Deepgram/Mistral/Telegram getMe) and records ok/failed/unchecked with a status-derived reason; the router adds describeSecretProbe() and a 'suspect' state, which SecretsSection-box renders as the act-now badge or 'no verification available'.

verdict.note: webapp/trpc/routers/secrets.ts setValue (authenticatedOwnerProcedure) awaits probeSecret({name}) after setSecret and returns the SecretVerified to the admin UI; core/secrets/probe-registry.ts holds a server-owned registry of read-only endpoints (mistral/openai/gemini/deepgram GET listings, telegram getMe) and records ok/failed/unchecked with a status-code-derived reason, 'no verification is available for this credential' when a name has no entry. markSecretVerificationFailed closes the real-use loop and is called from core/transcription/deepgram.ts:170 and voxtral.ts:96 behind isAuthRejection(401/403); resolve.ts:147 turns a stored 'failed' into suspect:true, which the router surfaces per name (secrets.ts:92). SecretsSection-box.tsx renders 'may be expired' (danger badge) for suspect, 'verified'/'unverified' otherwise, plus ' · no verification available' when probe is null. The CB_SECRET_PROBES=off gate only applies when the env var is explicitly set (test harness), so the capability is on by default.

browser.note: Could not reach any secret rows: the secrets.boxStatus / secrets.machineView queries are both refused for this non-owner-authenticated session, so no probe badge ('ok'/'suspect'/'no verification available') was rendered to inspect, and saving a value to trigger probeSecret was impossible.

title: Land back on the page I was trying to reach after signing in
story: As a box user whose session lapsed on a deep link, I want the login to carry me back to the exact page I was on — even when a proxy stripped a path prefix from the URL the box saw — so that signing in resumes my work instead of dumping me at the box root.
evidence: loginRedirect() builds /auth/login?returnTo=<prefix+url> from the trusted x-cb-base-prefix header; sanitizeReturnTo re-validates it to a same-origin path, the login form and GoogleSignInButton carry it through, and handleLoginPost redirects to it on success. In-app, trpcFetch turns a 401 into window.location = /auth/login?returnTo=<pathname+search>.

verdict.note: src/webapp/base-prefix.ts loginRedirect() builds `${prefix}/auth/login?returnTo=${encodeURIComponent(prefix + request.url)}` from the validated x-cb-base-prefix header (validateBasePrefix rejects traversal/non-segment values), and it is called from server-root.ts:336 and server-box-scope.ts:139 on unauthenticated navigations. login-page.ts sanitizeReturnTo re-validates to a same-origin path (rejects //, /\, control chars) falling back to `${prefix}/`; the rendered form carries a hidden returnTo and the Google link passes it through, and routes/auth-password-post.ts redirects to the sanitized returnTo on success (loginErrorLocation preserves it on failure). In-app, src/frontend/src/lib/trpc/index.ts turns a 401 into window.location = withBase(`/auth/login?returnTo=` + pathname+search), and LoginPage.tsx reads returnTo from the query and navigates there after login.

browser.note: Deep link while logged out: GET /user-stories-refresh/test1/auth/me 302s to /user-stories-refresh/auth/login?returnTo=%2Fuser-stories-refresh%2Ftest1%2Fauth%2Fme — the returnTo carries the proxy-stripped prefix back. On the rendered page the form action is /user-stories-refresh/auth/login and a hidden input carries returnTo=/user-stories-refresh/test1/browse; after a failed submit the value was still intact (verified in the DOM) and the URL kept ?returnTo=...&error=1. The final redirect-to-returnTo on a successful login was not observable (no credentials).

title: Let the box's own agents call the box's API
story: As the box's agent or a scheduled script, I want a per-box loopback token injected into my environment that the auth wall accepts, so that I can call my own box's HTTP API without a browser session.
evidence: getOrCreateAgentToken() persists a 0600 token at .callback-box/agent-token that buildScriptEnv exports as CB_AGENT_TOKEN; addBoxAuthHook and the tRPC createContext both admit it via verifyAgentBearer, and POST /api/secrets/resolve accepts that credential alone.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/agent/token.ts getOrCreateAgentToken() writes a 32-byte hex token to <boxRoot>/.callback-box/agent-token with mode 0o600 and verifyAgentBearer() timing-safe-compares an Authorization header against it; resolveAgentToken() reads CB_AGENT_TOKEN or the cwd token file. src/core/script-env.ts:116 sets env.CB_AGENT_TOKEN = getOrCreateAgentToken(boxRoot) for spawned scripts. src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts:93 (inside addBoxAuthHook) returns early when verifyAgentBearer passes, and createContext recomputes it at line 212 for tRPC/WS. src/webapp/routes/secrets.ts:97-108 gates POST /api/secrets/resolve on verifyAgentBearer alone, 401-ing cookies/hub headers/device tokens.

title: Machine secret store with per-box grants
story: As an operator, I want to store a credential once on the machine and grant named boxes access to it, so that rotating a key is one edit instead of a hunt through box trees.
evidence: core/secrets/store.ts keeps one 0600 JSON file outside every box with `secrets` and per-box-slug `grants`; lifecycle.ts implements set/rm/declare/grant/revoke/list/status behind `cb secrets` (cli/commands/secrets.ts), and `resolveSecret` (resolve.ts) is the only read path, returning typed refusals from errors.ts.

verdict.note: core/secrets/store.ts defines a machine-level 0600 JSON store outside every box tree with `secrets` (one entry per flat name) and `grants: Record<boxSlug, Record<name, SecretAccessLevel>>`, written via withFileLock + writeFileAtomic(mode 0o600). lifecycle.ts exports setSecret/declareSecret/removeSecret/grantSecret/revokeSecret/listSecrets/boxSecretStatus, which cli/commands/secrets.ts wires into `cb secrets` subcommands (set/declare/grant/revoke/list/status); secretsCommand is registered in cli/index.ts:112. resolve.ts exports resolveSecret returning Result<ResolvedSecret, SecretRefusal>, with typed refusals in errors.ts (UnknownSecretError, SecretNotGrantedError, SecretAgentAccessNotGrantedError, DanglingSecretGrantError, SecretStoreUnreadableError). Rotating = one setSecret on the single stored value; grants are per-box-slug as claimed.

title: Manage box accounts from a shell
story: As an operator on the box's host, I want `cb auth` subcommands to create the owner, add or remove users, and set passwords directly against the auth file, so that I can recover access over SSH without a browser or a setup token.
evidence: cli/commands/auth.ts wires create-user/add-user/set-password/remove-user/list onto local-users.ts, taking the password from --password-file or a no-echo TTY prompt, with no HTTP involved.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/auth.ts defines the `auth` Commander command with create-user/add-user/set-password/remove-user/list subcommands calling createFirstUser/addUser/setPassword/removeUser/listUsers from webapp/local-users.ts directly (no HTTP), and cli/index.ts:111 does program.addCommand(authCommand). resolvePassword() reads --password-file (stripping one trailing newline) or calls promptHidden() from cli/lib/prompt-hidden.ts for a no-echo TTY prompt with confirmation on account-creating commands. The only gate is refuseIfUnconfirmedAgent(), which triggers on detected agent sessions and is bypassable with --agent-confirmed; a human operator over SSH is unaffected.

title: Owner-gated OAuth callback rejects forged grants
story: As a box owner, I want the OAuth callback to accept only a grant I started myself from behind the auth wall, so that nobody can plant their own Google credentials in my box.
evidence: createGoogleOAuthState stores a hashed, TTL'd nonce plus returnPath and createdBy on disk; the callback calls parseOAuthState/consumeGoogleOAuthState and 400s on a missing, expired or replayed nonce, then 403s when `consumed.createdBy` does not match resolveRequestIdentity's email.

verdict.note: webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts googleSetup is an ownerProcedure and calls createGoogleOAuthState({boxRoot, boxSlug, returnPath, createdBy: ctx.user?.email}) before generateAuthUrl; connectors/google-oauth-state.ts stores a sha256 nonceHash with a 15-minute expiresAt plus returnPath/createdBy in .callback-box/google-oauth-state.secret.json (mode 0600). registerGoogleServicesCallback in webapp/routes/admin.ts (mounted at /auth/google-services/callback from webapp/server.ts:199) calls parseOAuthState and 400s on malformed state or unknown box, calls consumeGoogleOAuthState (timing-safe compare, prunes expired, rewrites the store so a nonce is single-use) and 400s on null, then when consumed.createdBy is set compares it to resolveRequestIdentity(request).email and 403s on mismatch — all before any code exchange.

title: Per-box configuration
story: As an operator, I want to set a box's timezone, public URL, allowed emails, agent engine, enabled Google services and health-alert channel in one config file, so that every surface of the box behaves according to that box's setup.
evidence: core/box/config.ts loads and caches config/box.json with typed fields agentEngine, publicUrl, allowedEmails, timezone, googleServices, externalRoots and healthAlerts; resolveBoxPublicUrl in lib/public-url.ts reads publicUrl first, then the env cascade.

verdict.note: src/core/box/config.ts BoxConfig declares agentEngine ('claude'|'codex'), publicUrl, allowedEmails, timezone, googleServices (calendar/gmail/drive booleans), externalRoots and healthAlerts.telegramChat, loaded from config/box.json by loadBoxConfig with mtime-based caching plus clearBoxConfigCache. Consumers exist: isGoogleServiceAllowed is the gate referenced by connectors/gmail.ts and requirements.ts; healthAlerts.telegramChat drives core/notify-boxholder.ts and core/schedule/health-alert.ts; allowedEmails/googleServices are editable through webapp/box-config-write.ts and the admin UI. resolveBoxPublicUrl in src/lib/public-url.ts reads config/box.json#publicUrl first, then CB_PUBLIC_URL/PUBLIC_URL, then a caller fallback, as the story says.

title: Provider API keys resolved from one store
story: As an operator, I want the box's Mistral, Gemini, Deepgram and OpenAI keys resolved from the machine secret store with legacy file and env fallbacks, so that I can move credentials out of per-box files without breaking transcription, vision or TTS.
evidence: Each module runs the same cascade — resolveSecret at `server` access first, then the legacy config/connectors/<name>.secret.json (warned once per process, where one exists), then the named env vars; deepgram-key.ts parses the two-field JSON value used to mint short-TTL browser keys.

verdict.note: mistral-key.ts (getMistralApiKey) and deepgram-key.ts (getDeepgramCredentials) each call resolveSecret at access `server`, fall through only on an unknown-secret refusal (refusalAllowsLegacyFallback) to config/connectors/<name>.secret.json with a once-per-process console.warn latch, then to CALLBACK_MISTRAL_API_KEY / CALLBACK_DEEPGRAM_API_KEY+CALLBACK_DEEPGRAM_PROJECT. deepgram-key parses the two-field JSON value via parseJsonSecret, and its doc points at trpc/routers/transcription.ts minting short-TTL browser keys. gemini-key.ts and openai-thinking-key.ts follow the same cascade minus the legacy-file arm (GEMINI_KEY/SKE_GEMINI_API_KEY, THINKING_OPENAI_API_KEY) — matching the story's 'where one exists' qualifier.

title: Redeem an invite and set a password
story: As an invited person, I want to open an invite link and choose my name and password, so that I get my own account on the box.
evidence: `registerAuthInviteRoutes` serves `GET /auth/invite` (rendered by invite-page.ts) and `POST /auth/invite`, which validates the token plus password/confirmPassword and creates the local user.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/routes/auth-invite.ts exports registerAuthInviteRoutes, registered from routes/auth.ts:186 inside the form-body scope, and defines GET /auth/invite (inspects the token, renders renderInvitePage from invite-page.ts, 410s on dead tokens) and POST /auth/invite. invite-page.ts renders a form with Name, Password, and Confirm password inputs plus a hidden token (and an email field for open invites). acceptInvite() parses those fields with inviteFieldsSchema (password min 8, must equal confirmPassword), hashes with hashPassword, consumes the invite, calls addInvitedMemberWithPasswordHash in local-users.ts, grants box access, sets the session cookie, and redirects to the box. Matches the story as written.

title: Refs cannot escape the box
story: As a person whose box holds private files, I want a card ref — written by a person, an agent, or injected content — to resolve only inside the box, so that a crafted path cannot read files elsewhere on the machine.
evidence: lib/box-containment.ts is the hand-rolled, doctested containment layer every ref resolution passes through; prompt-fence.ts emits a fence longer than any backtick run in embedded content so untrusted text cannot pose as prompt structure; expandClaudeIncludes throws UnsafeAgentContextIncludeError for an include escaping the box package.

verdict.note: src/lib/box-containment.ts implements containWithinBox (path.resolve + explicit `=== root || startsWith(root + sep)` check, returning a branded BoxRelativePath or null), resolveBoxRelativeRef, realpathContained (fs.realpath on both sides, RefEscapesBoxError) and readContainedFile; it is imported by the ref sinks (core/ref-exists.ts resolveContainedRef, core/nav.ts, core/reactor/batch-jobs.ts, webapp/trpc/routers/views.ts, webapp/routes/figure.ts, cli/commands/wakeup-steps.ts). src/lib/prompt-fence.ts's fenceForPrompt emits max(3, longestBacktickRun+1) backticks so embedded content cannot close the fence. src/core/agent-context-includes.ts expandClaudeIncludes throws UnsafeAgentContextIncludeError for an absolute specifier or a relative path escaping the package (rel.startsWith('..')). Story matches the code as written.

title: Reset a member's forgotten password with a link
story: As a box owner, I want to mint a one-time password-reset link for a member of my box, so that someone who forgot their password can set a new one without me knowing the old one.
evidence: admin.createPasswordReset (ownerProcedure) mints a capability for a member listed in allowedEmails and returns /auth/reset-password?token=…; routes/auth-password-reset.ts consumes it and calls setPasswordWithPasswordHash, with its own passwordResetThrottle.

verdict.note: admin-password-resets.ts exports createPasswordReset as an ownerProcedure: it canonicalizes the email, requires getLocalUser(email).role === 'member' AND membership in the box config's normalized allowedEmails, then mintAuthPasswordReset returns `/auth/reset-password?token=…` plus expiresAt. It is spread into the admin router (trpc/routers/admin.ts line 47). routes/auth-password-reset.ts serves GET/POST /auth/reset-password, guards with its own `passwordResetThrottle = new LoginThrottle()`, calls consumeAuthPasswordReset(token) and setPasswordWithPasswordHash for the consumed reset's email — no old password required. UI entry: useAllowedEmails.createReset wired through components/admin/AllowedEmailsSection.tsx (onReset).

browser.note: No password-reset control appears anywhere on the page. It is per-allowed-email, and this box's allowed-email list is empty ('Owner-only — no additional users can access this box.'), so the control has nothing to hang on; the section is also owner-gated. Cannot distinguish 'absent' from 'no data' here.

title: Resolve a secret from code running in the box
story: As agent-authored box code making an outbound call, I want to ask my own box for a granted credential at the moment I need it, so that the value never has to sit in env, a file, or a log.
evidence: `POST /api/secrets/resolve` accepts ONLY the per-box agent bearer (`verifyAgentBearer`, re-checked in the handler), calls `resolveSecret` with `access: "agent"`, and returns the store's typed refusal `kind` verbatim with a mapped HTTP status.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/routes/secrets.ts registers POST /api/secrets/resolve via registerSecretsRoutes, which is wired into the box scope at src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts:274, so the route is reachable on a running box. The handler calls verifyAgentBearer(boxRoot, request.headers['authorization']) itself and returns 401 with kind 'not-agent-authenticated' for any other credential (cookie, hub header, device token), then validates {name, purpose} with zod (SECRET_PURPOSE_PATTERN) and calls resolveSecret({boxRoot, slug, name, purpose, access: 'agent'}) from src/core/secrets/resolve.ts. Refusals are returned with the store's typed kind verbatim and a mapped status via statusForRefusal (403 not-granted/agent-access-not-granted, 404 unknown-secret/empty-slot/dangling-grant, 503 store-unreadable); success returns {value, suspect} in the response only, never written to env/file/log.

title: Revoking a grant actually stops the connector
story: As a boxholder, I want a withheld or revoked secret grant to shut a connector down even on a box that still has the old in-tree credential file or an exported env var, so that revoking access is a real act rather than a no-op the stale file papers over.
evidence: `refusalAllowsLegacyFallback` (core/secrets/legacy-fallback.ts) returns true only for `unknown-secret`; `not-granted`, `agent-access-not-granted`, `empty-slot`, `dangling-grant` and `store-unreadable` fail closed and emit one warning per reader per kind carrying the refusal's relay-ready message. Every per-key reader (mistral-key.ts, embeddings-key.ts and siblings) gates its legacy file/env cascade on that call.

verdict.note: src/core/secrets/legacy-fallback.ts refusalAllowsLegacyFallback() returns true only when refusal.kind === 'unknown-secret'; every other kind returns false after a console.warn latched once per `${reader}:${kind}` that names the kind and appends refusal.message. src/core/secrets/errors.ts defines the SecretRefusalKind discriminants unknown-secret, empty-slot, not-granted, agent-access-not-granted, dangling-grant, store-unreadable on SecretRefusalError subclasses with a relay-ready message. mistral-key.ts getMistralApiKey() and search/embeddings-key.ts getOpenAiEmbeddingsKey() both `if (!refusalAllowsLegacyFallback(...)) return null;` before touching config/connectors/*.secret.json or the CALLBACK_*_API_KEY env var, and the same gate is applied by gemini-key, deepgram-key, openai-thinking-key, telegram-helpers, google-auth, api-adapters and publish/connector-secret. `cb secrets revoke` exists (src/cli/commands/secrets.ts:345), so a revoked grant produces a not-granted refusal that fails closed.

title: Revoking the OAuth app secret cuts the box off for good
story: As an operator, I want a revoked or withheld `google-oauth-client-id`/`-secret` grant to leave Google simply unconfigured for that box, rather than falling through to whatever GOOGLE_OAUTH_* env vars are still exported, so that revoking a grant actually stops the box reaching Google.
evidence: `getGoogleClientCreds` resolves both halves from the machine store and only lets a "no such secret on this machine" refusal reach the env-var arm — `refusalAllowsLegacyFallback` — returning null for any other refusal (revoked, withheld, empty, unreadable), and refusing to pair a store id with an env secret.

verdict.note: connectors/google-auth.ts getGoogleClientCreds() resolves google-oauth-client-id and google-oauth-client-secret via resolveSecret({access:'server'}); if both ok it returns them, otherwise it computes `blocked` by asking refusalAllowsLegacyFallback for each failing half and returns null when any refusal is not fall-through-eligible. core/secrets/legacy-fallback.ts allows fallback only for kind 'unknown-secret' and warns-once for everything else; errors.ts enumerates the other kinds (not-granted, agent-access-not-granted, empty-slot, dangling-grant, store-unreadable), all of which therefore fail closed rather than reading GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET. A store id is never paired with an env secret since a partial answer either returns both from the store or falls through wholly to env. Note the store path only engages when boxRoot is supplied (box-less hub callers stay env-only), which matches the story's per-box framing.

title: See what each stored credential is actually used for
story: As a box owner deciding whether to revoke a grant, I want each secret to show what the engine spends it on, what someone declared it for, and which purposes real resolves have actually passed, so that I can tell what breaks before I take it away.
evidence: uses.ts derives a built-in reason list from the repo's own resolveSecret call sites, entry.uses holds declared reasons (cb secrets describe --add-use), and appendSecretAccessEvent records each resolve/refuse/mint into monthly JSONL while stamping observed purposes and an hourly-throttled lastUsed; SecretUsesBlock renders the three sources separately and formatSecretUsesLines prints them in cb secrets list/status.

verdict.note: src/core/secrets/uses.ts holds `builtinUses` (a per-secret-name list derived from repo resolveSecret call sites, keyed via name-match.ts) plus formatSecretUsesLines, used by src/cli/commands/secrets.ts (lines 184, 244, 257) in list/status output; secrets-describe.ts exposes the repeatable `--add-use <reason>` option writing entry.uses. src/core/secrets/access-log.ts appends resolve/refuse/mint events and stamps the distinct observed `purpose` labels onto `entry.purposes` (lines 144-155) alongside a throttled lastUsed. The web UI component SecretsSection-uses.tsx's SecretUsesBlock renders uses.builtin, uses.declared (tagged "(declared)") and uses.observed (italic "observed: …") as three separate presentations, and is rendered from SecretsSection-box.tsx (lines 58, 159) and SecretsSection-machine.tsx (line 55).

browser.note: Same gate as r1-20: no secret entries render, so the built-in / declared / observed uses blocks in SecretUsesBlock could not be observed.

title: See who I am and which boxes I can open
story: As a signed-in user, I want the app to tell me my identity, whether I'm the owner, and the list of boxes I'm allowed into, so that the UI can show me only the boxes that are mine.
evidence: `registerAuthMe` serves `GET /auth/me` with email, isOwner, hasPassword and the accessible box slugs; `GET /api/boxes` (server-root.ts) returns the same access-filtered list via `listAccessibleBoxes`/`filterAccessibleBoxes`. `GET /auth/logout` clears the cookie.

verdict.note: src/webapp/routes/auth.ts registerAuthMe registers GET /auth/me always; with a resolved identity it returns { email, name, picture, isOwner: email === ownerEmail, hasPassword: currentUserHasPassword(email), boxes: accessibleBoxes } where accessibleBoxes is built by looping options.boxes through canAccessBox from src/webapp/box-access.ts. server-root.ts line 247 registers GET /api/boxes, which for an authenticated identity returns listAccessibleBoxes(boxes, identity.email) (box-access.ts's canAccessBox/filterAccessibleBoxes are the shared predicate, fail-closed owner-only when allowedEmails is empty). registerPasswordRoutes also registers GET /auth/logout, clearing COOKIE_NAME and redirecting to /. Story matches the code.

browser.note: GET /user-stories-refresh/auth/me responds (returns {"error":"Not authenticated"} — correct for a session-less request) and GET /user-stories-refresh/api/boxes returns {"boxes":[{"slug":"test1","name":"test1"}]}, so the access-filtered box list is served. The identity/isOwner half is unverifiable: no signed-in session is obtainable, and the User menu shows only Settings/Admin/Source View/Debug Log/Reload — no email, no owner marker, no sign-out.

title: See who I'm signed in as, and reach settings, admin, or sign-out from any page
story: As a person using the box, I want the app bar's avatar menu to show the account I'm signed in as and lead to Settings, Admin, a hard reload, and sign-out, so that account and box administration are one tap away from wherever I am.
evidence: AppNav's ProfileMenu renders an Avatar (picture, or initials derived from name/email) as the Dropdown trigger, a header showing the useCurrentUser name and email, MenuItems to `/<box>/settings` and `/<box>/admin` marked active by pathname, and Reload plus a Sign out item pointing at `/auth/logout` (omitted when no user is signed in).

verdict.note: AppNav.tsx's `ProfileMenu` (lines 44-85) renders `<Avatar name/email/picture>` as the Dropdown trigger, a header div with `user.name` and `user.email` when signed in, `<MenuItem to={`/${boxSlug}/settings`} active={isOnSettings}>` and the same for `/admin` (active derived from useRouterState location.pathname), Source View / Debug Log / `Reload` (window.location.reload), and `{user ? <MenuItem href={withBase('/auth/logout')}>Sign out</MenuItem> : null}`. Avatar.tsx falls back from picture to an initial derived from name-then-email, then a generic user icon. useCurrentUser.ts backs this with a react-query `/auth/me` fetch resolving to null when signed out. AppNav is mounted app-wide in app-shell.tsx:78.

browser.note: The avatar menu opens from the app bar on every page and contains Settings (/test1/settings), Admin (/test1/admin), Source View, Debug Log and Reload. It shows no signed-in name/email header and no 'Sign out' item — consistent with the story's 'omitted when no user is signed in', since this browse session authenticates with the dev browse key rather than an account. The identity-display and sign-out half of the story therefore could not be exercised.

title: Sign in once at the hub and pick a box
story: As a boxholder with several boxes behind one hub, I want to log in at the hub and choose from the boxes I can reach, so that I get to any of them with one session instead of authenticating per box.
evidence: hub-server.ts registers the auth surface on the hub itself, reads cb_session (only the hub holds the signing secret), strips client x-cb-* headers and injects x-cb-authenticated-email plus x-cb-hub-secret before proxying; box-picker.ts serves / with filterAccessibleBoxes, rendered by BoxSelectionTiles.
