verdict.note: src/hub/hub-server.ts (reachable as `cb hub` — hubCommand is added in src/cli/index.ts) calls registerAuthSurface(app, {boxes, publicUrlFallback: baseUrl}) so /auth/login|callback|logout|me live on the hub itself; proxied requests pass through the HUB_HEADER_PREFIX ('x-cb-') strip wall and then get x-cb-hub-secret plus x-cb-authenticated-email (or x-cb-hub-auth: off) injected, and src/webapp/auth.ts's resolveRequestIdentity takes the hub-header path when isHubMode(). src/hub/box-picker.ts registers GET /: unauthenticated → loginRedirect, otherwise serves the SPA (whose / route renders BoxSelectionTiles and fetches the hub's /api/boxes, hub-server.ts line 353) or falls back to a server-rendered list built with filterAccessibleBoxes (src/webapp/box-access.ts). One cookie at the hub therefore reaches every accessible box; boxes never verify the cookie themselves.

title: Sign in with email and password
story: As a box user, I want to sign in with my email and password on the box's login page, so that I can reach my box without depending on an external identity provider.
evidence: LoginPage posts {email,password} to POST /auth/login; handleLoginPost verifies against the scrypt hashes in ~/.cb-auth.json (local-users.ts verifyPassword) and replies 204 after setting the session cookie.

verdict.note: src/frontend/src/pages/login/LoginPage.tsx (routed at /login in src/frontend/src/router.tsx:53) fetches GET /auth/methods, renders LoginFields when methods.password, and postLogin POSTs {email,password} JSON to /auth/login, redirecting on a 204 and handling 401/429. Server side, registerPasswordRoutes in src/webapp/routes/auth.ts registers POST /auth/login -> handleLoginPost (src/webapp/routes/auth-password-post.ts:210), which calls verifyPassword({email,password}) from src/webapp/local-users.ts (scrypt hashes in ~/.cb-auth.json, CB_AUTH_FILE override) and replies 204 with the session cookie (line 255). /auth/methods returns password:true unconditionally, so the password path is not flag-gated, and Google is only offered when creds exist — no external IdP required.

browser.note: The login page renders a self-contained email+password form (labels Email/Password, Sign in button). Submitting nobody-storycheck@example.com with a wrong password POSTs to /user-stories-refresh/auth/login and re-renders with an alert 'Incorrect email or password.' and ?error=1, so the box does verify credentials against its local users. The success branch was not exercised — I have no plaintext box password and must not create one.

title: Sign in with Google when the box is configured for it
story: As a box user, I want a 'Sign in with Google' option when the operator has configured OAuth credentials, so that I can use my Google identity instead of a box-local password.
evidence: registerAuthRoutes mounts GET /auth/google (consent redirect with a sanitized returnTo as OAuth state) and GET /auth/callback (code exchange, then signSession + cb_session cookie); GET /auth/methods advertises google:true so LoginPage renders GoogleSignInButton.

verdict.note: src/webapp/routes/auth.ts registerAuthSurface registers auth-google.ts's registerAuthRoutes only when GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID is set (and getGoogleClientCreds() must return an id+secret pair or MissingOAuthClientSecretError throws). registerAuthRoutes mounts GET /auth/google (generateAuthUrl with scope openid/email/profile and state = sanitizeReturnTo(query.returnTo)) and GET /auth/callback (getToken + verifyIdToken, then signSession from src/webapp/auth.ts:223 and the COOKIE_NAME cb_session cookie). GET /auth/methods returns { password: true, google: (await getGoogleClientCreds()) !== null, setupRequired }, and src/frontend/src/pages/login/LoginPage.tsx fetches /auth/methods and renders GoogleSignInButton (an <a> to /auth/google?returnTo=...) when google is advertised.

browser.note: This box has no Google OAuth configured: GET /auth/methods returns {"password":true,"google":false,"setupRequired":false}, the login page shows no 'Sign in with Google' button, and GET /auth/google 302s to /auth/login?returnTo=%2Fauth%2Fgoogle instead of a Google consent URL. Behavior is consistent with the story's precondition (option appears only when configured), but the configured case cannot be checked here.

title: Stay signed in across visits and sign out on demand
story: As a box user, I want my sign-in to persist in a signed cookie for thirty days and to be able to sign out from the app menu, so that I am not re-authenticating on every visit but can end the session when I want.
evidence: auth.ts signs the cb_session cookie with HMAC-SHA256 and a SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS of 30 days (no server-side store); routes/auth.ts serves GET /auth/me and GET /auth/logout, and AppNav renders a 'Sign out' item linking to /auth/logout.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/auth.ts sets COOKIE_NAME="cb_session" and SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS = 30*24*60*60*1000; signSession HMAC-SHA256s a JSON payload (base64url payload + hex sig) and verifySession recomputes it with a timing-safe compare — no server-side session store. routes/auth-password-post.ts and routes/auth-google.ts set the cookie with maxAge: SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS/1000. routes/auth.ts registers GET /auth/logout (clearCookie then redirect to /) and GET /auth/me. AppNav.tsx line 82 renders <MenuItem href={withBase("/auth/logout")}>Sign out</MenuItem> when a user is present, with the user coming from useCurrentUser.ts's react-query fetch of /auth/me.

browser.note: Sign-out endpoint verified: GET /auth/logout 302s to / with 'set-cookie: cb_session=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970...; SameSite=Lax'. But the App nav User menu in the running app shows only Settings, Admin, Source View, Debug Log, Reload — no 'Sign out'. That is because this browser is authorized by the CB_BROWSE_API_KEY cookie, not a cb_session: /auth/me returns 401 {"error":"Not authenticated"}, and AppNav.tsx renders the Sign out item only when a user is present. Neither the 30-day cookie lifetime nor the menu item could be observed without a real password sign-in.

title: Supply the OAuth app credentials as machine secrets
story: As an operator, I want to grant `google-oauth-client-id` and `google-oauth-client-secret` from the secret store (or set the matching env vars), so that boxes on this server can offer Google connection at all.
evidence: getGoogleClientCreds resolves both secret names with `access: "server"` through resolveSecret and falls back to GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET only when both halves are absent; `googleStatus` returns `available: false` (hiding the section) and `googleSetup` throws BAD_REQUEST naming those secrets when they're missing.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/connectors/google-auth.ts defines GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID_SECRET_NAME="google-oauth-client-id" and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET_SECRET_NAME="google-oauth-client-secret" (lines 48-49) and getGoogleClientCreds() resolves both via resolveSecret({purpose:"google-oauth", access:"server"}) from core/secrets/resolve.ts, falling back to process.env.GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET only when both refusals are the benign 'no such secret' kind (refusalAllowsLegacyFallback); any other refusal returns null. In src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts, googleStatus returns {available:false,...} when creds are null and googleSetup throws TRPCError BAD_REQUEST naming both secret names; the frontend consumes it in src/frontend/src/components/admin/useGoogleServices.ts. Story matches.

title: The box refuses to let an agent change login credentials on its own
story: As the boxholder, I want `cb auth` to refuse password and account changes when it detects that a coding agent — not a person at a terminal — is running it, unless the agent passes an explicit confirmation flag, so that an agent that hits a login wall cannot manufacture credentials and lock me out of every local box.
evidence: `detectAgentContext()` reports an agent from known runtime env vars (CLAUDECODE, CURSOR_AGENT, OPENAI_CODEX, …) or a non-TTY stdin; `refuseIfUnconfirmedAgent` in cli/commands/auth.ts calls it and aborts with a message naming the auth file's global blast radius unless `--agent-confirmed` was passed.

verdict.note: src/lib/agent-context.ts defines detectAgentContext(), which returns isAgent:true when any of CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, CURSOR_AGENT, AIDER_CHAT, OPENAI_CODEX is set non-empty/non-"0", or when process.stdin.isTTY !== true. src/cli/commands/auth.ts has its own refuseIfUnconfirmedAgent({action, agentConfirmed}) (lines 123-144) that returns early on agentConfirmed===true, otherwise calls detectAgentContext() and, if an agent, console.errors a message stating the local auth file is GLOBAL across every local box and that changing a password revokes sessions irrecoverably, then process.exit(1). It is called from runCreateUser, runAddUser, runSetPassword and runRemoveUser, and each corresponding commander subcommand registers --agent-confirmed. Matches the story as written.

title: A hung scheduled script is killed with its whole process tree
story: As the boxholder relying on scheduled tasks, I want a script that hangs to be killed — together with any grandchildren it spawned — after a bounded amount of running time, with the tail of its output kept in the failure, so that one stuck script does not occupy the scheduler forever and I can see how it was behaving when it died.
evidence: `execWithTimeout` spawns through its own process group and kills the group on expiry, capturing stdout/stderr tails for the error message; the deadline is `SCRIPT_TIMEOUT` (10 minutes) counted by `startAwakeTimeout`, which excludes machine-sleep gaps so a run spanning a laptop sleep is not killed on wake. Callers are the scheduler tick (cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts, tick-utils.ts) and the manual run-now path (trpc/routers/scheduler-run.ts).

verdict.note: src/lib/exec-with-timeout.ts spawns `sh -c command` with detached:true and, on expiry, does process.kill(-child.pid, "SIGKILL") — killing the whole process group, so grandchildren die too. The deadline is options.timeout defaulting to the exported SCRIPT_TIMEOUT = 10*60*1000, counted by startAwakeTimeout (src/lib/awake-timeout.ts), which folds inter-tick gaps and excludes sleep-sized gaps from awakeMs. The rejection is a CommandTimedOutError whose message is built by appendOutputTail(), attaching the last 500 chars of stderr and 2000 of stdout. Callers are the scheduler tick (src/cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts:277, tick-utils.ts:144) and the manual run-now path (src/webapp/trpc/routers/scheduler-run.ts:91), both passing `parsed.timeoutMs ?? SCRIPT_TIMEOUT` and recording the resulting error text as the run outcome.

title: A mail rule that runs a procedure instead of making cards
story: As a box owner, I want a Gmail rule whose action is a procedure ref, so that arriving mail can drive an agent procedure without leaving card clutter behind.
evidence: ProcedureActionInputSchema constrains the ref to `config/procedures/*.procedure.card`; evaluateGmailRules returns ConnectorProcedureTrigger entries on the SyncResult, and runConnectorProcedureTriggers runs each as a `procedure-run` command after the connector writes complete.

verdict.note: gmail-config.ts defines ProcedureActionInputSchema (type literal "procedure", ref regex ^config/procedures/(?!.*\.\.)[^/]+\.procedure\.card$) in the GmailRuleAction union alongside track/stage. title: An item triage can't place becomes a question that teaches a rule

The 37 questions whose names contain 'unsure' are scan page-classification questions ('What is unsure-001.jpg? (photo, back-of-photo, or trash)') with input.type: text — free-text boxes, not the per-category option list plus _other escape hatch this story describes, and they carry no learning proposal. title: Answer a pending question and queue the follow-up
story: As the boxholder, I want to answer a question the box asked me — free text, a selected option, or yes/no — and have a follow-up job created in the same atomic commit, so that my answer actually gets acted on.
evidence: `executeAnswer` normalizes select/confirm/text answers (`resolveAnswer`), flips `status: answered` with `answered-at`/`answered-via`, and writes a `question-followup.job.card` into `box/jobs` before the card write inside `withQuestionTransition`'s single guarded commit.

Web entry point confirmed: src/webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts `answer` procedure (line 20) dispatches the same command and emits question-answered, and src/frontend/src/components/questions/QuestionForm.tsx calls trpc.actions.answer for confirm/select/text variants.

browser.note: Typed 'trash' into a question's Answer box and hit Submit Answer; the card flipped to status: answered with answer.text: trash, answered-at, answered-via: web, and box/jobs/...question-followup.job.card was written in the same commit carrying source: question-answer, question-ref, the directive, and answer: trash. Confirm-type questions render Yes / No buttons plus an optional Note field (not submitted, to avoid queueing a briefing edit). No select-type question exists in this box, so that input variant was not exercised.

title: Answer a question from two places without corrupting it
story: As the boxholder, I want a question answered from the web while the CLI or the aging sweep is touching it to end with exactly one recorded answer, so that a double-tap on my phone never produces two follow-up jobs or a half-written card.
evidence: `withQuestionTransition` acquires a cross-process lock under `.callback-box/question-locks/` (bounded retry, then `QuestionLockError`) plus the in-process `withCardLock`, re-reads and re-checks the status inside both, and `applyAndCommit` restores every written file and unstages the paths if the single commit fails, leaving the question retryable.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/commands/question-transition.ts `withQuestionTransition` acquires a cross-process lock file under `.callback-box/question-locks/<safe>.lock` via `acquireLock` with 50 x 100ms retries then throws `QuestionLockError`, wraps `withCardLock(fullPath, ...)` inside it, and re-reads/re-validates status through `loadForTransition` inside both locks. `applyAndCommit` snapshots each write's prior content, writes, commits all paths in one `stageAndCommitPaths`, and on failure unstages and restores/deletes each file, returning a failure so the question stays retryable. answer.ts:219 routes through it with allowedStatuses pending/expired/dismissed (answered is terminal, so a double-tap loses and produces no second follow-up job), the web path is webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts `answer` mutation (via: 'web'), the CLI is cli/commands/answer.ts, and core/question-aging.ts:102 uses the same guard.

title: Answer a question I already dismissed or let expire

title: Ask the agent in chat to remind me later

evidence: `parseScheduleTags` turns `<schedule>` tags in the agent's reply into entries persisted in `.callback-box/chat-schedules.json` and re-armed at server start; on fire, `chat-schedule-fire.ts` resumes the originating `sessionId` and injects a `<schedule-fired>` message; the frontend renders `SchedulePill` with cancel and plays `alarm`/TTS on the `schedule-fired` bus event; `chat.schedules`/`cancel` list and cancel by label.

Frontend: InteractiveChat-layout.tsx renders SchedulePill (countdown + × cancel from InteractiveChat-controls.tsx), hooks.ts cancels via trpc chat.cancelSchedule and lists via chat.schedules (chat-control-procedures.ts:252-261), and InteractiveChat-ws.ts plays `alarm` and TTS-speaks `announce` on the schedule-fired bus event.

The × cancelled it and the pill disappeared. No schedule card involved. The optional alarm-sound / spoken-announcement variants were not exercised (I did not let it fire).

title: Ask the boxholder a question and route the answer back to an agent
story: As an agent that needs input, I want a question card with select/text/confirm input, an expiry, a learning sink, and a directive, so that the boxholder's answer comes back as work an agent acts on rather than sitting unread.

title: Be reminded about an upload batch nobody ever filed
story: As a boxholder, I want a file batch that has sat unfiled for a week to raise itself once in the chat it came from, so that uploads I forgot about get filed instead of aging out in a staging directory.

Reachable: registerBulkUploadRoutes (routes/bulk-upload.ts:360) calls startBulkUploadLifecycle, and server-box-scope.ts:275 registers those routes per box.

title: Be warned when the queue has stopped draining

title: Cards that hide their todos are named
story: As a boxholder, I want any card the todo scan couldn't fully read — bad frontmatter, a body that fails Markdoc validation on a todo tag, a card type with no schema, or a todo id used twice — listed alongside the collected todos, so that a broken card can't quietly park work where nothing will ever surface it.

title: Check whether a retrospective has anything to do
story: As a scheduled procedure, I want `cb retro status --check` to report how many quiet chat sessions are ready for observation and exit non-zero when none are, so that a retro run can skip cheaply instead of spending an agent on nothing.
evidence: `statusCommand` in cli/commands/retro.ts calls `discoverSessions` (core/retro/discovery.ts), which qualifies sessions with real `<typed>`/`<speech>` user messages, past the 30-minute `QUIESCENCE_MS` window, not already settled in `loadRetroState`, and exits 1 under `--check` when the count is zero.

title: Close out a finished job
story: As a box agent, I want finishing a job to delete its job card and commit that removal, so that completed work leaves the queue in one step rather than lingering as a stale card.

title: Come back to a conversation later
story: As a boxholder, I want the agent to be able to schedule its own return to a chat by writing `callback-in` on its seen marker with a note to its future self, so that it can follow up on an unanswered question without a message arriving to wake it.
evidence: `recordCallbackTimers` (telegram-outbound.ts) reads a trailing `kind: seen` entry's `callback-in`, parses it with `parseDuration` and stores `callbacks[threadRelPath] = { at }` in the connector's transient state; `checkCallbackTimers` in connectors/telegram.ts creates a chat job via `createChatJob` for each expired timer and clears it, and the seen entry's `text` carries the note the agent left itself.

title: Connectors run on wakeup and report per-connector results
story: As a box owner, I want every configured connector to sync when the box wakes up, with one flaky service reported rather than aborting the cycle, so that mail, calendar and Drive stay current without me asking.
evidence: runConnectors registers the Gmail, Calendar, Telegram, Drive and publish-submissions connectors, resolves the `--connector X` scope, runs each `sync()` and prints per-connector plus total counts; the loop absorbs sync failures but ConnectorFatalError (a misconfiguration) stops it.

title: Control how long a procedure's runs are kept
story: As a procedure author or operator, I want to set a procedure's completed and failed run retention, or pin one run by editing its card's expires to never, so that an interesting run survives while routine runs are still swept up.
evidence: `loadProcedureDefinition` validates the card's `run-expiry`/`failed-run-expiry` via `validateRunExpiry` (duration or "never"); `computeRunExpires` stamps `expires` on the run card at finalization; `gcProcedureRuns`'s `resolveExpiry` keeps any run whose `expires` is `never` — and keeps, with a warning, one whose `expires` is unparseable because that was an attempt to pin it.

title: Define a multi-step procedure and watch a run of it

title: Define a recurring task as a scheduled-script card

title: Dismiss a question without answering it
story: As the boxholder, I want to dismiss a pending question, so that it stops waiting on me while remaining answerable later if I change my mind.
evidence: `executeDismiss` sets `status: dismissed` and `dismissed-at` through `withQuestionTransition` with `allowedStatuses: ["pending"]` and no follow-up job; `answer.ts` still lists `dismissed` among its allowed source statuses.

Reachable from the web UI: frontend/src/components/questions/QuestionForm.tsx:87 calls `trpc.actions.dismiss`, whose procedure in webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts runs the `dismiss` command and emits `question-dismissed` (a `cb dismiss` CLI command also exists).
