title: Flush everything the automation produced to its outbound channel
story: As the box's agent, I want `cb finalize` to run the outbound connectors that deliver queued output cards, so that Telegram messages and push notifications produced by unattended work actually leave the box.
evidence: `cb finalize` initializes the gmail/calendar/telegram/drive/push connectors and runs their outbound phase over `box/output/` cards, after first running the question alert and aging sweeps so the cards they write ship in the same pass.

verdict.note: cli/commands/finalize.ts (registered via cli/index.ts program.addCommand(finalizeCommand)) runs checkPendingQuestionsAndNotify and ageQuestions first, then createGmailConnector/createGoogleCalendarConnector/createTelegramConnector/createGoogleDriveConnector/createPushConnector and iterates getAllConnectors() calling connector.sync() with triggeredBy = 'cb finalize'. connectors/push.ts PushConnector.sync -> sendOutputPushCards -> deliverPendingOutputCards over `box/output/*.web-push.card`; connectors/telegram-output-cards.ts sendOutputCards does the same for telegram-message cards in box/output/. Matches the story exactly, including the ordering rationale in the comments.

title: Garbage-collect old procedure runs
story: As an operator, I want expired procedure run directories deleted and each procedure capped at a bounded number of retained runs, so that a frequently-scheduled procedure cannot fill the box with run dirs.
evidence: `procedure-gc` calls `gcProcedureRuns`, which reads each run card's `expires` (defaults `COMPLETED_RUN_EXPIRY` 30d / `FAILED_RUN_EXPIRY` 90d), skips runs pinned `never` or still running (`loadRunningProcedures`), and trims beyond `MAX_RUNS_PER_PROCEDURE`, committing the deletions.

verdict.note: src/core/commands/procedure.ts registers the command named `procedure-gc` whose run() calls gcProcedureRuns(); src/cli/commands/procedure.ts wires `cb procedure gc` to that same command name. src/core/procedure/gc.ts groups run dirs under procedure/runs by procedure name, resolves each run card's `expires` (falling back to COMPLETED_RUN_EXPIRY 30d / FAILED_RUN_EXPIRY 90d from src/core/procedure/run-expiry.ts, and treating missing/unparseable cards as failure-like), keeps runs pinned `never`, the newest run per procedure, and anything in loadRunningProcedures(), then deletes expired dirs plus per-procedure overflow beyond MAX_RUNS_PER_PROCEDURE (100), committing via commitPaths when tracked files changed.

title: Get a box that already knows what it could do on a schedule, with the costly parts off
story: As an operator, I want a new box provisioned with a stock set of schedule cards — email and calendar pulls, map refresh, procedure-run GC, weekly retrospective, nightly chat review — where the ones that spend quota or edit prose ship disabled, so that automation is discoverable without anything expensive starting behind my back.
evidence: `DEFAULT_SCHEDULES` in `core/box/defaults.ts` declares each seeded schedule with an explicit `enabled` flag — `check-email`, `check-calendar`, `process-retrospective` and `chat-review` seeded `false`, `refresh-maps` and `gc-procedure-runs` `true` — and `installSchedules` writes them into `config/schedules/`; `cb init` calls it and reports the installed names.

verdict.note: core/box/defaults.ts DEFAULT_SCHEDULES declares exactly the six named seeds: check-email (cb wakeup --connector gmail, enabled:false), check-calendar (enabled:false), refresh-maps (enabled:true), gc-procedure-runs (enabled:true), process-retrospective (enabled:false, comment says opt-in because it can spend quota), chat-review (enabled:false, comment says it writes generated prose to git-tracked cards). installSchedules writes each as config/schedules/<name>.scheduled-script.card via installTemplateFile, passing enabled:false through when set, and returns the installed names. cli/commands/init.ts line 152 calls it and prints 'Installed N schedule(s) in config/schedules/ (map refresh and run cleanup enabled; other seeds disabled)' plus each name.

title: Get told when a scheduled task starts failing or goes overdue
story: As a boxholder, I want one proactive alert per unhealthy episode when a scheduled task fails, goes overdue, or won't parse, so that silent automation breakage doesn't go unnoticed for days.
evidence: The scheduler daemon calls `checkHealthAndAlert` after each box tick; it selects alertable tasks from `loadScheduleHealth`, fans out via `notifyBoxholder` with immediate delivery, and latches `alertedAt`/`alertedFor` in script state so a task failing for days alerts once.

verdict.note: src/core/schedule/scheduler.ts line 253 calls checkHealthAndAlert(boxPath, {now}) after each box tick and logs a health-alert box-log event. src/core/schedule/health-alert.ts loads loadScheduleHealth and selectAlertableTasks (health-box.ts: status failing with consecutiveFailures >= ALERT_AFTER_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES=2, or invalid, or overdue — covering fail/overdue/won't-parse), filters to tasks with alertedAt === null, sends one aggregated message through notifyBoxholder with deliver: true and severity 'alert', then latches alertedAt/alertedFor per task via saveScriptState (state.ts fields at lines 50-51; recordOutcome clears them at lines 216-217 on success), so a task failing for days alerts once per episode. Requires a reachable channel — notifyChannels returns early unless healthAlerts.telegramChat or a push subscription exists — which is the ordinary opt-in for notifications, not a blocking gate.

title: Hand each job to the agent with its content already loaded
story: As the boxholder, I want every job card in a reactor prompt rendered with its referenced cards inlined and its job type's schema instructions attached, so that the agent works the job in one pass instead of spending turns hunting for context.
evidence: `buildJobDescription` parses the job card with the real schema map, walks `collectInlineRefs` to append each inline-safe ref's file contents (skipping opaque-content refs), appends `#### Instructions for <type>` from `schema.instructions`, and wraps every embedded blob in `fenceForPrompt`; refs that escape the box are dropped with a warning and an unparseable job is shown raw rather than crashing the batch.

verdict.note: core/reactor/batch-jobs.ts buildJobDescription (called for each job from processBatchJobs, which cycle.ts:259 invokes) parses the job with createCardSchemaMap/parseCardText, iterates collectInlineRefs(parsed.schema.frontmatterSchema, parsed.fields) appending `#### <ref>` plus the file contents read via readContainedFile, and then appends `#### Instructions for <type>` from parsed.schema.instructions. All embedded content passes through fenceForPrompt; refs failing resolveBoxRelativeRef or RefEscapesBoxError are omitted with a console.warn, and a CardIOError yields a flagged raw-content block instead of throwing. prompts.ts's buildReactorUserPrompt receives those jobDescriptions and tells the agent the content is already loaded.

title: Hand triaged items to their category's handler
story: As a person whose box files things by category, I want each triaged bucket handed to the procedure its landmark declares, so that categorized items get processed the way that category is supposed to be processed.
evidence: For each `inbox/triaged/<category>/` bucket, core/handle.ts finds the landmark defining the category, reads its matching `destinations:` entry's `procedure` ref, and invokes that procedure card with the bucket passed as null-delimited paths in TRIAGE_ITEMS; `cb handle [category]` is the entry point.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/handle.ts runHandle() lists inbox/triaged/<category>/ buckets (skipping _unsure and dotdirs), matches each to a TriageCategory from compileTriageInstructions (src/core/triage/instructions.ts, which reads the landmark's findDestination(destinations,'triage').procedure.ref via src/core/landmark/destination.ts), resolves that ref with resolveRefPath, and calls the procedure engine with TRIAGE_ITEMS set to null-delimited box-relative item paths (liveRunProcedure joins with \0). Entry point exists: src/core/commands/handle.ts registers command 'handle' with an optional [category] arg, and src/cli/commands/handle.ts wires `cb handle [category]`, added in src/cli/index.ts line 145.

title: Have a model judge whether an automated step actually did what it was for
story: As the box's agent, I want a procedure step's `validate` phase to hand its natural-language success criteria, the step's `whys`, and the step's git diff to a review model for a pass/fail verdict, so that an unattended step is checked against intent and not just against an exit code.
evidence: `evaluateInstructions` assembles the validate phase's `instructions:`, the step's `whys:` and its `baseline..finalRef` diff and asks a sonnet-default judge (`REVIEW_MAX_TURNS` 8) for the `InstructionVerdict` `{passed, reasoning}` zod shape; `executePhaseShells`/`runAndValidate` call it as part of the step's validate phase, and the resulting `ValidateStatus` plus the step's `severity` decide whether the run continues.

verdict.note: engine-validate-model.ts evaluateInstructions() builds buildJudgePrompt({instructions, whys, diff}) and calls agent.invokeStructured(InstructionVerdict = z.object({passed, reasoning})) with model MODEL_MAP[model ?? 'sonnet'] and maxTurns REVIEW_MAX_TURNS = 8, failing closed (passed:false) when no verdict parses. engine-phase.ts executeValidation() runs the validate phase's shells, then when phase.instructions.length > 0 computes getRangeDiff(`${baseline}..${gitRef}`) and calls evaluateInstructions with phase.whys, mapping !passed to failStatus(severity). engine-run-phase.ts runAndValidate() invokes it and applies severity 'review' self-heal retries; engine-step.ts recordStepResults() fails the step on status 'fail' with severity 'abort' or exhausted review retries. Reachable via `cb procedure` (src/core/commands/procedure.ts:80) and core/handle.ts. The only wording slack: `whys` are read off the validate phase, which is where the step declares them.

title: Have automation stand down while the box is in use
story: As a boxholder, I want a tick to defer whenever a script, procedure, or chat session is already in flight, so that scheduled work never collides with — or commits over — what I am doing right now.
evidence: `runTick` calls `findBusyBlockers` (running script locks, `loadRunningProcedures`, `loadActiveChats`) and returns with everything skipped when any blocker is present; `effectiveBusyBlockers` drops only chat blockers under `--force`. `handlePostSuccess` re-reads `loadActiveChats` inside `withBoxGitLock` right before its `stageAll`/`commit`, deferring the housekeeping commit rather than sweeping a chat agent's half-written files.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/tick.ts runTick calls effectiveBusyBlockers(await findBusyBlockers(boxRoot, running), {force}) and, when blockers exist, prints 'Tick deferred — system busy: ...' and returns {ranCount:0, skipCount: files.length}. findBusyBlockers in tick-helpers.ts combines running script locks, loadRunningProcedures, and loadActiveChats (core/schedule/state.ts, chat lock scan / procedure/runs mtime scan); effectiveBusyBlockers filters out only 'chat:' blockers under --force. handlePostSuccess re-reads loadActiveChats inside withBoxGitLock right before stageAll/commit and skips the housekeeping commit ('changes stay uncommitted until the next at-rest tick') when a chat is active. All three cited files implement exactly what the evidence claims.

title: Have last night's long chats titled and summarized for me
story: As a boxholder, I want a nightly pass that finds chat sessions which have gone quiet and accumulated enough new material, and writes a title and a `contains` summary back onto each chat's card, so that past conversations are findable without me naming them.
evidence: `cb chat review status|run` discovers sessions via `discoverSessions` (30m `QUIESCENCE_MS`, `REVIEW_CHAR_THRESHOLD`, prior review state) and `runChatReview` reads each unread span and writes `title`/`contains`/`contains-evidence` onto the husk card, capped at `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS` (20) per run and held by a lock; the seeded `chat-review` schedule runs it at 4am.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/chat-review.ts registers `status` and `run` subcommands; `discover()` calls discoverSessions() from core/chat/review/discovery.ts with QUIESCENCE_MS = 30*60*1000 and REVIEW_CHAR_THRESHOLD = 6000 (plus REVIEW_MIN_USER_TURNS) and prior state from state.ts, and `run` calls runChatReview() (run.ts) under withChatReviewLock, default --max-sessions 20. husk-write.ts applyReviewToHusk() writes `title` (only when the pass still owns it, via resolveTitleOwner), `contains`, `contains-evidence` and `review-span` onto the husk card. Caveat, not a refutation: the seeded schedule in src/core/box/defaults.ts (cron "0 4 * * *", runs `cb chat review run`) ships with enabled:false — opt-in per box — so the nightly cadence requires the boxholder to enable it; the pass itself is fully reachable via the CLI.

title: Have optional background work wait for a quiet moment without waiting forever
story: As a boxholder, I want low-priority jobs to ride along with real work rather than spending an agent turn on their own — but to earn their own cycle, a bounded batch at a time, once they've waited a day — so that filler work neither burns quota nor gets stranded forever.
evidence: `discoverStage` skips a cycle when `skipLowPriority` is set (which `cb wakeup` always sets) and no normal-priority job exists — except for jobs past `LOW_PRIORITY_MAX_WAIT_MS` (24h), of which it admits `OVERDUE_LOW_PRIORITY_PER_CYCLE` (5); `findJobCards` sorts normal-before-low and oldest-first so the admitted batch is FIFO and a backlog tail isn't starved.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/reactor/cycle.ts discoverStage(): when skipLowPriority is set and no job has priority "normal", it returns {kind:"skipped"} unless jobs are past LOW_PRIORITY_MAX_WAIT_MS (24h), in which case it selects overdue.slice(0, OVERDUE_LOW_PRIORITY_PER_CYCLE=5). skipLowPriority is passed true unconditionally by src/cli/commands/wakeup.ts:129 (and optionally by cli/commands/reactor.ts). When a normal job exists, selected stays the full jobCards list, so low-priority work rides along. src/core/reactor/job-discovery.ts findJobCards() parses `priority: low` from frontmatter and sorts normal-before-low then oldest-first by createdAt, making the admitted overdue batch FIFO.

title: Have scanned documents processed without asking for it
story: As a boxholder feeding a scanner, I want an upload to schedule a full box wakeup after a settle window — one wakeup per scanning session, retried until it succeeds — so that scanned pages get imported and filed on their own rather than waiting for the next scheduled tick.
evidence: The scan PUT route calls `notifyScanUpload`, which (re)starts the `SCAN_SETTLE_MS` debouncer so a ten-page session yields one pass; `runScanPromotePass` runs the owed wakeup through `promote-wakeup.ts`, which writes a durable `wakeup-pending` marker and clears it only on success, and `runPass` re-arms the settle window whenever the pass was locked, failed, or its wakeup failed. A slow 6-hour sweep covers a box that stops scanning.

verdict.note: scan-upload.ts:215 calls notifyScanUpload(boxRoot) after every accepted or rejected PUT; scan-promote-lifecycle.ts's createPromoteDebouncer (promote-debounce.ts, SCAN_SETTLE_MS = 2 min, awake-time timer) re-arms so a multi-page session yields one pass. runScanPromotePass (promote.ts:174) calls markWakeupPending before the batch and runPendingWakeup (promote-wakeup.ts) after, which runs cb wakeup via runCbWakeup and deletes the 'wakeup-pending' marker only on ok, keeping it for retry otherwise. runPass re-arms the debouncer when skipped==='locked' || failed>0 || wakeup==='failed', and scheduleScanSweep runs a 6-hour GC/retry sweep. Routes registered per box from server-box-scope.ts:309.

title: Have the box notice work nobody queued and work that can no longer run
story: As a boxholder, I want each wakeup to queue intake jobs for inbox items that have no job card and delete job cards whose referenced files are gone, so that nothing that landed in the box is forgotten and the queue doesn't fill with work that can never complete.
evidence: `createIntakeJobsForUnjobbed` diffs inbox items against `collectExistingJobRefs` and batches the remainder into intake jobs (captures/images/audio at `priority: low`, tagged `source: wakeup`/`wakeup-captures`, or the connector name under a scoped wakeup); `cleanupStaleJobs` deletes pending `.job.card`s whose non-URL refs no longer resolve and commits the removal with an error-indicating message.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/wakeup-steps.ts:200 createIntakeJobsForUnjobbed builds existingRefs via collectExistingJobRefs (line 273, reading refs from every *job.card frontmatter in box/jobs), passes them to findUnjobbedInboxItems, then batches the remainder through createBatchedIntakeJobs with priority "low" for capture-session/image/audio cards and "normal" otherwise, sourced "wakeup"/"wakeup-captures" or the connector name under a scoped wakeup, committing the new job paths. cleanupStaleJobs (line 90) reads each .job.card, treats missing status as "pending", filters out http(s) refs, and when every remaining ref fails fs.access (escaping/symlink-escaping refs count as missing) unlinks the card and commits with Phase: stale-job-cleanup. Both run unconditionally in src/cli/commands/wakeup.ts steps 4a (line 212) and 4b (line 222) of `cb wakeup`.

title: Health of scheduled tasks
story: As a boxholder, I want each scheduled task classified as ok, failing, overdue, blocked, waiting, invalid or disabled alongside the scheduler's heartbeat, so that a task that quietly stopped running is visible instead of silently missing.
evidence: `evaluateTaskHealth` (core/schedule/health.ts) derives status from lastRun/lastSuccess divergence and unserved cron/rrule occurrences; `loadScheduleHealth` + `checkSchedulerHeartbeat` (health-box.ts) add the daemon heartbeat and the engine-quota `engineWait` phrase; `cb health` and the chat session snapshot (session-context.ts, `summarizeScheduleHealth`) both print it.

verdict.note: core/schedule/health.ts defines TaskHealthStatus as exactly ok|waiting|failing|overdue|blocked|invalid|disabled, and evaluateTaskHealth derives it from parsed.enabled/until, engineWaitReason, consecutiveFailures (lastRun vs lastSuccess), missing connectors/budget, and unserved cron/rrule occurrences. loadScheduleHealth in health-box.ts iterates config/schedules/*.scheduled-script.card, marks unparseable cards 'invalid', and bundles checkSchedulerHeartbeat (running/stale/never, from a heartbeat file) plus the box-level engineWait phrase from engine-wait.ts engineWaitReason(). Both surfaces cited exist: cli/commands/health.ts healthCommand (registered in src/cli/index.ts:122) prints per-task status plus 'scheduler:' and 'engine:' lines, and core/session-context.ts:249 calls summarizeScheduleHealth(loadScheduleHealth(...)) into the chat session snapshot.

title: Hear in chat that a scheduled task is failing
story: As a boxholder, I want the chat agent to be told — rarely, not every turn — that a scheduled task is failing or overdue, so that broken automation surfaces in the conversation I'm already having instead of only on a page I have to visit.
evidence: `buildSnapshotContext` summarizes `loadScheduleHealth` into the per-send `<chat-app>` snapshot, gated by `admitHealth`: a fresh per-session `HealthGate` (`createHealthGate`, one per `ChatSession`) admits the first failure, then a changed message only after `HEALTH_CHANGED_MIN_TURNS` (10) sends and the same message only after `HEALTH_REPEAT_MS` (10 days).

verdict.note: src/core/session-context.ts defines HealthGate/createHealthGate and admitHealth with HEALTH_REPEAT_MS = 10 days and HEALTH_CHANGED_MIN_TURNS = 10; buildSnapshotContext calls summarizeScheduleHealth(await loadScheduleHealth(boxRoot, now)) on every send and only sets out.health when admitHealth returns true (first failure of a session, a changed message after 10 turns, or a re-nudge after 10 days). src/core/chat/session/index.ts holds `private readonly healthGate = createHealthGate()` per ChatSession and passes it at line 334 into the send path (start.ts -> composeSendSnapshot), so the string rides the per-send <chat-app> snapshot the agent sees. summarizeScheduleHealth in src/core/schedule/health-box.ts builds that string from tasks whose status is failing/invalid/overdue (overdue only when the scheduler is running), plus stale-scheduler and engine-wait lines — i.e. failing or overdue automation, matching the story.

title: Keep a box running so its pending timers fire
story: As an operator, I want the hub to pre-start and refuse to idle-stop any box that holds an unfired chat schedule, so that a lazily-managed box still fires reminders on time.
evidence: `boxHasPendingSchedules` reuses `loadChatSchedules` (counting overdue-unfired entries); the supervisor calls it at boot to `prestartBox` and again in the idle-timer decision to keep such a box up.

verdict.note: hub/pending-schedules.ts boxHasPendingSchedules resolves the hub entry path via resolveBoxRoot and returns loadChatSchedules({boxRoot}).length > 0; core/chat/schedules.ts loadChatSchedules returns ALL surviving entries including overdue-unfired (getActive's future-only filter deliberately unused). hub/supervisor.ts prestartLazy() runs a schedule pass at boot independent of keepRecent, calling prestartBox for any non-running box with pending schedules, and evaluateIdle() returns 'kept-schedule' and re-arms the idle timer instead of stopping such a box.

title: Keep open todos in front of the agent
story: As the boxholder, I want the count of todos on the plate prepended to every reactor prompt when it is non-zero, so that the agent working a job knows there is outstanding work and how to list it.
evidence: Both `processBatchJobs` and `processChatJobs` call `computeTodoAmbientLine(boxRoot)` and prefix the user prompt with its `N open todos on the plate (M escalated) — \`cb todos\`` line; the helper returns `null` when nothing is on the plate, in which case no line is added.

verdict.note: core/todo/ambient-summary.ts computeTodoAmbientLine collects todos, filters plateState escalated/on-plate, returns null when none, else 'N open todos on the plate (M escalated) — `cb todos`'. processBatchJobs (core/reactor/batch-jobs.ts:42) awaits it and passes ambientLine into buildReactorUserPrompt (reactor/prompts.ts:37-42), which prefixes the prompt with it when non-null; processChatJobs (chat-jobs.ts:50-52) builds ambientBlock the same way and prepends it to 'Please process this job:'. Both reactor prompt paths therefore carry the line only when the plate is non-empty.

title: Keep two scheduled tasks that touch the same thing from overlapping
story: As someone authoring the box's automation, I want to put two schedules in a named lock group so one is skipped while the other is running, so that tasks that walk the same transcripts or edit the same cards never run on top of each other.
evidence: `lock-group` is a scheduled-script frontmatter field; `acquireScriptLock` writes it into the lock metadata, and `evaluateSkip` in tick-helpers.ts skips a due script when another running lock carries the same `lockGroup` (`checkTriggerPreconditions` throws CONFLICT for the dashboard's run-now path). The shipped `process-retrospective` and `chat-review` schedules in core/box/defaults.ts both declare `lockGroup: "retro"`.

verdict.note: src/schemas/scheduled-script.tsx:64 defines the `lock-group` frontmatter field (documented at line 88 as a named concurrency group), parsed into parsed.lockGroup at line 187. tick-helpers.ts evaluateSkip (line 154) skips a due script when any other running lock has the same lockGroup, and acquireScriptLock (line 265, implemented in core/schedule/state.ts:247-283) writes lockGroup into the lock metadata that loadRunningScripts reads back. The dashboard run-now path checkTriggerPreconditions in webapp/trpc/routers/scheduler-run.ts:51-60 throws TRPCError CONFLICT on the same condition. core/box/defaults.ts seeds process-retrospective (line 283) and chat-review (line 299) both with lockGroup: "retro".

title: Landmarks as filing destinations
story: As a box agent, I want landmarks to advertise which kinds of filing they accept (triage, commentary, share), so that routing an item has a declared destination instead of a guess.
evidence: destination.ts defines DESTINATION_KINDS (triage/commentary/share) and findDestination over a landmark's `destinations` list; listDestinations() enumerates them box-wide for the filing pickers; core/handle.ts reads the matching entry's `procedure` ref to run the handler.

verdict.note: core/landmark/destination.ts defines DESTINATION_KINDS = ['triage','commentary','share'] and findDestination(destinations, kind) over the landmark card's `destinations` array (schemas/landmark.ts:122, LandmarkDestination with a `for` list). core/landmark/list-destinations.ts globs **/*.landmark.card and enumerates matching destinations box-wide; it is reached from webapp/trpc/routers/share.ts (kind 'share') and clerk.ts (kind 'commentary'). Triage routing uses the same data: core/triage/instructions.ts:90 pulls the 'triage' destination's rules and procedure.ref into TriageCategory, and core/handle.ts resolves category.procedureRef to a .procedure.card and runs it with TRIAGE_ITEMS.

title: Let a failing step fix itself before it gates
story: As a procedure author, I want a step whose validation is `severity: review` to re-run its agent once with the failure detail and the step's whys, so that a near-miss heals itself instead of failing the whole procedure.
evidence: `runAndValidate` in engine-run-phase.ts, on a `fail` verdict with `severity: review`, builds a `<validation-failure>` prompt via `buildFailureContext` (detail + `whys:`), resumes the run agent's session through `runRunAgents({retry})` under `REVIEW_RETRY_BUDGET_USD = 2` for `MAX_REVIEW_RETRIES` attempts, re-validates, and only then reports `reviewExhausted`. Run shells are never repeated on a retry.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/procedure/engine-run-phase.ts: runAndValidate validates after the run phase; when validateResult.status === 'fail' and step.validate.severity === 'review' (severity parsed in engine-parse.ts line 78, enum includes 'review' per engine-types.ts), it loops while attempt < MAX_REVIEW_RETRIES (=1), builds buildFailureContext() which emits a <validation-failure> block with the failure detail plus the step's whys ('Why this matters:'), and calls runRunAgents({...params, retry:{sessionId, failureContext}}) which resumes the same session with maxBudgetUsd = REVIEW_RETRY_BUDGET_USD (2), then re-validates. runRunShells is called only once before the loop, so run shells never repeat. If it still fails, reviewExhausted is returned and engine-step.ts gates the step.

title: Let the browser extension act on my tabs
story: As a person with the callback-clerk extension installed, I want the page to advertise which box the tab belongs to and to relay tab-arrangement requests to the extension, so that my box agent can organize my open tabs.
evidence: useBoxIdentityMeta writes <meta name="callback-box"> carrying {slug, title, boxUrl} for the extension to read from the active tab; requestTabArrangement() postMessages to the callback-clerk-relay content script and resolves a validated {ok, state: ready|applied|partial, undoAvailable} result under 4s status / 60s mutation timeouts.

verdict.note: useBoxIdentityMeta (frontend/src/hooks/useBoxIdentityMeta.ts) creates/updates <meta name="callback-box"> whose content is JSON.stringify({slug, title, boxUrl}) with boxUrl = origin + BASE_URL + slug; it is called from app-shell.tsx:68 for the active box, so every box page advertises identity. lib/tab-arrangement-relay.ts requestTabArrangement() postMessages {source:'callback-box-app', type:'tab-arrangement-status|apply|undo-request', correlationId, transferId, proposal} to same-origin window, listens for responses from source 'callback-clerk-relay', validates via parseResult into {ok, state: ready|applied|partial, message, undoAvailable}, and times out at STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS=4000 / MUTATION_TIMEOUT_MS=60000. It is reachable: components/TabArrangementView.tsx calls status on mount and apply/undo from buttons, and is registered as the 'Organizer' renderer in renderers/tab-arrangement.tsx.

title: List procedures and inspect a run
story: As the box agent or an operator, I want to list the box's procedure definitions and show the status of a run (the latest one by default), so that I can see what is runnable and what a run did without reading its card by hand.
evidence: `procedure-list` calls `listProcedures`, which reads `config/procedures/*.procedure.card`; `procedure-status` calls `procedureStatus(ctx, runDir)`, which resolves the run dir (latest by name sort) and parses its run card with `parseProcedureRun`.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/commands/procedure.ts registers `procedure-list` (execute -> listProcedures(ctx)) and `procedure-status` with an optional `runDir` arg defaulting to latest (execute -> procedureStatus(ctx, runDir)). In src/core/procedure/engine-query.ts, listProcedures reads ctx.boxRoot + 'config/procedures' and filters '*.procedure.card'; procedureStatus calls resolveRunDir, which with no arg reads 'procedure/runs', sorts and takes the last name (latest), then reads 'run.procedure-run.card' and parseProcedureRun, printing status, started/completed and per-step icons. Reachable: src/core/commands/index.ts imports './procedure.js', and src/cli/commands/procedure.ts exposes the same `procedure-list`/`procedure-status` names on the CLI.

title: Needs-attention cards
story: As a boxholder, I want pending questions and a waiting-inbox count called out at the top of the dashboard, so that the things asking for me are the first thing I see.
evidence: AttentionCards filters status.questions to `pending`, links the first five to /$boxSlug/card/<path>, shows the inbox count from status.counts.inbox with a Browse link to box/inbox, and renders nothing when both are zero.

verdict.note: components/dashboard/AttentionCards.tsx filters the passed questions to status === 'pending', renders the first five as Links to `/${boxSlug}/card/${q.relativePath}` with a '+N more' line, shows the inbox count with a Browse link to `/${boxSlug}/browse/box/inbox`, and returns null when pendingQuestions.length === 0 && inboxCount === 0. pages/DashboardPage.tsx:113 mounts it with questions from trpc.status.questions and inboxCount={status?.counts.inbox ?? 0}, high in the dashboard column (after OpsLinks/HealthWarnings, above ScheduleOverview and RecentActivity). The section carries aria-label='Needs attention'.

browser.note: 'Needs attention' section shows 'Questions 39' with the first five pending questions linking to /user-stories-refresh/test1/card/box/questions/<name>.question.card and a '+34 more' trailer, plus 'Inbox 136' with '136 items waiting' and a 'Browse →' link. It sits below the Box-tools/inventory row and Box warnings rather than literally at the very top.

title: Never lose an agent's work to a forgotten commit
story: As the boxholder, I want anything an agent leaves uncommitted after a procedure step or a reactor job committed automatically with provenance trailers, so that box history records who changed what even when the agent skips its own commit.
evidence: `ensureGitClean` (engine-phase.ts) reads `getStatus` inside `withBoxGitLock` and, when dirty, stages everything and commits `[procedure] <stepId>: <summary>` with `Procedure`/`Step`/`Session`/`Commit-Source: procedure-fallback` trailers, returning the ref used as the step's diff range; the reactor's `processBatchJobs`/`processChatJobs` call `captureBaseline` then `ensureAgentCommitted` with `fallbackMessage: "Reactor: … (fallback commit)"` and `Phase: reactor`.

verdict.note: engine-phase.ts `ensureGitClean` runs inside `withBoxGitLock`, reads `getStatus`, and when dirty does `stageAll` + `commit` with message `[procedure] ${stepId}: ${summary}` and trailers Procedure/Step/Commit-Source: procedure-fallback (Session added when sessionId is present), returning the commit ref; it is called at three points in engine-run-phase.ts (lines 244/260/326) and its return is used as the step's git ref. reactor/batch-jobs.ts:58-74 and reactor/chat-jobs.ts:69-84 call `captureBaseline` before `agent.invoke` and then `ensureAgentCommitted` with fallbackMessage "Reactor: agent work (fallback commit)" / "Reactor: chat agent work (fallback commit)" and fallbackTrailers { Phase: "reactor" }; agent/commit.ts first nudges the agent to commit itself and only then stages+commits with `Fallback: true` added to the trailers. Story matches.

title: Not be told automation is broken when the model engine is just out of quota
story: As a boxholder, I want a due schedule that can't run because the agent engine is unavailable to be recorded as deferred and stay due, so that a quota outage doesn't burn attempts, reset my failure counts, or fire a false 'your automation is failing' alert.
evidence: `evaluateSkip` consults `boxEngineUnavailability(boxRoot)` and skips with `engineWaitReason` while leaving `lastRun` untouched; a failure during a run goes through `classifyScheduleFailure`, which can return `result: "deferred"` — and `recordOutcome`/`ScriptState` deliberately neither increment nor reset `consecutiveFailures` for it, while `TaskHealthStatus` reports the task as `waiting` rather than `failing`.

verdict.note: tick-helpers.ts evaluateSkip() calls boxEngineUnavailability(boxRoot) before the requires/budget gates and returns a skip reason from engineWaitReason() without touching state.lastRun, so the script stays due (comment and code agree; --force bypasses). classifyScheduleFailure() in core/schedule/engine-wait.ts returns result:'deferred' when a live unavailability record was detected during the run's span, and state.ts recordOutcome() increments consecutiveFailures only for 'failure' and resets only on 'success', leaving it frozen for 'deferred' (lastResult schema includes 'deferred'). health.ts evaluateTaskHealth() returns status 'waiting' with the engineWaitReason before any failing/overdue/blocked branch, and health-box.ts selectAlertableTasks() only alerts on failing/invalid/overdue, so health-alert.ts sends nothing for a waiting task.

title: On-plate todo badge in the nav
story: As a boxholder, I want the app nav to badge how many todos are on my plate right now, so that escalated work is visible from any page.
evidence: `countOnPlateTodos` (core/todo/count.ts) is a bounded-parallelism fast path over the same collector machinery that skips cards whose text cannot name a todo; core/nav-counts.ts imports it for the nav counts AppNav.tsx renders.

verdict.note: src/core/todo/count.ts `countOnPlateTodos` reads all `**/*.card` with mapInBatches (READ_CONCURRENCY 64), skips cards failing `mayHaveTodo`, runs `collectCardTodos` and returns the count of plateState escalated|on-plate. src/core/nav-counts.ts `getNavCounts` calls it alongside countPendingQuestions; src/webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts exposes it (`{counts: await getNavCounts(ctx.boxRoot)}`), and AppNav.tsx:105/140 reads `statusQuery.data.counts.onPlateTodos` and renders `<PlateBadge>` linking to store/plate.todo-view.card. AppNav mounts on every page, so the badge is present app-wide.

browser.note: No on-plate todo badge exists in the app nav. The nav bar renders only the Place chip and the avatar; nothing in the nav markup carries a todo count on any page I visited (dashboard, card view).

triage.reasoning: The browser check failed on missing data, not on missing code. `PlateBadge` (callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/AppNav.tsx:165) opens with `if (count === 0) return null;` — zero renders nothing by design — and the test box has zero on-plate todos. Ran `getNavCounts` (core/nav-counts.ts) directly against `~/src/box-worktrees/user-stories-refresh/test1/content`: `{ pendingQuestions: 38, onPlateTodos: 0 }`; only three cards in the box even contain the string 'todo' and none carry a todo. Added one temporary memo card with a frontmatter `todos:` entry, re-ran the count (`onPlateTodos: 1`), reloaded `/dashboard`, and the nav rendered the badge: nav text 'test1 > Dashboard 1' with a link `aria-label="1 todo on the plate"` pointing at `/browse/store/plate.todo-view.card`. Removed the probe card afterwards. AppNav mounts on every page via app-shell.tsx, and status.navStatus supplies the count, so the story is accurate as written. (Unrelated but worth noting from the same browser pass: the dashboard reporter also expected a pending-questions badge; that one really was removed — AppNav's own comment says the question events 'moved out with the questions badge' — but this story only claims todos.)

title: Pending questions chase themselves
story: As a person using the box, I want to be notified when the box has a new question waiting for me, nudged once if it goes unanswered, and have it expire rather than linger forever, so that open questions neither get lost nor pile up.
evidence: `cb finalize` calls checkPendingQuestionsAndNotify (diffing pending questions against a per-box latch so each notifies once) and the aging sweep in question-aging.ts, which computes age from the durable `asked-at` field to nudge once and then expire.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/finalize.ts (lines 34 and 44) calls checkPendingQuestionsAndNotify then ageQuestions on every `cb finalize`. question-alert.ts diffs generateContext's pendingQuestions against the per-box latch at .callback-box/notified-questions.json and calls notifyBoxholder (push/Telegram fan-out) once per newly-pending question, rewriting `paths` to the current pending set so answered ones drop out. question-aging.ts computes ageMs from the durable `asked-at` field, sends exactly one nudge (dedup via latch.nudged) at DEFAULT_NUDGE_AFTER_MS (7d) or half an `expires-after` override, and flips the card to status `expired` past DEFAULT_EXPIRE_AFTER_MS (30d) via withQuestionTransition. Notify, nudge-once, expire all present as described.

browser.note: Notification, nudge and expiry run in `cb finalize` / the aging sweep, not in the page. The questions page shows no age, nudge or expiry affordance and no question here is in an expired state, and the box has all schedules disabled — verifying would need triggering an agent/finalize run, which is out of bounds here.

title: Pick the model and turn budget for a procedure step
story: As a procedure author, I want to name the model and max-turns for a step's agent and for its model validation judge, so that cheap steps run on a cheap model and no single step can run away with turns.
evidence: `toPhase` in engine-parse.ts reads each agent's `model` and `max-turns` into `ParsedPhase.agents`; `runRunAgents` resolves them through `MODEL_MAP` and defaults `maxTurns` to 20; `evaluateInstructions` resolves the validate phase's `model` the same way, defaulting to sonnet with `REVIEW_MAX_TURNS`.

verdict.note: engine-parse.ts `toPhase` copies each agent's `model` and `max-turns` into ParsedPhase.agents (lines 50-60), and `toParsedStep` carries `step.validate.model` onto the parsed validate phase. engine-run-phase.ts sets `maxTurns: agentDef.maxTurns ?? 20` and `invokeOpts.model = MODEL_MAP[agentDef.model] ?? agentDef.model` for both agent invocation paths (lines ~103-147). engine-validate-model.ts `evaluateInstructions` resolves `MODEL_MAP[params.model ?? DEFAULT_REVIEW_MODEL] ?? MODEL_ID.sonnet` with `maxTurns: REVIEW_MAX_TURNS` (=8), and is called from engine-phase.ts:121. The authoring surface is real: schemas/procedure.ts:25 declares `max-turns` on the agent object and its instructions document `{ prompt, model?, max-turns? }`.

title: Query todos across the box
story: As the box's agent, I want `cb todos` to collect every `{% todo %}` tag and frontmatter `todos:` entry across the box with filters for status, assignee, glob and on-plate, so that I can answer what's outstanding without hunting through cards.
evidence: `todosCommand` (cli/commands/todos.ts) calls `collectTodos` (core/todo/collect.ts), which globs every card, merges the body-tag walker (collect-body.ts) with frontmatter `todos:` entries, derives each todo's plate-state, and reports unreadable/duplicate-id cards as visible `issues` — printed as a listing or `--json`.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/todos.ts defines todosCommand with --status/--assigned/--glob/--on-plate/--json, registered at src/cli/index.ts:150. runTodosForBox validates status via isTodoStatus, calls collectTodos(boxRoot, {glob}) from src/core/todo/collect.ts, filters with matchesFilters (status, assigned exact match, plateState escalated|on-plate for --on-plate), then prints grouped by plate-state or emits {todos, issues} JSON. collect.ts globs every card (listTodoCardPaths with an absolute/`..` guard), merges collectBodyTodos (collect-body.ts, {% todo %} tag spans) with Zod-validated frontmatter `todos:` entries, derives plate state via deriveTodoPlateState, and reports load/parse failures and duplicate ids as TodoCollectionIssue (collect-types.ts).

title: Question archive and invalid cards
story: As a boxholder, I want answered questions shown with the answer I gave, dismissed/expired ones still answerable in an archive, and unparseable question cards named with a link to the raw file, so that no question silently disappears.
evidence: QuestionsList buckets items into invalid/pending/answered/demoted, renders demoted ones with a live QuestionForm, and links `invalid: true` cards to /$boxSlug/browse/<path>; answer-display renders a confirm question's decision plus any note.

verdict.note: components/questions/QuestionsList.tsx filters trpc.status.questions items into invalid (q.invalid===true), pending, answered, and demoted (status dismissed|expired); answeredCard renders renderQuestionAnswer plus a StatusBadge, demotedCard renders a live <QuestionForm> under an Archive heading so dismissed/expired remain answerable, and invalidCard renders the card's relativePath as a <Link to={href(`/${boxSlug}/browse/${q.relativePath}`)}> under an 'Invalid' heading. answer-display.tsx renderQuestionAnswer special-cases inputType 'confirm', showing the Yes/No decision from answer.selected and appending answer.text as a note when it differs. Reachable via pages/QuestionsPage.tsx and the `questions` view renderer in renderers/view.tsx.

browser.note: All three clauses seen. Answered: the archive entry shows the prompt with my recorded answer 'trash' and an 'answered' badge. Dismissed: archived under a 'dismissed' badge with a working QuestionForm still attached, which I used to answer it. Invalid: I planted a malformed zz-broken-probe.question.card and the page grew an INVALID section reading 'Invalid question card' with a link to http://localhost:3210/user-stories-refresh/test1/browse/box/questions/zz-broken-probe.question.card (probe file since removed).

title: Queue background work as system job cards
story: As the box's machinery, I want intake-job, chat-job, contains-backfill-job, todo-review-job and question-followup-job card types carrying a description and refs to their subject, so that connectors and wakeup can queue agent work as ordinary cards the reactor picks up.
evidence: Each is a cardSchema with category:"system", searchable:false and a description field plus a create*Template() helper — e.g. IntakeJobSchema ("triage newly arrived inbox items; created by connectors and cb wakeup") and ContainsBackfillJobSchema, which generates its description from the count of cards missing contains:.

verdict.note: All five files exist under callback-box/src/schemas/ and each declares cardSchema(..., {category: "system", searchable: false}) with a `description` string field and a create*Template() helper: IntakeJobSchema (description "A system job to triage newly arrived inbox items; created by connectors and cb wakeup", fields source/priority/items: array(cardRef())) + createIntakeJobTemplate; ChatJobSchema (thread: cardRef()) + createChatJobTemplate; ContainsBackfillJobSchema (items: array(cardRef()), priority default "low") whose createContainsBackfillJobTemplate builds the description from the batch count plus a remaining count; TodoReviewJobSchema + createTodoReviewJobTemplate; QuestionFollowupJobSchema (question-ref: cardRef(), directive, answer) + createQuestionFollowupJobTemplate. Reactor pickup is real: core/reactor/cycle.ts runs these pending job cards and each schema's instructions end in `cb finish {thisJobFile}`; job priority is read in job-discovery.ts. Only slack: todo-review-job carries `locator` strings rather than cardRefs for its items, which is a minor wording gap, not an over-claim about the capability.

title: Read the tick log to see what ran and what failed
story: As a boxholder, I want a recent-activity view of scheduler ticks and commits, and a CLI listing of every schedule's last result, so that I can audit what the box did unattended.
evidence: `scheduler.log` streams and validates `.callback-box/scheduler.jsonl` lines with optional event/status filters into `RecentActivity`; `cb scheduled` prints each script's cadence, last-run age, duration and error, and `cb scheduler log` renders entries across boxes.

verdict.note: trpc/routers/scheduler.ts exposes a `log` query that streams and Zod-validates `.callback-box/scheduler.jsonl` (boxLogFile from core/schedule/scheduler.ts, SCHEDULER_LOG_FILENAME) with optional `event`/`status` filters; DashboardPage.tsx calls trpc.scheduler.log.useQuery({limit:20,event:'tick'}) and feeds the result into both ScheduleOverview and RecentActivity, which interleaves git commits (status.activity) with scheduler ticks. On the CLI, src/cli/commands/scheduled.ts (registered in cli/index.ts as `cb scheduled`) prints each schedule's cadence via describeCadence plus 'last: Nm ago (ran/error, X.Xs)' from loadScriptState, and `cb scheduler log` (scheduler.ts subcommand using resolveLogBoxes/readBoxEntries/renderLogEntry from scheduler-helpers.ts) renders entries across all configured boxes.

browser.note: The Recent Activity view exists and renders the commit half of the audit trail, but the tick half is unverifiable on this box: scheduler.log has no entries (every schedule's Last Run is 'never'), so no tick rows, statuses or failures appeared. The CLI half of the story was out of scope for a browser check.

title: Resurface todos that have gone due, started, or gone stale
story: As a boxholder, I want a wakeup sweep that finds escalated, newly-started and long-stale todos and queues a review job for the agent to raise with me, so that dated todos come back to my attention on their own.
evidence: `runTodoReviewSweep`, called from wakeup housekeeping, collects todos and computes escalated/stirring/stale sets against a persisted box-local-date baseline, then writes a `todo-review-job` card (skipped when one is already pending) that the same wakeup's reactor cycle picks up.

verdict.note: core/todo/review-sweep.ts exports runTodoReviewSweep, imported and called at cli/commands/wakeup.ts:105 inside the housekeeping step. runTodoReviewSweepLocked calls collectTodos (core/todo/collect.ts), computes escalated (past due) / stirring (crossed start since state.lastSweepDateEpoch, persisted in .callback-box/todo-review-sweep.json as a box-local date epoch) / stale (open, >45 days since created, no start/due), and queueReviewJob writes a `<stamp>.todo-review.job.card` from createTodoReviewJobTemplate (schemas/todo-review-job.ts) unless findJobCards finds a pending source='todo-review' job. The card defaults priority 'normal' so wakeup's own skipLowPriority reactor cycle (processPendingJobs) picks it up, and its instructions tell the agent to judge and raise with the boxholder.

title: Retrospective scan of past chats
story: As a boxholder, I want `cb retro scan` to read my finished chat sessions and record what I implicitly taught the assistant — corrections, preferences, register, recurring asks — into a ledger plus a per-run report I can read, so that the box can learn from how I actually talk to it.
evidence: `runRetroScan` (core/retro/scan.ts) renders each qualified session, runs the tool-less observer pass (`createSdkRetroObserver`, haiku, $0.25 cap, literal-quote evidence per observations.ts), dedupes on `evidenceHash` against `.callback-box/retro/observations.jsonl`, saves walker state, and writes `store/reviews/retro/<runId>.md` via `writeRunReport`.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/retro.ts defines `scan` under retroCommand, registered in src/cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(retroCommand)); its action builds createSdkRetroObserver (observer.ts: DEFAULT_OBSERVER_MODEL 'haiku', MAX_BUDGET_USD 0.25, prompt says 'Do not use any tools') and calls runRetroScan. scan.ts dedupes via evidenceHash (observations.ts, sha256 of normalized literal quote) against the ledger at .callback-box/retro/observations.jsonl (ledger.ts LEDGER_FILE), saves walker state, and calls writeRunReport into store/reviews/retro/<runId>.md (report.ts RETRO_REPORTS_DIR). Observation kinds are correction/preference/register/recurring-ask/context-gap/experiment-evidence; discovery.ts qualifies only quiesced chat sessions. Matches the story.

title: Review and apply a proposed browser-tab arrangement
story: As a person who handed my open tabs to the box, I want to see the proposed windows, check off tabs to close, then apply or undo the arrangement, so that I stay in control of what happens to my browser.
evidence: TabArrangementEditor renders the proposal's windows with per-tab CheckboxFields marking tabs for closure, polls status via requestTabArrangement, and gates the Apply button on status==="ready" plus a ready relay; Undo calls the same relay with action "undo".

verdict.note: renderers/tab-arrangement.tsx registers TabArrangementView for file type `tab-arrangement` (imported by renderers/setup.ts), so the card renders in the app. TabArrangementEditor in components/TabArrangementView.tsx renders proposal.windows as sections of TabRow rows, each a CheckboxField that toggles the tab into proposal.close (toggleDeleted; a guard keeps at least one tab). It polls status on mount via requestTabArrangement({action:'status'}), gates Apply on `arrangement.status === 'ready' && relay?.ok === true && relay.state === 'ready'` (canApply, line 75), and offers 'Best-effort undo' when relay.undoAvailable, calling requestTabArrangement({action:'undo'}). lib/tab-arrangement-relay.ts implements the postMessage relay to the Clerk extension for status/apply/undo.

title: Route fresh inbox items into the triage pipeline
story: As a person whose box receives items from connectors and scans, I want new inbox items pulled into intake and advanced automatically once each step's precondition is met, so that captured material starts moving without me sorting it.
evidence: runIntake() routes top-level `box/inbox/*` cards into `box/inbox/intake/`, then applies each intake step whose precondition matches, looping until quiescent, and advances intake-complete items to staged; `cb intake` runs one pass.

verdict.note: src/core/intake.ts runIntake() calls routeArrivals() (moves non-dot, non-directory card files at the top of box/inbox into box/inbox/intake/, skipping reserved subdirs intake/staged/triaged/unhandled/feedback and never clobbering), then loops intakeSteps (currently filenameNormalizationStep, whose apply() checks its own cheap precondition SAFE_NAME_RE) until no step reports changed, capped at MAX_PASSES=100, then advanceToStaged() moves everything left in intake/ to box/inbox/staged/. src/core/commands/intake.ts registers the `intake` command running one pass and printing routed/applied/staged; src/cli/commands/intake.ts wires `cb intake` into the CLI (registered at src/cli/index.ts:143). Matches the story as written.

title: Run a background agent turn for a job or procedure
story: As a script or procedure in the box, I want to invoke an agent with a prompt, a turn and budget cap, and optionally a schema for its answer, so that background work is done by an agent whose result I can act on programmatically.
evidence: `createAgent`/`createClaudeAgent` expose `invoke` and `invokeStructured`; `runAgent` builds the SDK `query()` options (cwd, `maxTurns`, `maxBudgetUsd`, model, resume-or-create session id, `outputFormat` json_schema), `consumeAgentStream` drives the message stream to a result, and `validateStructuredResult` checks the structured output against the caller's zod schema.

verdict.note: src/core/agent/index.ts exports createClaudeAgent and createAgent, both returning an Agent with `invoke(opts)` and `invokeStructured(schema, opts)`; invokeStructured converts the zod schema with toJSONSchema, strips `$schema`, and passes it as `outputSchema`. src/core/agent/run.ts builds the SDK query() options with cwd/additionalDirectories, `maxTurns` (default 20, line 210), `maxBudgetUsd` (line 77), model, resume-or-create session id, and `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema", schema }` (lines 84-85); src/core/agent/stream.ts exports consumeAgentStream and src/core/agent/json.ts exports validateStructuredResult (with extractJsonFromText fallback). Reachable from real background work: src/core/triage/index.ts:147, src/core/chat/review/reviewer.ts:164, src/core/retro/observer.ts:68, src/core/procedure/engine-validate-model.ts, and src/core/reactor/{batch-jobs,chat-jobs}.ts all call createAgent/invokeStructured.

title: Run a full wakeup cycle from the web app
story: As the boxholder, I want to trigger the box's whole wakeup cycle (preprocess, triage, connectors, jobs, reactor) and watch its output stream, so that I can make the box catch up on demand instead of waiting for a schedule.
evidence: `registerCommand({name:"wakeup"})` calls `runCbWakeup` with `triggeredBy: "webapp"`, which resolves the `cb` binary, builds the tooling env via `buildToolingScriptEnv`, and spawns `cb wakeup` through `runCollectedChild`, forwarding each output chunk to `ctx.write`.

verdict.note: core/commands/wakeup.ts does register a 'wakeup' command that calls runCbWakeup with triggeredBy:'webapp', resolves cb via `which cb`, builds env with buildToolingScriptEnv, and spawns `cb wakeup` through runCollectedChild with onChunk forwarded to ctx.write — but no web-app entry point reaches it. webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts:16-17 and webapp/routes/actions.ts:28-29 both carry explicit notes that the wakeup trigger procedure and POST /api/actions/wakeup were REMOVED and 'the web UI no longer triggers it directly'. The only remaining server surface is the generic commands.executeSync tRPC procedure (webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts), which buffers output into an array rather than streaming it, and grep of frontend/src finds no caller of trpc.commands at all. The real in-process caller is core/scan/promote-wakeup.ts; the 'webapp' label is vestigial, so the boxholder cannot trigger a wakeup and watch it stream from the web app.

panel.note: callback-box/src/core/commands/wakeup.ts is live, non-dead code: it calls registerCommand({name:'wakeup'}) and its executeWakeup calls runCbWakeup with triggeredBy:'webapp', resolving cb via `which cb`, building env with buildToolingScriptEnv, and spawning `cb wakeup` through runCollectedChild from src/lib/run-child.ts with onChunk wired to ctx.write. It is wired into the registry (core/commands/index.ts:21 `import "./wakeup.js"`), and that registry is imported by mounted server code — webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts (commandsRouter, mounted at router.ts:38 as `commands`, exposing executeSync which can run any registered command including wakeup) and webapp/routes/commands.ts — plus runCbWakeup is imported directly by core/scan/promote-wakeup.ts. What is missing is a frontend caller (no trpc.commands usage in frontend/src) and the removed dedicated streaming trigger (notes at webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts and webapp/routes/actions.ts; executeSync buffers output into an array instead of streaming); that is a reachability/accuracy question for the other lenses, not an existence-or-wiring failure of the cited code.

No web-app entry point reaches the wakeup command. src/webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts:16-18 and src/webapp/routes/actions.ts:28-29 carry explicit removal notes ('a wakeup/connector-sync trigger procedure was removed', 'POST /api/actions/wakeup was removed... the web UI no longer triggers it directly'). The only remaining server surface is the generic commands.executeSync tRPC procedure (src/webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts:33, mounted at src/webapp/trpc/router.ts:38), and a grep of src/frontend/src finds zero callers of trpc.commands / executeSync and no wakeup-triggering control (the only frontend 'wakeup' hits are settings copy, an engine-description string, a schedule label, and a wakeup-complete event listener in DashboardPage.tsx). That procedure also buffers output into an array rather than streaming, so even the theoretical raw-HTTP path does not deliver the story's 'watch its output stream'. The real in-process caller of runCbWakeup is core/scan/promote-wakeup.ts; the triggeredBy:'webapp' label is vestigial.

The scope half holds: runCbWakeup spawns an unscoped `cb wakeup` (no --connector), and cli/commands/wakeup.ts runs preprocess, housekeeping/on-wakeup scripts, connectors, intake/stale-job handling, and a reactor cycle — matching the command's own description string. The 'watch its output stream' half does not: runCollectedChild forwards chunks to ctx.write, but every web-side CommandContext discards the live-ness — webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts executeSync builds `write: (text) => outputLines.push(text)` and returns `output: outputLines` only after `await runCommand` resolves, and webapp/trpc/routers/card.ts calls createCollectorContext with no onOutput. There is no subscription/SSE surface for command output anywhere in webapp/, so even granting reachability the boxholder gets a single buffered dump at completion, not a stream to watch.

triage.reasoning: The web-app trigger this story is built on was deliberately removed, and both removal sites say so in the code: webapp/trpc/routers/actions.ts:16-18 ('a wakeup/connector-sync trigger procedure was removed — the box agent runs the wakeup cycle (via the scheduler / cb wakeup); the web UI no longer exposes a bare command trigger') and webapp/routes/actions.ts:28-29 ('POST /api/actions/wakeup was removed... the web UI no longer triggers it directly'). I confirmed the frontend has no replacement: no trpc.commands / executeSync caller anywhere in src/frontend/src, and the only 'wakeup' hits there are settings copy, an engine-description string, a schedule label, and DashboardPage's wakeup-complete event listener. core/commands/wakeup.ts is not dead — it is registered and reachable via commands.executeSync, and runCbWakeup's real caller is core/scan/promote-wakeup.ts — but executeSync buffers output into an array and returns it after runCommand resolves, so even that path could not deliver 'watch its output stream'; there is no command-output subscription/SSE surface in webapp/. So the code is in the intended state and the story describes a capability that was taken out: it should be dropped, or rewritten as the scheduler/`cb wakeup`/scan-promote path with an agent-scripts audience. The `triggeredBy: "webapp"` label in wakeup.ts is now vestigial and is what misled the story author; renaming it is optional tidying, not a gap.

title: Run a multi-step procedure and resume it where it failed
story: As the box's agent, I want to run a declarative procedure whose steps execute in order into a committed run directory, and resume a failed run from its first incomplete step, so that long automated jobs survive interruption instead of restarting.
evidence: `cb procedure run|resume|list|status|gc` dispatch to the procedure commands; `startProcedure` resolves `config/procedures/<name>.procedure.card`, writes a run card, and `runSteps`/`finalizeRun` execute steps (shell steps via `runShell`, with exit code 75 meaning skip), committing between them.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/procedure.ts defines run/resume/list/status/gc (registered via cli/commands/index.ts into cli/index.ts:110) dispatching through runCommand to core/commands/procedure.ts, which calls startProcedure/resumeProcedure in core/procedure/engine.ts. startProcedure resolves a bare name to config/procedures/<name>.procedure.card (engine.ts:50-53), writes a run card, and runSteps/finalizeRun (engine-orchestrate.ts) execute steps in definition order, with engine-step.ts committing at three points via lib/git commit(). resumeProcedure loads run.procedure-run.card, picks the first step whose status is neither 'completed' nor 'skipped', re-opens the run as 'running', and re-runs from there via options.fromStep, which runSteps implements as procedure.steps.slice(indexOf(fromStep)). shell.ts exports CHECK_SKIP_CODE = 75 for shell steps run by runShell.

title: Run a schedule immediately from the dashboard
story: As a boxholder, I want a Run button that fires a schedule now, so that I don't have to wait for its next due time to see what it does.
evidence: `scheduler.trigger` parses the schedule card, runs `checkTriggerPreconditions` (enabled, connector requirements, self and lock-group conflicts) and then `runScheduledScript`, which locks, executes with a timeout, and records the outcome; `TriggerButton` calls it.

verdict.note: src/webapp/trpc/routers/scheduler.ts:158 defines the `trigger` mutation, which parses the schedule, calls checkTriggerPreconditions and then runScheduledScript from scheduler-run.ts. checkTriggerPreconditions rejects disabled schedules (BAD_REQUEST), missing connectors from parsed.requires (PRECONDITION_FAILED), a self-run already in progress and lock-group conflicts (CONFLICT). runScheduledScript acquires the script lock with triggeredBy 'webapp-trigger', runs execWithTimeout(parsed.runs) with the tooling env, and recordOutcome/saveScriptState on success or failure. TriggerButton in src/frontend/src/components/dashboard/ScheduleOverview.tsx (rendered from pages/DashboardPage.tsx) is a 'Run' button calling trpc.scheduler.trigger.useMutation, disabled when the schedule is disabled.

browser.note: A per-row 'Run' button exists and its enablement already reflects the precondition check — Run is disabled on the eight disabled schedules and enabled on the two enabled ones (gc-procedure-runs, process-retrospective). I did not click it: triggering a scheduled task is outside the non-destructive brief.

title: Run and manage scheduled scripts
story: As a person maintaining my box's automations, I want to list scheduled scripts, enable or disable one, trigger a run now, and read its log, so that I can supervise what the box does on its own.
evidence: `schedulerRouter` exposes `schedules` (listSchedules), `setEnabled` (rewrites the card's frontmatter under a card lock), `trigger` (`checkTriggerPreconditions` + `runScheduledScript` with lock-group conflict detection) and `log` (tails the box schedule log).

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/scheduler.ts defines schedulerRouter with all four procedures: `schedules` (delegates to listSchedules in scheduler-schedules.ts), `setEnabled` (reads config/schedules/<name>.scheduled-script.card under withCardLock, sets/deletes the `enabled` frontmatter key, rewrites via renderFrontmatterBlock and git-commits), `trigger` (parses the schedule card, calls checkTriggerPreconditions then runScheduledScript from scheduler-run.ts), and `log` (streams boxLogFile(ctx.boxRoot) JSONL, validates lines, reverses and limits). scheduler-run.ts checkTriggerPreconditions throws TRPCError CONFLICT for a self lock or a lockGroup held by another script. Web UI entry points exist: src/frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx uses trpc.scheduler.schedules and trpc.scheduler.log, and components/dashboard/ScheduleOverview.tsx wires setEnabled and trigger mutations.

browser.note: From the dashboard the schedules list renders (schedules), the enable/disable toggle works end-to-end and commits (verified both directions on gc-procedure-runs), and Run buttons are present with precondition-driven enablement. The log tail is wired into Recent Activity but empty on this box, and I did not trigger a run.

title: Run box-local agent-authored scripts
story: As an agent, I want to run tricks — TypeScript scripts I wrote inside the box, with their own dependencies — so that box-specific automation is callable by name.
evidence: `trickCommand [name]` resolves `<tricksDir>/scripts/<name>/index.ts` via boxCodePaths, runs it as a tsx subprocess with its own package context, and commits anything it left dirty.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/trick.ts defines trickCommand = new Command("trick").argument("[name]"), registered at src/cli/index.ts:124 (program.addCommand(trickCommand)). It resolves <tricksDir>/scripts/<name>/index.ts where tricksDir comes from boxCodePaths(shape).tricksDir (boxRoot/tricks for v1, packageRoot/src/tricks for v2), spawns it via node + resolveTsx() with cwd set to tricksDir so the trick's own package.json/deps resolve, and on exit 0 calls commitIfDirty() which stages and commits leftovers with a Run-By: trick/<name> trailer. Bare `cb trick` lists discovered tricks with their exported description.

title: Run due scheduled scripts with cb tick
story: As the box's agent or a cron-like caller, I want `cb tick` to evaluate every scheduled-script card and run the ones that are due, so that recurring box work happens without anyone asking for it now.
evidence: `tickCommand` in cli/commands/tick.ts reads `config/schedules/*.scheduled-script.card`, parses cron/at/rrule/onWakeup timing, checks budget and busy blockers via tick-helpers (`evaluateSkip`, `executeScript`), takes a per-script lock (`acquireScriptLock` in core/schedule/state.ts), and records the outcome. `--dry-run`, `--script`, and `--force` are options on the same command.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/tick.ts defines `tickCommand = new Command("tick")` with --dry-run/--script/--force/--box, registered in cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(tickCommand)). runTick reads config/schedules via readScheduleFiles, parses each *.scheduled-script.card with parseScheduledScript, and calls evaluateSkip (due/enabled/engine/requires/budget/lock-group gates) and executeScript in tick-helpers.ts; executeScript calls acquireScriptLock/releaseScriptLock from core/schedule/state.ts and recordOutcome/saveScriptState. schemas/scheduled-script.tsx declares cron/at/rrule/on-wakeup fields (cron-parser + rrule imports). All cited files exist and do what the evidence says.

title: Run shell and agent phases inside a procedure step
story: As a procedure author, I want a step's phases to run shell commands under strict bash and agent invocations, with exit code 75 meaning 'skip this step', so that a procedure can gate itself on real conditions instead of always doing the work.
evidence: `runShell` wraps the script in `set -euo pipefail`, runs it in the box root with `buildScriptEnv` and `CHECK_SKIP=75`, and reports `skipped` on `CHECK_SKIP_CODE`; `executePhaseShells` short-circuits the phase on skip or non-zero, and `runAndValidate` in engine-run-phase.ts runs the step's agents separately so a review retry doesn't repeat side-effecting shells.

verdict.note: src/core/procedure/shell.ts sets CHECK_SKIP_CODE=75, wraps each script as `set -euo pipefail\n<script>`, runs it in boxRoot with buildScriptEnv({CHECK_SKIP:'75'}), and returns skipped when exitCode===75. engine-phase.ts executePhaseShells loops the phase's shells and short-circuits on skipped (returning exitCode 75) or any non-zero exit. engine-run-phase.ts runs run-phase agents (runRunAgents) separately from run-phase shells (runRunShells → executePhaseShells at line 182), and runAndValidate re-invokes only the agent on severity=review retries, so shells don't re-run; engine-step.ts uses executePhaseShells for the precheck phase and prints 'Skipped: … precheck exit $CHECK_SKIP'.

title: Run the intake, triage and handling passes
story: As an agent, I want each stage of the inbox pipeline to be runnable as its own pass, so that fresh items get routed, classified and handled step by step.
evidence: `intakeCommand` routes fresh inbox items and advances intake-complete ones to staged; `triageCommand` classifies staged items into buckets (--dry-run prints decisions without moving files); `handleCommand` runs handler procedures per category bucket.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/intake.ts exports `intakeCommand` ("Run one intake pass: route fresh inbox items, normalize filenames, advance intake-complete items to staged") dispatching runCommand({name:"intake"}); triage.ts exports `triageCommand` with a `--dry-run` option ("Print agent decisions without moving files") dispatching name:"triage"; handle.ts exports `handleCommand` with an optional [category] argument dispatching name:"handle" ("Run handler procedures for triaged category buckets"). All three are registered on the CLI program at src/cli/index.ts:143-145 and re-exported from src/cli/commands/index.ts, and the core command definitions exist at src/core/commands/{intake,triage,handle}.ts, so each stage is separately runnable as `cb intake` / `cb triage` / `cb handle`.

title: Schedule a one-shot task that removes itself and hands off to the next
story: As a boxholder, I want a scheduled-script card marked `once` to be deleted after it succeeds and to create the follow-up card it names, so that a one-time task doesn't linger and a multi-stage plan advances itself.
evidence: `ScheduledScriptSchema` carries `once` and `create-after-success`; after a successful run `handlePostSuccess` calls `handleCreateAfterSuccess` (which resolves each chain path, skips one that already exists, and creates the card from its template args) and then unlinks the one-shot card — unless the script rewrote its own card during the run (post-run mtime check) — committing both with a `Triggered-By: cb tick` trailer.

verdict.note: src/schemas/scheduled-script.tsx defines `once` (line 61) and `create-after-success` (line 69, array of {path,args}), parsed into once/createAfterSuccess. In src/cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts, executeScript snapshots the card mtime pre-run (line ~255) and on success calls handlePostSuccess, which first calls handleCreateAfterSuccess (src/cli/commands/tick-utils.ts:181 — resolves each chain path via resolveRefPath as a write-target, skips a target that already exists, parses the card name and renders the default template with args) and then, if parsed.once, fs.unlink(cardPath) unless postStat.mtimeMs > preRunMtimeMs (script rewrote its own card). The housekeeping commit adds trailers {'Triggered-By':'cb tick'} at line 233.

title: Scheduled work that needs a connector waits instead of failing
story: As a box owner, I want a scheduled script that declares a required connector to be skipped and shown as blocked while Google isn't connected for that service, so that an unconfigured box reports a waiting task rather than a stream of failures.
evidence: checkMissingConnectors resolves gmail/calendar/drive (and legacy `google`) by requiring both stored Google tokens and the per-box googleServices allowlist, other names by a granted secret-store entry or legacy secret file; the tick loop logs "Skipping <script>: missing connectors: …" and continues, evaluateTaskHealth sets that same list as the task's blockedReason, and the scheduler router returns it per schedule.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/connectors/requirements.ts: checkMissingConnectors dispatches gmail/calendar/drive plus legacy `google` through googleServicePredicate, which requires hasGoogleTokens (CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE or legacy config/connectors/google.secret.json) AND isGoogleServiceAllowed(boxRoot, service) from the per-box googleServices policy; other names fall back to storeSecretPresent (granted, non-empty store entry) || legacySecretPresent. src/cli/commands/tick-utils.ts:104-108 logs `Skipping <script>: missing connectors: …` and `continue`s rather than running/failing (same in tick-helpers.ts:141-143). src/core/schedule/health-box.ts:112 feeds missingConnectors into evaluateTaskHealth, which in src/core/schedule/health.ts:113-134 sets blockedReason `missing connectors: …` and status "blocked". src/webapp/trpc/routers/scheduler-schedules.ts:103 returns the same list per schedule as `missingRequirements`.

title: Scheduler daemon across boxes
story: As an operator, I want a scheduler daemon that ticks every box listed in the machine manifest and logs each cycle per box, so that schedules keep running on a machine without a person invoking them.
evidence: `runScheduler` in core/schedule/scheduler.ts loops over `loadBoxesConfig()` boxes calling `runTick`, writes `<boxRoot>/.callback-box/scheduler.jsonl`, and touches a heartbeat (`touchSchedulerHeartbeat`). `cb scheduler` (cli/commands/scheduler.ts) installs/loads a launchd plist, adds/removes boxes from the manifest, and renders the log.

verdict.note: runScheduler (core/schedule/scheduler.ts:124) runs a while loop that reloads loadSchedulerConfig() (a thin wrapper over loadBoxesConfig from core/box/boxes-config.ts, i.e. ~/.config/cb/boxes.json) each cycle, validates each path with isBox, calls touchSchedulerHeartbeat(boxPath) before the tick, runs runTick(boxPath, {quiet:true}), and writeBoxLog appends JSONL events (tick/dirty-repo/box-growth-scan/health-alert/shutdown) to <boxRoot>/.callback-box/scheduler.jsonl (SCHEDULER_LOG_FILENAME). cli/commands/scheduler.ts exposes `start` (foreground daemon, --interval), `install` (writes ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.callback.scheduler.plist with RunAtLoad/KeepAlive and optional launchctl load), `status`, `uninstall`, deprecated add/remove/list against the manifest, and `log` which uses resolveLogBoxes/readBoxEntries/renderLogEntry from scheduler-helpers.ts. Every element of the story is present and reachable.

title: Scope and pace reactor runs
story: As an operator or a schedule, I want the reactor to process only one connector's jobs or one job type, defer low-priority jobs until they are overdue, refuse to run concurrently, and optionally poll on an interval, so that a partial sync or an idle box does not burn agent turns or collide with another run.
evidence: `ReactorOptions` carries `sourceFilter`, `type`, `skipLowPriority`, `pollInterval`, `maxCycles` and `resetSessions`; `findJobCards` drops jobs whose frontmatter `source:` doesn't match, and `discoverStage` in cycle.ts returns `skipped` for all-low-priority batches unless a job is past its wait deadline (age from the filename timestamp prefix). `runReactor` acquires a PID lock via `acquireFileLock` and sleeps between polls.

verdict.note: engine.ts ReactorOptions declares maxCycles, pollInterval, skipLowPriority, type, sourceFilter, resetSessions (lines 43-58) with defaults resolved at 227-232; runReactor loops `for (let cycle = 0; cycle < maxCycles; cycle++)` and sleeps `pollInterval * 1000` between polls when pollInterval > 0, and calls acquireFileLock(lockPath, {kind:'reactor'}) (line 257) — src/lib/file-lock.ts acquireLock writes a {pid,hostname,acquiredAt} holder file and throws LockHeldError when held, so a second run refuses. job-discovery.ts findJobCards applies typeFilter as the `.<type>.job.card` suffix and drops cards whose frontmatter `source:` != sourceFilter (line 99); cycle.ts discoverStage returns {kind:'skipped'} when skipLowPriority is set and no normal-priority job exists, unless jobs are past LOW_PRIORITY_MAX_WAIT (age via readCreatedAt → createdAtFromFilename, falling back to mtime), and then admits only a bounded oldest-first batch. Reachable from operators via src/cli/commands/reactor.ts flags (--poll, --max-cycles, --skip-low-priority, --type, --reset-sessions) and from cb wakeup (wakeup.ts sets skipLowPriority:true and sourceFilter to the active connector).

title: See a note in chat about what the box did while I was away
story: As the box's agent running a scheduled script, I want to post a self-note into the live chat session that reads as a record of background work rather than as something the user typed, so that unattended work is waiting in the conversation without anyone being pinged for a reply.
evidence: `cb chat self-note "<body>" [--ref] [--commit]` POSTs to `/<box>/api/chat/self-note` using `CB_SERVER_URL`/`CB_BOX_NAME` from `buildScriptEnv`; the route wraps it as `<self-note ref= commit=>` and sends or enqueues it on the target session, the chat prompt tells the agent nobody is waiting on a reply, and `ChatMessages` renders the group as a distinct self-note bubble.

verdict.note: cli/commands/chat.ts defines `self-note` with <body> plus --ref/--commit/--session; postSelfNote POSTs {body,ref,commit,session} to `${CB_SERVER_URL}/${CB_BOX_NAME}/api/chat/self-note` with loopback headers, and core/script-env.ts documents building CB_SERVER_URL/CB_BOX_NAME from box.json publicUrl for spawned scripts. webapp/routes/chat-send-routes.ts's POST /api/chat/self-note resolves explicit-or-most-active session, wraps the text as `<self-note ref="…" commit="…">…</self-note>`, and enqueues it when the target isBusy() else sends it. core/chat/session/prompts.ts line 97 tells the agent a <self-note> is a record of background work, not user input, and 'no one is waiting on a reply'; ChatMessages.tsx SelfNoteMessage renders it as a distinct bordered self-note bubble with ref/short commit, dispatched from InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx group.type === 'self-note'.

title: See every schedule and its recent ticks on the dashboard
story: As a boxholder, I want a dashboard table of all schedules with cadence, last run, budget use, missing connectors and whether one is running right now, so that I can tell what the box is doing on its own.
