title: Stand down when the model engine is unavailable
story: As the boxholder, I want a procedure step or reactor cycle that hits an exhausted model quota to stop immediately with that reason recorded, leaving jobs pending, so that a quota outage costs one clean failure instead of a burst of misleading errors.
evidence: When `agentResult.unavailability` is set, `runRunAgents` returns `engineUnavailable`, `runAndValidate` skips shells/validation, and `recordStepResults` fails the step with that message in `run.stdout` (resumable later); `runReactor` checks `boxEngineUnavailability(boxRoot)` after a failed cycle and breaks out with `engineWaitReason`, while `processChatJobs` breaks the per-thread loop and leaves remaining chat jobs for a later cycle.

verdict.note: engine-run-phase.ts:112/154 return engineUnavailable when agentResult.unavailability is set; runAndValidate (line ~240) then returns immediately with runStdout/validateResult undefined, skipping runRunShells and validation. engine-step.ts recordStepResults marks the step failed when engineUnavailable !== undefined and sets runResult.stdout to that message (lines 224, 247-249). reactor/engine.ts:155-162 calls boxEngineUnavailability(boxRoot) after an unsuccessful cycle and breaks with fmt.warn(`Stopping cycles: ${engineWaitReason(wait)}`); chat-jobs.ts:92-97 breaks the per-thread loop on unavailability, leaving remaining chat jobs for a later cycle.

title: Sync and triage just one connector
story: As a box agent, I want `cb wakeup --connector gmail` to sync only that connector, scan only its inbox paths, and run the reactor only on jobs from that source, so that I can pull and process new mail without dragging the whole box through a full wakeup.
evidence: `runConnectors` filters the registry by name and returns the `activeConnector`; wakeup.ts passes it to the inbox scan (which walks only `connector.inboxPaths`, tagging jobs `source=<name>`), sets `reactorOptions.sourceFilter`, and passes the name to `processPendingJobs`.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/wakeup.ts registers `-c, --connector <name>`; runConnectors (src/cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts) filters getAllConnectors() by name, exits 1 on no match, and returns activeConnector only when the flag was given. wakeup.ts then skips on-wakeup scripts under the flag, passes `{connector: activeConnector}` to createIntakeJobsForUnjobbed, which in wakeup-steps.ts walks only `connector.inboxPaths` (gmail.ts: ['box/inbox/email']) and tags jobs source=connector.name instead of 'wakeup'/'wakeup-captures', and processPendingJobs sets reactorOptions.sourceFilter = activeConnector.name, which src/core/reactor/engine.ts and cycle.ts thread into job discovery. Matches the story.

title: Tell a step's agent where it is
story: As a procedure author, I want each step's agent prompt prefixed with the box's current date, the run card path, the step's exact line range in the procedure card, the precheck's output and the run's directive, so that the agent can read its own definition and state without me repeating them in every prompt.
evidence: `buildContextBlock` emits `Current date` (from `getBoxTime`), `Procedure run:`, `Step: <id> (defined at <path> lines N-M)` via `getStepLineRange`, plus `<precheck>` and `<directive>` blocks; `runRunAgents` prepends it to each agent's `systemPrompt`. The precheck block only appears when the step sets `pass-output: true` (`toParsedStep`'s `passOutput`).

verdict.note: src/core/procedure/engine-phase.ts:253 `buildContextBlock` emits '# Context / Current date: <getBoxTime(boxRoot) ISO date> / Procedure run: <runCardPath> / Step: <id> (defined at <procedurePath> <lines N-M>)' using `getStepLineRange` (same file, line 288, scans the YAML `- id:` list items), then optional `<precheck>` and `<directive>` blocks. engine-run-phase.ts:126 (inside `runRunAgents`) builds that block per agent and sets `systemPrompt = contextBlock + '\n\n' + agentDef.prompt`. The precheck output is gated on pass-output: engine-parse.ts:69 sets `passOutput: step.precheck['pass-output'] === true` and engine-step.ts:162 only forwards stdout when `step.precheck.passOutput` is set.

title: Triage new intake automatically and ask when unsure
story: As a boxholder, I want intake-complete items classified and filed into the right destination on their own, with a question card raised only when the agent is guessing, so that my inbox sorts itself without silent misfiles.

title: Wake the box up to sync, tidy, and process new work
story: As the box's agent, I want `cb wakeup` to run preprocessors, housekeeping, on-wakeup schedules, connectors, and one reactor cycle in order, so that everything that arrived since the last wakeup gets picked up in one pass.
evidence: `wakeup.ts` sequences `runPreprocessors`, `runHousekeeping` (tmp sweep, capture sweep, root landmark refill, `runTodoReviewSweep`), `runOnWakeupScripts`, `runConnectors`, `cleanupStaleJobs`/`createIntakeJobsForUnjobbed`, then `runReactor`, and finally pushes to the git remote.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/wakeup.ts exports wakeupCommand = new Command("wakeup") whose action runs, in order: runPreprocessors (from wakeup-steps.ts), runHousekeeping (stale tmp sweep, sweepAbandonedCaptures, root-landmark refill+commit, runTodoReviewSweep), runOnWakeupScripts (tick-utils.ts, 'Run all on-wakeup scheduled scripts that are due'), runConnectors (wakeup-connectors.ts), cleanupStaleJobs + createIntakeJobsForUnjobbed, then processPendingJobs calling runReactor({maxCycles: 1, skipLowPriority: true}) from core/reactor/index.ts, and finally pushChanges -> pushToRemote unless --skip-push. Matches the story's ordering and the one-reactor-cycle claim.

title: Watch the agent's background tasks while they run
story: As a person whose agent kicked off long-running work, I want a strip of pills showing each running task, its last tool and elapsed time, so that I know something is still happening between replies.

title: Deep-link to any box surface
story: As a person using the web app, I want every surface of my box (chat, browse, card, views, history, landmarks, capture, settings, admin) to live at a stable URL with validated query params, so that I can bookmark, reload, or share a link and land exactly where I was.
evidence: router.tsx builds the TanStack route tree: /$boxSlug/{chat,browse/$,card/$,views/$,history/$hash,landmarks,chats,capture,settings,admin,dashboard,inventory,questions}, each with a zod validateSearch (e.g. chat's session/contextDir/companion/card/capture params); the box index redirects to /chat and an unknown path redirects to the box root.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/router.tsx does define all the named routes under boxLayoutRoute (/$boxSlug/{dashboard,inventory,chat,questions,browse/$,history,history/$hash,capture,settings,admin,card/$,views/$,landmarks,chats}), with boxIndexRoute redirecting to /chat and boxCatchAllRoute redirecting to the box root — so the deep-linking half checks out. But the story's qualifier 'with validated query params' and the evidence's 'each with a zod validateSearch' are false: only chatRoute, historyRoute/historyDetailRoute, adminRoute (plus the non-box loginRoute/setupRoute) declare validateSearch. browseRoute, cardRoute, viewRoute, landmarksRoute, captureRoute, settingsRoute, dashboardRoute, questionsRoute, inventoryRoute and chatsRoute declare none, so their search params are unvalidated passthrough. The third cited file, lib/routing.ts, is not validation at all — href() returns `any` and toSearch() is a documented `as never` escape hatch that deliberately BYPASSES search-param type checking for dynamically built links.

panel.note: router.tsx (299 lines) defines the full TanStack route tree under boxLayoutRoute (/$boxSlug) — dashboard, inventory, chat, questions, browse/$, history + history/$hash, capture, settings, admin, card/$, views/$, landmarks, chats — all registered via rootRoute.addChildren([...boxLayoutRoute.addChildren([...])]), plus boxIndexRoute redirecting to /$boxSlug/chat and boxCatchAllRoute redirecting to the box root. The tree is live: createAppRouter() is exported from router.tsx and instantiated in main.tsx (line 15), and boxLayoutRoute mounts AppLayout from app-shell.tsx. Zod validateSearch code genuinely exists and runs on chatRoute (session/contextDir/companion/card/nativeComposer/capture), historyRoute/historyDetailRoute, adminRoute, loginRoute and setupRoute — not on every route, but that is a wording/accuracy question for another lens, not an existence one. lib/routing.ts is real and imported by ~25 components (href/toSearch), so nothing here is dead code.

The routes are live in the shipped web app: router.tsx builds routeTree with boxLayoutRoute ('/$boxSlug') plus children for chat, browse/$, card/$, views/$, history, history/$hash, landmarks, chats, capture, settings, admin, dashboard, inventory, questions, with boxIndexRoute redirecting to /chat and boxCatchAllRoute ('/$') redirecting to the box root; dev-only routes are the sole flag-gated ones (import.meta.env.DEV). createAppRouter() is instantiated and mounted in frontend/src/main.tsx, and app-shell.tsx navigates to these paths (e.g. href(`/${boxSlug}/browse/${path}`) at app-shell.tsx:151). Bookmark/reload of a deep URL works because webapp/server.ts:258 and server-root.ts:340 install an SPA fallback serving index.html for non-API page routes. My lens (reachability by a person using the web app) is satisfied; the verifier's objection was about validateSearch coverage, which is another reviewer's lens.

The deep-link half of the story holds: router.tsx defines every named surface under boxLayoutRoute (/$boxSlug/{dashboard,inventory,chat,questions,browse/$,history,history/$hash,capture,settings,admin,card/$,views/$,landmarks,chats}), with boxIndexRoute redirecting to /chat and boxCatchAllRoute to the box root, so bookmark/reload/share lands where you were. But the story's qualifier 'every surface ... with validated query params' is an over-claim: only chatRoute (lines 103-125), historyRoute/historyDetailRoute (historySearchSchema) and adminRoute declare validateSearch. browseRoute, cardRoute, viewRoute, landmarksRoute, captureRoute, settingsRoute, dashboardRoute, inventoryRoute, questionsRoute and chatsRoute declare none — and pages/ViewPage.tsx and pages/browse/BrowsePage.tsx read the raw `location.searchStr` as passthrough, so those surfaces' query params are never validated. lib/routing.ts is the opposite of validation: href() returns `any` and toSearch() is a documented `as never` escape hatch that deliberately bypasses search-param type checking.

browser.note: Direct navigation works and stays put for /browse, /browse/<dir>, /browse/<file>, /card/<path>, /landmarks, /history, /settings. Query params are real state: toggling to Source put ?view=Source on the browse URL, and the chat capture flow produced /chat?capture=%221%22&session=<uuid>.

triage.reasoning: The user-facing capability is real and browser-confirmed: router.tsx defines every named surface under boxLayoutRoute (/$boxSlug/{dashboard,inventory,chat,questions,browse/$,history,history/$hash,capture,settings,admin,card/$,views/$,landmarks,chats}), boxIndexRoute redirects to /chat, boxCatchAllRoute redirects to the box root, and webapp/server.ts installs an SPA fallback so a deep URL survives bookmark/reload. The browser check (browser/browse-1.json) confirmed direct navigation stays put on /browse, /browse/<dir>, /browse/<file>, /card/<path>, /landmarks, /history, /settings, with ?view=Source and /chat?capture=1&session=<uuid> round-tripping. What is wrong is the story's own qualifier: only chatRoute, historyRoute/historyDetailRoute and adminRoute (plus non-box loginRoute/setupRoute) declare a zod validateSearch; browse, card, views, landmarks, capture, settings, dashboard, inventory, questions and chats declare none and pass search through unvalidated — deliberately so for /views/$ and /browse/$, whose params are view-defined. The third cited file, lib/routing.ts, is the opposite of validation (href() returns any; toSearch() is a documented `as never` escape hatch). No product consequence: unvalidated passthrough is what those surfaces want. Fix is in the catalog — drop 'with validated query params' (or narrow it to chat/history/admin) and drop the lib/routing.ts citation. Not a false-negative: the clause as literally written is false for most routes, so the entry needs correcting rather than restoring as-is.

title: Edit and commit box files from inside a view
story: As a boxholder, I want an agent-written view to save my edits back into box files and commit them when I choose, so that a view can be a working editor for box data instead of a read-only display.

title: Embed one figure card several ways with parameters
story: As a box author, I want a figure card to declare typed parameters with defaults in its frontmatter and each embed link to supply values in its query string, so that one sketch renders as several different figures instead of being copied per variant.
evidence: parseDeclaredParams() reads the card's frontmatter `params` into string/number/boolean declarations (warning on a malformed or unknown-typed entry rather than silently dropping it), and coerceFigureParams() coerces the embed's query-string strings to the declared type, falling back to the declared default and omitting a param with neither; FigureView.tsx calls both to build the figure's params object.

verdict.note: lib/figure-params.ts exports parseDeclaredParams(), which reads frontmatter `params` into {name,type,default} decls restricted to string|number|boolean and console.warns on non-object entries, missing string names, or unknown types, and coerceFigureParams(), which coerces supplied query strings per type, falls back to the declared default, and omits a param with neither. FigureView.tsx lines 54-55 calls both and passes the result as figure.params (line 104), keyed by paramsKey for remount. Embed query strings reach it: FigureEmbed.tsx's Img override resolves `![](store/figures/Foo.figure.card?p=v)` with resolveContentTarget() from lib/view-url.ts (parseViewQuery splits off the reserved `view` key) and passes target.params to FileView. src/schemas/figure.ts declares the `params: z.array(FigureParam).optional()` frontmatter field with instructions describing embed-query declarations.

title: Every card change lands in git, with history to browse
story: As a person using the box, I want card edits to be committed to the box's git repository and browsable as a list of commits with diffs, so that I can see what changed in my box and when.
evidence: lib/git.ts provides `stageAndCommitPaths`/`commitPaths` used by the create, move, and trash commands; the history tRPC router exposes `list`, `facets`, `diff`, and `sessionLog` queries behind the `/history` and `/history/$hash` routes.

verdict.note: lib/git.ts exports commitPaths/stageAndCommitPaths (staging-race-aware), used by core/commands/create.ts (line 212), move.ts, trash.ts, and many other mutation paths including webapp tRPC routers (drive, scheduler, share, calendar). webapp/trpc/routers/history.ts exposes list (paginated git log with --grep facet filters), facets, diff (getCommitDiff), and sessionLog procedures; frontend router.tsx declares /history and /history/$hash routes rendering HistoryPage.tsx, which drives HistoryBrowser, and components/history/CommitDetail.tsx calls trpc.history.diff to show the commit's diff.

title: Filterable commit history
story: As a boxholder, I want to browse the box's commit timeline and narrow it by connector, workflow, touchpoint, feedback or session, with the filter and selected commit in the URL, so that I can share or return to a filtered view of what the agent did.
evidence: HistoryPage maps search params to a filter and the /history/$hash path to the selection; HistoryBrowser drives history.list infinite pagination plus history.facets, and HistoryFilterBar offers connector/workflow multi-selects, touchpoint/feedback toggles and dismissible session/path chips.

HistoryBrowser.tsx drives `trpc.history.list.useInfiniteQuery` plus `trpc.history.facets.useQuery` and renders HistoryFilterBar + CommitTimeline. HistoryFilterBar.tsx has connector/workflow multi-select FilterChipButtons fed by facets, ToggleChips for touchpoint/feedback, and a dismissible session chip. Server side: trpc/routers/history.ts builds `--grep` regexes per axis and exposes list/facets, backed by src/lib/git-log.ts `getLogPaginated`/`getTrailerFacets` and git-trailers.ts trailer-key constants.

HistoryFilterBar shows Connector and Workflow multi-selects (facets populated: capture-connector, gmail-connector, cb create, ... / process-captures, process-news, test-echo, ...), Touchpoint and Feedback switches, and dismissible Session and Path chips ('Clear session filter', 'Clear path filter', plus a global 'Clear'). Selecting gmail-connector rewrote the URL to ?connector=%5B%22gmail-connector%22%5D and narrowed the list to Gmail pull commits; ?touchpoint=true and ?feedback=true round-trip into checked switches and filtered lists; clicking a row put the hash in the path (/history/d0a43e92) and reloading that URL reselects it. title: Follow a link from a card to another card or file
story: As a person browsing my box, I want links and embeds inside cards, views, and chat to resolve to the right box path with their viewer and parameters, and to open in a dismissible overlay rather than stranding me, so that I can follow a reference and get back.
evidence: parseViewUrl/serializeViewUrl/resolveRelativePath/classifyMarkdownHref turn a href into a ViewTarget (path + ?view= viewer + params) and apiFileUrl/apiImageUrl/externalImageProxyUrl build the fetch URLs; useViewNavigate opens the target in the ViewOverlay, falling back to /$box/views/$path; refLabel/externalLabel name the chip and detectVideoEmbed swaps a YouTube image src for a player.

verdict.note: lib/view-url.ts exports parseViewUrl/serializeViewUrl/resolveRelativePath/resolveContentTarget/classifyMarkdownHref producing ViewTarget {path, viewer, params}, plus apiFileUrl/apiImageUrl/externalImageProxyUrl/resolveImageSrc. Markdown.tsx's makeLink calls classifyMarkdownHref + resolveContentTarget and hands the target to ctx.onNavigate (external hrefs open normally; retired view: links render as BrokenLink); makeImg calls detectVideoEmbed (lib/video-url.ts) and swaps in components/ui/VideoEmbed. hooks/useViewNavigate.ts opens the target via useViewOverlay (ViewOverlayProvider mounted in app-shell.tsx line 76), falling back to navigate(/$boxSlug/views/<serializeViewUrl>) when no provider exists; ViewOverlay's panel is a dismissible role=dialog with Escape/backdrop/✕ close. refLabel/externalLabel/refToViewTarget (lib/ref-label.ts) name chips in Source.tsx and SeeAlso.tsx, and chat renders through the same Markdown (components/chat/markdown-rendering.tsx, CalloutBlock.tsx).

title: Give the file the whole screen on a phone, or the whole width on a desktop
story: As a person browsing the box on a narrow screen, I want the file list to step aside when I open a file and a Back button to bring it back, and on a wide screen to collapse the list pane to a stripe, so that reading a card isn't squeezed into a leftover column.
evidence: Sidebar takes `detailSelected` and switches to `hidden sm:flex` when a detail item is open (full-width list otherwise), and keeps its own collapsed state that shrinks the desktop pane to a 40px hamburger stripe via the `--sidebar-desktop-w` custom property; BrowseDetailPanel and CommitDetail render MobileBackButton (`sm:hidden`) at the top of the detail pane to return to the list.

BrowsePage.tsx passes `detailSelected={hasDetail}` and gives BrowseDetailPanel an `onBack` that navigates back to the dir with replace; BrowseDetailPanel.tsx:67 and CommitDetail.tsx:91 render MobileBackButton, which is `sm:hidden`. Matches the story as written.

At 1440px the list pane is 319px wide with a 'Collapse sidebar' button; clicking it removes the list region and swaps in a 'Show browse' control (stripe).

title: Images still show when the source blocks hotlinking or hasn't landed yet
story: As a person reading box content full of images, I want an image that fails to load to be retried through the box's proxy or on a short backoff before it gives up, and to show a labeled placeholder when it truly can't load, so that transient and hotlink-blocked images don't leave silent holes in the page.
evidence: Image.tsx runs a two-stage load (src → proxyFallbackSrc → ErrorPlaceholder) keyed by a module-level failedImageUrls set so a markdown re-render doesn't replay dead fetches, and uses useImageRetry for the retryOnError case (in-box chat images referenced before they exist); makeImg supplies proxyFallbackSrc from externalImageProxyUrl for external sources; ErrorPlaceholder renders a broken-image glyph, "Failed to load", and the alt text with role="img".

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/ui/Image.tsx implements exactly the described two-stage load: getLoadState/handleError move src -> proxyFallbackSrc -> ErrorPlaceholder, with the module-level failedImageUrls Set keeping a markdown remount from replaying dead fetches. ErrorPlaceholder renders BrokenImageIcon, the literal text 'Failed to load', the alt text, and role="img" with aria-label 'Failed to load image: <alt>'. useImageRetry (hooks/use-image-retry.ts) retries on a bounded backoff RETRY_DELAYS_MS [500,1500,3000,5000] with an imageRetry=<attempt> cache-buster, and is enabled by shouldRetryPrimary only when there is no proxy fallback. Markdown.tsx makeImg (line 168) and chat/markdown-rendering.tsx both supply proxyFallbackSrc from externalImageProxyUrl (lib/view-url.ts:223), which points at the /api/proxy-image route in webapp/routes/proxy-image.ts, and set retryOnError when no proxy URL exists.

browser.note: An image the app cannot load shows the browser's native broken-image glyph, not the app's labeled placeholder: at /browse/box/inbox/scan-20260429T0246-6c66f791.attach/attach/photo-001.jpg (a 404 from /api/files) the DOM has no element with role="img"/aria-label 'Failed to load' and the page text contains no 'Failed to load'; naturalWidth is 0 and the keeps the dead src across a reload. The retry/proxy half is untestable — every external image in the box's webpage cards loads directly on the first try.

title: Land on a card that isn't there and find out what happened to it
story: As a person following a link to a card path, I want the not-found page to tell me whether the card ever existed and offer its history when it did, so that a moved or trashed card reads as a relocation I can trace rather than a dead end.
evidence: FileView.tsx renders `MissingCardState` (instead of the plain "File not found" line) when `card.get` returns nothing for an `isCardPath` path; MissingCardState queries `history.list({count:1, filter:{path}})` and switches between "This card is no longer here" with a `/history?path=…` link and "Card not found" based on whether any commit touched that path.

verdict.note: FileView.tsx line 372: when no data and isCardPath(path) (path ends in .card) it renders <MissingCardState path onClose/> instead of the plain 'File not found' div, and line 364 lets a 'Card not found:' error fall through to it. MissingCardState.tsx queries trpc.history.list({count:1, filter:{path}}) and switches the heading between 'This card is no longer here' (with a TextLink to /<box>/history?path=…) and 'Card not found' on whether any commit touched the path. trpc/routers/history.ts filterSchema includes path and resolves/validates it into a git path filter; router.tsx defines the /history route with a path search param.

browser.note: Both branches seen. /card/procedure/runs/process-retrospective_2026-06-27T1152/run.procedure-run.card (a git-deleted path) renders 'This card is no longer here' + 'It may have been moved or sent to Trash. Its history can show what happened.' + the path + a 'See history for this path' link + 'Close this view'. /card/store/does-not-exist-xyz.note.card renders 'Card not found' + 'No card or git history exists at this path. Check the path or close this view.' with no history link.

title: Land somewhere real when a page breaks or the URL is wrong
story: As a person using the web app, I want a render crash to show the error with retry and reload buttons instead of a blank page, and an unrecognized path under my box to send me to the box's home surface, so that a bad link or a broken page is recoverable without me guessing a URL.
evidence: router.tsx sets errorComponent: RouteError on the root route (without it TanStack renders nothing), and boxCatchAllRoute's beforeLoad throws a redirect to /$boxSlug for any unknown path under a box, while boxIndexRoute redirects the box root to /chat. RouteError renders error.stack in a Pre with 'Try again' (router reset) and 'Reload page' buttons and console.errors the componentStack so the crash also reaches the debug log.

verdict.note: router.tsx line 39 sets errorComponent: RouteError on createRootRoute, and components/RouteError.tsx renders error.stack in a <Pre error boxed>, a 'Try again' button wired to the router's reset and a 'Reload page' button calling window.location.reload(), plus a useEffect console.error('Route error:', error, info?.componentStack) that feeds the DebugLog console patch. boxCatchAllRoute (path '/$' under boxLayoutRoute, ~line 230) throws redirect({to: '/$boxSlug'}) in beforeLoad, and boxIndexRoute (~line 83) in turn throws redirect to '/$boxSlug/chat', so an unknown path under a box lands on the box's chat home. Both routes are in the routeTree passed to the router. Matches the story as written.

browser.note: Unknown path under the box redirects to the home surface: /no-such-surface-xyz landed on /chat?session=…, and the box index also resolves to /chat. The render-crash RouteError panel could not be triggered without breaking the app, so only the routing half was observed.

title: Landmarks map of the box

evidence: LandmarksList queries landmarks.list, indents rows by depth, and names landmark cards that failed to parse; LandmarkSection renders the symbol (emoji or symbolSrc image), a path link into browse, LinkTiles to /$boxSlug/card/<ref> including a Missing state, and collapsible link groups.

LandmarksList queries trpc.landmarks.list (webapp/trpc/routers/landmarks.ts, which uses core/landmark/resolve.ts resolveLandmark and core/landmark/symbol.ts readLandmarkSymbol and assigns depth) plus chat.byLandmark, and renders a LandmarkProblems card naming landmark cards that didn't parse. LandmarkSection.tsx renders LandmarkSymbol (symbolSrc image via apiFileUrl, else emoji), a PathLink to /$boxSlug/browse/<dir>, INDENT_CLASSES by depth, LinkTiles linking to /$boxSlug/card/<ref> with a 'Missing' state when !link.exists, LandmarkLinks capped at LINK_CAP=6 behind a 'Show all'/'Show fewer' disclosure, and collapsible LandmarkGroup sections.

browser.note: /landmarks lists both landmark cards as sections with emoji symbol (📦 Box, ⚗️ Acids & Bases), a path link to /user-stories-refresh/test1/browse/store/courses/Acids_Bases.attach, and three link tiles (Course guide / Lesson plan / Progress) whose hrefs are /<box>/card/<ref>. Not exercisable in this box: depth indentation (no nested landmarks), the Show-all disclosure and link groups (only 3 links), the Missing tile state, and the parse-failure list — no such data present.

title: Link and expand cards from inside a custom view
story: As an agent authoring a box view, I want CardLink and CardRef widgets that resolve a card's title and type and open or expand it correctly for whichever surface the view is shown in, so that I don't have to reimplement navigation per surface.
evidence: CardLink/CardRef read the ViewHost (openCard, useResolvedRef via trpc.views.resolveRef, renderInline), CardRef offering Open plus an Expand that renders the card inline and a "missing" badge; index.tsx installs them on window.__cbViewWidgets for compiled views, and node-entry.tsx supplies a Node host so `cb view test` renders the same widgets.

verdict.note: CardLink.tsx and CardRef.tsx both call useViewHost() from frontend/src/lib/view-host.tsx and use host.useResolvedRef(cardRef) for title/type/exists (CardLink falls back title -> raw ref; CardRef shows a 'missing' Badge and the resolved type Badge), host.openCard for follow/Open, and host.renderInline for CardRef's Expand toggle. The browser host is built in AgentViewRenderer.tsx buildViewHost(): useBrowserResolvedRef uses trpc.views.resolveRef.useQuery (procedure exists at src/webapp/trpc/routers/views.ts:57) and makeOpenCard delegates to the surface's onNavigate (companion/browse/page), so navigation is surface-correct. index.tsx installs {CardLink, CardRef} on window.__cbViewWidgets for compiled views, and node-entry.tsx exports NodeViewHostProvider with a filename-derived resolver/no-op openCard, imported by src/cli/commands/view.ts:176 for `cb view test`.

title: List cards with a frontmatter format template
story: As the box agent or a script, I want to list cards by glob or directory and print chosen frontmatter fields with a {field} template, so that I can extract card metadata without parsing files myself.
evidence: `executeLs` in commands/ls.ts expands globs/directories via `expandPath`, then `applyTemplate` substitutes `{dotted.path}` placeholders using `lookupField(loadCardFrontmatter(file))`, printing `path\tformatted` per card.

verdict.note: src/core/commands/ls.ts registers the 'ls' command with args paths (string[], required) and format; executeLs calls expandPath per argument, which globs when the pattern has glob chars, lists non-recursive .card files when it is a directory, else treats it as a literal file. With --format, applyTemplate replaces /{([^}]+)}/ via lookupField(loadCardFrontmatter(file)) (dotted paths) and writes `${relativePath}\t${formatted}`; without it, just the path. src/cli/commands/ls.ts is the commander wrapper ('cb ls <paths...> -f/--format'), exported through src/cli/commands/index.ts and added to the program at src/cli/index.ts:132, so both the box agent's command runner and the CLI reach it.

title: Mark a directory as a notable place to browse to or file into
story: As a boxholder, I want a landmark card in a directory declaring its symbol, ordering, links and expansion, so that the directory shows up as a curated navigation bookmark and as a destination triage can file things into.
evidence: LandmarkSchema ("Marks its directory as a notable spot", searchable:false) declares LandmarkNavigation (symbol/order/links/expand/chat-app) and LandmarkDestination, with parseLandmarkFields() and createLandmarkTemplate() for readers and creation.

verdict.note: src/schemas/landmark.ts defines LandmarkSchema = cardSchema("landmark", { description: "Marks its directory as a notable spot — a curated navigation bookmark and/or a triage filing destination; one per directory", searchable: false, fields: { navigation, destinations } }). LandmarkNavigation carries label/symbol (LandmarkSymbol: string or {src})/links (LandmarkLink ref+label)/expand (LandmarkExpand query, group, order via LandmarkOrder)/chat-app (LandmarkChatApp); LandmarkDestination carries for/rules/procedure. parseLandmarkFields() and createLandmarkTemplate() are exported (schemas/index.ts) and consumed by webapp/trpc/routers/landmarks.ts, core/landmark/{card-cache,summaries,features}.ts, core/triage/instructions.ts and core/box/defaults.ts — so both the navigation surface and the triage-destination use are real.

title: Move or rename a card and rewrite references
story: As the box agent or a script, I want to move or rename a card (or a whole directory of cards) and have every reference to it rewritten, so that reorganizing the box does not leave dangling refs.
evidence: `registerCommand({name:"move"})` in commands/move.ts parses from/to (single path, list, or directory), dispatches to `moveDir`/`moveOne` in move-operations.ts which relocates the file plus its attach dir (move-phase2.ts) and runs the resolution-based ref rewrite over referring cards; supports `--dry-run` and `--commit`.

verdict.note: src/core/commands/move.ts ends with registerCommand({name:"move"}) and parses from (string|string[]) / to / commit / dryRun; handleSource() dispatches directory sources to moveDir and .card sources to moveOne in move-operations.ts. move-operations.ts imports rewriteReferrerRefs/rewriteMovedCardRefs/rewriteViewRefs from src/core/rewrite-card-refs.ts and rewrites refs in every other card, plain .md, and views, reporting updatedCards. move-phase2.ts movePhase2CardFiles() renames the card file plus its sibling <basename>.attach/ dir. The CLI entry is `cb mv` (src/cli/commands/move.ts, Command("mv") with --commit/--dry-run) delegating to runCommand({name:"move"}).

title: Nav bar with live pending counts
story: As a person using the box, I want the app nav to carry my box's own menu entries and a badge for pending questions and on-plate todos, so that I can see outstanding work from any page.
evidence: core/nav.ts loads the box root's nav.card into render-ready entries for the nav tRPC router (an invalid card degrades to a health warning, not a broken menu); nav-counts.ts reads question frontmatter and todos directly so the globally-mounted status query stays cheap.

verdict.note: The nav card half checks out (core/nav.ts resolveNav -> navRouter.get, consumed by useNavMenuEntries/PlacePill; invalid nav.card degrades to status 'invalid' + health warning), and core/nav-counts.ts does read question frontmatter and todos cheaply for status.navStatus. But the app nav renders NO pending-questions badge: src/frontend/src/components/AppNav.tsx reads only `statusQuery.data.counts.onPlateTodos` and renders `PlateBadge` (plus ErrorBadge/ProfileMenu); its own comment says 'the question events this used to watch moved out with the questions badge'. `pendingQuestions` from getNavCounts is only consumed by status.status for the dashboard (AttentionCards), not by the nav bar. The story over-claims a badge for pending questions in the nav.

panel.note: The nav-card half is fully live: core/nav.ts resolveNav is exported through webapp/trpc/routers/nav.ts, mounted as `nav: navRouter` in webapp/trpc/router.ts:47, and consumed by frontend hooks/useNavMenuEntries.ts (trpc.nav.get) inside PlacePill. core/nav-counts.ts getNavCounts is imported by webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts and served by both status.navStatus and status.status. But the pending-questions badge in the nav has no code at all: AppNav.tsx:104-105 reads only `statusQuery.data.counts.onPlateTodos` and renders PlateBadge/ErrorBadge/ProfileMenu, and its own comment at line 118 says the question events it used to watch 'moved out with the questions badge'; grep finds no questions badge in AppNav.tsx or PlacePill.tsx. The only consumer of navCounts.pendingQuestions is status.status, read by the dashboard's AttentionCards.tsx, not the nav bar — so half the claimed capability is not implemented anywhere in the nav.

The nav is globally mounted: src/frontend/src/app-shell.tsx renders <AppNav> above the route Outlet on every box page, and AppNav renders <nav aria-label="Primary"> with PlacePill plus PlateBadge fed by trpc.status.navStatus.useQuery() (status.ts:65 navStatus is a publicProcedure). The box's own nav.card entries reach the UI through hooks/useNavMenuEntries.ts -> trpc.nav.get, registered as `nav: navRouter` in src/webapp/trpc/router.ts:47 and opened from PlacePill.tsx:140's switch menu. No flag or opt-in config gates any of this. The one element with no rendered control is the pending-questions badge (AppNav renders only PlateBadge/ErrorBadge/ProfileMenu; getNavCounts.pendingQuestions is consumed by status.status for the dashboard instead) - but that is an accuracy question about what the story claims exists, which is another reviewer's lens; the nav surface itself is fully reachable.

The nav-entries half holds (core/nav.ts feeds navRouter, surfaced in PlacePill's menus), but the story's badge claim over-reaches. src/frontend/src/components/AppNav.tsx reads only statusQuery.data.counts.onPlateTodos from status.navStatus and renders <PlateBadge> alongside ErrorBadge/ProfileMenu; there is no pending-questions badge anywhere in the bar, and its bus-subscription comment says 'The question events this used to watch moved out with the questions badge'. getNavCounts().pendingQuestions is still computed and returned by status.navStatus, but the only UI consumer of a pending-questions count is the dashboard's AttentionCards.tsx, which is one page, not 'any page'. So the code delivers half of the promised badge and half of the 'see outstanding work from any page' benefit.

browser.note: The primary nav has no pending-count badge. Its markup is a Place dropdown ('test1 ▸ Dashboard') and a User avatar button only; opening the Place menu gives Box: test1 / All landmarks / place switcher, and its Box submenu lists hardcoded Dashboard, Browse, History, Inventory summary, Other boxes — no box-authored nav entries and no badge for questions or todos anywhere in the nav bar, on the dashboard or elsewhere.

triage.reasoning: The pending-questions badge was deliberately retired, so the story describes a removed capability. `src/frontend/src/components/AppNav.tsx:104-105` reads only `statusQuery.data.counts.onPlateTodos` and renders PlateBadge/ErrorBadge/ProfileMenu; its bus-subscription comment says 'The question events this used to watch moved out with the questions badge.' Commit eaa86c79 ('feat(nav): single responsive bar…', Track C3 of docs/plans/top-nav-ia.md, 2026-08-02) lists 'Out: … QuestionsBadge, and the always-on chat.byLandmark fetch that fed the fresh badge' — an intentional IA decision, not a regression; pending questions surface on the dashboard's AttentionCards instead. The nav-entries half is real and reachable (core/nav.ts -> navRouter, mounted at trpc/router.ts:47, consumed by useNavMenuEntries inside PlacePill). The browser check (browser/dashboard.json) saw no badges and no box entries on test1, which matches the code given that box's data: it has no nav.card (so no box-authored section renders) and PlateBadge hides at zero on-plate todos; its ~40 pending question cards correctly produce no nav badge because none exists. Correct the story to 'the box's own menu entries plus a badge for on-plate todos'. Leftover cruft worth noting but not a user-visible gap: getNavCounts still computes `pendingQuestions` for status.navStatus with no consumer, and src/core/nav-counts.ts's header comment still claims the nav renders two badges.

title: Navigate the box from the app bar's place pill

evidence: PlacePill renders a split pill whose left half opens SwitchMenuBody (box submenu, All landmarks, per-landmark rows with fresh counts from chat.placeMenu) and whose right half opens HereMenuBody ("Open <dir>/" plus the landmark's curated links, missing targets shown inert); AppNav mounts it with the plate/error badges and profile menu, and app-bar-chrome portals page-owned chips into the bar.

verdict.note: AppNav.tsx (mounted in app-shell.tsx on every page) resolves a Place (published place or placeLabel fallback) and renders <PlacePill>. PlacePill.tsx draws a split pill: the left half opens SwitchMenuBody (PlacePill-panels.tsx: box submenu panel, 'All landmarks →' to /<box>/landmarks, per-landmark rows with FreshCount from chat.placeMenu, plus nav.card entries via useNavMenuEntries); the right half renders only when landmarks.forDir resolves a landmark and opens HereMenuBody (PlacePill-here.tsx: 'Open <dir>/', curated links/groups, links with exists=false rendered inert and marked '(missing)') or the chat-owned portal slot from app-bar-chrome.tsx. All cited backend files exist.

browser.note: App bar pill names the location ('Box: test1' at the box root, 'Browse: config/main.personality.card' on a card). Opening it shows 'Box: test1 ›', 'All landmarks →' and a SWITCH TO list of landmarks (📦 Box ✓ (current), ⚗️ Acids & Bases); the '›' sub-panel lists box destinations (Dashboard, Browse, History, Inventory summary, Other boxes →). A second 'Here: /' pill at the box root opens a directory menu ('Open /'); it is not rendered inside /browse/config.

title: Old chats and capture links keep working

title: Open images full-size with swipe and arrow navigation

title: Open views refresh when the file changes
story: As a person with a card open while the agent is editing it, I want the view to reload itself when the file changes on disk, so that I'm not reading a stale copy.
evidence: useFileData subscribes with useBusSubscription and resyncs on a matching file-change bus event plus on WebSocket reconnect (useDeferredResync); AgentViewRenderer and FigureView do the same for view modules, card data, and figure entry sources.

verdict.note: components/FileView.tsx registers useBusSubscription and, on a 'file-change' event whose boxRelativePath matches this view's path, calls resync() — utils.card.get.invalidate for cards or textQuery.refetch() for text — and also resyncs on WebSocket re-connect via useDeferredResync (skipping the first connect). components/AgentViewRenderer.tsx does the same for view modules and card data (loadCards({refetch:true}) from the file-change handler and a triggerCardsResync on reconnect), and components/FigureView.tsx recompiles via loadModule() when a file-change matches entryPath. The events are real: core/box/file-watcher.ts emits transient 'file-change' onto the EventBus (schema in core/event-bus-schemas.ts), started from webapp/trpc/routers/events.ts.

title: Page through every image in a conversation
story: As a person looking at a picture in the chat, I want the lightbox to hold every image in the whole conversation in order, so that I can step from one to the next even when the message it came from is scrolled out of the list.
evidence: `extractChatImages` walks every entry's image blocks plus markdown `![](…)` sources (cache-busted, box-slug resolved) and appends still-streaming ones from `streamText`; InteractiveChat-messages.tsx serializes the list into the hidden `data-image-list` node the lightbox provider reads, so navigation works past the virtualizer's mounted window.

verdict.note: message-parsing.ts:318 `extractChatImages(entries, {streamText, boxSlug})` iterates every entry's content blocks, pushing image-block srcs via imageBlockSrc (data: URI or imageUrl) and markdown `![](…)` matches via extractImagesFromMarkdown, which resolves via resolveImageSrc(boxSlug) and bustImageSrc; streamText is appended at the end. InteractiveChat-messages.tsx:172 memoizes JSON.stringify(extractChatImages(messages,…)) and renders it at line 224 as `<div data-image-list hidden>`. browser.note: A hidden <div data-image-list hidden> holds the conversation's images as JSON (empty [] before any images; after the agent posted two inline images it held both entries with src/alt/caption). Clicking one image opened the lightbox showing '2 / 2' with Previous/Next/Close controls, and Previous stepped to the other conversation image.

title: Peek at a file from a list without leaving the list

evidence: FileEntry draws [icon][middle slot][peek] using resolveFileTypeUI, and the peek state swaps the row for a FileView plus escalate-to-panel / open-as-page controls; file-types/builtins.tsx maps ~23 card types and path patterns onto the icon vocabulary and gives image cards ImageCardListEntry's thumbnail.

The FileEntry peek component is used by chat's Recent files panel, which I could not reach: the composer's 'Add' menu offers only Capture…/Attach file…/Upload files…/Send screenshot…/Share location. Not checkable from this page.

title: Print a card as a document
story: As a person who wants a card on paper, I want printing to drop the app chrome and let the content flow across pages, so that I get the document instead of a screenshot of a scroll pane.
evidence: index.css's @media print block forces white background, releases the shell's h-screen/h-app/min-h-0/overflow and max-h-96 constraints, and restyles .prose as a serif print layout with page-break rules; AppNav, Sidebar, ViewOverlay, FileView's toggle row and BrowseDetailPanel's header/back button all carry print:hidden, and the panel drops its card shadow and max-width in print.

verdict.note: index.css has an @media print block that forces white background/dark text, sets height:auto on .h-screen/.h-app/.h-full, min-height:0, overflow:visible on .overflow-auto/hidden/scroll, max-height:none on .max-h-96, and restyles .prose as an 11pt serif layout with page-break-after:avoid on headings, orphans/widows, and break-inside:avoid for pre/blockquote/table/img. AppNav.tsx:134 (nav) and Sidebar.tsx:44 carry print:hidden; FileView.tsx:412 hides the toggle row; BrowseDetailPanel.tsx:66-74 drops max-width/margins (print:max-w-none print:mx-0 print:py-0), removes the card shadow/background (print:bg-transparent print:shadow-none), and print:hidden on the back button and header row. Chrome is dropped and content flows as claimed.

browser.note: Printing (Chrome print rendering to PDF) a card at both /views/... and /browse/... drops the app chrome — top nav, browse sidebar and the panel header/back row are all gone — and the content flows as a white-background serif document across numbered pages ('page 1', 'page 2') instead of a clipped scroll pane.

title: Read a card in the browser as fields plus prose
story: As a person using the box, I want to open a card at its URL and see its frontmatter as a labeled field table above its rendered markdown body, with each `{ ref: … }` value as a link I can click through, so that I can read and navigate box data without touching files.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/card.ts defines loadFrontmatterCard, returning {kind:'frontmatter', frontmatter, body, validationError} and falling back to loose parseYaml when the schema is unregistered/invalid. src/frontend/src/renderers/markdown-card.tsx registers MarkdownCardView at priority 30 for data.kind === 'frontmatter'. browser.note: Opened /card/config/main.personality.card and /card/store/courses/Acids_Bases.course.card: frontmatter renders as a labeled DescriptionList field table (nested maps/lists included) above the rendered markdown body (h1/h2 headings, emphasis). title: Read a card's raw markdown source in the browser

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/renderers/builtins.tsx defines SourceRenderer and calls registerFileType({match: (_path, data) => data?.kind === 'frontmatter'}, {renderer: {name: 'Source', Component: SourceRenderer, priority: 10}}); it useQuery-fetches `${getApiBase()}/files/${data.path}` and renders resp.text() in <Pre boxed>. The module is loaded via renderers/setup.ts (`import "./builtins"`), and renderers/index.ts documents multiple renderers per file sorted by priority with a user toggle, which FileView.tsx renders as <RendererToggle> (lines 282/314/413). card.ts (trpc/routers/card.ts) is what emits kind: 'frontmatter'. The route exists: registerApiFilesRoutes in src/webapp/routes/api-files.ts registers GET /api/files/* and its comment explicitly says .card files are served as plain text there because the Source view fetches them, while card.get returns the parsed form. browser.note: A 'Source' tab sits beside 'Card' (and the typed renderer tab where one exists) on every card page checked. On config/main.personality.card it printed the verbatim file text — the `---` fenced frontmatter block with original YAML wrapping/quoting, then the prose body — matching the file on disk.

title: Read a commit's agent session log

SessionLog.tsx uses trpc.history.sessionLog.useInfiniteQuery({sessionId, limit:100}) with getNextPageParam paging, renders user/assistant EntryView rows, and ContentBlock renders tool_use blocks as an expandable button with toolName/inputSummary. The procedure exists at webapp/trpc/routers/history.ts:122 and CommitDetail is mounted from components/history/HistoryBrowser.tsx:159, so it is reachable in the web UI.

browser.note: The '▸ Session log' disclosure appears on commits carrying a Session trailer and expands to '▾', but for both session commits in this box (8d65fe14/b1aeac8f…, 8e43da37/44aa0bde…) the body reads 'Session log not found for <id>…'. The box clone at ~/src/box-worktrees/user-stories-refresh/test1 has no Claude session JSONLs (~/.claude/projects/-Users-…-user-stories-refresh-test1 contains only `memory`), so there is no transcript to render and the user/assistant entries and collapsible tool_use blocks could not be exercised. Toggle: verified. Transcript rendering: not reachable with this box's data.

title: Read a live external file through its in-box pointer, with a drift warning
story: As a person who pointed a card at a file outside the box, I want the current file rendered inline and a warning when it has changed since the card was stamped, so that I know when the card's record is out of date.
evidence: ExtfileView fetches the href through useExternalTarget (/api/external), compares the sha256 in the live markers against the card's stamped version and shows a "Stale — run cb extfile sync" banner; ExternalDocument decodes the envelope and dispatches to the renderer registry by the target's path.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/renderers/extfile.tsx registers ExtfileView for type `extfile` (wired via renderers/setup.ts). ExtfileView reads frontmatter href/version, and ExtfileLiveFile calls useExternalTarget(href) (ExternalDocument.tsx) against GET /api/external (src/webapp/routes/api-external.ts, which returns base64 bytes + buildVersionMarkers), compares sha256Of(live markers) to sha256Of(stored version) and renders the banner '⚠ Stale — the file changed since the card was last stamped. Run cb extfile sync'; ExternalDocument then dispatches to the registry renderer by path. `cb extfile sync` exists (src/cli/commands/extfile.ts → core/extfile-sync.ts). Caveat, not a refutation: api.ts mounts /api/external only when NODE_ENV !== 'production' and the file comments call it 'never mounted in production', but deploy/setup-server.sh's systemd units set no NODE_ENV, so the route is in fact mounted on the deployed server too; hrefs must also resolve under the box root or config/box.json externalRoots (core/external/roots.ts).

title: Read PDFs, JSON, plain text, and unknown binaries in place
story: As a person browsing non-card files, I want PDFs embedded, JSON shown as a readable tree, text files shown as text, and anything else shown with its size, type and a download link, so that every file in the box opens to something useful.
evidence: pdf.tsx iframes /api/files; json.tsx HEADs for size and gates anything over 1 MiB behind a "Load JSON" button before rendering JsonView; plaintext.tsx is the priority-1 text fallback; binary.tsx shows name/size/content-type, a download link, and a distinct "not fetched" state for annexed-absent (HTTP 409) files.

verdict.note: renderers/pdf.tsx registers a .pdf match rendering an iframe on `${getApiBase()}/files/<path>` (priority 30). json.tsx HEADs the file for size/content-type, auto-loads under LARGE_THRESHOLD = 1 MiB and otherwise shows name/size/type plus a 'Load JSON (size)' button and Download link, then renders components/ui/JsonView (present); invalid JSON falls back to the parse error plus raw text. plaintext.tsx registers at priority 1 for any non-directory, non-.card, non-.json, non-binary path and renders data.content in a <Pre>. binary.tsx matches isBinaryPath, shows basename/path/size/content-type plus a Download ExternalLink, and treats HEAD 409 as annexed-but-absent with a 'Content is not stored on this machine' message and no download button. All are imported by renderers/setup.ts.

browser.note: PDF: source.pdf embeds Chrome's PDF viewer with page thumbnails (12 pages). JSON: config/box.json renders as an indented key/value tree with '208 B' and a Download link. Text: msg-001.body.txt and a .ics render as plain text. Binary: a .webm shows name, 'Size: 317 KB', 'Type: audio/webm' and a Download link.

title: Read prose the way it was written
story: As a person reading a card or chat message, I want explicit URLs auto-linked but bare filenames left alone, and file sizes and ages shown in human terms, so that markdown in a box full of file references renders sensibly.
evidence: parseMarkdown() enables markdown-it linkify on the shared Markdoc tokenizer with fuzzyLink off so README.md does not become a link; formatBytes()/formatElapsed()/formatAgo() render sizes and ages; isBinaryPath() tells FileView not to fetch a binary body as text.

verdict.note: lib/markdoc-parse.ts constructs `new Tokenizer({ linkify: true })` and then sets fuzzyLink:false (plus fuzzyEmail/fuzzyIP) on the underlying linkify-it instance, so only explicit-scheme URLs auto-link and a bare README.md stays plain text; parseMarkdown is the parser used by components/Markdown.tsx (line 385), which renders card and chat prose. lib/format-bytes.ts exports formatBytes and lib/relative-time.ts exports formatElapsed/formatAgo, used in renderers (e.g. renderers/json.tsx, renderers/binary.tsx) for sizes. lib/binary-files.ts exports isBinaryPath/pathExt, consumed by components/FileView.tsx (line 133) and ExtfileView/plaintext/binary renderers to avoid fetching a binary body as text.

browser.note: Human byte formatting confirmed ('208 B' on box.json, 'Size: 317 KB' on a .webm). The linkify clause could not be tested: no card or .md body in the box contains a bare URL or a bare filename outside code spans/frontmatter (the only bare URLs are in frontmatter and in .txt/chat-thread text, which render as plain text, not markdown). No relative-age ('… ago') string appeared on any page visited.

title: Recent activity feed
story: As a boxholder, I want recent git commits and scheduler ticks interleaved newest-first on the dashboard, so that I can see what the box has been doing and jump to a commit's detail.
evidence: RecentActivity merges status.activity commits with scheduler ticks that had activity, sorts by timestamp, shows the Phase trailer badge and per-script durations, and links each commit to /$boxSlug/history/$hash plus an 'All history' link.

verdict.note: RecentActivity.tsx builds an ActivityItem[] merging `commits` (status.activity entries) with `ticks` filtered to those whose result.ran>0 || errors>0, sorts descending by ts (items.sort((a,b)=>b.ts-a.ts)) and slices 15. CommitRow links the subject to href(`/${boxSlug}/history/${commit.hash}`) and shows the `Phase` trailer badge; TickRow shows per-script names with durationMs formatted ms/s. DashboardPage.tsx runs trpc.status.activity.useQuery({count:15}) and trpc.scheduler.log.useQuery({limit:20,event:'tick'}) and passes both into <RecentActivity commits ticks/>, plus an 'All history →' link to /$boxSlug/history. router.tsx defines both /history and /history/$hash (historyDetailRoute), so the commit link resolves.

browser.note: Recent Activity lists 15 commits newest-first with subject, short hash and relative age, each linking to /user-stories-refresh/test1/history/<hash>, plus an 'All history →' link. Scheduler ticks could not be seen interleaved because this box has never run a schedule (every row's Last Run is 'never'), so no Phase badge or per-script duration appeared.

title: Reference an image by one canonical URL
story: As a person or view referencing an image, I want one URL that works whether the image is a raw file or wrapped in an image card, so that I don't have to know how the image happens to be stored.
evidence: `registerApiImageRoutes` serves `GET /api/image/*`, serving plain image files directly and resolving an `.image.card`'s `filename.ref` (`attach/...`) to the attached bytes before serving with `applyRawFileServingHeaders`.

verdict.note: src/webapp/routes/api-image.ts defines registerApiImageRoutes, registering GET /api/image/* (exposeHeadRoute) and registered from src/webapp/routes/api.ts:69. The handler serves plain image files (extension in IMAGE_EXTS) directly, and for a path ending in .image.card calls resolveImageCard, which reads filename.ref (YAML frontmatter or legacy XML ref="attach/...") and maps the virtual attach/ prefix to <stem>.attach/<file>, then serves the bytes via applyRawFileServingHeaders with ETag/Last-Modified. The frontend treats this as the canonical form: src/frontend/src/lib/view-url.ts builds `<base>/<boxSlug>/api/image/<path>` and normalizes legacy /api/files/ forms into it. image-orientation.ts is not used by this route, but it is a secondary citation and the claimed capability is fully implemented.

browser.note: One URL shape serves both storage forms: GET /api/image/box/inbox/scan-20260429T0322-dbe99514.attach/unsure-008.jpg and GET /api/image/box/inbox/scan-20260429T0320-8170f534.attach/photo-002.image.card both return 200 image/jpeg with ETag + nosniff, the second resolving the card's attached bytes.

title: Repair broken internal links
story: As an agent, I want the box's broken internal markdown links repaired by locating their targets elsewhere in the box, so that content survives reorganization and retired link schemes.
evidence: `relinkCommand` rewrites unambiguous matches and reports ambiguous ones (--dry-run, --json); `migrateViewLinksCommand` rewrites retired `view:` links to plain paths.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/relink.ts defines `relinkCommand` (`cb relink`, registered at src/cli/index.ts:108) with --dry-run and --json; it calls repairBoxLinks() from src/core/link-repair.ts and prints fixed, ambiguous (with candidate lists), and unresolvable buckets — unambiguous matches rewritten, ambiguous reported. src/cli/commands/migrate-view-links.ts defines `migrateViewLinksCommand` (registered at index.ts:109) which calls migrateBoxViewLinks() to rewrite retired `view:` links to plain paths, also with --dry-run. Both are reachable CLI commands, matching the story.

title: Saved history filter as a card
story: As a boxholder, I want a history view card whose frontmatter is a saved filter, adjustable per-visit through URL overrides that I can reset, so that a recurring history question lives in the box rather than in a bookmark.
evidence: HistoryViewCard parses HISTORY_VIEW_PARAMS (rendering an explicit error when invalid), renders HistoryBrowser without the filter bar, writes chip interactions as query-string overrides diffed against the card layer, names URL-overridden keys with a reset, and links 'Open in History' carrying the merged filter.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/history/HistoryViewCard.tsx is registered as the `history` entry in VIEW_COMPONENTS in frontend/src/renderers/view.tsx (which is the `view` card renderer, and named-views.ts registers a `history` named view), so a `view: history` card reaches it. It safeParses HISTORY_VIEW_PARAMS and renders an explicit 'Invalid history params' card on failure; paramsToFilter/filterToSearch/describeFilter in history-filter.ts convert frontmatter params to filter state; HistoryBrowser is rendered with filterBar={false} and onFilterChange=applyOverride, which diffs the next filter against params.card and navigates to the same card address with HISTORY_QUERY_CODEC query overrides. Keys whose origin is 'url' (from resolveViewParams) are listed with a 'reset' button clearing search, and an 'Open in History →' Link carries filterToSearch(merged filter) to /<box>/history.

browser.note: The renderer exists (renderers/view.tsx maps view 'history' -> HistoryViewCard) and the box's generated docs document `view: history` with params, but this box contains no `view: history` card — no *.view.card at all, and grep for '^view: history' in content/ hits only docs/generated/card-view.md. Verifying the saved-filter card, its URL overrides, the reset affordance and 'Open in History →' would require creating a card in the box (a write/commit), so I stopped.

title: See a fresh image after the agent overwrites it
story: As a person with a page open, I want an image whose file changed this session to reload rather than show the browser's cached copy, and a not-yet-written image to retry briefly instead of showing broken, so that regenerated media appears without a reload.
evidence: bumpFileVersion() records a per-path token from the file-change event and useBustedImageSrc/bustImageSrc append ?v=<token> to /api/files/ URLs; useImageRetry retries a failed image on a 500/1500/3000/5000ms schedule with the attempt count kept outside the component so a remount cannot reset the budget.

verdict.note: lib/file-version.ts holds a module-level Map of per-path tokens; bumpFileVersion is called from components/chat/InteractiveChat-ws.ts:48 on the file-change event (stampFileVersion, timestamp digits as token), and useBustedImageSrc/bustImageSrc extract the path after '/api/files/' and append ?v=<token> (used in components/chat/markdown-rendering.tsx and message-parsing.ts:299). hooks/use-image-retry.ts useImageRetry retries with RETRY_DELAYS_MS = [500,1500,3000,5000] and keeps RetryState in a module-level Map keyed by src so a remount cannot reset the budget; components/ui/Image.tsx:286 enables it via shouldRetryPrimary when retryOnError is set and there is no proxy fallback. Two narrowings worth noting but not fatal: the busting/retry entry points are chat markdown images only (no card/browse page caller), and between attempts the Image renders the ErrorPlaceholder since getLoadState treats the 'waiting' phase as errored.

title: See a running sketch on a figure card
story: As a person opening a figure card, I want its sketch compiled and mounted live with the parameters the link supplied, so that I get an interactive drawing instead of a source listing.
evidence: FigureView resolves the card's entry, imports /api/figure/module.js?path=…, coerces embed query params against the card's declared params, and hands the sketch to FigureMount, which lazily loads p5/three/d3/canvas-loop and runs the returned teardown on unmount; a file-change on the entry recompiles.

FigureView.tsx resolves frontmatter.entry against the card path (resolveRelativePath), dynamically imports `${apiBase}/figure/module.js?path=…&v=…`, coerces the URL params against the card's declared `params` via parseDeclaredParams/coerceFigureParams, and passes the sketch plus a FigureContext to <FigureMount key={paramsKey} …>; a bus `file-change` event on entryPath re-calls loadModule (recompile on edit). FigureMount.tsx loadRuntimeLib lazily import()s p5/three/@ianbicking/canvas-loop/browser/d3 and invokes the returned teardown on unmount. webapp/routes/figure.ts serves GET /api/figure/module.js, guarding path containment/attach-scope, and compiles via bundleView from webapp/views/compiler.ts, returning a figureError-exporting module on compile failure.

browser.note: store/figures/Spinner.figure.card renders a live p5 canvas with a rotating blue square (not a source listing); Bars/Cube also exist. The card declares a `size` param, but appending ?size=150 to the browse URL was stripped on navigation, so the URL-supplied-parameter clause was not verified.

title: See my remarks attached to a document and jump to the quoted span
story: As a person who annotated a saved page or an external file, I want my commentary shown above the document with each source chip jumping to the exact quoted span, so that a remark and the text it is about stay connected.
evidence: AttachedCommentary browses the host card's .attach scope for commentary cards and renders each body; WebpageView/ExtfileView pass an onJumpToQuote that uses findQuoteRange/highlightRange/scrollRangeIntoView on the rendered pane, falling back to opening the frozen snapshot at a #:~:text= fragment.

verdict.note: AttachedCommentary.tsx browses attachDirFor(cardPath) via trpc.status.browse, filters cards of type 'commentary', and renders each body through Markdown with onJumpToQuote. WebpageView.tsx (line ~98) and ExtfileView.tsx (line ~113) both render <AttachedCommentary> above the body div, and supply an onJumpToQuote that calls findQuoteRange/highlightRange/scrollRangeIntoView from lib/selection/quote-anchor on the pane ref, falling back to window.open(frozenUrl + '#:~:text=') when no in-pane match. Source.tsx's CitationChip/ContainerChip invoke linkCtx.onJumpToQuote(quoteText) on click.
