browser.note: On store/reviews/Callback_Box_Guide.extfile.card the COMMENTARY block renders above the document with the remark text and a [→] source chip. The document itself fails to load ('Couldn't load the file...') because the extfile points at an absolute path outside this checkout, so clicking the chip does nothing and jump-to-quoted-span could not be verified.

title: See the box's current state at a glance
story: As a person opening the app, I want counts and summaries of my inbox, open questions, recent activity and current context, so that I can tell what the box wants from me without digging.
evidence: `statusRouter` exposes `navStatus`, `status`, `inbox`, `questions`, `context` (via `generateContext`), `activity` (git log) and `browse`, drawing on `getSystemState` and `getNavCounts`.

verdict.note: src/webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts does expose navStatus, status, inbox, questions, activity (getLog), browse and context (generateContext from src/webapp/context.ts), and DashboardPage.tsx consumes status.status, status.activity and status.questions (AttentionCards renders questions plus status.counts.inbox). But the story's 'current context' item has no UI entry point: grep for 'status.context' across src/ returns nothing, and generateContext's only other caller is src/core/question-alert.ts. So a person opening the app gets inbox/questions/activity counts, not current context; the story over-claims on that fourth item. Also note status.inbox (the item list) is unused by the frontend — only the count from status.status is rendered.

panel.note: callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts defines statusRouter with navStatus, status, inbox, questions, context, activity and browse procedures, all built on getSystemState (core/state.ts), getNavCounts (core/nav-counts.ts), getLog (lib/git.ts) and generateContext (src/webapp/context.ts). The router is imported and mounted as `status: statusRouter` in src/webapp/trpc/router.ts, and appRouter is registered with fastifyTRPCPlugin in src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts, so it is live over HTTP. The frontend consumes it: DashboardPage.tsx calls trpc.status.status/activity/questions, AppNav.tsx calls trpc.status.navStatus, QuestionsList/QuestionCardView call trpc.status.questions. The `context` procedure has no frontend caller (grep for status.context in src/frontend finds nothing), but it is a registered procedure on a mounted router and generateContext is also used by core/question-alert.ts, so nothing here is dead or unwired; whether the browser UI surfaces context is a reachability question outside my lens.

Entry point is concrete: frontend/src/router.tsx mounts dashboardRoute at /$boxSlug/dashboard with DashboardPage, and PlacePill-panels.tsx:276 renders a 'Dashboard' MenuItem linking there (SettingsPage, AdminPage, CardViewPage, InventoryHeader also link to it). DashboardPage.tsx queries trpc.status.status, trpc.status.activity ({count:15}) and trpc.status.questions, feeding HeaderStrip/AttentionCards/RecentActivity, so inbox counts, open questions and recent git activity are all reachable by an ordinary web user with no flag or config. The one sub-item without a UI caller is status.context (generateContext) — grep shows no frontend reference — but that is a partial over-claim in the story text, not a missing entry point for the capability as a whole; the accuracy call belongs to another lens. My reachability lens is satisfied.

statusRouter (callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts) covers every item the story names: `status` returns counts.inbox/questions/pendingQuestions/onPlateTodos from getSystemState+getNavCounts, `questions` returns each pending question with prompt/memo/options, `activity` returns git log entries, and `context` returns generateContext's {summary, pendingQuestions, inboxCount} from src/webapp/context.ts — a literal one-line summary of current state. DashboardPage.tsx assembles that into one overview (HeaderStrip, AttentionCards with questions + inbox count, ScheduleOverview, RecentActivity, SystemInfo), which delivers the 'tell what the box wants from me without digging' clause. The earlier verifier's objection is that `status.context` has no frontend consumer (confirmed: generateContext's only other caller is src/core/question-alert.ts) — but that is a reachability/wiring question my lens is told to assume away, and generateContext's content is inbox count + pending questions, which the dashboard does render. Nothing in the story claims a capability broader than what these procedures compute, so my lens is satisfied.

browser.note: The dashboard shows inbox count (136), pending-question count (39) with the five newest, git cleanliness, and a recent-activity commit list — enough to tell what the box wants without digging. The 'current context' part of the story is not surfaced on this page (no context summary block on the dashboard).

title: See which changes the box made on its own and what set them off
story: As a boxholder, I want each entry in the box's history to say what triggered it — a tick, a wakeup, a connector, a procedure, a trick — so that I can tell my own edits apart from what automation did and trace a change back to the run that made it.
evidence: Automated commits carry trailers at write time — `Triggered-By: cb tick` in `tick-helpers.ts`, `cb wakeup` in `wakeup-steps.ts`, `Run-By: trick/<name>` in `trick.ts`, connector names in `connectors/*` — and `CommitRow` reads `Triggered-By` and `Phase` into each row's badge and aria-label, with `CommitDetail-commit` showing the trailers on the selected commit.

verdict.note: The trigger display is narrower than the story's list. CommitTimeline.tsx CommitRow reads only trailers.Phase and trailers['Triggered-By'] into the badge/aria-label, and CommitDetail-commit.tsx additionally shows Session, Workflow, and connector chips from CONNECTOR_KEYS (Pulled-By/Created-By/Fetched-By/Pushed-By/Sent-By). Ticks (tick-helpers.ts:233 'Triggered-By: cb tick'), wakeups (wakeup-steps.ts), and connectors do work. But a trick commits with `Run-By: trick/<name>` (src/cli/commands/trick.ts:42) and no frontend code reads 'Run-By' anywhere (grep over src/frontend returns nothing), so a trick-triggered commit gets no trigger badge; and no code in src emits a `Workflow:` trailer at all — history.ts:42 and git-log.ts only read/filter it — so the claimed 'procedure' trigger has no writer. Two of the five listed triggers are not surfaced as the story claims.

panel.note: The whole chain is live code. Writers stamp trailers at commit time (cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts:233 'Triggered-By: cb tick', cli/commands/wakeup-steps.ts:75/181/259 'cb wakeup', connectors/*.ts passing this.triggeredBy plus Pulled-By/Sent-By/Created-By, cli/commands/trick.ts:42 'Run-By: trick/<name>'); lib/git-trailers.ts (parseTrailersMulti, CONNECTOR_TRAILER_KEYS) and lib/git-log.ts parse them into HistoryCommit.trailers; CommitTimeline.tsx CommitRow renders Phase and Triggered-By into the badge row and aria-label, and CommitDetail-commit.tsx CommitTab renders phase/triggered-by/session/workflow/connector chips. It is mounted, not dead: HistoryBrowser.tsx imports both components, and it is reached from pages/HistoryPage.tsx (router.tsx:150,157) and HistoryViewCard.tsx. The earlier verifier's points (no frontend reader for 'Run-By', no writer for 'Workflow:') are about which triggers are covered/wording, not about whether implemented, wired code exists — outside this lens.

A boxholder reaches this through ordinary web-UI navigation: router.tsx registers `/history` and `/history/$hash` (HistoryPage), and links exist from the place menu (PlacePill-panels.tsx:278 'History'), card actions (CardActions.tsx:54 'View history'), MissingCardState, and the dashboard (OpsLinks.tsx, RecentActivity.tsx). HistoryPage renders HistoryBrowser -> CommitTimeline/CommitDetail, fed by tRPC `history.list` (webapp/trpc/routers/history.ts, mounted in webapp/trpc/router.ts:32) which calls getLogPaginated; lib/git-log.ts parses commit trailers via parseTrailersMulti and returns them on each commit, so CommitRow's `commit.trailers['Triggered-By']`/`Phase` badges have real data. No feature flag or config gate on the route or the components. My lens is satisfied; the earlier verifier's objection was about which triggers get displayed (coverage), not reachability, which is another reviewer's call.

The story enumerates five trigger kinds (tick, wakeup, connector, procedure, trick), but the UI only surfaces three. CommitTimeline.tsx:156-157 reads only trailers.Phase and trailers['Triggered-By'], and CommitDetail-commit.tsx reads Phase, Triggered-By, Session, Workflow, and CONNECTOR_KEYS (Pulled-By/Created-By/Fetched-By/Pushed-By/Sent-By) — which covers cb tick (tick-helpers.ts:233), cb wakeup (wakeup-steps.ts:75,181,259), and connectors. Tricks commit with `Run-By: trick/<name>` (cli/commands/trick.ts:42) and procedures commit with `Procedure: <name>` / `Step: <id>` (core/procedure/engine.ts:163, engine-step.ts:152,184,272, engine-orchestrate.ts:104); grep over src/frontend/src finds no reader for either key, so those rows get no trigger badge or chip. The 'trace a change back to the run' clause is likewise partial: the Workflow chip/facet the UI offers (CommitDetail-commit.tsx:108, git-log.ts:230, history.ts:42) has no writer anywhere in src, and nothing links a procedure commit to its run directory. Code delivers a narrower capability than the story's literal claim.

browser.note: Timeline rows carry a trigger badge and say it in the aria-label — e.g. 'Commit 993f5e8, Sync templates from upstream, 1h ago, triggered by generateDocs' and 'triggered by cb wakeup' on the Gmail pulls; rows without a trigger (hand/procedure commits) show none, so automated vs. manual is distinguishable at a glance. The selected commit's detail repeats the trigger ('cb wakeup') and shows related trailers as chips — 'pulled: gmail-connector', 'Procedure: process-retrospective', 'Step: fix-views', 'Commit-Source: procedure-fallback', 'session: b1aeac8f…' — and the session chip/filter traces the change back to the run (?session=<id> narrows the timeline to that run's commits).

triage.reasoning: Confirmed against both the code and the running box. Three of the five triggers the story names work: tick (cli/commands/tick-helpers.ts:233 'Triggered-By: cb tick'), wakeup (wakeup-steps.ts:75/181/259), and connectors (Pulled-By/Created-By/Fetched-By/Pushed-By/Sent-By plus Triggered-By) — CommitTimeline.tsx:157 reads Triggered-By into the row badge and aria-label, CommitDetail-commit.tsx adds session/workflow/connector chips, and the browser pass saw 'triggered by cb wakeup' rows and a session chip that filters the timeline to a run. The other two are not surfaced. Procedures write `Procedure: <name>` / `Step: <id>` (core/procedure/engine.ts:163, engine-step.ts:152/184/272, engine-phase.ts:185, engine-orchestrate.ts:104) and tricks write `Run-By: trick/<name>` (cli/commands/trick.ts:42); grep over src/frontend/src finds no reader for either key, so those rows carry no trigger badge and read like hand edits in the badge column. Worse, the axis that would cover them is stale: the History filter bar's 'Workflow' facet (HistoryFilterBar.tsx:72, git-log.ts:230 getTrailerFacets, history.ts:42 `^Workflow: `) keys on the PRE-RENAME trailer name — in ~/src/box-worktrees/user-stories-refresh/test1 the log holds 104 `Workflow:` trailers, all from commits subjected '[workflow] …' before the workflow→procedure rename, and 54 `Procedure:` trailers from current runs. So the filter offers only ancient runs (process-captures, process-news, test-echo) as options and cannot select a single procedure run made since the rename. The trailers are visible in the detail pane only incidentally: stripTrailers (CommitDetail-commit.tsx:33) doesn't strip Procedure/Step/Run-By, so they render as leftover body text rather than as chips.

title: Summarize files for list views
story: As a person browsing the box, I want list views to show a real title and typed metadata for each file without loading its full content, so that directory and search listings stay readable and fast.
evidence: core/loader-registry.ts dispatches a file to a FileLoader by exact card type first, then path pattern, falling back to a filename-derived title; loader-registrations.ts registers the built-ins, and file-summary.ts is the slim FileSummary shape the files.summarize endpoint returns.

verdict.note: The loader machinery exists (core/file-summary.ts FileSummary/titleFromFilename, core/loader-registry.ts resolveLoader/summarize with type-then-path-then-fallback dispatch, loader-registrations.ts registering exactly two loaders: memo and image) and webapp/trpc/routers/files.ts exposes files.summarize. But its only consumer is frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts -> components/chat/RecentFilesPanel.tsx, i.e. the recent-files strip in chat. Directory listings do NOT use it: status.browse in webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts builds its listing itself with parseCardName + loadCardFrontmatter and returns only name/type/status/title, never touching the loader registry or typed attrs. And there is no search endpoint at all in the tRPC routers, so 'search listings' has no implementation. The story over-claims scope.

panel.note: All five cited files exist with live code. core/file-summary.ts defines FileSummary/LoaderInput/FileLoader plus titleFromFilename; core/loader-registry.ts implements registerTypeLoader/registerPathLoader, resolveLoader with type-then-path-then-fallback dispatch, and summarize() which also lifts the global contains: field; core/loader-registrations.ts registers the real memoLoader (src/schemas/memo.ts:89) and imageLoader (src/schemas/image.tsx:159). webapp/trpc/routers/files.ts imports both, calls registerBuiltinLoaders() at module load, parses cards via loadCardFile/buildLoadContext (or reads small non-card files) and exposes files.summarize, and filesRouter is mounted at webapp/trpc/router.ts:44 (files:). It has a live client: frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts calls trpc.files.summarize (routed over POST in lib/trpc/index.ts) and feeds RecentFilesPanel, which is rendered by components/chat/ContextMenuBody.tsx. shared/card-name.ts also exists and is imported by core/card-io.ts, core/search/walk.ts and frontend view-widgets. The prior verifier's objection was about which listings consume it (scope/reachability), not about whether the code exists or is wired — that is another reviewer's lens.

There is a live, unflagged entry point: src/webapp/trpc/router.ts:44 mounts filesRouter, and src/webapp/trpc/routers/files.ts:71 exposes files.summarize as a publicProcedure that calls summarize() from core/loader-registry.ts and returns the slim FileSummary from core/file-summary.ts. On the web UI side, frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts:126 calls trpc.files.summarize.useQuery, feeding RecentFilesPanel.tsx, which renders per-file FileEntry rows with the loader-derived title/metadata; that panel is mounted by ContextMenuBody.tsx:109/177 from ChatBarChrome.tsx:137, i.e. a real menu a person in the chat UI clicks. No feature flag or unset config gates it. Whether other listings (status.browse directory listing, search) also use this path is a scope/accuracy question for another lens; my lens is satisfied.

The summarize machinery is real (core/file-summary.ts, core/loader-registry.ts resolveLoader/summarize with type-then-path-then-fallback dispatch, files.summarize in webapp/trpc/routers/files.ts), but it is narrower than the story's wording. Typed metadata exists for exactly two card types: loader-registrations.ts registers only memo and image; every other file falls through to fallbackLoader, which returns {path, title: titleFromFilename(path)} and no attrs at all, so 'typed metadata for each file' overstates it. The benefit clause names surfaces the code does not serve: BrowsePage.tsx calls trpc.status.browse, and status.ts's browse handler builds its own listing with parseCardName + loadCardFrontmatter returning only name/type/status/title, never touching the loader registry; core/search/extract.ts imports titleFromFilename but not summarize, and no tRPC search-listing endpoint consumes summaries. The sole consumer of files.summarize is frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts feeding the chat RecentFilesPanel — a chat strip, not directory or search listings. Also, summarizePath loads the whole card via loadCardFile (and reads non-card files up to 64KB), so 'without loading its full content' holds only for what ships over the wire.

browser.note: List rows carry derived titles and typed metadata without opening files: 'Box — landmark', 'briefing — briefing', 'main, personality card', 'Charles_Babbage — person — active', directory rows with item counts (box/ 792, config/ 24). Same summaries drive the browse sidebar and the directory renderer.

triage.reasoning: The user-facing claim is true and was watched working: the browser check (browser/browse-1.json) confirmed list rows carrying derived titles and typed metadata without opening files ('Charles_Babbage — person — active', 'briefing — briefing', directory rows with item counts). The exists and reachable lenses both cleared the story; only the wording lens refuted, and its objection is about plumbing and one extra clause, not about the capability. It is right on two narrow points: (a) the loader registry the story cites (core/loader-registry.ts + core/loader-registrations.ts, which registers only memo and image loaders) is consumed by files.summarize -> frontend/src/hooks/useRecentFiles.ts -> components/chat/RecentFilesPanel.tsx, i.e. the chat recent-files strip; the browse directory listing is built separately by the status.browse handler in webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts using parseCardName + loadCardFrontmatter; and (b) there is no search router at all in webapp/trpc/routers/, so 'search listings' has no implementation. Both are catalog corrections: the story stays, its file list should gain webapp/trpc/routers/status.ts, and the benefit clause should say directory and recent-file listings rather than search.

title: Switch between alternate renderers for a file
story: As a person viewing a card, I want to toggle between the renderers that match it (e.g. its typed view versus the raw Source), so that I can drop to the underlying text when the pretty view isn't what I need.
evidence: RendererToggle in FileView.tsx renders a button per registered renderer sorted by priority; onSelectRenderer lets the host (browse) keep the choice in the URL's ?view= param, and renderers/builtins.tsx registers the Source renderer for every frontmatter card.

verdict.note: FileView.tsx's RendererToggle renders one button per entry of `renderers` (returns null when <2), and `renderers` comes from getRenderers() in file-type-registry.ts, which filters matching entries and .toSorted((a,b)=>b.priority-a.priority). The active renderer is `requested ? renderers.find(...) : renderers.at(0)` where requested comes from rendererName (the ?view= param) or a local pick; onSelectRenderer is wired in BrowsePage.tsx's handleSelectRenderer which calls onNavigate with search {...urlParams, view: name, replace:true}, and BrowsePage parses `view` out of the query into `viewer` passed back as rendererName via BrowseDetailPanel. renderers/builtins.tsx does registerFileType({match:(_path,data)=>data?.kind==='frontmatter'},{renderer:{name:'Source',...,priority:10}}), so every frontmatter card gets a Source renderer alongside its typed one.

browser.note: The detail panel offers a button per matching renderer — 'Card'/'Source' for a personality card, 'Image'/'Download' for a jpg. Clicking Source swapped the body to the raw YAML front matter and put the choice in the URL as ?view=Source; the same toggle appears on the /card page.

title: Tap to reveal content held back on purpose
story: As a person working through material the agent redacted (a quiz answer, a hint), I want it blurred until I tap it, so that I can attempt something first and check afterwards.
evidence: RedactedInline/RedactedBlock render the {% redacted %} body under a blur plus an animated SVG-turbulence overlay with role="button" and Enter/Space handling; revealing keeps a tint so the span still reads as previously redacted. Registered in Markdown.tsx's component map.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/Redacted.tsx defines Shimmer (role="button", tabIndex=0, onClick + Enter/Space onKeyDown, blur(6px) saturate(0) plus an inline feTurbulence noise data-URL overlay with a redacted-shimmer keyframe animation) wrapped by RedactedInline/RedactedBlock, which flip a useState and then render the children with REVEALED_TINT="text-info-dark" and data-redacted="revealed" so revealed content still reads as previously redacted. Markdown.tsx lines 33 and 341-342 import and register RedactedInline/RedactedBlock in the Markdoc component map, and src/shared/markdoc-config.ts line 303 defines the `redacted` tag schema (registered at line 472), so agent-authored {% redacted %} bodies actually reach these components. The file's own header names quiz answers and hints as the use case, matching the story.

title: The UI updates when the box changes
story: As a person using the box, I want pages to refresh when the agent edits a file or a job progresses, so that I see the box's current state without reloading.
evidence: The SQLite-backed EventBus persists and dispatches events cross-process with cursor replay, validated on read by the per-event zod schemas in event-bus-schemas.ts; core/box/file-watcher.ts watches box directories (capped at MAX_WATCHED_DIRS, high-churn trees excluded, throttled per event+path) and emits `file-change` onto that bus for the events.subscribe subscription.

verdict.note: core/event-bus.ts + event-bus-schemas.ts define the validated event map (file-change, cards-changed, command-complete, chat-task, schedule-fired, capture-status, ...). core/box/file-watcher.ts watches the box root (MAX_WATCHED_DIRS = 1024, COALESCE_MS throttling per event+path) and calls `this.eventBus.emitTransient("file-change", ...)` at line 404. webapp/trpc/routers/events.ts `eventsRouter.subscribe` starts that watcher and streams bus events over the tRPC WebSocket with cursor replay and transient coalescing (MAX_BUS_QUEUE). frontend/src/hooks/useBusSubscription.ts consumes `trpc.events.subscribe.useSubscription` and is used by FileView, FigureView, AppNav, AgentViewRenderer, QuestionsList and the chat WS hook, each refetching (often through useDeferredResync) on matching events — FileView.tsx:182 refetches when a `file-change` path matches the viewed file. Pages therefore update without a reload.

title: Trash cards with their attachments
story: As the box agent or a script, I want to move one or more cards plus their attach scopes into box/trash and be told which other cards still reference them, so that deleting content is reversible and I can see what I would break.
evidence: `executeTrash` in commands/trash.ts calls `reportInboundRefs` (findInboundCardRefs), then `trashOne` renames card + `attachDirFor` scope into `getBoxDir(boxRoot,"trash")` with a timestamp suffix on collision, with `--dry-run` and an optional commit; `rollbackTrashReceipt`/`recoverTrashReceipt` undo or reconstruct an uncommitted trash receipt.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/commands/trash.ts: executeTrash accepts multiple paths, runs reportInboundRefs (which calls findInboundCardRefs and writes 'Inbound ref: ...' lines plus returns inboundRefs in the result data), and trashOne renames the card into getBoxDir(boxRoot,'trash') with a timestamp-suffixed name on collision and also renames attachDirFor(sourcePath) (the attach scope), rolling the card back if the attach move fails. --dry-run and --commit are honored, and trash-recovery.ts exports rollbackTrashReceipt/recoverTrashReceipt. The CLI entry is `cb rm` (src/cli/commands/trash.ts) with --dry-run/--commit/--reason. Only wording nit: the trash dir comes from BOX_DIRS (store/trash per paths.ts), not literally 'box/trash'.

title: Use an agent-written view on a card
story: As a person whose box agent wrote a custom view for a card type, I want that view rendered as the card's own presentation, kept fed with the matching cards and files, and reloaded when its source changes, so that the box can build me a purpose-made screen.
evidence: FileView's useCardViewBinding prepends the bound view as a priority-100 renderer backed by AgentViewRenderer, which imports /api/views/<slug>/module.js, fetches /api/views/<slug>/cards through a coalescer, reloads on file-change/reconnect, and wraps the component in ViewErrorBoundary with a Retry.

verdict.note: FileView.tsx line 344 calls useCardViewBinding(data?.type) and, when a binding exists, prepends {name, Component: Bound, priority: 100} ahead of the built-in renderers, where Bound renders <AgentViewRenderer>. view-bindings.ts builds the type->slug map from trpcClient.views.list (rendersCardTypes), invalidates on a file-change matching /^views\/.+\.tsx$/ and on bus reconnect. AgentViewRenderer dynamically imports `${apiBase}/views/${slug}/module.js?v=<version>`, fetches `/api/views/:slug/cards` through createFetchCoalescer, sets both cards and files from the response, resyncs on file-change/reconnect, and wraps the component in <ViewErrorBoundary onRetry={loadModule} resetKey={reloadSeq}>. src/webapp/routes/views.ts registers both GET /api/views/:slug/module.js and /api/views/:slug/cards (cards + non-card files).

browser.note: The box's views/ directory contains only AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md — there is no agent-written view module to bind, so no card can exercise AgentViewRenderer. Every card viewed fell back to its builtin renderer.

title: View a photo card with its analysis

title: View and delete raw box files
story: As a person browsing my box, I want images, audio and other raw files served with caching and safe content headers, and to be able to delete one, so that attachments are viewable in the app without being a security hazard.

title: Views render live box data
story: As a box agent, I want a view to receive the cards and files matched by its dependency globs, including each card's attachments and git status, so that the interface I write for a card type shows real, current box content.

title: Watch a linked video inline instead of a broken image

title: Zoom and dismiss a photo by touch
story: As a person viewing an image on a touch device, I want double-tap zoom, pinch, pan, and swipe-to-dismiss with spring settling, so that looking at a photo feels like the photo viewer I already know.
evidence: useLightboxGestures owns the element refs and LightboxGestureController lifecycle; the controller feeds pointer events (LightboxPointerTracker) through the pure reduceGesture machine and executes actions against LightboxRenderTarget, which writes transform/dismiss offsets and runs the rAF springs.

verdict.note: use-lightbox-gestures.ts owns rootRef/figureRef/wrapperRef/imgRef and the LightboxGestureController lifecycle; the controller (lightbox-gesture-controller.ts) tracks pointers, feeds container-centered points into the pure reduceGesture machine (lightbox-gesture-reducer.ts with modes pending/dismissing/swiping/panning/pinching/settling), and executes actions such as toggleZoom, beginPan, beginPinch, beginDismiss, settleDismiss, close against LightboxRenderTarget (lightbox-render-target.ts, which has toggleZoom(anchor) fit<->ZOOM_SCALE and writes transform/dismiss offsets). lightbox-spring.ts is the critically-damped rAF spring used for snap-back/settle. Double-tap pairing is real (lastTap state, toggleZoom action at reducer line 183) and dismiss uses shouldDismiss(velocityY, displacementY, viewportHeight). Reachable: ImageLightbox.tsx uses the hook and LightboxProvider is mounted in main.tsx, opened from Image.tsx and ChatAttachments.tsx.

title: A camera roll of photos routes through upload instead of the message
story: As a person attaching many photos at once, I want the selection routed through the upload pipeline past a small inline limit, so that the send does not die on the device under a huge inline payload.

verdict.note: photo-batch-threshold.ts exports INLINE_PHOTO_LIMIT = 4 and shouldBatchPhotos({existingInline, incoming}) returning existingInline + incoming > 4. InteractiveChat-attachments.ts `useChatAttachments.addImageFiles` calls it with draft.images.length + draft.pendingImages and, when true, calls onBatchPhotos({files, foldInComposerImages}) and returns 0 instead of base64-encoding via processImageBlob; InteractiveChat.tsx line 215 wires onBatchPhotos to `openWithPhotos` from useBulkUploadLaunch, so the selection goes to the bulk-upload pipeline rather than the inline /chat/send payload. ios-app/CallbackBox/Models/BulkPhotoThreshold.swift mirrors the rule (inlineLimit = 4, shouldBatch) and is called at NativeComposerView.swift:1039. The path applies to picker, paste and drop alike, matching the story.

title: A capture still arrives when transcription is down
story: As a person recording a voice note while the transcription provider is unavailable, I want the capture delivered anyway with a 'transcription failed' badge and the flag recorded on the card, so that my audio is in the box and the missing text can be filled in later instead of the whole capture being held up.
evidence: prepare.ts sets `transcriptionFailed = transcription.transcribed < transcription.total` and passes it into the delivered wrapper, which encodes `transcription-failed="1"`; CaptureChip renders a `transcription failed` badge from the parsed model. The capture-session schema documents the `transcription-failed` field and the audio schema tells the agent to retry via `cb chat retranscribe --file` and to record a `transcription-error` if that also fails.

verdict.note: The previously-flagged gap is fixed. prepare.ts:249 now calls recordTranscriptionOutcome({ sessionCardAbsPath, transcriptionFailed }) at step c, before the timeline reassembly (step d) and before validation (step e). write-cards.ts:287-308 implements it: it reads the just-written capture-session card, sets fields["transcription-failed"] = true when transcriptionFailed (or deletes the key when false, since the schema declares it optional), and writes the card back via serializeCardText — so the flag is a real persisted frontmatter field, not just documentation. timeline.ts:257 rewrites the body while re-emitting split.frontmatterText verbatim, so the flag written in step c survives into the committed card. Delivery is still not blocked by transcription failure (transcribeCaptureClips collects per-clip errors, prepare.ts:235 computes transcriptionFailed = transcription.transcribed < transcription.total from that, and the wrapper is built and delivered regardless), and CaptureChip.tsx still renders the 'transcription failed' badge from the parsed delivered-user-message wrapper. Both conjuncts of the story now hold: the capture is delivered with the chat badge, and the flag is recorded on the card itself.

title: A scan is checked at the door, before the box keeps it
story: As a scanning machine, I want each uploaded file sniffed for magic bytes that agree with its claimed extension and structurally checked (`qpdf --check` for PDFs, a full decode for images) before the box says it accepted it, so that a truncated scan or a file that isn't what its name claims is refused while I still hold the original.
evidence: `validateScanFile` checks the extension against `ACCEPTED_TYPES`, compares `fileTypeFromFile` magic bytes to it, then runs `checkPdf` (qpdf, time-boxed) or `checkImage` (a sharp resize that walks every pixel). The PUT handler in scan-upload.ts answers 422 with the reason on `rejected`, and — when qpdf is missing — 503 with `status: "server-error"` while recording nothing, so the uploader retries rather than discarding its copy.

verdict.note: validateScanFile in callback-box/src/core/scan/validate.ts checks the claimed extension against ACCEPTED_TYPES, sniffs magic bytes with fileTypeFromFile and rejects on mismatch, then runs checkPdf (qpdf --check, 20s timeout, exit 0/3 clean) for .pdf or checkImage (dynamic sharp import, failOn:"error", resize to 32x32 forcing a full decode) for images. The PUT handler in callback-box/src/webapp/routes/scan-upload.ts calls it on the temp file before renaming into quarantine: status "rejected" records a rejected quarantine entry and replies 422 with the reason, and status "unavailable" (qpdf missing) rm's the temp file, records nothing, and replies 503 {status:"server-error"} so the uploader retries. registerScanUploadRoutes is wired per box in webapp/server-box-scope.ts:309.

title: Analyze scanned photos with a vision model
story: As a boxholder, I want batches of scanned photos described by a vision model, with each analysis provably attached to the right page, so that a scan import produces usable per-photo detail.
evidence: selectScanVisionBackend() picks Claude (default, via createClaudeScanVision) or Gemini (CB_SCAN_VISION=gemini plus a resolved key); analyzeBatch enforces batch alignment and classifies failures as transient/split/batch/fatal for the scan-import runner.

verdict.note: src/services/scan-vision.ts defines selectScanVisionBackend (default 'claude' from CB_SCAN_VISION, 'gemini' only with a resolved key, else a fail-closed err) and the ScanVisionService.analyzeBatch contract with ScanVisionRetry = transient|split|batch|fatal. resolveScanVision in src/core/commands/scan-import-session.ts wires it: Gemini via createGeminiScanVision or Claude via createClaudeScanVision (src/services/scan-vision-claude.ts, backend 'claude'), and src/core/commands/scan-import.ts calls resolveScanVision before running batches. Batch alignment is enforced by assertBatchAlignment in scan-import-gemini.ts throwing ScanBatchMisalignedError, which scan-vision.ts/scan-vision-claude.ts classify as 'split' for the runner; the entry point is the `cb scan-import` command (src/cli/commands/scan-import.ts).

title: Approve or decline the agent's request to see my screen
story: As a person whose agent asked for a screenshot, I want a consent popup that expires on its own and an ephemeral confirmation of what was shared, so that the agent can only see my screen when I say yes.
evidence: `useScreenshotRequests` takes `screenshot-request` bus events matching this tab's exact session (`matchesRequestSession`), acks, tries the clerk extension relay (`captureViaRelay`) and otherwise queues ScreenshotConsentPopup, whose Share captures directly on click and Decline/Escape/expiry post declined or nothing; ScreenshotIndicatorStrip shows the shared thumbnail briefly.

verdict.note: components/chat/screenshot-request-handler.ts: useScreenshotRequests(sessionId) filters bus events with matchesRequestSession + isRequestExpired, fire-and-forget postAck, tries captureViaRelay (screenshot-relay.ts) and otherwise dispatches {type:'enqueue'} so ScreenshotConsentPopup renders for the FIFO head (wired via ScreenshotRequestUI in InteractiveChat-view.tsx, event fed by InteractiveChat-ws.ts onScreenshotRequest). ScreenshotConsentPopup.tsx has Share (shareViaPopup -> captureTabScreenshot under the click) / Decline, treats Escape and click-away as declineViaPopup ({declined:true}), and a setTimeout to Date.parse(expiresAt) auto-dismisses posting nothing. ScreenshotIndicatorStrip.tsx renders 'screenshot shared with the agent' rows with a thumbnail that self-dismiss after INDICATOR_TTL_MS = 6s and revoke the object URL. Caveat noted, not fatal: when the clerk extension relay answers, the capture is silent with no per-request popup — the 'only when I say yes' consent there is the prior act of installing/enabling the extension.

title: Ask a question about a recording
story: As a person who recorded audio, I want to ask a question about the recording itself — tone, pronunciation, what that sound was — rather than only get a transcript, so that the agent can answer things text cannot carry.
evidence: core/audio-question.ts sends the audio to gemini-2.5-flash (Claude has no audio input modality) with the box's Gemini key resolved by gemini-key.ts; `cb chat ask-about-audio` is the consumer.

The consumer askAboutAudioCommand in src/cli/commands/chat-audio.ts is registered on the chat command (src/cli/commands/chat.ts:283 .addCommand(askAboutAudioCommand)) and fetches the message's recording via fetchLastAudio, passing the system transcript along; the agent prompt in src/core/chat/session/prompts.ts instructs agents to use it. Reachable and does what the story says.

title: Attach images and files to a message
story: As a person composing a message, I want to paste, drop, or pick images and files into the composer and see them as removable thumbnails/chips, so that I can send the agent things to look at alongside my words.
evidence: `useChatAttachments` downscales pasted/dropped images and uploads files, inserting `[imageN]`/`[fileN]` tokens at the caret via `insertTokensAtCursor`; `handlePaste`/`handleDrop` in InteractiveChat-actions.ts feed `extractImageFiles`; AttachmentPanel/FileAttachmentPanel render and remove them.

A pasted image produced a thumbnail chip with an ×. Sent messages render the attachment as a chip on the user bubble.

title: Automatically transcribe every recorded clip in a capture
story: As a person recording a voice memo, I want each audio clip transcribed with word timings and the text written back onto its audio card, so that my spoken capture is searchable, readable text rather than an opaque media file.
evidence: `transcribeCaptureClips` walks every `.audio.card` with `status: new`, calls `transcribeAudio({ options: { wordTimestamps: true } })`, writes `transcript`/`filename.duration` back with `status: transcribed`, and drops a `<basename>.timing.json` sidecar; already-transcribed clips are skipped so a re-run doesn't re-bill.

It is reachable from the web UI: core/capture/prepare.ts:226 calls it, and prepareCaptureSession is invoked from webapp/routes/capture.ts (lines 63, 253) and from resume.ts. title: Be told about delivered captures nobody ever filed
story: As a box operator, I want the sweep to report delivered capture documents still sitting in a chat's `tmp-capture/` a week later, so that captures the agent forgot to file don't accumulate unnoticed in scratch space.

It is reachable: src/cli/commands/wakeup.ts:70 and src/webapp/routes/capture.ts:60 both call sweepAbandonedCaptures, and src/webapp/trpc/routers/health-stale.ts also surfaces findStaleTmpCaptureCards. title: Be told the camera or mic is blocked, with the way to unblock it
story: As a person opening capture on a device where I denied camera or microphone access, I want the surface to name the refusal and offer a jump to Settings while still letting me capture with whatever is available, so that a blocked permission is a fixable message rather than a dead black screen.
evidence: CaptureAcquisition.requestCameraPermission returns false for .denied/.restricted, raising CaptureAcquisitionError.cameraPermissionDenied; NativeCaptureController sets surfaceState.canOpenSettings on that exact error (and on microphonePermissionDenied) and openSettings() opens UIApplication.openSettingsURLString, while the surface stays .active with cameraAvailable = false. NativeCaptureView renders the banner with the Settings button. On the web the equivalent failures ('Camera access failed', 'Microphone access failed') land in useCaptureSession's error state and render as a dismissible CaptureErrorBanner over the viewport.

verdict.note: CaptureAcquisition.swift:452 requestCameraPermission returns false for .denied/.restricted and line 416-417 throws CaptureAcquisitionError.cameraPermissionDenied; NativeCaptureController.swift:433 sets surfaceState.canOpenSettings when the camera-start error is exactly that case, and line 564 does the same for microphonePermissionDenied, while both paths keep surfaceState.phase = .active (only cameraAvailable flips false, disabling the photo/video buttons at NativeCaptureView.swift:281/304). openSettings() at controller line 349 opens UIApplication.openSettingsURLString, and NativeCaptureView.swift:238-239 renders the Settings button in the error banner when canOpenSettings. On the web the parallel failures are the 'Camera access failed' / 'Microphone access failed' strings set in useCaptureCamera.ts:71 and useCaptureSession.ts:155, rendered by the dismissible CaptureErrorBanner overlay (no Settings jump there, which the story does not claim).

The 'jump to Settings' affordance is iOS-native (NativeCaptureView) and cannot be checked from a browser. Note the banner overlaps the device-settings labels (pageNotes).

title: Be told when a clip's audio bytes aren't actually present
story: As a box operator, I want a clip whose audio is only an annex pointer to be reported as absent content instead of being shipped to the transcription provider, so that a missing-content problem reads as missing content rather than as an opaque provider error.
evidence: `transcribeCaptureClips` calls `readAssetContent(audioPath)` first and, when `!audio.ok`, pushes `describeAbsentContent(audio.error.pointer, …)` into the per-clip `errors` array and skips the provider call entirely — the comment notes that ~101 bytes of pointer text would otherwise come back as garbage or an opaque API error.

verdict.note: src/core/capture/transcribe-clips.ts line 97 calls `readAssetContent(audioPath)` before any provider call; on `!audio.ok` it pushes `${cardFile}: ${describeAbsentContent(audio.error.pointer, path.basename(audioPath))}` into `errors` and `continue`s, so `transcribeAudio` is never reached. The comment there is exactly the '101 bytes of pointer text is not audio... garbage or an opaque API error' rationale. src/lib/asset-content.ts returns `{kind:'not-present', pointer}` via probePointer/parseAnnexPointer, and src/lib/annex-pointer.ts:124 describeAbsentContent produces 'content not present locally (N bytes, sha256 …). Fetch it with `git annex get …`'. All three cited files implement the claim.

title: Bound what a capture client can write into the box
story: As a box operator, I want staged uploads capped in bytes and item count and confined to their own session directory, so that a runaway or hostile client can't fill the disk or overwrite the session manifest.
evidence: `enforceStagingLimits` throws `StagingByteLimitError`/`StagingItemLimitError` past `MAX_STAGED_BYTES` (1 GiB) or `MAX_STAGED_ITEMS` (500), called inside the per-session lock; `resolveStagedFile` + `assertStagingFilename` reject path traversal, `session.json*`, and any dot-leading filename.

verdict.note: staging-limits.ts defines MAX_STAGED_BYTES = 1 GiB and MAX_STAGED_ITEMS = 500, and enforceStagingLimits() throws StagingByteLimitError/StagingItemLimitError counting audio chunks + photos + files; it is called from staging-store.ts mutateSession() inside withStagingLock (and from staging-stream.ts:104 for streamed uploads), so concurrent uploads cannot jointly overshoot. staging-store.ts assertStagingFilename() rejects 'session.json', 'session.json.*' and any dot-leading name, and resolveStagedFile() re-resolves against the session dir and throws StagingPathError on escape. webapp/routes/capture-upload.ts calls resolveStagedFile for a 400 on a bad filename and maps isStagingLimitError to HTTP 413; the handler is wired at webapp/routes/capture.ts:183. upload-replay.ts handleStagingUploadReplay makes a re-uploaded filename idempotent and conflicts on differing bytes.

title: Bulk file upload from the composer
story: As a person with a folder of files to hand the box, I want an upload overlay that streams them with per-item state and per-item retry, so that a big batch lands in this chat and any failure is named rather than silent.
evidence: BulkUploadOverlay is launched from the composer's Add menu bound to targetSessionId, showing queued/uploading/uploaded/failed badges with a retry action; the bulk routes predeclare an item registry and stream each item to disk via addFileStreamed, hashing and counting bytes as it goes.

verdict.note: BulkUploadOverlay.tsx renders a fixed-inset role=dialog with an ItemRow per file showing Badge states from STATE_LABEL (queued/uploading/uploaded/failed) and an InlineAction 'retry' calling bulk.retry(id) on failed items; failures are also named in the footer counts and the 'Deliver with N failed' button label. It is launched from the composer: InteractiveChat.tsx line 214 uses useBulkUploadLaunch (openEmpty), wired at line 332 as onUploadFiles to the composer's 'Upload files…' Add-menu entry (InteractiveChat-composer.tsx:236), and the overlay is bound to targetSessionId so the batch lands in that chat. Server side, registerBulkUploadRoutes (webapp/routes/bulk-upload.ts, registered in server-box-scope.ts:275) calls addFileStreamed from core/capture/staging-stream.ts, which streams each predeclared registry item to a temp file while hashing and counting bytes.

browser.note: Add > 'Upload files...' opens a full-screen 'Upload files' overlay with an Add files button plus a drag-and-drop target, one row per file, a running '0 uploaded / 2 failed / 0 pending — 50 B total' counter, and Cancel batch / 'Deliver with 2 failed'. Each failed row showed a 'Failed' badge, a named reason ('Could not register with server'), and its own 'retry' link, with the batch-level cause banner 'Create bulk batch failed: Not authenticated'. So the failure-naming and per-item retry contract is confirmed; I could not observe a successful transfer because the bulk endpoint rejected the session (see pageNotes).

title: Bulk-upload files with content-hash dedup
story: As an operator or upload worker, I want to push a batch of files into the box grouped into scan sessions and skipped when their SHA-256 is already in the upload ledger, so that re-running an import does not create duplicate cards.
evidence: `executeUpload` validates `--as scan`, groups files with `groupScanFiles`, hashes each with `sha256File`, skips groups whose hashes are all in the ledger unless `--force`, dispatches the rest to `runCommand({name:"scan-import"})`, and records entries under the ledger lock via `updateLedger`.

verdict.note: src/core/commands/upload.ts `executeUpload` validates `--as <kind>` against SUPPORTED_KINDS=['scan'], resolves/stats files, groups via `groupScanFiles` (upload-helpers.ts, pdf singletons + image pairs), and per group `processGroup` hashes each file with `sha256File`, skips when every hash is already in the ledger (`findEntry`) unless `--force`, otherwise dispatches `runCommand({name:'scan-import'})` and records entries via `updateLedger` under the ledger lock (re-reading fresh inside). CLI entry exists and is wired: src/cli/commands/upload.ts `uploadCommand` with `--as/--force/--context/--source/--limit`, added in src/cli/index.ts:130. 'Scan sessions' matches the returned `sessionRelDir` recorded on ledger entries.

title: Cancel a capture or upload batch that hasn't been handed off yet
story: As a person who changes their mind mid-capture, I want to discard the staged batch and have the box refuse the discard once preparation already owns it, so that cancelling never silently deletes a capture the box already told me it accepted.
evidence: `discardStagingSessionIfCancellable` re-reads the session under `withStagingLock` and deletes only while it is `open` or `failed:*`, returning `{ discarded: false, blockedBy: state }` for anything past the seal; `cleanupStagingSession` is the unconditional post-delivery teardown.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/capture/staging-teardown.ts defines discardStagingSessionIfCancellable, which runs withStagingLock (from staging-store.ts), re-reads via readStagingSession, and deletes the session dir only when state is 'open' or startsWith('failed:'), otherwise returns {discarded:false, blockedBy: session.state}; cleanupStagingSession in the same file is the unconditional post-delivery rm. It is reachable from the web UI: DELETE /api/capture/sessions/:id (src/webapp/routes/capture.ts:209) and DELETE /api/bulk/sessions/:id (src/webapp/routes/bulk-upload.ts:296) both return 409 with 'already <state> ... can no longer be discarded' when the discard is refused, and the frontend calls them (src/frontend/src/pages/capture/capture-api.ts:316 DELETE, src/frontend/src/lib/bulk-upload-api.ts:167-171), with CaptureOverlay/useCaptureFinish handling the sealed-under-us case.

browser.note: Discard-and-exit calls the fake cancel (log-only). The box-side refusal past the seal is only visible as a static caption in the bubble gallery ('couldn't discard — Cancel failed: 409'), not as real behavior.

title: Capture arrives as a message in the chat
story: As a person who submitted a capture, I want it delivered into the chat as a real user message summarizing what I captured, so that the agent responds to it in the conversation I captured from.
evidence: deliverCaptureMessage resolves the target chat (creating one when none resolves), wraps the capture in a <capture> block via buildCaptureWrapper with summarizeCapture's one-line summary, and enqueues or awaits send through deliverUserMessage.

verdict.note: core/capture/prepare.ts step g builds the message with summarizeCapture() + buildCaptureWrapper() (both re-exported from core/capture/deliver.ts; the serializer lives in shared/delivered-user-message.ts) and calls deliverCaptureMessage() at prepare.ts:305. deliverCaptureMessage delegates to core/chat/session/deliver-user-message.ts deliverUserMessage, which emits the persisted `chat-user-message` event and then either session.enqueue({text}) when the agent is busy or awaits session.send({text}) — a real user message in the chat transcript. resolveCaptureDeliveryTarget picks the staging session's targetSessionId (including a registry reservation), else the most-active session, else {sessionId: null} which creates a fresh session at delivery time, matching the story's 'creating one when none resolves'. Reachable from webapp/routes/capture.ts (prepareCaptureSession at lines 63 and 253) and from capture/resume.ts.

title: Capture mode over the chat composer
story: As a person in a chat with my box, I want to open capture mode over the composer and record audio, take photos, pick from my gallery, or attach a disk file, so that whatever I capture lands in this conversation without leaving it.
evidence: CaptureOverlay renders the dark capture surface (StatusBar/CameraViewport/DeviceSettings/CaptureControls) bound to the current chat via targetSessionId; useCaptureInputs wires the gallery and disk-file pickers; POST /api/capture/sessions in routes/capture.ts creates the staging session. The /capture route is a deep link that redirects into chat with ?capture=1.

verdict.note: components/capture/CaptureOverlay.tsx renders CaptureShell/StatusBar/CameraViewport/DeviceSettings/CaptureControls and is mounted by InteractiveChat.tsx (ChatModeOverlays, line 140) when captureMode is set from the composer entry point onEnterCapture (line 331), with the /capture route surviving as a ?capture=1 deep link (CapturePage.tsx header, InteractiveChat line 101). useCaptureSession.ts provides ChunkedRecorder audio recording (toggleRecording/recordingTime) and takePhoto; useCaptureInputs.ts supplies pickFromGallery (accept="image/*") and pickFileToUpload (any file), wired to hidden inputs at CaptureOverlay.tsx:160-161. webapp/routes/capture.ts registers POST /api/capture/sessions (createStagingSession with targetSessionId), /:id/upload, and delete; targetSessionId=sessionId ties delivery of the <capture> message to the current chat. Capture is disabled only under usesNativeShell (iOS shell), so a web user can reach it.

browser.note: Opening the overlay logs createCaptureSession(target=dev-chat) and renders the dark capture surface with Upload file (disk picker), Add from gallery (image/* picker), Device settings, Start camera, Start audio recording, Finalize and Discard-and-exit. Both file inputs exist (accept 'image/*' and ''); uploading two disk files worked. The chat-composer entry point itself is not on this page — the harness mounts CaptureOverlay directly — so only the surface, not the composer launch, was verified here.

title: Capture upload recovery
story: As a boxholder on a weak connection, I want failed uploads named with a big Retry button, per-transfer progress, and the option to finalize without them or skip transfers still in flight, so that a bad link never traps me in capture mode.
evidence: CaptureControls' UploadFailureBanner reports retrying/recovered/failed-again and offers Retry N uploads plus 'Skip them' while finalizing; useCaptureFinish waits on pending transfers, aborts them on skip, and bounces Done back when a new failure appears during the wait.

verdict.note: CaptureControls.tsx's UploadFailureBanner names the failures via summarizeFailures ('2 photos, 1 audio chunk … failed to upload'/'failed again'), renders a full-width min-h-48px 'Retry N uploads' button, says 'Or press Done to finalize without them', and shows retrying/recovered faces driven by pages/capture/retry-feedback.ts (nextRetryFeedback/useRetryFeedback). While finalizing with pendingUploads>0 it shows 'Waiting for N uploads. Skip them' wired to skipPendingUploads. useCaptureFinish.handleDone stops the recorder, closes the barrier, awaits pending, and if readFailureSeq() grew during the wait and skip wasn't requested it reopens, clears finalizing, and sets 'Some uploads failed while finishing…'; skipPendingUploads sets the flag and calls abortPending. StatusBar.tsx shows per-transfer progress via activeUploadPercent (percentLabel), fed from uploads.activeUpload.percent in CaptureOverlay.tsx, which renders both components (reached from InteractiveChat capture mode and /capture route).

browser.note: With 'fail every upload' on, two uploaded files produced the banner '2 files failed to upload.' + a large 'Retry 2 uploads' button + 'Or press Done to finalize without them.' Clicking Retry showed 'Retrying 2 uploads…' with live per-transfer progress ('0/2 files 40%'), then '2 files failed again.' Pressing Done then finalized without them (finalize(fake-qbp757), overlay closed). The static gallery also shows the recovered face ('✓ All uploads recovered.'). Per-transfer progress confirmed in the success path too ('0/2 files 47%').

title: Choose capture camera and microphone
story: As a boxholder, I want to pick which camera and microphone capture uses and to flip or turn off the camera, so that capture works on a device with several inputs.
evidence: DeviceSettings renders camera/microphone <select>s over enumerated MediaDeviceInfo lists writing devicePrefs (persisted by loadDevicePrefs/saveDevicePrefs in capture-api.ts), and useCaptureCamera restarts the stream on a video-device change and exposes toggle/flip used by CameraViewport's corner buttons.

verdict.note: DeviceSettings.tsx renders two <select>s (Camera, Microphone) over videoDevices/audioDevices from useCaptureDevices' enumerateDevices, calling updateDevicePref which persists via saveDevicePrefs (localStorage helpers in pages/capture/capture-api.ts). It is reachable: CaptureOverlay's CaptureSurface renders <DeviceSettings> when state.showSettings, toggled by StatusBar's settings button. useCaptureCamera has an effect keyed on videoDeviceId that stops and restarts the stream (startWithDeviceId/start) and exposes toggleCamera (camera off/on) and flipCamera (cycleDevice on desktop, flip on mobile), both wired to CameraViewport's onToggleCamera/onFlipCamera corner controls. audioDeviceId is consumed in useCaptureSession.ts:147 as the recorder's constraint deviceId.

browser.note: Device settings (gear) opens a panel with a Camera <select> (Default / Camera) and a Microphone <select> (Default / Mic) over enumerated devices. Flip / turn-off camera buttons live on the live viewport and could not be reached because the headless browser denies camera permission, so only the picker half was seen working.

title: Chunked audio upload while still recording
story: As a person recording a long note, I want each audio chunk uploaded as it is produced rather than at the end, so that a long recording is already mostly transferred when I press Done.
evidence: useCaptureUploads feeds per-segment ChunkedRecorder chunks into useUploadRunner's UploadQueue, which runs audio chunks in a dedicated priority lane and bulk media at concurrency 1; POST /api/capture/sessions/:id/upload dispatches on X-Capture-Kind to addAudioChunk/addPhoto/addFile.

verdict.note: useCaptureSession.ts:144 constructs a ChunkedRecorder whose onChunk calls uploads.handleChunk with segment ids; ChunkedRecorder (src/frontend/src/lib/audio/recorder.ts) starts MediaRecorder with a timeslice (5s in capture mode, 20s default), so dataavailable fires and chunks are handed off while recording continues. useCaptureUploads.handleChunk (line 165) enqueues each chunk with priority:true through useUploadRunner, whose UploadQueue is constructed { concurrency: 1, priorityConcurrency: 1 } (useUploadRunner.ts:64) — upload-queue.ts gives the priority lane its own slot so audio chunks don't queue behind bulk media. Server: src/webapp/routes/capture-upload.ts dispatches on the X-Capture-Kind header to addAudioChunk/addPhoto/addFile in src/core/capture/staging-store.ts.

title: Commit batch blobs of arbitrary file types into the annex
story: As a box operator, I want a bulk batch's blobs — zips, CSVs, extensionless files — committed into git-annex alongside their manifest and card, so that a batch card never describes bytes that live in no repository.
evidence: `prepareBulkBatch` writes a batch-local `.gitattributes` (`* annex.largefiles=anything`, with `manifest.json`/`.gitattributes`/`*.card` exempted), saves the scope's asset manifest via `saveManifest`, and stages the whole `attachRelDir` — not just the control files — through `stageAndCommitPaths`.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/bulk-upload/prepare.ts `prepareBulkBatch` copies each staged file into `<batch>/Batch.upload-batch.attach`, calls `computeEntry`/`saveManifest` from src/core/asset-manifest.ts to write that scope's manifest.json, writes a batch-local .gitattributes with `* annex.largefiles=anything` and `annex.largefiles=nothing` exemptions for manifest.json/.gitattributes/*.card, and then `stageAndCommitPaths(boxRoot,{paths:[cardRelPath, attachRelDir]})` — the whole attach dir, not just control files. The complementary filter scoping exists: `BULK_BATCH_ATTACH_PATTERN = "**/*.upload-batch.attach/**"` with `filter=annex` in src/lib/asset-extensions.ts (written into .git/info/attributes, see src/core/annex/info-attributes.ts). Reachable: prepareBulkBatch <- worker.ts `prepareAndDeliverBulkBatch` <- webapp/routes/bulk-upload.ts and bulk-upload-lifecycle.ts.

title: Commit capture media as hash-tracked assets rather than raw bytes in git
story: As a box operator, I want each capture clip and photo recorded in its own attach scope's asset manifest with size and sha256 while only manifests and cards are committed, so that a card never claims media whose bytes were never accounted for.
evidence: `SessionBuilder.writeChildCard` writes the media into `<basename>.attach/`, then `computeEntry` + `saveManifest` record it in that scope's `manifest.json`, and only `<attach>/manifest.json` and the `.card` are pushed onto `filesToStage`; the worker commits exactly the capture card plus the session attach dir via `stageAndCommitPaths`.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/capture/write-cards.ts SessionBuilder.writeChildCard() writes media into <sessionAttach>/<childBasename>.attach/, then builds a manifest with computeEntry(mediaAbsPath) (asset-manifest.ts:78 returns {size, mtime, sha256}) and saveManifest(), pushing only `<childAttach>/manifest.json` and the `.card` onto filesToStage — never the raw bytes. asset-manifest.ts's header documents that asset bytes stay gitignored while the manifest is committed. core/capture/prepare.ts step f commits paths [sessionCardRelPath, sessionAttachRelDir] via commitPathsSerialized -> stageAndCommitPaths (staged-only scoping so a fully gitignored attach scope still commits). Reachable from the capture routes (webapp/routes/capture.ts calls prepareCaptureSession) and resume/sweep.

title: Deliver a prepared upload batch to its chat exactly once
story: As a person who uploaded a batch, I want a single message about it in the chat I launched the upload from, even across a crash mid-delivery, so that the agent is told about my files once and never twice.
evidence: `runBulkPreparation` probes `userMessageAlreadyLanded` against the deterministic batch card path before mutating state, marks `delivering` before send, and sends the `<upload>` wrapper via `deliverUserMessage`; `resolveBulkDeliveryTarget` refuses any most-active fallback, and `resumeBulkSessions` re-fires mid-flight batches at startup.

verdict.note: src/core/bulk-upload/worker.ts runBulkPreparation computes the deterministic batch card path via bulkBatchCardRelPath, and when that card already exists probes userMessageAlreadyLanded (src/core/chat/session/deliver-user-message.ts:65) against the target chat's transcript before mutating state; if landed it calls finishBulkDelivery instead of re-sending. It sets staging state to 'delivering' before deliverUserMessage sends the <upload> wrapper (buildUploadWrapper), so a crash between send and the 'delivered' write is recoverable. deliver.ts resolveBulkDeliveryTarget returns null (fail-loud, retryable) when the batch's targetSessionId is not in loadHistory and not a live reservation — no most-active fallback, so the message goes to the chat the upload was launched from. resume.ts resumeBulkSessions re-fires sealed/preparing/delivering sessions at startup and is wired in src/webapp/routes/bulk-upload-lifecycle.ts:166.

title: File a PDF even when extraction fails
story: As the boxholder, I want a document import whose Docling extraction failed to still produce a document card carrying the original PDF and the failure reason, so that a broken extractor never swallows the scan I just sent.
evidence: `runDocumentMode` copies the source into the card's attach scope before extracting; when `extractDocument` returns an error result it writes the card with `status: "new"`, `template.error = extraction.error`, an empty body and the PDF as the only asset, prints `Extraction failed (filed as status: new)`, and still commits, files the capture-session card and creates the intake job.

verdict.note: Read runDocumentMode in callback-box/src/core/commands/scan-import-document.ts. It copies the source PDF into `<session>.attach/<DOCUMENT_BASENAME>.attach/` before calling extractDocument (src/core/commands/document-extract.ts). When extraction is not ok it sets status "new", body "", template.error = extraction.error, leaves assetRelPaths as just the source PDF, prints `Extraction failed (filed as status: new) — <error>`, then still writes the document card, writes the capture-session card, stageAndCommitPaths, and createOrAppendIntakeJob. Reachable via `cb scan-import` (src/cli/commands/scan-import.ts → runCommand "scan-import" → runDocumentMode for a PDF).

title: Finalize a capture into a committed capture document delivered to chat
story: As a person using the box, I want pressing Done on a capture to turn the staged media into a committed capture-session card with child audio/image/file cards and a chat message pointing at it, so that my recording becomes real box content the agent can act on.
evidence: `prepareCaptureSession`/`runPreparation` runs resolve-target → `writeCaptureDocument` (capture-session card plus `audio-NNN`/`photo-NNN`/file child cards in `<contextDir>/tmp-capture/<basename>.attach/`) → transcribe → timeline → lint → `stageAndCommitPaths` → `deliverCaptureMessage`, which sends the `<capture>` wrapper built by `buildCaptureWrapper`.

verdict.note: CaptureControls.tsx/CaptureOverlay.tsx expose the Done button (onDone -> handleDone) which seals the staging session; src/webapp/routes/capture.ts (lines 63 and 253) fires prepareCaptureSession. runPreparation in src/core/capture/prepare.ts calls writeCaptureDocument, then transcription/timeline/lint, then stageAndCommitPaths (lib/git.js) and deliverCaptureMessage. write-cards.ts writeCaptureDocument creates <basename>.capture-session.card via createCaptureSessionTemplate (src/schemas/capture-session.tsx) plus child cards numbered audio-001.../photo-N/file cards inside <destRelDir>/<basename>.attach/, with per-scope manifests via computeEntry/saveManifest from core/asset-manifest.ts. deliver.ts's deliverCaptureMessage re-exports and sends the <capture> wrapper from shared/delivered-user-message.js into the resolved chat target.

browser.note: Done fires finalize(fake-<id>) into the fake api and exits the overlay; no capture-session card is written and no chat message is delivered. The committed-document path is not exercisable here.

title: Finish without waiting on stuck transfers
story: As a person who is done capturing, I want Done to wait on outstanding transfers while offering to skip them, so that a slow link delays my submit but a broken one does not trap me.
evidence: useCaptureFinish never gates Done on uploads finishing — it drains, exposes skipPendingUploads, and hands the decision back if a new failure appears during the wait; CaptureControls renders the skip affordance; POST /api/capture/sessions/:id/finalize seals.

verdict.note: useCaptureFinish.ts handleDone stops the recorder, calls closeForSealing(), then awaits awaitPending() rather than disabling Done on outstanding uploads (doneDisabled in CaptureControls.tsx line 96 is only !sessionId || finalizing || !hasContent). skipPendingUploads sets skipRequested and calls abortPending(), so aborted transfers settle as failures and the awaited drain resolves; CaptureControls.tsx lines 99-103 render 'Waiting for N upload(s). Skip them' wired through CaptureOverlay.tsx onSkipPending. If readFailureSeq() rises during the wait without a skip, it reopens, clears finalizing, and shows 'Retry them, or press Done again to finalize without them'; otherwise finalizeCaptureSession posts to POST /api/capture/sessions/:id/finalize (src/webapp/routes/capture.ts line 228), which CAS-seals the session.

browser.note: With a slow fake transport, pressing Done mid-upload did not block: the status bar showed '1/2 files 16%' and the footer showed 'Waiting for 1 upload.' next to a 'Skip them' button; once the transfer drained, finalize(fake-…) fired automatically and the overlay closed.

title: Get a truthful report of which uploaded files actually arrived
story: As a person uploading a batch, I want the resulting batch card to list what was received, what the uploader reported as failed, and what never arrived at all, alongside the note I typed, so that I can trust the box's account of my upload instead of guessing.
evidence: `buildBatchSummary` reconciles the predeclared `expectedItems` registry against arrived files (keyed by `itemId`, name only as fallback) and the uploader's `failedItems` to compute received/missing/failed, sanitizes and dedupes stored names, and writes an `upload-batch` card carrying the counts, the `note`, and `summarizeBatch`'s one-line body.

verdict.note: prepare.ts `prepareBulkBatch` -> `buildBatchSummary` copies staged files into the attach scope (names via `sanitizeFilename`/`dedupeName` from batch-format.ts), builds `arrivedKeys` keyed `id:<itemId>` with `name:` fallback, builds `failedKeys` from the uploader-reported `failedItems`, and computes `missing` from `session.expectedItems` minus arrived/failed. It then writes an `upload-batch` card via `createUploadBatchTemplate` with `counts {registered,received,missing,failed}`, the `received`/`missing`/`failed` arrays, `total-bytes`, `note` (the boxholder's composer text), and `summarizeBatch`'s one-line body. src/schemas/upload-batch.tsx defines exactly those frontmatter fields (BatchCounts, ReceivedItem, MissingItem, FailedItem, note).

title: Get every scanned page through a flaky vision model
story: As the boxholder's agent, I want a failing vision batch retried with backoff, then split into smaller overlap-preserving batches, and any page that still fails filed as a card flagged for review, so that one bad batch costs a review flag instead of losing pages from the scan.
evidence: `runScanBatches` classifies each `ScanVisionBatchError` via `retryClassOf`: `transient` retries with exponential backoff, `split` re-runs boundary-sharing halves (`splitAndRerun`, with `retrySingletonLastResort`), `batch` fails just that batch, and `fatal` aborts before anything is staged; pages with no surviving analysis get `makeMissingAnalysis` (`kind: unsure`, `flag_reason: "Page analysis missing — vision batch failed"`), which `buildPhotoBundle` turns into a review flag.

verdict.note: src/core/commands/scan-import-helpers.ts runScanBatches → runOneBatch retries the same batch up to 3 times with exponential backoff (2000 * 2**attempt) while retryClassOf(err) === 'transient'; handleBatchFailure rethrows on 'fatal' (scan-import-session.ts catches it before staging), calls splitAndRerun for 'split' (halves share the boundary page, `[0,1,2]` → `[0,1]`+`[1,2]`) and retrySingletonLastResort for a 1-page batch, and otherwise fails just that batch. In scan-import-reconcile.ts pickAnalysis falls back to makeMissingAnalysis (kind 'unsure', flag_for_review true, flag_reason 'Page analysis missing — vision batch failed'); such pages land in unsurePages and scan-import.ts calls emitUnsureQuestion (scan-import-cards.ts), which writes a .question.card with the page attached — a card flagged for review. Minor evidence slip (buildPhotoBundle handles kind 'photo', not the unsure path) does not change the story's claim.

title: Get readable, language-tagged transcript text rather than a raw dump
story: As a person recording into the box, I want transcripts punctuated, paragraphed, and tagged with the language actually spoken, so that a recording in any language reads as prose instead of an unbroken run-on string.
evidence: `transcribeAudioDeepgram` sets `smart_format`, `paragraphs`, `punctuate`, and `detect_language` on the request and prefers `alternatives[0].paragraphs.transcript`, returning `detected_language`; `shapeVoxtralResult` resolves `language` and rebuilds text via `joinSegmentTexts` / `repairMissingSentenceSpaces` to fix Voxtral's missing inter-sentence spaces; `transcribeCaptureClips` writes the resolved `language` into each clip's `.timing.json` sidecar.

verdict.note: core/transcription/deepgram.ts sets smart_format, paragraphs, punctuate and detect_language on the request URL (lines 126-129), prefers alternatives[0].paragraphs.transcript over the flat transcript (line 147), and returns language from channel.detected_language (line 149, defaulting to 'unknown'). voxtral-request.ts shapeVoxtralResult resolves `language` (line 153) and rebuilds text via joinSegmentTexts / repairMissingSentenceSpaces from voxtral-text.ts (lines 182-183). core/capture/transcribe-clips.ts writes { words, duration, language } into `<basename>.timing.json` beside the clip (lines 128-130). transcription/index.ts dispatches to Whisper/Voxtral/Deepgram per box config, so the language tag flows on the live path.

title: Hand the agent the audio behind a voice message
story: As the box agent, I want to ask the open tab for a recent voice recording and receive the audio plus its transcript, so that I can check what was actually said instead of only the transcription.
evidence: last-audio.ts keeps recordings per emission id in a RetentionStore and fulfillLastAudioRequest() answers the server-relayed chat-last-audio-request by uploading the blob (transcript capped at 1500 chars on a header), also relaying to the native shell when one is present.

verdict.note: src/frontend/src/lib/audio/last-audio.ts keeps VoiceAudioPayload {blob,text,recordedAt} per emission id in createRetentionStore (capacity 5) and fulfillLastAudioRequest() POSTs the blob plus `text` (sliced to MAX_TEXT_CHARS=1500) and recordedAt to /chat/last-audio/<requestId>, relaying to the native shell via postNativeLastAudioRequest when isNativeShell(). The agent-side entry is `cb chat get-last-audio --message <id>` (src/cli/commands/chat-audio.ts getLastAudioCommand, plumbing in chat-audio-fetch.ts), which writes the audio to a file and prints the path, recorded-at and `text:` transcript; the box prompt (src/core/chat/session/prompts.ts) documents it. Minor deviations that do not break the story: the transcript rides a FormData field on the tab->server hop (the header cap is server-side), and the second cited file mic-tab-lock.ts is unrelated cross-tab mic exclusion.

title: Have a capture started outside any chat still reach me
story: As a person who opens the capture deep link with no chat behind it, or whose original chat has since been deleted, I want the finished capture delivered to my most recently active chat — or into a brand-new one if the box has none — so that a recording is never stranded for want of a destination.
evidence: `resolveCaptureDeliveryTarget` warns and falls back to `getMostActive(boxRoot)` when `targetSessionId` is null or names a chat no longer in `loadHistory`, and returns `{ sessionId: null }` — "create a fresh session at delivery time" — when the box has no chats at all.

title: Have a corrupted capture manifest quarantined instead of silently dropped
story: As a box operator, I want a staging session whose `session.json` is unreadable or fails schema validation to be logged loudly and set aside as `session.json.corrupt`, so that the staged media next to it is investigable rather than vanishing without a trace.

title: Have uploaded files stored under safe, non-colliding names

verdict.note: src/core/bulk-upload/batch-format.ts sanitizeFilename() takes the last path segment (splits on / and \\), replaces non-word chars in the stem with '-', collapses runs, falls back to 'file', and re-appends the sanitized extension; dedupeName() inserts -2, -3, … before the extension against a used-name Set. src/core/bulk-upload/prepare.ts buildBatchSummary() (line ~225) computes destName = dedupeName(sanitizeFilename(file.originalName || file.filename), usedNames), copies the staged file to attachAbsDir/destName, records it in manifest.files[destName] and pushes {name: destName, size} into the card's received list. Reachable from the web bulk-upload route (src/webapp/routes/bulk-upload.ts → core/bulk-upload/worker.ts → prepareBulkBatch).

title: Import a batch of scanned photos into a capture session
story: As the boxholder's agent, I want to import scanned JPEGs or a textless PDF as a capture session — vision-analyzed, front/back paired, with image cards and review questions for anything uncertain, so that a pile of scans becomes described, filed cards instead of loose files.

story: As an operator running an unattended scanner uploader, I want each upload credential's requests capped per minute with a Retry-After, so that a looping or misconfigured uploader backs off instead of flooding the box.

title: Never commit a capture document that fails card validation
story: As a box operator, I want a capture whose written cards fail schema validation to be torn back down and recorded as failed rather than committed, so that a bug in capture writing can't push invalid cards into the box's git history.
evidence: Step e runs `lintCardsDispatch` over the capture card plus every child card before the commit step; on `summary.totalErrors > 0` it logs the per-card messages, calls `discardWrittenDocument` to delete the uncommitted card and attach scope, and marks the session `failed:assemble` — the staging media is left intact so a re-fire rebuilds from scratch.

On summary.totalErrors > 0 it logs per-card messages, calls discardWrittenDocument (rm of the uncommitted card file and attach dir), then markCapturePreparationFailed with state 'failed:assemble' and returns before any commit; staging media is untouched.

title: Never have an upload batch land in the wrong chat
story: As a person who uploads files from a specific chat, I want a batch whose target chat can no longer be resolved to stay retryable and be surfaced for recovery rather than dumped into whichever chat was most active, so that a pile of files never appears in an unrelated conversation.
evidence: `resolveBulkDeliveryTarget` returns `null` — with no most-active fallback, unlike capture's resolver — when the batch's `targetSessionId` is neither a live reservation nor in `loadHistory`; `runBulkPreparation` then logs and calls `markBulkPreparationFailed({ state: "failed:deliver" })`, leaving the batch retryable.

verdict.note: resolveBulkDeliveryTarget in src/core/bulk-upload/deliver.ts returns the target only when targetSessionId is a live registry reservation or present in loadHistory(), and returns null otherwise with no most-active fallback (contrasted in its own comment with capture's resolver). runBulkPreparation in src/core/bulk-upload/worker.ts (lines ~100-115) logs '[bulk] Target chat ... no longer exists; leaving retryable' and calls markBulkPreparationFailed({ state: 'failed:deliver' }), which only sets staging state — bytes and staging session persist. sweepBulkBatches in src/core/bulk-upload/sweep.ts treats any state starting with 'failed:' as a StrandedBatch and calls notifyStranded once (strandedNotifiedAt guard); that callback is wired in src/webapp/routes/bulk-upload-lifecycle.ts (scheduleBulkSweep → injectStrandedSelfNote), which sends a self-note into a chat session, so recovery is surfaced rather than the batch being dumped elsewhere.

title: Not be messaged about an upload batch with nothing in it
story: As a person who opened the file picker and cancelled, I want a batch with no files, no failures, no registered items and no note to be discarded quietly, so that a mis-tap doesn't put a meaningless upload message in my chat.
evidence: `bulkBatchHasNothingToReport` is the single predicate shared by `runBulkPreparation` (which calls `cleanupStagingSession` and returns before preparing) and `sweepBulkBatches` (which discards such an idle open batch through the locked `discardStagingSessionIfCancellable`); a batch with registered-but-missing items or a note fails the predicate and still produces its report.

verdict.note: bulkBatchHasNothingToReport in callback-box/src/core/bulk-upload/batch-format.ts returns true only when files.length===0 AND failedItems empty AND expectedItems empty AND note===undefined. runBulkPreparation in worker.ts calls it right after reading the staging session and, when true, calls cleanupStagingSession and returns before preparing/delivering any batch card. sweepBulkBatches in sweep.ts uses the same predicate on idle `open` batches past BULK_ABANDONMENT_WINDOW_MS and discards through discardStagingSessionIfCancellable with a stillDiscardable re-check under the lock; batches with registered-but-missing items or a note fall to the `abandoned`/report path instead.

title: Only one tab holds the mic, and the screen stays awake
story: As a person recording, I want a second tab's recording to yield the microphone and the screen to stay awake while I speak, so that I do not record twice or lose the session to a screen lock.

title: Pick the scan analyzer and see what a run cost
story: As an operator, I want scan analysis to run on Claude by default or on Gemini when I opt in, fail before staging anything if the credential is missing, and report tokens and dollars for the run, so that I can control which vision backend processes my photos and what it costs.
