title: Preparation survives a server restart
story: As a person who submitted a capture just before the box restarted, I want preparation to pick up where it stopped, so that my capture still arrives without re-doing (or re-billing) work already done.
evidence: prepareCaptureSession persists progress through the staging state machine (sealed → preparing → delivering → delivered, failed:<step> on error) with each step checking for its own output; resumeStagingSessions re-fires on startup and handleStagingUploadReplay makes a repeated upload of the same bytes a no-op.

title: Queue an imported scan for the box to process
story: As the boxholder's agent, I want each scan or document import to file an intake job listing the session and its review questions, appended to a pending job from the same source, so that imported material is picked up by the next reactor run instead of sitting in the inbox unnoticed.
evidence: `runPhotoMode` calls `createOrAppendIntakeJob({source: "scan", items: [sessionCardRelPath, ...questionPaths], description})` after committing and prints the job path; `runDocumentMode` does the same with the session card. `createOrAppendIntakeJob` appends to an existing pending `scan` job under a cross-process lock rather than creating a second one.

title: Re-extract an existing document card

title: Re-transcribe an audio card using the text it already has as context
story: As the box's own transcription pass over an audio card that already carries text, I want the existing text sent to the service as a prompt, so that names, jargon, and spellings established in the first transcript carry into the new one.
evidence: `TranscribeAudioParams.prompt` is forwarded by `transcribeAudioWhisper` as the OpenAI multipart `prompt` field, and `core/preactions/transcribe.ts` passes `...(existingContent !== null && { prompt: existingContent })` when re-transcribing a card that already has content.

verdict.note: The mechanism exists but is narrower than the story. In callback-box/src/core/preactions/transcribe.ts, `getFrontmatterContent` (line 156) returns only the card's `body` field — a human-typed note — not a prior transcript; `applyFrontmatterTranscription` writes results to `fields["transcription"]`, never to `body`. Moreover `transcribePreAction.shouldRun` returns false when `fields["transcription"] !== undefined`, so the pre-action never re-transcribes a card that already has a transcript: there is no path where 'names, jargon, and spellings established in the first transcript carry into the new one.' The prompt forwarding itself is real (transcription/index.ts:329-331 adds the OpenAI multipart `prompt` field), but it applies to the first transcription using the typed body, not a re-transcription.

panel.note: The code exists and is live. transcribeAudio (callback-box/src/core/transcription/index.ts:228) delegates to transcribeAudioWhisper, which at lines 329-331 pushes a multipart field {name: "prompt", value: prompt} when TranscribeAudioParams.prompt (declared line 124) is set. callback-box/src/core/preactions/transcribe.ts:92 passes `...(existingContent !== null && { prompt: existingContent })` from getFrontmatterContent(fields) into that call, and the pre-action is imported and registered via registerPreAction(transcribePreAction) in callback-box/src/core/preactions/index.ts:21,110 — nothing here is dead. The earlier verifier's objection is about which text feeds the prompt (fields.body vs a prior transcript) and whether a re-transcribe path is reachable, which is a wording/reachability question outside my lens; on wiring the story stands.

The path has a real, unflagged entry point: `cb wakeup` (src/cli/commands/wakeup.ts:176) calls `runPreprocessors` (src/cli/commands/wakeup-steps.ts:31), which calls `runPreActions` over every inbox card; `transcribePreAction` is unconditionally registered at src/core/preactions/index.ts:110 for memo and feedback cards, and its execute() passes `...(existingContent !== null && { prompt: existingContent })` into transcribeAudio, which appends the OpenAI multipart `prompt` field (src/core/transcription/index.ts, `if (prompt) parts.push(...)`) on the default `whisper` variant. No feature flag or opt-in config gates it — only the ordinary openai-thinking API key. Whether that existing text is a prior transcript or only the typed `body`, and whether shouldRun permits a second pass, is an accuracy question outside my lens; the mechanism itself is reachable by the box's own transcription pass.

The prompt-forwarding half is real: transcription/index.ts pushes a `prompt` multipart field when one is supplied, and transcribe.ts passes `...(existingContent !== null && { prompt: existingContent })`. But `getFrontmatterContent` sources that text only from `fields["body"]` (a typed note), while `applyFrontmatterTranscription` writes results to `fields["transcription"]` and never to `body` — so the prompt can never be a prior transcript. `transcribePreAction.shouldRun` also returns false whenever `fields["transcription"] !== undefined`, so the pre-action never runs a second time on an already-transcribed card. The story's title/`so that` clause (re-transcription seeded by the first transcript's names and spellings) describes an outcome the code does not produce; what exists is a narrower first-pass hint from a human-typed body.

triage.reasoning: The prompt plumbing is real but the story's scenario does not exist anywhere. In core/preactions/transcribe.ts the prompt comes from `getFrontmatterContent`, which returns `fields["body"]` (a human-typed note) and nothing else, while `applyFrontmatterTranscription` writes results into `fields["transcription"]` and never into `body` — so the prompt can never be a prior transcript. `transcribePreAction.shouldRun` also returns false as soon as `fields["transcription"] !== undefined`, so the pre-action never makes a second pass over an already-transcribed card. I also checked the one genuine re-transcription path, `cb chat retranscribe` (cli/commands/chat-audio.ts:199): it fetches the message's realtime transcript into `realtimeTranscript`, then calls `transcribeAudioHq` WITHOUT a `prompt` and merely prints the old text in the report. So no code path seeds a re-transcription with the text a card already carries. What exists — a first-pass Whisper hint taken from a typed body (transcription/index.ts pushes the multipart `prompt` field when supplied) — is a different and narrower story. Rewrite the catalog entry to that; feeding the prior transcript into `cb chat retranscribe` would be a new feature idea, not a repair of a claimed capability.

title: Record a capture in several takes
story: As a person capturing, I want to stop recording, take photos or pick files, then start recording again inside the same capture, so that one capture holds several clips in the order I made them instead of forcing me to submit and start over.

title: Recover an abandoned capture as an explicitly partial one
story: As a person whose phone died mid-capture, I want the box to eventually finalize what it already has and mark it partial, so that the recording reaches my chat labeled as incomplete instead of rotting in staging.
evidence: `sweepAbandonedCaptures` CAS-seals `open` sessions idle past `ABANDONMENT_WINDOW_MS` with `partial: true` (`sealStagingSession({ requireOpen: true })`) and fires preparation, discards empty ones, re-fires stuck sealed/preparing/delivering sessions, and warns about stale `failed:*` sessions without auto-retrying them.

title: Rejected scans raise a question

title: Rescue a capture whose preparation failed
story: As a person whose submitted capture failed on the box side, I want the pending bubble to show the failure with its age and offer both Retry and Discard, so that a broken capture is something I can act on instead of a dead row sitting in the chat.
evidence: capture-bubble.tsx defines phases `working`/`resolved`/`failed-fresh`/`failed-aged` and takes a CaptureVerbs pair; useCaptureBubbles.retry re-POSTs `finalizeCaptureSession` (the finalize route re-fires from a `failed:*` state) and discard calls `cancelCaptureSession`, surfacing `already being delivered` when the guarded DELETE returns 409. Past ABANDONMENT_WINDOW_MS the bubble emphasizes discard over another retry.

title: Retry an interrupted upload without duplicating or corrupting it
story: As a person capturing or uploading over a flaky mobile connection, I want a retried upload of the same file to be recognized as the same upload rather than staged twice, so that a dropped connection costs me a retry and not a duplicate file or a broken batch.
evidence: `handleStagingUploadReplay` treats the upload filename as an idempotency key: an already-manifested filename whose bytes match is accepted as a replay (and re-written if the bytes went missing), while different bytes under the same filename raise `StagingUploadReplayConflictError`. `addFileStreamed` does the same under the session lock via the staged file's sha256, returning `replay: true`.

verdict.note: src/core/capture/upload-replay.ts handleStagingUploadReplay() returns true when the filename is already referenced by a segment chunk, photo, or file in the manifest and the on-disk bytes equal the incoming buffer (re-writing the file if it went ENOENT), and throws StagingUploadReplayConflictError (src/core/capture/staging-errors.ts) when the bytes differ; it is called from src/core/capture/staging-store.ts:196. src/core/capture/staging-stream.ts addFileStreamed() hashes to a temp file then, under withStagingLock, returns {replay:true} when an existing session file has the same filename and sha256, else throws the same conflict error. Reachable from the web upload route src/webapp/routes/bulk-upload.ts handleUploadBulkItem(), which takes the client's X-Upload-Filename and maps the conflict to a 409, so a retry of the same file under the same filename is not staged twice.

title: See why a transcription failed, and not retry a hopeless one
story: As the boxholder, I want a failed voice transcription recorded on the card as permanent or retryable, so that a bad file stops being retried every sync while a temporary failure gets another attempt.
evidence: `transcribePreAction.execute` writes a `transcription-error` field with `permanent`, `code`, `attempted-at` and `message`; `shouldRun` returns false when `isPermanentError(fields["transcription-error"])`. Audio whose annex content is absent is reported via `describeAbsentContent` and marked `permanent: false` so fetching the file makes it retryable; a success deletes the error field.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/preactions/transcribe.ts `transcribePreAction` (registered at preactions/index.ts:110, appliesTo memo/feedback) writes `transcription-error` with `permanent`, optional `code`, `attempted-at`, `message` via applyFrontmatterError, and `shouldRun` returns false when `isPermanentError(fields['transcription-error'])` (permanent === true), so a hopeless card stops being retried. Absent annex content is caught by `readAssetContent`/`describeAbsentContent` and recorded with `permanent: false`, and `applyFrontmatterTranscription` deletes `transcription-error` on success. title: Send scanned documents from a laptop scanner
story: As someone scanning paper, I want the uploader to ask which hashes the box still needs and stream each file into a validated quarantine, so that only new scans are sent and I learn per-file whether the box accepted it.
evidence: POST /api/scan/check answers per-hash state from the upload ledger and quarantine sidecar; PUT /api/scan/files/<sha256> streams request.raw to disk through hashStreamToFile, re-hashes, runs validateScanFile, and returns a per-file verdict — all behind makeScanAuthPreHandler's scan bearer.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/routes/scan-upload.ts registers POST /api/scan/check (handleCheck answers per-hash unknown/pending/imported/rejected from loadLedger + readQuarantineEntry) and PUT /api/scan/files/:sha256 (handlePut streams request.raw through hashStreamToFile into a quarantine temp file, re-hashes with a 422 hash-mismatch on divergence, runs validateScanFile from core/scan/validate.ts, records the entry via recordQuarantineEntry, and returns accepted/duplicate/rejected/413/503). Both routes sit in their own Fastify scope behind makeScanAuthPreHandler (webapp/scan-auth.ts) plus consumeScanRateLimit, registered from webapp/server-box-scope.ts:309, so they are reachable. The only precondition is isAnnexBox — a non-annex box answers 503 up front, which is a box-shape gate rather than a flag that hides the feature.

title: Send the agent a picture of what I am seeing

title: Agent-added card fields survive a connector rewrite
story: As a box agent, I want the fields I added to a connector-managed card to be re-injected when sync rebuilds that card from its template, so that my annotations aren't erased by the next sync.
evidence: preserveAgentFields re-injects its AGENT_FIELDS list (currently `contains`) into the freshly rendered frontmatter, and is called by writeThreadCards and by the Drive sheets handler before each rewrite.

verdict.note: Over-claim on scope. callback-box/src/connectors/preserve-agent-fields.ts preserves only a hardcoded AGENT_FIELDS allowlist — ['contains', 'contains-evidence'] — and only when the value is a non-empty string and the template did not set that key; every other field an agent added to a connector-managed card is still destroyed by the wholesale template rewrite. The story says 'the fields I added ... aren't erased', which the code does not deliver for arbitrary annotations. The call sites are real (gmail-threads.ts:186 in writeThreadCards, drive-handler-sheets.ts:198, plus drive-handler-docs.ts:321, which the story omits), so the mechanism exists but is far narrower than stated; the story's own evidence line also mis-states the list as 'currently contains'.

panel.note: callback-box/src/connectors/preserve-agent-fields.ts exports a real preserveAgentFields() that reads the existing card, parses both frontmatters, and re-injects its AGENT_FIELDS (["contains", "contains-evidence"]) into the freshly rendered frontmatter before the write. It is imported and called at gmail-threads.ts:186 (inside writeThreadCard, the per-card writer under the exported writeThreadCards, which gmail.ts:114 and gmail-track.ts:77 call), drive-handler-sheets.ts:198, and drive-handler-docs.ts:321. The sheets handler is itself live: drive-handler-sheets.ts:259 calls registerDriveHandler(sheetsHandler) and the module is side-effect imported by google-drive.ts:38 and cli/commands/drive.ts:27. Nothing here is dead code; the scope/wording concerns in the earlier verdict (allowlist narrower than 'the fields I added', evidence line saying 'currently contains') fall outside this lens.

The preservation path is reachable with no flag or opt-in config. preserveAgentFields is called unconditionally inside the rewrite paths: gmail-threads.ts:186 in writeThreadCards, drive-handler-sheets.ts:198, and drive-handler-docs.ts:321. Those rewrites are driven by real entry points a box agent hits: `cb connector gmail track <thread-id>` (src/cli/commands/connector.ts, registered at src/cli/index.ts:151 -> gmail-track.ts:77 -> writeThreadCards) and the scheduled/wakeup sync (`cb wakeup`, registered at src/cli/index.ts:105, wakeup.ts:205 -> runConnectors in wakeup-connectors.ts -> createGmailConnector/gmail.ts:114). No flag defaults off and nothing extra must be configured beyond having the connector itself set up, so my lens is satisfied; scope-of-preservation concerns are another reviewer's lens.

The story promises that "the fields I added to a connector-managed card" are re-injected "so that my annotations aren't erased by the next sync" — an unqualified, general capability. preserve-agent-fields.ts carries over only a hardcoded two-item allowlist (`const AGENT_FIELDS = ["contains", "contains-evidence"]`), and only when the existing value is a non-empty string and the freshly rendered template did not already set that key (`if (nextFields[field] !== undefined) continue;`). Every other frontmatter key an agent adds is dropped by the wholesale template rewrite at the call sites (gmail-threads.ts:186, drive-handler-sheets.ts:198, drive-handler-docs.ts:321), so the benefit clause holds for two specific fields, not for agent annotations in general.

triage.reasoning: The mechanism is real, unconditional on the rewrite paths, and deliberately narrow — the story is what is wrong. `callback-box/src/connectors/preserve-agent-fields.ts` carries over a hardcoded `AGENT_FIELDS = ['contains', 'contains-evidence']`, and only when the existing value is a non-empty string and the freshly rendered template did not already set that key. Its own docblock calls these 'the fields agents own on connector-managed cards', and those two are exactly the global card fields the agent-facing docs steer agents to write (`docs/adding-schemas.md:72`: 'contains is the field agents should populate'). The call sites are unconditional (gmail-threads.ts:186 inside writeThreadCards, drive-handler-sheets.ts:198, drive-handler-docs.ts:321 — the story omits the docs handler). So the design is 'template owns the card, these two named fields survive', not 'anything an agent adds survives', and the story's unqualified 'the fields I added ... aren't erased' describes a capability that never existed. Fix the catalog entry to name the two preserved fields (and the third call site); no product change is warranted. Worth noting without inflating it into a gap: `todos` is also a global card field (`src/cards/schema.ts:87-92`) and is a list, which the `typeof value !== 'string'` guard skips, so a todo attached to a connector-managed card would not survive a sync — a narrow, speculative case, not something observed.

title: Declare a card type as a typed schema
story: As a box agent or developer, I want to declare a card type with `cardSchema()` — Zod-typed frontmatter fields plus at most one markdown body field — so that every card of that type has a checked shape and a single place its metadata lives.
evidence: `cardSchema()` and `body()` in src/cards/schema.ts build a CardSchema (rejecting more than one body field via CardSchemaDeclarationError); src/schemas/registry.ts imports and registers ~60 built-in schemas (MemoSchema, QuestionSchema, …) into the map `createCardSchemaMap` returns.

verdict.note: src/cards/schema.ts exports cardSchema(type, {fields}) which splits FieldDecl entries into a Zod frontmatter object (auto-adding the `type` literal and GLOBAL_CARD_FIELDS) and at most one body() field; body() is documented as markdown/plain UTF-8, and cardSchema throws CardSchemaDeclarationError unless the body field is named "body" (which makes multiple body fields impossible since object keys are unique) and when no fields are declared. src/cards/index.ts re-exports cardSchema and body; src/schemas/memo.ts uses them (MemoSchema), and src/schemas/registry.ts imports the built-in schemas and assembles them in createCardSchemaMap (line 405). Only the evidence sentence's mechanism for the multi-body rejection is slightly off (name check rather than a count), which does not change the story.

title: Define box-local card types that hot-reload
story: As a box agent, I want to add a new card type in the box's own `config/schemas/*.ts` and have the running server pick it up, so that a box can grow its own vocabulary without a code deploy or restart.
evidence: `loadBoxSchemas(boxRoot)` in schemas/registry.ts dynamically imports the box's `config/schemas/*.ts` (content-hash-busted) and merges them into `createCardSchemaMap`; core/schema-watcher.ts watches that dir with chokidar and calls `invalidateBoxSchemas` so `cb serve` reloads. The agent guide tells agents to define new types there.

verdict.note: Hot-reloading box-local schemas exists (schemas/registry.ts loadBoxSchemas/invalidateBoxSchemas with content-hash cache busting, core/schema-watcher.ts ensureSchemaWatcher via webapp/server-box-scope.ts:171), but NOT at the path the story names. rebuildBoxSchemas reads only boxCodePaths(shape).schemasDir, which lib/box-shape.ts defines as path.join(shape.packageRoot, 'src/schemas'). box-shape.ts's findLegacySchemaFiles/describeLegacySchemaFiles exist precisely because a *.ts left in the box's config/schemas/ is 'invisible to the schema loader (which only reads the v2 path)' — so a card type added to config/schemas/*.ts is never picked up at all. (The cited agent guide, core/agent-guide/cards.ts:175, still tells agents 'config/schemas/', which is stale prose, not a second supported location.)

panel.note: The capability is real and fully wired. src/schemas/registry.ts has loadBoxSchemas/rebuildBoxSchemas (reads boxCodePaths(shape).schemasDir, dynamic-imports each *.ts with a content-hash-busted URL, caches with keep-last-good) and invalidateBoxSchemas; loadBoxSchemas is merged into createCardSchemaMap (registry.ts:405-411) and called from server-root.ts:173, init-rules.ts, docs-gen, health-engine, and CLI status/create. src/core/schema-watcher.ts's ensureSchemaWatcher chokidar-watches that dir and calls invalidateBoxSchemas on any event; it is imported and invoked at box registration in src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts:171 (with closeSchemaWatcher on teardown), so a running cb serve does reload box-local schemas without restart. The only defect the earlier verifier showed is the directory name: boxCodePaths defines schemasDir as packageRoot/src/schemas (box-shape.ts:242) and box-shape.ts:205-236 explicitly treats a stray config/schemas/*.ts as legacy/invisible, so the story's cited path is stale — but that is a wording/accuracy issue, not a missing-or-unwired-code issue, so on my lens the story stands.

The capability has a live, always-on entry point: webapp/server-box-scope.ts:171 calls ensureSchemaWatcher(box.boxRoot) at box registration (not on a UI subscription), and core/schema-watcher.ts chokidar-watches the box's schemas dir, calling invalidateBoxSchemas so the next loadBoxSchemas (schemas/registry.ts rebuildBoxSchemas, content-hash-busted dynamic import) rebuilds inside the running cb serve — no flag, no config, no restart. The acting role (a box agent with filesystem access) is told exactly where to write the file by the generated agent guide: core/agent-guide/box-shape.ts boxCodeLocationSection renders a table of boxCodePathsRelativeToBoxRoot and says those dirs are 'Editable, hot-reloaded - no restart needed', and core/box/templates.ts writes SCHEMAS_CLAUDE_MD_V2 into that dir. The only defect is which directory the story names: boxCodePaths (lib/box-shape.ts:242) resolves schemasDir to packageRoot/src/schemas, and findLegacySchemaFiles exists because a .ts left in boxRoot/config/schemas is invisible to the loader; that is a path-accuracy problem for another lens, not an absence of an entry point, so my lens is satisfied.

The hot-reload machinery is real (schemas/registry.ts rebuild + invalidateBoxSchemas, core/schema-watcher.ts chokidar watch), but it reads only boxCodePaths(shape).schemasDir, which lib/box-shape.ts:242 defines as path.join(shape.packageRoot, 'src/schemas') — registry.ts:250 and schema-watcher.ts:38 both use that single helper, with no fallback branch. The story literally names the box's `config/schemas/*.ts` as the place to add the card type; box-shape.ts:205-213 documents that dir as the legacy location whose stray *.ts is 'invisible to the schema loader (which only reads the v2 path)', and findLegacySchemaFiles/describeLegacySchemaFiles exist solely to warn about files left there. So a card type added at the path the story names is picked up by nothing; the delivered capability is narrower/differently located than the wording claims (the agent-guide line at core/agent-guide/cards.ts:175 still says config/schemas/, but it is prose, not a loader path).

triage.reasoning: The hot-reload machinery the story describes is real and always-on (registry.ts content-hash-busted dynamic import + invalidateBoxSchemas; schema-watcher chokidar watch started at box registration in webapp/server-box-scope.ts:171), so the reviewers were right that the story's path is stale — but stopping there misses why the story says `config/schemas/`: the box's own generated agent guide says it, in the imperative sentence that tells an agent what to do. Verified in the live test box guide (line 302) against the correct code-location table (line 445) in the same file. A card type written where the guide points is silently ignored — no loader read, no hook error — and the guide's `config/schemas/CLAUDE.md` reference dangles because `cb init` writes that file into `src/schemas/` while still mkdir-ing an empty decoy `config/schemas/`. That is a product defect an agent (and through it the boxholder) hits, not a catalog wording problem. The story itself should also be corrected to name `src/schemas/` at the package root.

title: Discover what templates exist and what arguments they take
story: As an agent about to create a card, I want cb create --list-templates and --describe-template <name> to print each template's description, card types, and per-argument optionality, array-ness, description and default, so that I can call it correctly without reading the source.
evidence: create.ts handles --list-templates via getAllTemplates() and --describe-template via describeTemplateArgs(); templates-describe.ts inspects the Zod args shape to render each line, and docs-gen/content.ts folds the same output into the generated card-type docs.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/create.ts registers --list-templates and --describe-template <name> on `cb create`; the action loads box schemas first, then prints each template's name, default-for types, description and card types for --list-templates, or console.log(describeTemplateArgs(name)) for --describe-template. src/schemas/templates-describe.ts's describeTemplateArgs prints Template/Description/Card types then one line per Zod shape key via describeArgLine, which marks array-ness (isArraySchema), '(optional)' via isOptional(), the arg description, and '[default: …]' from getDefaultValue. src/core/docs-gen/content.ts:61 calls the same describeTemplateArgs when generating the per-card-type docs' Templates section.

title: Edit a box schema live without breaking the running box
story: As a boxholder editing a box-local schema, I want the running box to pick up the change on the next load while a broken mid-edit save keeps serving the last good version, so that an incomplete file never regresses a working card type to unknown.
evidence: loadOneSchemaFile() hashes each file's source and cache-busts import() with ?v=<hash>, falling back to the record's last-good card on read/import/export failure; invalidateBoxSchemas() plus the dirtyEpoch/single-flight rebuild keeps the cache correct when an edit lands mid-rebuild.

verdict.note: src/schemas/registry.ts loadOneSchemaFile() sha256-hashes the file source (line 323) and imports via pathToFileURL(...)+`?v=${hash}` to defeat Node's permanent import cache; every failure path (readFile throw, import throw, missing/invalid default cardSchema export) pushes onto `failures` and returns reuse(prior, boxRoot) — the record's last-good card — so a broken mid-edit save keeps the previously working type. invalidateBoxSchemas() drops the assembled snapshot while preserving boxFileRecords and bumps dirtyEpoch; rebuildUntilStable() re-runs when the epoch changed mid-rebuild, and loadBoxSchemas shares one in-flight rebuild. src/core/schema-watcher.ts ensureSchemaWatcher() chokidar-watches config/schemas with awaitWriteFinish and calls invalidateBoxSchemas on any event; it is started per box from src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts, so a running box does pick up edits on next load.

title: Embed a card inside another card's prose
story: As someone writing a card body, I want `![caption](some.figure.card)` to render that card in place through its own viewer, so that a figure or photo reads as part of the document instead of a link away from it.
evidence: makeEmbedComponents overrides the markdown Img: an in-box non-image path resolves to a ViewTarget and renders <FileView mode="embed"> frameless with the alt text as caption and query params forwarded; ImageCardRenderer honors mode==="embed" by dropping its bbox/exif chrome.

verdict.note: components/FigureEmbed.tsx's makeEmbedComponents returns an Img override; for a src that is non-empty, not external (isExternalUrl) and not an image path (isImagePath), it calls resolveContentTarget(basePath, src) and renders <FileView path mode="embed" rendererName={target.viewer} params={target.params} caption={alt}> with no figure/header wrapper, falling back to the default markdown img otherwise. It is reached from components/MarkdownCardView.tsx line 215, which passes these overrides to <Markdown components=...>, so a markdown card body's ![caption](x.figure.card) embeds. FileView.tsx defines mode 'embed' (FileViewMode) and branches at line 391; renderers/image.tsx ImageCardRenderer checks mode === "embed" (line 98) and renders the photo with the embed caption and no bbox/exif chrome.

title: Enforce cross-field card rules Zod alone can't express
story: As a schema author, I want a validate() hook that returns lint issues and a superRefine() that makes a violating card fail to load, so that invariants like a question whose status and lifecycle timestamps disagree are caught at the right severity.
evidence: CardSchemaConfig declares validate (lint-time, returns LintIssue[]) and superRefine (parse-time, enforced by frontmatterSchema.safeParse); QuestionSchema passes refineQuestionLifecycle as superRefine and ConceptMapSchema passes conceptMapErrors as validate.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cards/schema.ts declares both hooks on CardSchemaConfig: `validate?: (input: CardValidateInput) => LintIssue[]` (line 180) and `superRefine?: (fields, ctx)` (line 200); buildCardSchema wires superRefine into the frontmatter parse (`baseFrontmatter.superRefine(config.superRefine)` at line 358-360) so a violating card fails safeParse, and carries `validate` onto the resolved schema (line 381). src/schemas/question.ts defines refineQuestionLifecycle (line 187) checking status against required/forbidden lifecycle timestamp fields and passes it as `superRefine` in QuestionSchema (line 212). src/schemas/concept-map.ts defines conceptMapErrors (line 65) and passes `validate: ({fields}) => conceptMapErrors(fields)` (line 129). The lint-time hook is actually invoked: src/core/card-lint.ts:231 calls `parsed.schema.validate({fields: parsed.fields})`. Both severities exist as described.

title: Every card type gets title, contains, contains-evidence and todos for free
story: As an agent writing cards, I want title, contains, contains-evidence and todos available on every card type without each schema redeclaring them, so that one retrieval summary and one todo vocabulary work across all card types.
evidence: GLOBAL_CARD_FIELDS in src/cards/schema.ts declares title/contains/contains-evidence/todos; cardSchema() injects each into the frontmatter shape unless the schema declares its own field of the same name, recording which were injected in globalFieldNames.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cards/schema.ts line 87 declares GLOBAL_CARD_FIELDS = { title, contains, 'contains-evidence', todos } (todos via TodosFieldSchema). In cardSchema(), the loop at line 341-346 iterates GLOBAL_CARD_FIELDS, skips any name already present in config.fields ('schema-wins' comment), otherwise adds the validator to frontmatterShape and pushes the name onto globalFieldNames, which is stored on the returned CardSchema (line 368, typed at line 229-230). This is exactly what the story and evidence describe.

title: Every chat has a card you can browse
story: As a person organizing my box, I want each web chat to exist as a `chat` card with an editable identity, so that a conversation is a first-class thing in the box rather than hidden runtime state.
evidence: `createChatHuskTemplate` writes a `chat` card at session-id assignment carrying `session` and `context-dir`; `runBackfillIfNeeded` + `reconcileChatHusks` (called from registerChatRoutes) create them for pre-husk sessions, and `ChatHuskView` renders the card with an open-the-session link and delete action.

verdict.note: src/schemas/chat.ts registers ChatSchema ('chat' card, fields session + context-dir + review-span + body) and createChatHuskTemplate; husk.ts's ensureChatHusk writes store/chat/web/<date>_<shortid>.chat.card and is called from session/session-start-record.ts:66 at session-id assignment. webapp/routes/chat.ts:79 runs runBackfillIfNeeded (session/backfill.ts) then reconcileChatHusks for pre-husk sessions. frontend renderers/chat-husk.tsx registers ChatHuskView for type 'chat', which renders a Link to /<box>/chat plus DeleteChatAction; the schema instructions state the card is renameable and a hand-set title wins permanently, so identity is editable.

browser.note: store/chat/web/*.chat.card exist (6 of them) and are browsable at their card URLs. /card/store/chat/web/2026-08-21_e9590f0c.chat.card renders the ChatHusk view: heading, 'Chat e9590f0c', 'session e9590f0c-c650-41ef-b37a-3071330ccd4b', an 'Open chat →' link and a 'Delete conversation…' button, with Chat/Card/Source tabs and the normal Card actions menu (so the card's fields are inspectable/editable as an ordinary card). Note: a session created via the card page's 'New' button had not yet produced a husk file on disk at check time (husk is written at session-id assignment / first message), which I did not push further since that needs a real agent run.

title: Exclude box-specific paths from validation
story: As an operator, I want a gitignore-style ignore file for `cb validate`, so that a vendored doc tree or imported data full of example links stops drowning out real findings.
evidence: core/validation-ignore.ts reads config/cb-validate.ignore as a gitignore-style exclusion list applied on top of the builtin skips, deliberately kept under config/ and unadvertised to agents.

verdict.note: src/core/validation-ignore.ts defines VALIDATION_IGNORE_PATH = 'config/cb-validate.ignore' and `loadValidationIgnore`, which feeds the file to the `ignore` package (gitignore semantics) and returns an allow-all matcher when absent. It is consumed by the real validate paths — cli/commands/validate.ts:359, validate-markdown.ts:91, validate-pre-commit.ts:62, validate-hook.ts:99/108, validate-canonical.ts, and core/find-inbound-card-refs.ts — layered on top of the builtin skips (isBuiltinLintableMarkdown). core/install-validation-hooks.ts seeds the commented template under config/ plus a path-conditional .claude/rules/cb-validate-ignore.md warning, matching the 'unadvertised to agents' claim.

title: External links are checked after the commit, not during it
story: As a boxholder, I want newly committed external URLs checked in the background after each commit, so that link rot gets reported without a network call ever sitting in the commit's critical path.
evidence: `install-validation-hooks.ts` splices a marker-delimited managed block into `.git/hooks/post-commit` that detaches `cb validate --urls --urls-since HEAD~1`, redirecting output to `.callback-box/url-check.log`, and coexists with any foreign post-commit hook; `core/external/url-check.ts` does the fetching behind a pending cache at `.callback-box/url-checks.json`.

verdict.note: src/core/install-validation-hooks.ts defines URLCHECK_BEGIN/END markers and postCommitBlock(), which writes into .git/hooks/post-commit a block that resolves CB_URLCHECK (explicit bin, else `command -v cb`) and runs `"$CB_URLCHECK" validate --urls --urls-since HEAD~1 >.callback-box/url-check.log 2>&1 &` inside a subshell, i.e. detached, so no network call blocks the commit; upsertPostCommitBlock() splices in place or appends, preserving a foreign hook (e.g. git-lfs). installValidationHooks is called from cli/commands/init.ts and core/docs-gen/index.ts. cli/commands/validate.ts registers --urls and --urls-since <ref>, and core/external/url-check.ts does the checking with a broken/pending cache at .callback-box/url-checks.json (CACHE_REL).

title: Give the box named people and places it can recognize
story: As a boxholder, I want person and place cards sharing a name/aliases vocabulary, so that briefings can reference key people by ref and location-aware context can recognize where I am.
evidence: namedEntityFields in named-entity-fields.ts supplies the shared name + aliases pair spread into PersonSchema and PlaceSchema; PlaceSchema's description names the location-aware context use and core/place-cards.ts reads them.

verdict.note: src/schemas/named-entity-fields.ts exports namedEntityFields = { name: z.string(), aliases: z.array(z.string()).optional() }; both PersonSchema (src/schemas/person.tsx) and PlaceSchema (src/schemas/place.tsx) spread ...namedEntityFields into their fields. PlaceSchema's description is 'A named location (Home, Office) with optional coordinates so location-aware context can recognize where the boxholder is', and src/core/place-cards.ts loadPlaces() globs **/*.place.card, parses via parseCardText, and returns active cards with both lat/lng as PlaceCircle{name,lat,lng,radius}. The briefing side is real too: src/schemas/briefing.tsx line 45 defines 'key-people': z.array(KeyPersonEntry) with ref entries pointing at person cards.

title: Keep a card's files beside it in an attach scope
story: As a box agent, I want a card's binary and auxiliary files to live in a sibling `<Name>.attach/` directory addressed as `attach/<file>`, so that a card's belongings travel with it and refs into them stay stable.
evidence: shared/attach-path.ts defines `ATTACH_SUFFIX`, the `attach/` virtual ref prefix, `cardBasename` and `attachDirFor`; lib/attach-lint.ts (`lintAttachLayout`) is run by `cb validate`, and `cb attachments` manages the assets inside those dirs.

verdict.note: src/shared/attach-path.ts defines ATTACH_SUFFIX='.attach', ATTACH_PREFIX='attach/', cardBasename(), attachDirFor() (sibling `<basename>.attach` in the card's own directory), attachmentPath(), isAttachRef()/resolveAttachRef(). Ref stability is real: shared/ref-path.ts:164 resolves attach/ refs against the card's scope, core/canonical-refs.ts and core/rewrite-card-refs.ts treat isAttachRef paths as canonical/not-rewritten. lib/attach-lint.ts exports lintAttachLayout (basename-collision + reserved literal `attach` name), invoked from src/cli/commands/validate.ts:203, and src/cli/commands/attachments.ts registers `cb attachments verify/migrate/add/overwrite/...` operating on assets inside .attach/ scopes.

title: Keep bookkeeping card types out of search and grouped apart in the guide
story: As an agent reading the box, I want operational card types marked searchable:false and every type tagged authored/synced/system, so that search results are content rather than job records and the agent guide's card catalogue groups types by who creates them.
evidence: getSearchableTypes() filters cardSchemas (plus box-local ones) on schema.searchable; CardCategory in cards/schema.ts defines authored/synced/system and the ordered cardSchemas array in registry.ts is documented as the guide catalogue's rendering order.

verdict.note: src/cards/schema.ts:119 defines `export type CardCategory = "authored" | "synced" | "system"`, and the schema builder (line ~369) defaults `searchable` to true and `category` to "authored", so every type carries a category. src/schemas/registry.ts:384 getSearchableTypes() concatenates cardSchemas with box-local schemas and filters on `s.searchable`; it is consumed by core/search/refresh.ts, contains-update.ts and query.ts, so non-searchable types stay out of the index/query. Bookkeeping types set searchable:false (chat-thread, chat-job, contains-backfill-job, todo-review-job, question-followup-job, procedure, procedure-run, nav, view, landmark). src/core/agent-guide/cards.ts defines CARD_CATEGORY_GROUPS and cardTypesSection() filters schemas per group heading ("Types you create and edit" / "Synced & captured" / "System bookkeeping"), which is the catalogue grouping the story describes.

title: Let a box own specific fields of a shipped template card
story: As an operator taking a template update, I want a schema to declare which frontmatter keys the box owns as state, so that a box that differs only in, say, a schedule's enabled toggle takes the new version with its own value preserved instead of parking the update.
evidence: TemplateMergePolicy in cards/schema.ts declares boxOwnedFields and cardSchema() carries it onto the resolved schema as templateMerge; the docblock states divergence outside those keys still parks the update for review.

verdict.note: src/cards/schema.ts:143-150 defines TemplateMergePolicy with readonly boxOwnedFields, CardSchemaConfig.templateMerge (line 206) carries it, and cardSchema() copies it onto the resolved schema (schema.ts:387-389). src/schemas/scheduled-script.tsx:106 declares templateMerge: { boxOwnedFields: ["enabled"] }. The behavior is real in src/core/install-template-file.ts: canonicalize() strips owned fields before hashing so a box differing only in `enabled` matches last-installed/prior stock and takes the 'overwritten' path, with applyBoxOwnedFields carrying the box's value onto the new template (lines 316-380); divergence elsewhere still falls through to the 'parked' branch. It is wired in: src/core/box/defaults.ts:332-334 passes ScheduledScriptSchema.templateMerge.boxOwnedFields to installTemplateFile for config/schedules cards.

title: Link one card to another with a typed ref
story: As a schema author, I want a card field to hold a `{ ref: … }` pointer to another card and to declare whether that target is safe to inline into an agent prompt, so that cards form a graph without raw external content leaking into context.
evidence: `cardRef()`/`opaqueContentRef()` in cards/ref-fields.ts tag the `{ ref: string }` shape with a ref-kind on the Zod schema; `collectInlineRefs` walks schema+value and returns only inline-safe refs. shared/box-path.ts defines the ref forms (leading-slash box-absolute vs document-relative).

verdict.note: cards/ref-fields.ts defines cardRef() and opaqueContentRef(), both returning z.object({ ref: z.string() }) tagged via zod .meta() with `callbackBoxRefKind` = card|opaque, and collectInlineRefs(schema, fields) walks schema+value in lockstep (objects, arrays, unions), pushing value.ref only where the schema declares `ref` and its kind is not 'opaque'. It is consumed at the prompt-inlining boundary in core/reactor/batch-jobs.ts:114. schemas/email-message.tsx:46 declares "body-file": opaqueContentRef(), the untrusted-email-bytes case named in the module docs. shared/box-path.ts documents the two ref forms (leading-slash box-absolute vs document-relative) and boxRelativePath normalizes them; core/find-inbound-card-refs.ts reads the ref graph in reverse.

title: Lint card references inside views
story: As a box agent, I want `cardRef=` attributes in my view files checked for existence and rewritten when the target moves, so that a view's links rot no differently from a card's.
evidence: extractViewRefs() matches literal `cardRef="…"` in views/*.tsx and lintViewRefs/collectViewRefWarnings resolve each through resolveRefExists for `cb validate`; the rewrite half rides rewrite-card-refs.ts on `cb mv`.

verdict.note: core/views/refs.ts's CARD_REF_ATTR regex extracts literal cardRef="…" from view sources; lintViewRefs resolves each via resolveRefExists (query stripped) and collectViewRefWarnings prefixes the view's relative path — called from cli/commands/validate.ts at three sites (lines ~193, 206, 231) for `cb validate`. The rewrite half is rewriteViewRefs/applyViewTransform in core/rewrite-card-refs.ts, invoked from core/commands/move-operations.ts (lines ~146, ~235) and find-inbound-card-refs.ts, i.e. on the move path. Expression-form cardRef={expr} is skipped, as the story's scope implies.

title: List cards with fields pulled from their frontmatter
story: As a box agent, I want `cb ls` to match cards by glob and print a format string whose `{field}` placeholders are dotted paths into each card's frontmatter, so that I can survey a set of cards without opening each one.
evidence: core/commands/ls.ts globs card paths and renders the `--format` template through `lookupField`/`loadCardFrontmatter` from core/frontmatter-field.ts, which walks dotted paths like `exif.camera`.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/commands/ls.ts registers the `ls` core command: expandPath() globs via `glob` (or lists a directory / literal path) filtered by isCardFile, and applyTemplate() replaces every `{...}` placeholder by calling lookupField() from core/frontmatter-field.ts, which splits the expression on '.' and walks nested frontmatter mappings (e.g. exif.camera), returning '' for missing/non-scalar values; frontmatter comes from loadCardFrontmatter(). The CLI entry exists and is reachable: src/cli/commands/ls.ts defines `cb ls <paths...> -f/--format <template>` and src/cli/index.ts line 132 does program.addCommand(lsCommand). Output is `relativePath\tformatted` per card, so a whole set is surveyed without opening files.

title: Name a card so its type and identity read off the filename
story: As a box agent, I want a card's filename (`Name.type.card`, or a bare `type.card` for the one card of that type in a directory) to carry its type and identity, so that I can tell what a file is and find cards by path without opening them.
evidence: `parseCardFileName` in shared/card-name.ts implements the nominal/positional/`.job.card` grammar; card-io.ts and lib/paths.ts (`isCardFile`, `parseCardName`) use it to route a file to its schema.

verdict.note: src/shared/card-name.ts parseCardFileName implements exactly the claimed grammar: nominal `Name.<type>.card`, positional bare `<type>.card` (name null, 'the type of this directory'), plus the `Name.<kind>.job.card` → `<kind>-job` convention; cardTypeFromName wraps it for paths/refs. src/core/card-io.ts imports it in typeFromFilename (line 448) and uses it at load time (card-io.ts:311, :425) to route a file to its registered schema, with further callers in card-lint.ts, core/todo/collect.ts and trpc/routers/card.ts. src/lib/paths.ts carries parseCardName/buildCardName/isCardFile implementing the same nominal/positional split (documented there as a legacy divergence on job cards only). The only inaccuracy is the evidence line saying lib/paths.ts uses parseCardFileName — it has its own copy — which does not change the capability.

title: Normalize refs to their box-root form
story: As a box agent, I want `cb validate --canonical --fix` to rewrite document-relative refs into box-root form — and only when the target actually resolves — so that refs across the box read the same way without inventing paths for links that were already broken.
evidence: canonical-refs.ts collects the non-canonical findings; canonicalize-refs.ts performs the text-surgical rewrite through the `cb mv` scanner (never parse-and-reserialize, so frontmatter key order is preserved) and skips refs that don't resolve; validate-canonical.ts (`runCanonicalFix`, `formatCanonicalReport`) is the CLI surface.

verdict.note: canonical-refs.ts has checkCanonicalRef/planCanonicalRef classifying refs as canonical/rewritable/escapes/dangling/ambiguous, probing existence twice (as-written and box-root reading) through resolveRefExists/dossierLinkProbe. canonicalize-refs.ts (canonicalizeBox, CanonicalizeReport with refsRewritten/refsRepaired/ambiguous/skipped) does the rewrite through rewrite-card-refs.ts's collect/rewrite token machinery (text-surgical, skipFencedCode for cards), and refs that resolve under neither reading or that escape the box are counted skipped, never rewritten. CLI surface is validate-canonical.ts `runCanonicalFix`/`formatCanonicalReport`, invoked from validate.ts's `cb validate` action at line 337-339 when --canonical and --fix are both given (--fix alone errors; --canonical is whole-box only). The one extension beyond the story's wording is the deliberate 'repair' of dangling refs that resolve from the box root, still gated on a resolving target.

title: One accumulating conversation card per outside chat
story: As a boxholder, I want each Telegram chat or group to have a single durable thread card in the box that the connector keeps appending incoming messages to, with its participants linked to person cards, so that the whole conversation is box content the agent can read rather than transient message traffic.
evidence: `ChatThreadSchema` (schemas/chat-thread.ts, registered in registry.ts) defines `chat-id`, `connector`, `description`, `participants[].ref` and a chronological `entries[]` of `kind: message` / `kind: seen`; `processUpdateToThread` (telegram-ingest.ts) calls `ensureThreadFile`, `ensureParticipant` and `appendMessageToThread` from chat-utils.ts to maintain `store/chat/telegram/<ChatSlug>/thread.chat-thread.card` and links each sender to `/people/<slug>.person.card`.

verdict.note: ChatThreadSchema in callback-box/src/schemas/chat-thread.ts defines chat-id, connector, description, participants[].ref and a chronological entries[] discriminated union of kind:message / kind:seen, and it is imported and listed in src/schemas/registry.ts (lines 42, 130). processUpdateToThread in src/connectors/telegram-ingest.ts builds a personRef of the form /people/<slug>.person.card, calls ensureThreadFile (which creates/reuses store/chat/<connector>/<chatSlug>/thread.chat-thread.card, one per chat, under a card lock), ensureParticipant, and appendMessageToThread — all from src/connectors/chat-utils.ts, which append to the same durable file rather than replacing it. It is reachable: src/connectors/telegram-webhook.ts:53 and src/connectors/telegram.ts:212/289 call it on inbound updates, and group chats get their own slug via getChatSlug with msg.chat.title.

title: Override a shipped card type or template from inside the box
story: As a box owner, I want a schema file in my box that reuses a built-in card type's name (or exports a template with a built-in template's name) to take precedence over the shipped one, so that I can change how a standard card type validates or what `cb create` writes for it without patching callback-box.
evidence: createCardSchemaMap() seeds the map with the built-in cardSchemas then writes box-local schemas over it, so a colliding `type` wins (last write). The template registry keeps an owner-stack per name where the last registration is effective, so registerBoxTemplate() shadows a same-named built-in and unregisterBoxTemplates(boxRoot) on reload restores the built-in rather than losing the name.

verdict.note: schemas/registry.ts createCardSchemaMap() seeds the Map from built-in `cardSchemas` then map.set()s each box-local schema from loadBoxSchemas(boxRoot), and the doc comment states a colliding type wins by last write; no collision check rejects the override (isKnownCardType only consults the built-ins). loadOneSchemaFile() calls registerBoxTemplate(template, boxRoot) for a schema module's optional `template` export, and schemas/templates-registry.ts keeps a per-name owner stack where effective() returns the last registration, so a box template shadows a same-named built-in; rebuildBoxSchemas() calls unregisterBoxTemplates(boxRoot) on reload, which filters that owner out and restores the shadowed built-in rather than deleting the name. createCardSchemaMap(boxRoot) is used on the live loader path (core/load-context.ts).

title: Read a card's frontmatter without the schema machinery
story: As a script scanning many cards, I want to split a .card file into its frontmatter block and body and get a best-effort parsed mapping (null on malformed YAML), so that scans can peek at fields cheaply and skip broken cards instead of crashing.
evidence: splitCardContent(), parseFrontmatterObject() and renderFrontmatterBlock() in src/cards/frontmatter.ts implement the fence split, validation-free YAML read, and the inverse render (lineWidth: 0 so long values never fold); ParseError in errors.ts carries the offending location.

verdict.note: src/cards/frontmatter.ts exports splitCardContent (regex FRONTMATTER_BLOCK splits fenced YAML into frontmatterText/body/lineOffset/hasFrontmatter, returning input unchanged when absent), parseFrontmatterObject (validation-free parseYaml wrapped in try/catch that returns null on malformed YAML, no frontmatter, or a non-mapping — its doc comment explicitly says 'so scans skip the card rather than crashing'), and renderFrontmatterBlock (stringifyYaml with lineWidth: 0). src/cards/errors.ts defines ParseError carrying a Location (source/line/column). Both the capability and the cited files match; nothing schema-related is required to call these.

title: Record everyday notes and extracted things as typed cards
story: As an agent filing what the box takes in, I want doc, record, memo and recipe card types with their own fields and handling instructions, so that agent-authored prose, discrete extracted units, inbox notes, and scaling-aware recipes each have the right shape instead of loose .md files.
evidence: DocSchema ("the default for agent-authored prose instead of a plain .md"), RecordSchema (discrete extracted unit), MemoSchema (captured text or voice note) and RecipeSchema (scaling-aware ingredients via the recipe Markdoc tags) each call cardSchema() with fields and agent instructions.

verdict.note: All four schema files exist and call cardSchema() with fields plus agent `instructions`: src/schemas/doc.tsx DocSchema (description literally 'the default for agent-authored prose instead of a plain .md'; title + body), record.tsx RecordSchema ('A discrete extracted unit (inventory item, archived document, contact)...' with status/name/sources/dates/persons/location/measures), memo.ts MemoSchema ('A captured text or voice note from the user — generic inbox input awaiting processing' with status/source/context/transcription), and recipe.tsx RecipeSchema ('scaling-aware ingredients, steps, and substitutions via the recipe Markdoc tags' with title/source/tags/hero-image/body). All four are imported and registered in src/schemas/registry.ts, so they are live card types, not orphans.

title: Refs between cards are found by convention and reported by path
story: As a boxholder renaming or deleting cards, I want every {ref: ...} and refs: [...] value found at any depth of a card's frontmatter with a JSON path attached, so that link checking and rewriting can point at the exact position that broke.
evidence: extractRefs()/walkForRefs() in src/cards/schema.ts recurse through objects and arrays collecting keys literally named ref (string) or refs (array of strings) with an indexed path; card-lint.ts resolves them and emits type "reference" issues.

verdict.note: src/cards/schema.ts:404 extractRefs() delegates to walkForRefs(), which recurses through arrays (appending `[i]`) and plain objects (appending `.key`), pushing {path, ref} for any key literally named `ref` with a string value and each string element of a key named `refs`, so refs are found at any depth with an indexed JSON path. src/core/card-lint.ts:168 calls extractRefs(parsed.fields), resolves each via resolveRefExists, and emits LintIssue entries with type "reference" naming the exact refPath; lint-format.ts:117 counts those `type === "reference"` warnings for reporting. Identification is by convention, not schema declaration, exactly as the story says.

title: Register a new card type's look in one place
story: As an agent or contributor adding a card type, I want one registration that gives it both a renderer and its list icon/row, so that a new type doesn't silently fall back to the generic view because only half of it was registered.
evidence: registerFileType takes one selector ({ type } or a path/data predicate) plus renderer and listUI facets; getRenderers returns every renderer match sorted by priority while resolveFileTypeUI picks exactly one list UI (warning on collisions), and renderers/setup.ts imports each renderer module to trigger registration.

verdict.note: file-type-registry.ts's registerFileType(selector, { renderer?, listUI? }) does share one store and both facets are optional, but no code anywhere registers both in one call: every renderer registration (renderers/question.tsx, webpage.tsx, extfile.tsx, gsheet.tsx, ... imported by renderers/setup.ts) passes only `renderer`, and every listUI registration lives separately in file-types/builtins.tsx's registerBuiltinFileTypes() as `{ listUI: { icon: ... } }`. `grep -rn 'listUI:'` finds hits only in file-types/builtins.tsx. So adding a card type still means two registrations in two files, and nothing detects a half-registration — the registry only warns on duplicate type-keyed listUI collisions in registerFileType/resolveFileTypeUI, never on a renderer with no listUI. The story's 'one registration ... so that only half of it was registered can't happen' overclaims what the code guarantees.

panel.note: file-type-registry.ts holds one live `entries` store with registerFileType(selector, {renderer?, listUI?}), plus getRenderers (priority-sorted, all matches) and resolveFileTypeUI (type match, then path match with a collision console.warn, then fallbackFileTypeUI) — exactly the unified API the story describes. Both facades re-export it: renderers/index.ts exports registerFileType/getRenderers, file-types/registry.tsx exports registerFileType/resolveFileTypeUI/fallbackFileTypeUI, and file-types/index.ts re-exports registerBuiltinFileTypes. It is wired end to end: main.tsx line 8 does `import "./renderers/setup"` (which imports all 22 renderer modules to trigger registration) and line 13 calls registerBuiltinFileTypes(); consumers actually read it — components/FileView.tsx and ExternalDocument.tsx and renderers/directory.tsx call getRenderers, components/ui/FileEntry.tsx calls resolveFileTypeUI. The earlier verifier's objection is that no single call site passes both facets at once (renderers pass `renderer`, file-types/builtins.tsx passes `listUI`), which is a wording/overclaim question, not an existence one — the shared registration code exists, is exported, imported, and mounted.

The registration API is live on the ordinary app boot path: main.tsx line 8 imports "./renderers/setup", which side-effect-imports all 24 renderer modules (each calling registerFileType from file-type-registry.ts), and line 13 calls registerBuiltinFileTypes(), whose builtins register listUI entries through the same registerFileType/shared `entries` store. Both facets are then consumed by real UI: getRenderers() drives components/FileView.tsx:346, ExternalDocument.tsx:78 and renderers/directory.tsx:81, and resolveFileTypeUI() drives components/ui/FileEntry.tsx:153 (falling back to fallbackFileTypeUI/GenericIcon). file-types/registry.tsx merely re-exports the same functions, so a contributor adding a card type reaches the capability by importing registerFileType and adding one line to renderers/setup.ts — no flag, no config, no gating. The earlier verdict's objection (that no existing call site passes both facets in one call, so half-registration isn't actually prevented) is a truthfulness/mechanism question, not a reachability one; on my lens the entry point plainly exists.

file-type-registry.ts exposes registerFileType(selector, { renderer?, listUI? }) over one shared `entries` store, so a single call CAN carry both facets — but both are optional, and its own header comment says 'a type can register a renderer only, a listUI only, or both in one call — exactly as before, just through one function instead of two.' Nothing detects a half-registration: the only console.warn paths are duplicate type-keyed listUI collisions in registerFileType and multi-match path collisions in resolveFileTypeUI; a renderer with no listUI silently yields fallbackFileTypeUI (GenericIcon). In practice no call site pairs them: all ~20 renderer registrations (renderers/question.tsx, gsheet.tsx, image.tsx, recipe.tsx, ...) pass only `renderer`, and every `listUI:` in the tree is in file-types/builtins.tsx, so types with both still take two registrations in two files. The 'so that' clause promises an outcome — no silent generic fallback from registering only half — that the code does not produce.

triage.reasoning: The capability the story names is real and reachable. file-type-registry.ts is one store with one entry point, `registerFileType(selector, { renderer?, listUI? })`, and a single call can carry both facets — its own header says so explicitly ('a type can register a renderer only, a listUI only, or both in one call — exactly as before, just through one function instead of two'). Both facades re-export it (renderers/index.ts, file-types/registry.tsx), main.tsx boots both sides (`import "./renderers/setup"` plus registerBuiltinFileTypes()), and consumers read both (FileView/ExternalDocument/directory via getRenderers, FileEntry via resolveFileTypeUI). The refutation rests on 'no existing call site passes both facets at once' — true (the ~20 renderer modules pass `renderer`; builtins.tsx is a deliberately centralized icon table of type→icon lines), but that describes where the pre-existing built-ins live, not what a contributor adding a card type can do today, which is exactly the one call the story asks for. The only genuine over-reach is the 'so that' clause implying half-registration is *prevented* — the registry warns only on duplicate type-keyed listUI collisions, so a renderer with no listUI still falls back to GenericIcon silently. That is a wording softening for the catalog ('so both facets are registered in one place'), not a product break: nothing is missing, broken, or unreachable.

title: Rename or move a card without breaking links to it
story: As a box agent, I want `cb mv` to relocate a card together with its attach scope and rewrite every ref that pointed at it, so that reorganizing the box doesn't leave dangling links.
evidence: cli/commands/move.ts takes `<paths...>` with `--commit`/`--dry-run` and runs the core move command; move-operations.ts (`moveOne`, `moveDir`) relocates the file plus same-basename companions and calls into core/rewrite-card-refs.ts, which text-splices new ref values into referring cards, views, and markdown.

verdict.note: cli/commands/move.ts registers the `mv` command (`<paths...>`, `--commit`, `--dry-run`) and is wired into the CLI at cli/index.ts:107; it calls runCommand({name:"move"}) into core/commands/move.ts, which delegates to moveOne/moveDir in core/commands/move-operations.ts. moveOne resolves the card's attach scope via attachDirFor and moves the same-basename companions including `<basename>.attach/`, then calls rewriteReferrerRefs/rewriteMovedCardRefs/rewriteViewRefs from core/rewrite-card-refs.ts, which resolves each ref against its holding file and rewrites frontmatter `ref:`/`refs:`, body `ref=` attributes, and inline markdown links across cards, views, and plain .md files. Matches the story's claim about moving the attach scope and rewriting refs.

title: Repair links whose target moved out from under them
story: As a box agent, I want `cb relink` to find the new home of a broken internal markdown link and rewrite it when the match is unambiguous, listing the ambiguous and unresolvable ones, so that links survive reorganizations that happened outside `cb mv`.
evidence: cli/commands/relink.ts calls `repairBoxLinks` and prints fixed / ambiguous (with candidates) / unresolvable buckets, with a `--dry-run` preview.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/relink.ts defines the `relink` Commander command (registered in src/cli/index.ts:108 via program.addCommand(relinkCommand)) with --dry-run and --json; it calls repairBoxLinks(boxRoot, { dryRun }) and printReport prints Fixed/Would-fix, ambiguous links with each candidate listed, and unresolvable links. src/core/link-repair.ts's decideRepair builds a basename index and returns status "fixed" with a box-root-absolute newUrl only when a single match (or a unique trailing-suffix winner) exists, "ambiguous" with sorted candidates on ties, and "unresolvable" when nothing matches; repairBoxLinks partitions these into RepairReport.fixed/ambiguous/unresolvable. This matches the story literally, including the ambiguous-are-listed-not-guessed behavior.

title: Scaffold a card's attachment files along with the card
story: As an agent creating a figure card, I want the template to also write starter files into the card's attach scope, so that a single cb create produces a card whose runnable source already renders.
evidence: TemplateDefinition.attachments returns {relPath, content} entries written into <basename>.attach/; figure-starters.ts holds one complete p5js/three/d3/canvas-loop entry module scaffolded into attach/sketch.ts by the figure template.

verdict.note: TemplateDefinition in src/schemas/templates-registry.ts:29 declares optional `attachments(args) => Array<{relPath, content}>`, and src/core/commands/create.ts:165 consumes it: it computes <basename>.attach/ from the card path, mkdir -p's and writes each relPath, printing `Scaffolded: <rel>`. src/schemas/templates-builtins.ts:234 registers the figure template with `attachments: (args) => [{relPath: "sketch.ts", content: figureStarterSketch(args.runtime)}]`, and createFigureTemplate in src/schemas/figure.ts sets `entry: "attach/sketch.ts"`. src/schemas/figure-starters.ts holds complete default-exporting entry modules for p5js/three/d3/canvas-loop behind figureStarterSketch(). So one `cb create` writes card plus runnable source as claimed.

title: See which box schemas failed to load
story: As an operator, I want a box's current schema load failures (file, message, timestamp) reported through cb status and /healthz, so that keep-last-good behaviour doesn't hide a broken schema file behind a console warning.
evidence: setSchemaLoadFailures()/listSchemaLoadFailures() in schema-load-status.ts hold a per-box snapshot replaced wholesale on each rebuild; rebuildBoxSchemas() pushes a SchemaLoadFailure for every unreadable, throwing, or wrong-shaped schema file.

verdict.note: src/schemas/schema-load-status.ts holds a per-box Map of SchemaLoadFailure {file,message,at} with setSchemaLoadFailures (replaces wholesale, deletes on empty) and listSchemaLoadFailures. registry.ts loadOneSchemaFile pushes a failure for an unreadable file (line 317), a module that isn't a cardSchema default export (334), and an import that throws (345), while returning the prior schema via reuse() — the keep-last-good path; rebuildBoxSchemas calls setSchemaLoadFailures at line 286 (and clears at 235). Consumers: src/cli/commands/status.ts:90-99 calls loadBoxSchemas then prints 'Schema load failures: N' plus 'file: message' under --verbose; src/webapp/server-root.ts:170-179 folds per-box failure counts into /healthz; health-engine.ts:77-89 adds a 'box-schemas' error check listing file: message. Caveat on wording only: /healthz reports counts per box (not file/message), and the `at` timestamp is stored but never printed on either surface.

title: Ship box-specific templates alongside box-specific card types
story: As a boxholder, I want a box schema file to also export a template that registers under my box's ownership, so that cb create offers it, it can shadow a built-in of the same name, and reloading my box never clobbers another hosted box's templates.
evidence: loadOneSchemaFile() guards a module's optional `template` export with isTemplateDefinition() and calls registerBoxTemplate(template, boxRoot); templates-registry.ts keys each name to an owner-stack so unregisterBoxTemplates(owner) restores a shadowed built-in.

verdict.note: src/schemas/registry.ts loadOneSchemaFile() reads mod.template, guards it with isTemplateDefinition() (line ~363) and calls registerBoxTemplate(template, boxRoot); loadBoxSchemas() calls unregisterBoxTemplates(boxRoot) up front so a reload drops only that box's registrations. src/schemas/templates-registry.ts keys each name to an owner-stack (Registration[]), effective() takes the last entry so a box template shadows the BUILTIN_OWNER entry, and unregisterBoxTemplates filters by owner so the shadowed built-in is restored and other boxes' entries survive. cb create reaches it: src/cli/commands/create.ts calls findBoxRoot + loadBoxSchemas before --list-templates/--describe-template and getAllTemplates().

title: Stamp a place card with where I am now
story: As a box agent, I want to write the current device fix into an existing place card, so that named places get real coordinates without anyone reading them off a map.
evidence: `cb location mark <card-path>` runs markPlace(), a parse-mutate-reserialize on the raw frontmatter (preserving unknown keys and the body) that sets lat/lng/radius; an existing place only grows when the fix is outside its radius and --expand is passed.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/place-mark.ts exports applyMark/markPlace: it splits the card with splitCardContent, parses frontmatter with yaml parseDocument and only doc.set()s lat/lng/radius, reserializing with the original body and other keys intact. loadLocation supplies the current device fix; a coordless card gets center=fix with radius max(accuracy, MIN_PLACE_RADIUS_M), a fix inside the radius is a no-op, and a fix outside only grows the radius when expand is true (Math.ceil(distance)). The CLI entry is callback-box/src/cli/commands/location.ts line 52, .command("mark <card-path>") with --expand, and locationCommand is registered in src/cli/index.ts:147.

title: Trash a card from its page, warned about what links to it
story: As a person using the box, I want to delete a card from its own page and be shown first how many files still link to it, so that I don't silently break references by removing something still in use.
evidence: CardActions.tsx opens a confirm dialog that queries `card.inboundRefs` then calls `card.trash`; the `trash` mutation refuses with PRECONDITION_FAILED when referrers exist unless `allowDanglingRefs`, then runs `moveCardsToTrash` + `commitTrashReceipt` (rolling back on commit failure) and emits a file-change event.

verdict.note: CardActions.tsx (rendered from FileView.tsx at three call sites, gated on isCardPath) puts 'Move to Trash…' in the card dropdown; opening it sets confirming, which enables the trpc.card.inboundRefs query and renders '<n> files link to this card' with the referrer paths and ref counts before the destructive button. webapp/trpc/routers/card.ts inboundRefs calls findInboundCardRefs, and the trash mutation re-checks referrers, throws PRECONDITION_FAILED unless allowDanglingRefs, then moveCardsToTrash + commitTrashReceipt with rollbackTrashReceipt on failure and a file-change event. Matches the story as written.

browser.note: Card actions menu on a card page offers 'View history' and 'Move to Trash…'. On box/inbox/scan-20260429T0322-dbe99514.capture-session.card the confirm dialog showed 'Move this card to Trash?', 'The card remains recoverable from box Trash and git history.', and a warning block '9 files link to this card' / 'Those links will stop working. They are not changed automatically.' listing each referrer path with its ref count. On config/main.personality.card (no referrers) the dialog showed no warning block. I cancelled both — did not delete.

title: Validate cards against their schemas
story: As a box agent, I want `cb validate` to parse every card, check it against its schema, and report broken or non-canonical refs, bad attach layout, and Markdoc body errors with file and line, so that I can find damage to box data before it spreads.
evidence: cli/commands/validate.ts assembles `lintCardsDispatch`, `lintAttachLayout`, `collectDossierCanonicalWarnings`, and markdown lint into a LintSummary printed by `formatLintResults` (cards/lint-format.ts); core/body-markdoc-lint.ts adds the universal `Markdoc.validate` body pass.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/validate.ts defines validateCommand (registered in src/cli/index.ts as `program.addCommand(validateCommand)`), and its collect* paths call lintCardsDispatch (core/card-lint.ts — frontmatter type dispatch, parseCardText Zod schema check, extractRefs/extractBodyRefs/extractBodyLinks broken-ref walk via resolveRefExists, lintBodyMarkdoc, lint-node-refs/lint-path-fields), lintAttachLayout (lib/attach-lint.ts), collectDossierCanonicalWarnings, and markdown lint, printed through formatLintResults (cards/lint-format.ts) which prefixes each issue with the card path and `startLine:startColumn`; body-markdoc-lint.ts embeds a 1-indexed line in its message. Non-canonical-ref reporting is behind the `--canonical` flag, which is a user-invocable option, not a gate.

title: Write rich, checked markup in a card body
story: As a box agent, I want card bodies to support Markdoc tags like `{% quote %}`, `{% source %}` and `{% todo %}` that are validated on write and rendered as real components in the UI, so that provenance and todos in prose are structured rather than convention.
evidence: shared/markdoc-config.ts declares the tag library (quote, source, purpose, correction, …) and is imported by both backend and frontend; body-markdoc-lint.ts runs `Markdoc.validate` over every card body during lint; frontend Markdown.tsx transforms and renders the same config into React components.

verdict.note: src/shared/markdoc-config.ts exports markdocConfig with a tag library including quote, source, purpose, correction, todo, see-also, redacted, task, image, silence and the recipe tags, each with typed Markdoc `attributes` and transforms. core/body-markdoc-lint.ts's lintBodyMarkdoc runs Markdoc parse+validate against that same config over card bodies; it is invoked from core/card-lint.ts (lintCardsDispatch), which runs on the agent write path via core/sdk-hooks.ts runCardLint as well as `cb validate`/validate-hook/pre-commit. frontend Markdown.tsx imports markdocConfig from @shared/markdoc-config, transforms and renders it with React components including QuoteInline/QuoteBlock from Quote.tsx and Source components.

title: A chat inherits the chat settings of the place it starts in
story: As a person opening a chat scoped to a directory, I want that place's landmark to decide whether the chat starts in narration mode or shows prose, so that voice-first corners of the box behave that way without me toggling settings each time.
evidence: `readLandmarkFeaturesForDir` reads `navigation.chat-app` off the directory's landmark card; both new-session paths — `resolveSendTarget` in chat-send-target.ts and the `reserveSession` mutation — pass it through `mergeSeedFeatures`, which layers the client's explicit pre-session choice over the landmark defaults.

verdict.note: src/core/landmark/features.ts readLandmarkFeaturesForDir finds the *.landmark.card at the top of contextDir, parses it, and returns navigation['chat-app'] entries filtered by isKnownFeature/isValidValue from src/core/chat/features.ts (registry: narration default off, prose default on); the landmark schema declares 'chat-app' at src/schemas/landmark.ts:100. Both new-session paths use it: freshSeedFeatures/resolveSendTarget in src/webapp/routes/chat-send-target.ts (mergeSeedFeatures({landmark, request: args.requestSeedFeatures}) — request wins) and the reserveSession mutation in src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat-control-procedures.ts. Seeds flow through registry.reserve/createNew into ChatSession, where src/core/chat/session/features.ts:84 does resolveFeatures(stored ?? seedFeatures), so a fresh chat starts on the landmark's values. UI entry points supply contextDir: ChatsLandmarkCard.tsx, LandmarkSessions.tsx, useOpenLandmarkChat.ts and OpenChatControl.tsx all navigate to /chat with search {session:'new', contextDir}.

browser.note: The mechanism is visibly wired — Acids_Bases.landmark.card declares chat-app: narration: "off", and chats opened there emit <chat-app narration="off" prose="on" .../> — but 'off' is also the global default, and test1 has no landmark that sets narration on or prose off, so I could not show the landmark (rather than the default) deciding. Proving it would need editing a landmark card, i.e. mutating box content.

title: A new chat is addressable before its first message
story: As a person opening a new chat, I want it to already have an id, so that a photo capture or a bulk upload lands in this chat instead of creating a second one.
evidence: The browser mints a UUID and calls the `chat.reserveSession` mutation, which records the reservation (with its landmark binding and seed features) and passes it to the harness as `coinedSessionId`; a Codex box answers `unsupported` and falls back to the `"new"` path.

verdict.note: frontend/src/pages/chat-coin-session.ts `useCoinedChat` (used by ChatPage.tsx:188 for a fresh chat) mints crypto.randomUUID() and calls the trpc `chat.reserveSession` mutation defined at webapp/trpc/routers/chat-control-procedures.ts:229, which records the reservation via registry.reserve with the landmark contextDir and merged seed features. core/chat/session/reserve.ts holds ChatReservationStore with a 6h TTL and returns reserved/taken/unsupported (unsupported for a Codex engine, and the hook falls back to the "new" path). The reserved id is passed to the harness as `coinedSessionId` (registry.ts:238, registry-warm.ts, services/claude-chat.ts sets queryOptions.sessionId), and core/bulk-upload/deliver.ts resolveBulkDeliveryTarget explicitly accepts a target whose only record is a reservation, so an upload lands in that chat rather than creating a second one.

browser.note: 'New session' fired POST /api/trpc/chat.reserveSession first, then chat.bootstrap with the already-minted id, and the URL became ?session=8548c3a1-… on an empty chat with no messages sent.

title: A send is not duplicated by a retry
story: As a person on a flaky connection, I want a resent message to be recognized as the same message and acknowledged, so that a retry does not post twice or vanish silently.
evidence: `claimMessageId`/`recordDurableClaim` dedupe by the client-minted `messageId` across in-flight and persisted claims; the frontend receipt registry settles `sent`/`queued`/`rejected` per emission id, and `<ack>` badges render the agent's acknowledgements beside the user bubble.

verdict.note: chat-send-dedup.ts implements claimMessageId/recordDurableClaim: a durable claim map persisted to .callback-box/message-dedup.json (7-day TTL) answers a retry with 200 {deduplicated:true}, and a volatile in-flight claim parks a concurrent duplicate on the first request's real outcome (createInFlightSends). chat-send-routes.ts:101 takes the claim on the client-supplied messageId and settles it on every exit via respond(); recordDurableClaim is written beside the persisted user message (line 150) so a crash loses claim and message together. api-chat.ts:245 mints the messageId client-side and retries with the same id; frontend/src/input/targets/receipts.ts defines sent/queued/rejected dispositions (with a deduplicated flag on sent), and components/chat/ack-badge.tsx renders AckBadgeCluster beside the user bubble.

title: An agent inside a chat can address that very chat
story: As the box's agent running a command mid-turn, I want `cb chat` to resolve the conversation I am running inside without being told its id, so that I can ask for a screenshot of the user's screen in this chat instead of guessing at the most-active session.
