evidence: claude-chat.ts mints a per-subprocess path and passes it as CB_CHAT_SESSION_ID_FILE (resumed sessions instead carry CB_CHAT_SESSION_ID in the spawn env); the backend writes the id into that file the moment the SDK assigns one. `cb chat screenshot` calls resolveChatSessionId() when --session is absent, which reads the env value or polls the file, and exits with 'run inside a chat session' when neither resolves.

verdict.note: core/chat/session/session-id-file.ts defines CB_CHAT_SESSION_ID / CB_CHAT_SESSION_ID_FILE, allocateSessionIdFilePath(), writeSessionIdFile(), and resolveChatSessionId() (env first, else poll the file for up to 2s). services/claude-chat.ts buildQueryOptions() mints the per-subprocess path and injects CB_CHAT_SESSION_ID_FILE only when there is no resumeSessionId and no CB_CHAT_SESSION_ID already in env, and line 295 writes the id once the SDK emits it; start.ts:132 and thread.ts:162 set CB_CHAT_SESSION_ID for resumed/coined sessions. cli/commands/chat.ts screenshotCommand ('cb chat screenshot', line 186) uses `options.session ?? await resolveChatSessionId()` and errors with 'no session — pass --session <id> or run inside a chat session' when null, then POSTs /<box>/api/chat/screenshot/request.

title: Ask the agent to change the chat's own display settings
story: As a person chatting with my box, I want to just tell the agent to stop showing its prose or to go into narration mode, so that I don't have to hunt for a settings toggle mid-conversation.
evidence: `parseChatAppDeltas` (chat/features.ts) pulls `<chat-app prose="on"/>` mutation tags out of the completed turn's text, drops read-only attributes and unknown/illegal values with a warning, and strips the tags from what the user sees; `applyAgentTurnDeltas` (session/features.ts) feeds them to `FeatureStore.applyDeltas`, which persists to chat-session-history and fires the features-changed notification. Wired at session/index.ts:271 on turn completion, and the prompt tells the agent to emit the tag (prompts.ts, "Toggle one mid-conversation").

verdict.note: src/core/chat/features.ts registers 'prose' (default on) and 'narration' (default off) with closed value sets, and parseChatAppDeltas extracts <chat-app prose="off"/> style mutation tags from agent output, skipping READ_ONLY_ATTRS and warning-dropping unknown features/invalid values while stripping the tags from the returned content. session/features.ts applyAgentTurnDeltas feeds those deltas to FeatureStore.applyDeltas, which persists via updateFeaturesForSession (chat-session-history) and fires onChange; it is invoked on turn completion at session/index.ts:271. session/prompts.ts:127 instructs the agent: 'Toggle one mid-conversation by emitting <chat-app feature="value"/> (e.g. <chat-app prose="on"/>); it applies after your turn.' So telling the agent in chat to turn off prose or enter narration mode is a supported path.

title: Ask the user's tab for a screenshot
story: As the box's agent, I want to request a screenshot of what the user is currently looking at and get their consent first, so that I can see the thing they are describing.
evidence: `cb chat screenshot --session --timeout` POSTs to `/api/chat/screenshot/request` and long-polls; the connected tab shows a FIFO `ScreenshotConsentPopup` and, on approval, captures and relays the image, with an ephemeral "shared" indicator strip.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/chat.ts defines `screenshot` with --session/--timeout (default 45s), POSTing to `${serverUrl}/${boxName}/api/chat/screenshot/request` and long-polling; src/webapp/routes/chat-screenshot-routes.ts registers POST /api/chat/screenshot/request and POST /api/chat/screenshot/:requestId (multipart PNG answer) with a screenshot-request bus event. In the frontend, useScreenshotRequests (screenshot-request-handler.ts) is mounted from InteractiveChat.tsx and rendered by ScreenshotRequestUI in InteractiveChat-view.tsx, keeping a FIFO queue whose head shows ScreenshotConsentPopup (shareViaPopup/declineViaPopup) plus the ephemeral shared-indicator rows. The one nuance: when the clerk extension relay is present, captureViaRelay answers without a per-request popup (install-time consent instead) — the popup is the fallback path, but consent-gated capture is what the code does.

title: Ask what changed in the box since the last reply
story: As the box's agent mid-conversation, I want a git-grounded report of commits and working-tree changes since my last turn, so that I answer about the box's current state rather than a stale one.
evidence: `cb chat whats-changed [--session] [--card]` POSTs to `/api/chat/whats-changed`; summarizeWhatsChanged reports commits in `marker.head..HEAD` plus the uncommitted tree, falling back to the last five commits when no turn marker exists.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/chat/whats-changed.ts summarizeWhatsChanged() loads the per-session marker (loadTurnMarker in core/chat/turn-marker.ts), prints commits in `marker.head..HEAD` via getOnelineLog/getDiffStat, falls back to the last FALLBACK_COMMITS=5 commits labeled 'No turn marker yet', then appends the uncommitted working tree (diff vs HEAD plus untracked from getStatus). The marker is actually written: core/chat/session/index.ts imports recordTurnMarkerForSession, which records HEAD at turn completion. Reachable from agents: cb chat whats-changed [--session] [--card] in src/cli/commands/chat.ts POSTs to /<box>/api/chat/whats-changed, served in src/webapp/routes/chat-send-routes.ts:270 (body validated by whatsChangedBodySchema in chat-helpers.ts:108) which calls summarizeWhatsChanged.

title: Attach pasted or dropped images to a message
story: As a person composing a chat message, I want to paste or drop images and have them ride along as `[imageN]` references, so that the agent can look at what I am talking about.
evidence: `useChatAttachments` downscales and base64-encodes pasted/dropped blobs into the emission store and inserts `[imageN]` tokens at the cursor; `validateInboundImages` in chat-send-routes.ts validates the `images` array on the wire.

verdict.note: InteractiveChat-actions.ts handlePaste/handleDrop call extractImageFiles on e.clipboardData / e.dataTransfer and feed addImageFiles from useChatAttachments (InteractiveChat-attachments.ts), which uses processImageBlob (lib/image-paste) to downscale + base64-encode and inserts `[image${a.id}]` tokens at the textarea cursor (line 195). These are bound on the textarea in InteractiveChat-view.tsx (onPaste/onDrop) via the composer and mobile-row components. draftAttachments in input/emission.ts carries {id, mimeType, dataBase64} into the emission, chat-send-routes.ts validateInboundImages/validateImages checks the wire `images` array before buildSendInput, and services/claude-chat-content.ts narrows each image block into a complete Anthropic base64/url source.

browser.note: Dispatched a real paste of an image/png File into the composer: it became '[image1] ' in the textarea with a thumbnail chip. (A file chosen through the file picker instead gets [file1], so the [imageN] namespace is specific to images.)

title: Chat scoped to the nearest landmark
story: As a person using the box, I want starting a chat from a card to bind it to the nearest enclosing landmark and inherit that landmark's chat settings, so that the conversation is already scoped to the right part of the box.
evidence: nearestLandmarkDir() walks up from a card's directory to the deepest ancestor holding a `*.landmark.card` (clamped at the box root, with isBoxRelativeCardPath rejecting traversal); readLandmarkFeaturesForDir() seeds chat features from the landmark's `navigation.chat-app` mapping at session creation.

verdict.note: nearestLandmarkDir (src/core/landmark/nearest.ts) globs **/*.landmark.card and nearestDirFromDirs picks the deepest ancestor-or-self directory, defaulting to "" (box root); isBoxRelativeCardPath rejects leading / and '..'. It is called by the tRPC procedure chat.openForCard (src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat.ts:101-113), whose UI entry point is the 'Chat'/'New' buttons in src/frontend/src/pages/card/components/OpenChatControl.tsx, rendered by CardViewPage; a new chat navigates to /<box>/chat?session=new&contextDir=<landmarkDir>&card=<path>. Feature inheritance is real: chat-control-procedures.ts reserveSession calls readLandmarkFeaturesForDir(boxRoot, contextDir) (src/core/landmark/features.ts), which reads the landmark card's navigation['chat-app'] map and merges it as seedFeatures; chat-send-target.ts does the same on send.

browser.note: From /card/store/courses/Acids_Bases.attach/Acids_Bases_Progress.progress.card the 'New' button opened /chat?session=<new>&contextDir=store%2Fcourses%2FAcids_Bases.attach&card=<that card> — bound to the nearest enclosing landmark's directory with the card already in the companion pane. The 'inherits the landmark's chat settings' half could not be distinguished: the only landmark carrying chat-app settings (Acids_Bases.landmark.card) sets narration:"off", which is also the default, so an inherited value and a default look identical.

title: Choose the model this chat runs on
story: As a person about to ask something hard or trivial, I want to switch the model for this chat, so that the next turn runs on the model I picked.
evidence: `chat.setModel` validates the model against the session's engine with `isChatModelAllowed`, persists it via the per-session model file, and restarts the subprocess (deferring the restart to turn end when busy) so the next turn picks it up.

verdict.note: Reachable end to end: SessionChip.tsx renders ModelPanel (SessionChip-model-panel.tsx) whose MenuItem calls onSelectModel; InteractiveChat-view.tsx wires handleSelectModel from InteractiveChat-hooks.ts:210 -> setChatModel (api-chat.ts:98) -> trpcClient.chat.setModel. chat-control-procedures.ts:154 validates with isChatModelAllowed(engine, model) (src/shared/chat-models.ts:35) and 400s otherwise, then calls target.setModel, which persists via saveCurrentModel to the per-session model file (src/core/chat/session/index.ts:384, state.ts modelFileForSession '.callback-box/chat-models/<id>.json'). The procedure restarts the running subprocess, deferring to a once('done') handler when busy, so the next turn runs on the picked model.

browser.note: Session menu > Model lists Default (Opus), Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Fable 5 with a ✓ on the current one. Picked Sonnet 5: the menu label became 'Model — Sonnet 5', the transcript got a 'Switched to Sonnet 5' system line, and the following turn ran under it. Restored to Default afterwards.

title: Command the composer by voice
story: As a person dictating hands-free, I want spoken phrases like "send message", "send and close", "erase message" and "microphone off" to act on the message, so that I can complete a whole turn without touching the screen.
evidence: The keyword spotter emits `VoiceIntent` (`submit | cancel | mic-off | erase`); `useChatVoice`'s `onVoiceIntent` switch runs `runKeywordSend` (re-arming the mic, or closing it for "send and close"), clears the composer for cancel/erase, and stops dictation on mic-off. KeywordHint rotates the valid phrases.

verdict.note: speech-keywords.ts compiles KeywordPattern sets for send ("send message"/"send now"/…), sendClose ("send and close/stop/finish", "over and out"), cancel, micOff ("microphone off", "mic off", "stop listening") and erase ("erase/clear the message", "start over"); useRealtimeTranscription.ts emits these as VoiceIntent (input/voice-intent.ts: submit|cancel|mic-off|erase) through onVoiceIntent. InteractiveChat-voice.ts line 263 switches on intent.kind: submit -> runKeywordSend (settleMic re-calls transcription.start(), or sends STOP_DICTATION when intent.closeMic is set for "send and close"), cancel/erase -> inputStore.set("") + clearDraftRef, mic-off -> STOP_DICTATION. KeywordHint.tsx rotates WITH_TEXT_HINTS ('"send message"', '"send and close"', '"erase message"', '"microphone off"', …) every 10s while the mic is live. Story matches the code as written.

title: Control and replay a message's narration
story: As a listener, I want to stop, skip, or replay a spoken message from any of its segments, so that I can re-hear a part I missed without re-running the turn.
evidence: The speaker icon on an assistant message opens a dropdown with Stop, fast-forward, Replay, and "Replay from:" a chosen segment; `TargetStrip` carries the stop-TTS control above the composer.

verdict.note: SpeechMenu.tsx renders a speaker-glyph dropdown trigger with a control row of Stop, Replay (onReplay(0)), and Fast-forward (shown when >1 segment), plus a 'Replay from:' section listing each SpeechSegment as a MenuItem calling onReplay(i). It is mounted on assistant messages in ChatMessages.tsx (sticky top-right bar, wired to onStopSpeech/onSkipSpeech/onReplaySpeech), fed from InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx -> InteractiveChat-voice.ts handleStopSpeech/handleSkipSpeech/handleReplaySpeech, which drive useSpeechPlayback's replay({fromIndex})/skip and the composer STOP_SPEECH event over speechPlaybackMachine.ts. TargetStrip.tsx carries the separate stop-TTS button (onStopSpeech, title 'Stop speaking') above the composer as the evidence states.

browser.note: After fixing the fixture-path environment issue above, the harness works as described. The speaker icon (button 'Speech options') opens a dropdown containing a 'Playback controls' group with Stop, Replay and Fast-forward, a divider, a 'REPLAY FROM:' heading, and one menu item per segment labeled by its text prefix ('This is the first segment of the test speech.', 'And now here is the second segment, a little diffe…', 'Finally, this is the third and last segment.'). Verified behavior against the harness status line: while idle Stop and Fast-forward are disabled and Replay is enabled; clicking 'Play all' gives isPlaying=true segment=0 remaining=3, at which point Stop and Fast-forward become enabled; Fast-forward advanced the queue (segment=0 -> segment=2 remaining=1); Stop returned the state to isPlaying=false playingMessageId=null remaining=0; 'Replay' restarted from the beginning (segment=0 remaining=3 states 0=playing,1/2=waiting); and 'Replay from:' the third segment started at segment=2 remaining=1 without re-running earlier segments. Segment aria states ('Speech audio is playing.' / 'Speech audio is being prepared.') render alongside each chunk. The TargetStrip stop-TTS control above the composer is on the chat page, not this harness, so that clause of the evidence was not exercised here.

title: Control voice output and transcription services
story: As a person who talks to their box, I want to mute speech, turn narration mode on, and pick the live and high-quality transcription services, so that voice behaves the way I want in this environment.
evidence: VoiceChip's root panel toggles Mute (localStorage `chat-muted` via `useChatMute`) and Narration mode (`setChatFeature`, optimistic with rollback); VoicePanel picks among the live and HQ transcription service options.

verdict.note: VoiceChip.tsx renders a Dropdown whose root panel has MenuItems for Mute (onToggleMute) and Narration mode (onToggleNarration), plus a 'Voice settings ›' row into VoicePanel; VoiceChip-panels.tsx's VoicePanel lists TRANSCRIPTION_OPTIONS (voxtral/deepgram/openai-realtime) under 'Live transcription' and HQ_TRANSCRIPTION_OPTIONS (whisper, whisper-llm, whisper-llm-mini, voxtral, voxtral-diarized) under 'HQ transcription', wired to trpc.transcription.setService/setHqService. InteractiveChat-hooks.ts provides useChatMute (localStorage key 'chat-muted') and handleToggleNarration via setChatFeature with an optimistic update and rollback on error. The chip is reachable: ChatBarChrome.tsx imports and renders <VoiceChip> into the app bar chip slot.

browser.note: The Voice menu in the header has Mute, Narration mode, and Voice settings showing the current pair inline ('Live: Deepgram', 'HQ: Whisper (OpenAI)'). Narration toggling verified live; muting and the toggle both persist per session.

title: Delete a conversation and everything attached to it
story: As the box owner, I want to delete a chat along with its transcript, husk card, history entry, and schedules, so that a conversation I do not want kept is actually gone.
evidence: The owner-only `chat.deleteSession` mutation runs the phased delete in core/chat/session/delete.ts (husks to trash, history and most-active pointer, review state, detached schedules, SDK/Codex transcript storage) with a compensate() rollback if it fails before transcript deletion.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/chat/session/delete.ts exports deleteChatSession, which runs the ordered phases the story names: registry.deletion.stopAndRemove (stop-for-deletion.ts), scheduleManager.detachForSession, clearMostActiveIfMatches + removeSessionFromHistory (history.ts), removeSessionFromReview, deleteSdkSessionStorage/deleteCodexSession (delete-storage.ts, codex-transcript.ts), then finishDeletedHusks (delete-husks.ts) which trashes the chat husk cards, plus rm of the chat model file. A compensate() helper restores review/history/pointer/schedules when the failure happened before storage changed. It is reachable: chat-control-procedures.ts line 83 exposes `deleteSession` as an ownerProcedure, and the frontend DeleteChatDialog/DeleteChatAction (used from SessionChip.tsx, SessionRow.tsx, ChatHuskView.tsx, UnavailableChat.tsx) calls trpc.chat.deleteSession.

browser.note: Advanced ▸ 'Delete conversation…' is present and enabled; the dialog enumerates exactly what the story claims (transcript + subagent sidecars removed, husk card to box Trash and git-recoverable, chat listing removed, pending reminders linked to the conversation removed; cards/files/commits stay) and chat.deleteSession exists on the server. I cancelled rather than deleting — actually performing the delete is destructive.

title: Dictate a message by voice with spoken controls
story: As a person who would rather talk than type, I want to dictate into the composer with live transcription and spoken commands like "send message" or "erase message", so that I can compose hands-free.
evidence: `realtimeTranscriptionMachine` runs idle→connecting→recording→finalizing against Voxtral (proxied via `GET /api/chat/transcribe-ws`), Deepgram, or OpenAI Realtime; `MicOverlay` shows volume bars and `KeywordHint` rotates the valid spoken keywords.

verdict.note: frontend/src/lib/audio/speech-keywords.ts compiles KeywordPattern sets for send / sendHq ("clean up and send") / sendClose / cancel / micOff / erase ("erase message", "clear the message", "start over"); hooks/useRealtimeTranscription.ts imports detectKeyword and runs it against finalTranscript (and at-start on interims, deduped) to fire the commands. machines/realtimeTranscriptionMachine.ts drives the connect/record/finalize lifecycle against the Voxtral proxy `GET /api/chat/transcribe-ws` registered in webapp/routes/chat-audio-routes.ts:159, with Deepgram/OpenAI-realtime key helpers in lib/audio/. UI entry points are real: InteractiveChat-composer.tsx renders VoiceToggleButton (InteractiveChat-voice-button.tsx) and MicOverlay, whose VolumeIndicator plus KeywordHint rotates the quoted phrases; the textarea shows joinTranscript(input, transcription.transcript) live while transcribing.

title: Find a chat by the place it belongs to
story: As a person with many conversations, I want chats grouped under the landmark they were held in, so that I can find the one about a given part of my box.
evidence: `chat.byLandmark` builds landmark buckets of `PickerSession` rows split into fresh (CHAT_FRESH_WINDOW_MS) and older, rendered by `ChatsPicker`; `chat.placeMenu` serves the app bar's cheaper counts-only place-switch menu.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat.ts defines `byLandmark` (line 141) returning { landmarks, unassigned, freshCount, problems }, splitting sessions with a cutoff of Date.now() - CHAT_FRESH_WINDOW_MS (from core/chat/session/recent-landmark.ts) into fresh vs olderSessions. ChatsPicker.tsx consumes trpc.chat.byLandmark.useQuery() and renders a ChatsLandmarkCard per landmark bucket plus an 'Other chats' bucket for the unassigned sessions; SessionRow.tsx types PickerSession off that output. The grouping is reachable as a real user surface: LandmarksList.tsx also queries chat.byLandmark and is rendered by pages/landmarks/LandmarksPage.tsx and the `landmarks` view renderer. chat-place-menu-procedure.ts defines the counts-only `chat.placeMenu`, used by PlacePill.tsx:127 for the app bar's switch menu, as the evidence states.

browser.note: The grouping structure exists and renders: chat.byLandmark returns per-landmark buckets with sessions/olderSessions/freshCount/latestActivity plus an 'unassigned' bucket, and each landmark section on the page has its own chat area. But the box has zero chat sessions, so every bucket is empty ('No chats here yet.') and no actual chat row grouped under a landmark, and no fresh/older split, could be seen. Creating a chat would trigger an agent run, so I did not.

title: Get a cleaned-up transcript before the message is sent
story: As a person dictating a long thought, I want a high-quality transcription pass over the recording before the message goes out, with a visible in-flight bubble, so that the agent reads accurate words rather than realtime approximations.
evidence: `runKeywordSend` calls `prepareVoiceSubmitEmission` with `postAudioForHqTranscription` when narration or the cleanup keyword is on, bracketed by START_HQ/HQ_DONE on composerMachine's `hq` region; the pending-HQ bubble renders the realtime text faded while it runs, falling back to realtime text on failure.

verdict.note: InteractiveChat-voice.ts runKeywordSend (line ~132) computes runHq = narrationEnabledRef.current || intent.hq (intent.hq comes from the 'sendHq' keyword action in useRealtimeTranscription.ts:201), and when an audioBlob exists it sends composerSend({type:'START_HQ', text: joinTranscript(...)}) then calls prepareVoiceSubmitEmission with transcribe: (blob)=>postAudioForHqTranscription(blob,{sessionId}), sending HQ_DONE before submit. composerMachine.ts has an `hq` region idle/inFlight with setPendingHq/clearPendingHq on pendingHqText, surfaced as pendingHqDraft through InteractiveChat-view -> InteractiveChat-messages -> buildDataItems, which pushes a {kind:'pendingHq'} item rendered as an opacity-60 user bubble in InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx (line ~59/280). prepareVoiceSubmitEmission (input/voice-intent.ts:106) catches transcribe failure/null and keeps intent.text (realtime) as fallback; api-chat.ts postAudioForHqTranscription POSTs /api/chat/transcribe-audio, which exists at webapp/routes/chat-audio-routes.ts:59 and dispatches to transcribeAudioHq.

title: Get a failed message back instead of losing it
story: As a person whose send failed, I want the message, its attachments and its quoted selections put back into the composer with the reason shown in a dismissible banner, so that a transport or backend failure never eats what I wrote.
evidence: `dispatchWithRestorePolicy` awaits the receipt and, on `disposition: "rejected"`, runs `planRestore`/`applyRestorePlan` — re-reserving image/file/selection ids, appending after any text typed since, and stripping keyword tags from a voice emission; `applyStreamError` drops the optimistic bubble when the send was never accepted, and `ChatStatusBanners` renders the error with a dismiss link.

verdict.note: InteractiveChat-dispatch.ts:65-78 dispatchWithRestorePolicy awaits the receipt and on disposition==="rejected" (with restoreRejected) calls planRestore(emissionStore.get(), emission) then applyRestorePlan(emissionStore.editor, plan). chat-target.ts planRestore (line 95) returns text plus images/files/selections, appending after any newly typed text and stripping keyword tags for voice-origin emissions; applyRestorePlan (line 125) calls editor.reserveIds for image/file/selection ids before restoring. machines/chat-actions.ts applyStreamError (line 100) drops the optimistic pendingMessages entry when STREAM_FAILED arrives with accepted false, and ChatStatusBanners in InteractiveChat-layout.tsx:27-50 renders the error text with a "dismiss" button wired to onDismissError.

title: Get the agent's acknowledgements and callouts as their own elements
story: As a person reading a reply, I want the agent's acknowledgements and callout blocks rendered as badges and highlighted panels rather than raw markup, so that what it did and what I must not miss stand apart from prose.
evidence: `parseAcks` feeds AckBadgeCluster's per-ack popovers (with ref links opening in the pane), CalloutBlock renders `<callout>` as an accent panel with markdown body, markdown-rendering.tsx strips the structured tags and renders images/videos/links, and MessageErrorBoundary keeps one broken message from taking down the transcript.

verdict.note: lib/structured-output-parsing.ts parses <ack kind ref>text</ack> (parseAcks) and <callout context>body</callout> (parseCallouts) and strips both plus <chat-app> in stripStructuredOutputTags. components/chat/ack-badge.tsx AckBadgeCluster renders one badge per ack with a popover whose ref click calls parseViewUrl + onZoomView; it is mounted at components/chat/user-message.tsx:213 with acks from parseAcks (InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx:139). CalloutBlock/CalloutStack render each callout as an accent-bordered bg-accent-50 panel with a Markdown body, mounted at ChatMessages.tsx:186. markdown-rendering.tsx:198 applies stripStructuredOutputTags(stripSpeechTags(text)) before rendering, and MessageErrorBoundary wraps each message body (InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx:263), so raw tags never reach prose and one bad message doesn't kill the transcript.

browser.note: Asked the agent for a callout: it rendered as a left-accent-bar panel with an uppercase accent title and a markdown body, not raw markup (bg-accent block, distinct from message bubbles). Caveat: I could not get the agent to emit an <ack> tag, so the AckBadgeCluster/popover half was not exercised — when I asked it to echo ack markup literally the tags were stripped from the rendered assistant text rather than shown raw.

title: Give a chat session a durable, renameable face in the box
story: As a boxholder, I want each web chat session to have a chat card whose title I can set by hand and whose contains/contains-evidence a nightly review maintains, so that a conversation becomes a findable, referenceable box object I can rename and annotate.
evidence: ChatSchema (created automatically under store/chat/web/, keyed by `session`, with a machine-owned `review-span`) states a hand-set title wins permanently and the body is the boxholder's; ChatThreadSchema is the accumulating connector-side conversation and FeedbackSchema records the user's response to something the box surfaced.

verdict.note: src/schemas/chat.ts defines ChatSchema (category 'synced') with fields session, context-dir and the machine-owned review-span, and its instructions state the card is created automatically under store/chat/web/, that a hand-set title wins permanently, that contains/contains-evidence are maintained by the nightly chat review, and that the body is the boxholder's. Creation is real: core/chat/session/session-start-record.ts calls ensureChatHusk() (core/chat/husk.ts, CHAT_HUSK_DIR = 'store/chat/web') at session-id assignment. The review exists in core/chat/review/* — husk-write.ts resolveTitleOwner/titleHash implements the 'hand-set title is never touched again' rule — run by `cb chat review run` (src/cli/commands/chat-review.ts) and by the 'chat-review' nightly schedule in core/box/defaults.ts (cron 0 4 * * *). That default schedule is seeded enabled:false as an explicit opt-in, which is the one qualifier the story understates; the capability itself is reachable via the schedule toggle or the CLI, so I am not refuting on it.

title: Have the microphone yield while the box is talking
story: As a person having a spoken back-and-forth, I want the mic to pause while the box speaks and reopen when it finishes, so that a voice conversation takes turns instead of the box transcribing itself.
evidence: composerMachine's `voice` region (`idle | speaking | pausedForSpeech`) emits startMic/resumeMic/cancelMic/stopSpeech device commands that useChatVoice executes against the live handles; `voicePaused` drives the voice button's resume affordance, and a wake lock is held for the whole voice window.

verdict.note: composerMachine.ts defines a voice region with states idle|speaking|pausedForSpeech: on SPEECH_QUEUED with guard 'recording' it targets pausedForSpeech with actions ['cancelMic','playSpeech']; SPEECH_DONE in pausedForSpeech returns to idle with 'resumeMic'; in 'speaking' (mic wasn't recording) SPEECH_DONE reopens the mic via 'startMic' when guard 'turnTaking' holds. InteractiveChat-voice.ts subscribes composerActor.on('command') and executes startMic -> transcription.start({earcon:true}), resumeMic -> transcription.start(), cancelMic -> transcription.cancel(), stopSpeech -> speechPlayback.stop() against a live device-handle ref, and calls useDebouncedWakeLock(voiceModeActive). InteractiveChat-voice-button.tsx renders a pulsing resume affordance titled 'Resume recording (stops speech)' when voicePaused. Matches the story.

title: Hear the agent's reply read aloud
story: As a person with the box open while doing something else, I want replies wrapped in `<speech>` spoken aloud as they stream, so that I can listen instead of watching the screen.
evidence: `speechPlaybackMachine` queues speech segments and prefetches the next while the current plays, fetching audio from `POST /api/chat/tts`; the voice and style come from `GET /api/chat/voice-config`, and per-message overrides are documented by generateChatVoiceDoc.

verdict.note: InteractiveChat-speech.ts (useSpeechDispatch) watches the streaming chat snapshot, counts closing </speech> tags and dispatches only complete segments mid-stream via parseAllSpeechTags (lib/audio/speech-parsing.ts, which parses <speech> with voice/instructions/emotion/name attributes), raising SPEECH_QUEUED into composerMachine; composerMachine's voice region emits the playSpeech command (handled at InteractiveChat-voice.ts:234) which calls useSpeechPlayback.playSegments, driving speechPlaybackMachine (queues segments, prefetches the next while the current plays). Audio comes from POST /api/chat/tts and voice settings from GET /api/chat/voice-config, both registered in webapp/routes/chat-audio-routes.ts. Playback is on by default (composer context muted defaults false; only the isMuted/transcriptNonEmpty guards suppress it).

title: Keep an unfinished message across reloads and chat switches
story: As a person who got interrupted mid-compose, I want my in-progress message — text, attachments and selections — to still be there after a reload or a switch to another chat, so that I do not lose what I was writing.
evidence: emission-persist.ts stores the whole emission under one per-box key `cb-input-emission:<box>`; InteractiveChat calls `useEmissionPersistence` and renders `ExpiredAttachmentsNotice` for restored attachments whose tmp/ uploads are gone.

verdict.note: input/emission-persist.ts serializes {text, images, files, selections} as PersistedEmission v1 under emissionKey() = `cb-input-emission:<box>` — one singleton key per box, explicitly not per session, so a chat switch keeps the draft. hooks/useEmissionPersistence.ts (called at InteractiveChat.tsx:174) debounce-writes via usePersistScheduler and restores once into an empty store: setText, addImage (re-materialized as a data: URI), addFile after a HEAD existence check on tmp/ uploads, addSelection, then editor.reserveIds. Files whose tmp/ upload was swept are reported as expiredAttachments and rendered by ExpiredAttachmentsNotice (InteractiveChat.tsx:256, defined in InteractiveChat-layout.tsx:85).

browser.note: Left a composer draft of text + a pasted image chip + a text-selection chip ('[selection1] [image1] draft survives?'), reloaded the page: all three came back intact (thumbnail chip, quoted selection chip, text). A plain-text draft also survived full navigations away and back in a separate browser profile earlier. Caveat in pageNotes: the draft is not scoped to one chat — it followed me into a newly created session.

title: Keep chat subprocesses bounded on an idle box
story: As someone running a box, I want chat to pre-warm a subprocess for the next message but cap live ones and reap idle ones, so that chat starts fast without a box holding agent processes around the clock.
evidence: `ChatSessionRegistry` prewarms via `prewarmBackend`, caps live subprocesses with `enforceLiveCap` (`DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE`), and `sweepIdle` evicts unpinned entries past `idleTimeoutMs`, expires reservations, and calls `backend.closeWarm()` once chat has gone quiet; `pin`/`pinSession` protect entries with an open stream or in-flight turn.

verdict.note: ChatSessionRegistry in src/core/chat/session/registry.ts has prewarm() calling prewarmBackend (registry-warm.ts), maxLive from DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE = 2 (registry.ts:37) enforced by enforceLiveCap (registry-cap.ts) which stops the LRU live subprocess with refCount 0, and sweepIdle() (registry.ts:404) which evicts entries whose lastActivity is past idleTimeoutMs and refCount === 0, calls sweepExpiredReservations, and invokes backend.closeWarm() once now()-lastUse exceeds idleTimeoutMs. pin()/pinSession() (registry.ts:374/379 via registry-pins.ts) bump refCount so pinned entries survive both the cap and the sweep. Reachable: src/webapp/routes/chat.ts calls registry.startCleanup() and registry.prewarm() when prewarmChat is true, which src/cli/commands/serve.ts:172 sets for the real server; enforceLiveCap is called from chat-send-routes.ts and deliver-user-message.ts.

title: Keep chat threads conversational across reactor cycles
story: As the boxholder chatting with my box, I want each chat job processed in its own agent session that resumes the thread's prior session, so that the box remembers earlier turns in the same conversation.
evidence: `processChatJobs` keys sessions by the job card's `thread.ref` (falling back to the job path), gets or mints one with `getOrCreateSession`, invokes the agent per job with resume, marks it used, and calls `resetSession` when a session fails.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/reactor/chat-jobs.ts `processChatJobs` loops jobs, derives `sessionKey = extractThreadRef(job.content) ?? job.relPath` (extractThreadRef reads frontmatter `thread.ref`), calls `getOrCreateSession(sessions, sessionKey)` for `{sessionId, resume}`, passes both into `opts.createAgent({name:"reactor-chat", sessionId, resume})` and one `agent.invoke` per job, then `markSessionUsed` on success and `resetSession` on failure, persisting via `saveChatSessions`. reactor-sessions.ts stores these in `.callback-box/chat-sessions.json` and exports exactly those helpers. Reachable from reactor/cycle.ts:257, and DESIGN.md documents the same per-thread resume design.

title: Keep dictating through a network or microphone blip
story: As a person dictating on a phone, I want a dropped socket or an OS grabbing the mic to be recovered transparently — with an amber "recovering…" signal — and my words folded into the composer if it cannot be, so that an interruption never silently eats what I said.
evidence: The actor runs a stalled-transport watchdog plus reconnect-with-backoff, replaying captured PCM and merging the committed prefix (`mergeFinalText`/`mergeFinalWords`); MicCapture re-acquires a revoked/muted mic; `onUnconsumedTranscript` in InteractiveChat-voice.ts folds unsent words into the composer.

verdict.note: transcription-actor.ts documents and implements all three recovery paths: initial-connect retry with full-jitter RETRY_BACKOFF, mid-recording reconnect on 1006/1011 closes, and a liveness watchdog (setInterval on bufferedAmount / no-PCM-frames) that emits CONNECTION_DEGRADED then transparently reconnects, replaying buffered PCM and folding a committedPrefix via mergeFinalText/mergeFinalWords in transcription-merge.ts. transcription-mic.ts MicCapture handles track `onended` and prolonged `onmute` (grace timer) by calling beginRecovery()/reacquire() to re-get the mic. MicOverlay.tsx renders amber bars (VolumeIndicator degraded -> bg-warning) plus a 'recovering…' chip, wired from InteractiveChat-composer.tsx line 203 (degraded={transcription.state === 'reconnecting'}). useRealtimeTranscription's onUnconsumedTranscript fires when a segment ends with untaken text, and InteractiveChat-voice.ts:294 folds it into the composer via inputStore.set(joinTranscript(existing, text)).

title: Land in a chat with the page I just clipped open beside it
story: As a person capturing a web page with the Clerk browser extension, I want the box to hand back a link that opens a fresh chat scoped to the destination folder with the captured page open in the companion pane, so that I can start talking about the clipping the moment it is filed.
evidence: The clerk router's commentary and tabArrangement mutations return `open: chat?session=new&contextDir=…&companion=view:<cardRel>`; the chat route's validateSearch accepts `companion`, and InteractiveChat-hooks opens it once on mount as a one-shot deep link and then strips the param from the URL.

verdict.note: webapp/trpc/routers/clerk.ts commentary mutation writes the webpage + commentary cards, commits them, and returns `open` = `chat?session=new&contextDir=<destDir>&companion=view:<cardRel>` (the tabArrangement mutation does the same with DEFAULT_COMMENTARY_DIR). callback-clerk/src/domain/commentary.ts commentaryOpenUrl joins that onto boxUrl and entrypoints/background.ts opens it via chrome.tabs.create. frontend/src/router.tsx chat validateSearch accepts session, contextDir, and companion; InteractiveChat.tsx line 196 calls useCompanionDeepLink from InteractiveChat-hooks.ts, which parses the view: URL, calls onZoomView once (openedRef guard) and navigates with replace to strip ?companion= from the URL.

title: Load older messages in a long chat
story: As a person in a long-running conversation, I want to page further back through the transcript, so that I can read what was said earlier without loading the entire history.
evidence: `chat.history` takes a discriminated `slice` of `{mode:"tail"}` or `{mode:"page", offset, limit}` and returns entries plus a total; the message list renders HISTORY_TAIL plus explicit "load older" pages with prepend anchoring.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat-session-procedures.ts defines historySliceSchema as a strict discriminated union of {mode:'tail'} and {mode:'page', offset, limit} and the chat.history procedure returns {sessionId, entries, total} from loadSessionHistory (src/core/chat/session/load-history.ts, CHAT_HISTORY_TAIL = 200 default window). On the frontend, InteractiveChat-actions.ts calls getChatHistory({slice:{mode:'page', offset, limit}}) on the user-initiated load-older action, and InteractiveChat-messages.tsx renders LoadOlderHeader (a 'Show earlier messages' button shown when totalEntries > messages.length) that snapshots the scroll anchor via captureForPrepend; InteractiveChat-scroll.ts / scroll-reconcile.ts hold the reader's position across the prepend.

browser.note: chat.history with slice {mode:'page',offset:0,limit:3} returned 3 entries plus total:29, so the paged seam works. But this session's total (29) is far under the 200-entry bootstrap tail, so no 'load older' control ever appears in the UI and I could not exercise the prepend/anchoring path.

title: Manage a chat session's lifecycle and settings
story: As a person chatting with my box, I want to list sessions, read a session's history, rename it, switch models, toggle features, interrupt a running turn, restart it, or delete it, so that I control the conversation instead of only feeding it.
evidence: `chatSessionProcedures` (history, sessions, label, defaultSession, features) and `chatControlProcedures` (status, statusAll, setModel, setFeature, interrupt, restart, reserveSession, deleteSession, sessionAvailability) are spread into `chatRouter`, reaching the live registry through `getChatRuntime`.

verdict.note: chatRouter (src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat.ts) does spread chatSessionProcedures (history, sessions, label, defaultSession, features) and chatControlProcedures (status, statusAll, setModel, setFeature, interrupt, restart, reserveSession, deleteSession, sessionAvailability), and the control ones reach the live registry via getChatRuntime from src/webapp/chat-runtime.ts. But the story claims the user can 'rename it', and no rename exists: `label` at chat-session-procedures.ts:126 is a publicProcedure *query* that reads titleForSession, not a mutation, and there is no setLabel/renameSession procedure anywhere in src (grep for rename in src/webapp and src/core/chat finds only a comment in core/chat/husk.ts saying a husk 'can be renamed freely'). The frontend has no rename control either — src/frontend/src/pages/ChatPage.tsx only calls trpc.chat.label.useQuery. Over-claim on one verb; everything else in the list checks out.

panel.note: Eight of the nine claimed verbs are real and wired: chat.ts spreads chatSessionProcedures (history, sessions, label, defaultSession, features) and chatControlProcedures (status/statusAll/setModel/setFeature/interrupt/restart/reserveSession/deleteSession/sessionAvailability, the live ones going through getChatRuntime), and chatRouter is mounted as `chat:` in src/webapp/trpc/router.ts:48. Rename has no implementing code: chat-session-procedures.ts:126 `label` is a read-only publicProcedure .query over titleForSession, there is no setLabel/rename mutation anywhere under src/webapp or src/core/chat (grep for rename/setLabel/setTitle finds only fs.rename and diff parsing), and the card router exposes only get/inboundRefs/trash — no card write — so the husk title cannot be edited through the web UI either. ChatHuskView.tsx renders the title as static text and offers only Open/Delete. So the story's 'rename it' capability does not exist in code at all.

Most of the story is reachable from rendered web-UI controls: src/frontend/src/api-chat.ts wraps trpc.chat.history/sessions/features/setModel/setFeature/interrupt/restart, and those are called from real controls (InteractiveChat-hooks.ts handleSelectModel/handleToggleNarration, machines/chat-actions.ts interruptChat, InteractiveChat-actions.ts restartChatSubprocess, SessionListPanel.tsx getChatSessions, chat-delete/DeleteChatDialog.tsx trpc.chat.deleteSession). Rename has no entry point at all: chat-session-procedures.ts contains zero mutations (`label` at line 126 is a publicProcedure query over titleForSession), there is no setLabel/rename procedure in the chat router, and the frontend offers no way to edit a husk's title — ChatHuskView.tsx renders the title as static Text with only 'Open chat' and 'Delete conversation', and the only card mutation wired in the frontend is trpc.card.trash (CardActions.tsx); there is no card frontmatter editor. src/core/chat/session/list.ts says the title comes from 'the nightly chat review or a hand edit', i.e. an agent or the filesystem, not the web-UI person. So one of the eight enumerated verbs is unreachable for the stated role.

Every verb but one is delivered: chat-session-procedures.ts supplies history/sessions/defaultSession/features and chat-control-procedures.ts supplies setModel, setFeature, interrupt, restart, deleteSession (all mutations, reaching the live registry via getChatRuntime). 'Rename it' is not: `label` at chat-session-procedures.ts:126 is a read-only publicProcedure query over titleForSession, and there is no setLabel/rename/setTitle mutation anywhere in src/webapp or src/core/chat (grep finds only unrelated fs.rename and git-rename hits). Nor is there a UI path: ChatHuskView.tsx renders the husk's frontmatter title as static text with only Open chat and Delete actions, and src/frontend/src/pages/card contains just CardViewPage.tsx plus OpenChatControl — no card/frontmatter editor. The story claims a capability the code does not provide, so it over-claims on one enumerated verb.

browser.note: All named procedures answer on the running server (sessions, history, defaultSession, features, label, status, statusAll, setModel, setFeature, interrupt, restart, reserveSession, deleteSession, sessionAvailability — a bogus name returns 'No procedure found', these return input-validation errors or data). Exercised through the UI: session list, history load, model menu ('Model Default (Opus)'), interrupt (Stop agent), restart/delete controls.

triage.reasoning: Eight of the nine enumerated verbs are real, wired and browser-verified (browser/chat-1.json exercised sessions, history, defaultSession, features, label, status, statusAll, setModel, setFeature, interrupt, restart, reserveSession, deleteSession, sessionAvailability against the running server, and drove the session list, model menu, Stop agent, restart and delete controls through the UI). 'Rename it' has no implementation: chat-session-procedures.ts:126 `label` is a read-only publicProcedure .query over titleForSession, chat-session-procedures.ts contains no mutations at all, and there is no setLabel/renameSession/setTitle procedure anywhere in src/webapp or src/core/chat (the only rename hits are fs.rename and a husk.ts comment). There is no UI path either — ChatHuskView renders the title as static text with Open/Delete only, and the sole card mutation the frontend wires is trpc.card.trash. The verb never existed, so the catalog entry should drop 'rename it'; the code is in its intended state for what it does ship. Not classified real-gap because the missing capability is already filed and prioritized: issues/features/2026-07-20-chat-thread-management.md ('Chat thread management: delete, rename, archive', priority important) records that delete shipped via worktree-chat-session-delete and that the issue stays open for rename and archive. A new issue would duplicate it; if the maintainer wants the audit to add anything, it belongs as a note on that item.

title: Not be left staring at a wedged "Agent is working…"
story: As a person whose tab was backgrounded or whose socket died mid-turn, I want the chat to check with the server and recover the finished reply, so that a dropped connection doesn't leave the conversation frozen until I reload.
evidence: `useProcessingStatusPoll` polls chat status and, after STREAM_WATCHDOG_IDLE_POLLS idle reads, sends STREAM_RECOVER; `useChatStallRecovery` does the same check on `visibilitychange`; `createReconnectRefreshGate` rate-limits reconnect-driven history REFRESHes.

verdict.note: processing-status-display.ts defines STREAM_WATCHDOG_IDLE_POLLS = 3 and useProcessingStatusPoll, which sends {type:'STREAM_RECOVER'} after that many consecutive idle status reads (line 132). InteractiveChat-hooks.ts useChatStallRecovery (line 374) registers a `visibilitychange` listener that, when the tab becomes visible while snapshot.matches('streaming'), calls getChatStatus({sessionId}) and dispatches STREAM_RECOVER if !status.busy, falling through to a history refresh. Both are wired in InteractiveChat.tsx lines 200-201, so this is live in the chat UI. reconnect-refresh-gate.ts createReconnectRefreshGate(minIntervalMs, baselineAt) is used in InteractiveChat-ws.ts line 201 to rate-limit reconnect-driven REFRESHes.

title: One broken message does not take the transcript down
story: As a person reading a chat, I want a message the renderer chokes on to appear as a small error bar with the rest of the conversation intact, so that a single malformed reply does not blank the whole chat.
evidence: MessageErrorBoundary is a per-message React error boundary that renders a compact red bar and logs to `console.error` (which the DebugLog pipe forwards to the server); InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx wraps each rendered entry in it, keyed by group index or entry uuid.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/components/chat/MessageErrorBoundary.tsx is a class component with getDerivedStateFromError/componentDidCatch that logs to console.error (doc comment notes the DebugLog pipe forwards to the server) and renders a compact bar with border-danger-light/bg-danger-50 carrying the error message. InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx imports it (line 11) and returns `<MessageErrorBoundary label={boundaryLabel}>{body}</MessageErrorBoundary>` at line 263 for each rendered entry/group, and that module is consumed by InteractiveChat-messages.tsx, so it is on the live chat render path. Only the failing message is replaced; siblings render normally.

title: Open a chat by id or resume the most active one
story: As a boxholder, I want /chat to open my most active session and ?session=<id> to open a specific one, with the resolved id written back into the URL, so that a reload or back navigation lands on the same conversation.
evidence: ChatPage runs one chat.bootstrap query that resolves a bare /chat to the most-active session and preloads its history, navigates with replace to `?session=<resolved id>`, keys InteractiveChat so a real session switch remounts while the new→assigned transition is carried, and renders UnavailableChat for a deleted session's husk.

verdict.note: ChatPage.tsx runs a single trpc.chat.bootstrap.useQuery with session omitted for a bare /chat; webapp/trpc/routers/chat-bootstrap-procedure.ts resolves it via getMostActive(ctx.boxRoot) and returns history+status+label in one round trip. The effect at ~line 246 seeds the explicit-session cache entry and navigates with replace:true to /<box>/chat?session=<resolvedId>, spreading prior search params. keyState/epoch keys InteractiveChat so a genuine session switch remounts while carriesFreshChatMachine (chat-session-transition.ts) carries the new→assigned transition, and bootstrap kind 'unavailable' renders UnavailableChat for a deleted session's husk. Matches the story as written.

browser.note: Bare /chat (once sessions existed) resolved to the most-active session and replaced the URL with ?session=e9590f0c-…; ?session=<id> opened that specific conversation; reload landed on the same transcript. Before any session existed, bare /chat correctly showed the empty 'Start a conversation' state.

title: Open a conversation from its chat card
story: As a person browsing my box, I want a chat's card to show its title, what the conversation contained, and an Open chat link, so that a conversation is a durable object in the box rather than just a session id.
evidence: ChatHuskView renders the husk card's `title`, `contains`, `contains-evidence` and binding, queries `trpc.chat.sessionAvailability`, and shows either "Open chat →" (linking to `?session=<id>`) or "Not available on this machine".

verdict.note: src/frontend/src/components/chat-husk/ChatHuskView.tsx reads the card frontmatter's session, context-dir, title, contains and contains-evidence, renders the title (falling back to 'Chat <id prefix>'), the binding line 'bound to <dir>/', the contains summary, the body, and a details disclosure for contains-evidence. It queries trpc.chat.sessionAvailability and renders either an 'Open chat →' Link to /<boxSlug>/chat with search {session} or 'Not available on this machine', plus DeleteChatAction from components/chat-delete/DeleteChatDialog. src/frontend/src/renderers/chat-husk.tsx registers the component for the 'chat' card type at priority 100, so the card page reaches it.

browser.note: Both availability states seen. 2026-07-01_2846d707.chat.card shows its `title` as the heading and body line, the session binding, and 'Not available on this machine' (no open link). 2026-08-21_e9590f0c.chat.card (no title on disk) falls back to 'Chat e9590f0c' and shows a working 'Open chat →' link plus 'Delete conversation…'. The `contains` / `contains-evidence` part is unverified: no chat husk card in this box has those fields.

title: Open the chat UI in one round-trip
story: As a person opening the app, I want the chat's session id, history, status and place context fetched in a single call, so that the conversation renders without a waterfall of requests.
evidence: `chat.bootstrap` (chat-bootstrap-procedure.ts) and `chat.placeMenu` (chat-place-menu-procedure.ts) are spread into `chatRouter`; the raw `GET /api/chat/default` in routes/chat.ts resolves the most-active session id for bare-`/chat` clients.

verdict.note: chat.bootstrap (callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/chat-bootstrap-procedure.ts) does resolve the session id via getMostActive and return history + status + label in one query, and GET /api/chat/default exists in src/webapp/routes/chat.ts. But it returns NO place context: the ChatBootstrap union is {kind, sessionId, history, label, status} only, and readSessionStatus (chat-control-procedures.ts:37-80) returns just sessionId/running/busy/model/engine. Place context comes from a separate procedure, chat.placeMenu, which PlacePill.tsx:127 calls as its own query gated on `enabled: switchOpened` and only warmed later from idle time (useIdlePrefetch) after bootstrap settles. So 'place context fetched in a single call' overclaims — it is deliberately a second, lazily-gated request.

panel.note: All three cited pieces are real and wired. chat-bootstrap-procedure.ts exports chatBootstrapProcedure (resolves the session via getMostActive, then composes loadHistoryForSession, titleForSession, resolveSessionAvailability and readSessionStatus into one ChatBootstrap result), and chat-place-menu-procedure.ts exports chatPlaceMenuProcedure; both are spread into chatRouter at trpc/routers/chat.ts:81-82. The frontend consumes them: ChatPage.tsx:189 calls trpc.chat.bootstrap.useQuery (with setData/invalidate at :259 and DeleteChatDialog.tsx:67) and PlacePill.tsx:127 calls trpc.chat.placeMenu.useQuery, prefetched from idle at ChatPage.tsx:242. GET /api/chat/default is registered inside registerChatRoutes (routes/chat.ts:197), which server-box-scope.ts:264 mounts. The earlier verifier's objection is about the story's wording (place context is a second, lazily gated query) rather than whether the code exists or is connected, which is outside my lens.

Reachable by an ordinary web user with no flag or config. frontend/src/router.tsx:103-106 registers the `/chat` route under the box layout rendering ChatPage; ChatPage.tsx:189 issues `trpc.chat.bootstrap.useQuery({slice, session})` on mount (enabled for any non-fresh chat), and `chatBootstrapProcedure` is spread into `chatRouter` at webapp/trpc/routers/chat.ts:81 (placeMenu at :82). The bare-`/chat` fallback route `GET /api/chat/default` is registered in webapp/routes/chat.ts:197. The place-menu data also has a rendered control: AppNav.tsx:136 renders `<PlacePill>`, which queries `chat.placeMenu` on open (PlacePill.tsx:127) and ChatPage prefetches it from idle (ChatPage.tsx:242). Whether that second lazy query undercuts the story's 'single call' claim is an accuracy question outside my lens; my lens is satisfied.

chat-bootstrap-procedure.ts returns exactly three of the four claimed things in one query: the resolved sessionId (getMostActive), history (loadHistoryForSession), status (readSessionStatus), plus a session label. The ChatBootstrap union has no place field of any kind. Place context is deliberately separate and lazy: PlacePill.tsx:122 runs trpc.landmarks.forDir per-place, and PlacePill.tsx:127 runs trpc.chat.placeMenu gated on `enabled: switchOpened`, with ChatPage.tsx:242 only warming it from idle time AFTER bootstrap settles — the file headers state this gating is intentional so the bar doesn't carry the cost at rest. So the story's literal 'session id, history, status and place context fetched in a single call' over-claims a payload the code narrows by one item; the 'so that' clause (no waterfall) holds for the first three but place context is still its own later request.

browser.note: On opening a chat the very first API calls are chat.reserveSession (new session only) then a single chat.bootstrap?batch=1 carrying {slice:{mode:'tail',tail:200,minRealUserMessages:2},session:<id>}; the transcript renders off that one call. A follow-up batched call (chat.directoryFor, capture.pendingSessions, chat.status, chat.features, transcription.config, chat.schedules) is itself one batched round-trip.

triage.reasoning: The code is fine and the goal is met; the story's payload list is wrong by one item. chat-bootstrap-procedure.ts returns exactly {kind, sessionId, history, label, status} — it resolves the session via getMostActive, loads history, and reads status in one query, and the browser check (browser/chat-1.json) watched a single chat.bootstrap?batch=1 call render the transcript. There is no place field in the ChatBootstrap union, and there cannot be: place context comes from chat.placeMenu (chat-place-menu-procedure.ts), which PlacePill.tsx:127 runs with `enabled: switchOpened` and ChatPage warms from idle only AFTER bootstrap settles. That laziness is deliberate and documented in both file headers — the bar is not supposed to pay for the menu at rest — so nothing is broken and nothing should change in the product. The catalog entry should drop 'and place context' (or say 'session id, history and status'), leaving the no-waterfall benefit clause intact, which the browser check confirms. Not a false-negative: the story enumerates a specific payload and one enumerated item is provably absent, so leaving the wording as-is would misdescribe the API.

title: Post a self-note into a chat transcript
story: As the box's agent or a script, I want to write a note into a chat's transcript without triggering a reply, so that the user sees what background work happened when they next open the chat.
evidence: `cb chat self-note <body>` POSTs to `/api/chat/self-note` with optional `--ref` and `--commit`, targeting the live session or `--session <id>`; the route injects it into the session transcript rather than starting a turn.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/chat.ts registers `selfNoteCommand` (`cb chat self-note <body>` with --ref/--commit/--session) which POSTs to `<server>/<box>/api/chat/self-note`. chat-send-routes.ts:223-262 validates the body, resolves the explicit `session` or the most-active session, wraps the text as `<self-note ref=... commit=...>` and enqueues or sends it into that session's transcript. shared/self-note.ts parses those tags so the CLI session renderer and frontend chat renderer show them as a distinct annotation and metadata scanners don't count them as user turns. Nuance: the route does dispatch a turn via ChatSession.send, and the "no reply" behavior is enforced by the agent prompt (core/chat/session/prompts.ts:97 — "no one is waiting on a reply. Default to producing nothing... write text only if there's something worth surfacing when the user next opens chat"), which matches the story's intent.

title: Quote a passage out of a rendered card
story: As a person reading a card, I want to select text and have its location described (section, nearest heading, paragraph, approximate line) so the agent can find it again, and to jump back to a quoted span from its source chip, so that commentary stays anchored to the words it is about.
evidence: extractSelection() walks the rendered DOM and formatPosition() renders the freeform locator hint; findQuoteRange/highlightRange/scrollRangeIntoView jump to a {% source %} chip's exact span using text-fragment matching plus the CSS Custom Highlight API; extractQuoteSpeakers() lists the from= attributions of a doc's {% quote %} tags.

verdict.note: lib/selection/position.ts exports extractSelection(selection, container), which walks the rendered DOM for [data-card-section], the nearest preceding h1-h6 (with id), paragraph index and data-line, and formatPosition() joins those into a freeform 'section; heading: X (#id); paragraph N; ~line L' hint. It is reachable: components/SelectionCapture.tsx calls it on mouseup/keyup and shows a floating 'Add selection to message' button, wrapped around the rendered card in FileView.tsx line 389. lib/selection/quote-anchor.ts exports findQuoteRange (text-fragments-polyfill processTextFragmentDirective), highlightRange (CSS Custom Highlight API, QUOTE_HIGHLIGHT) and scrollRangeIntoView, used by ExtfileView.tsx and WebpageView.tsx onJumpToQuote handlers for source chips; quote-extract.ts exports extractQuoteSpeakers, used in MarkdownCardView.tsx.

browser.note: Location is described and travels with the quote: selecting a paragraph in a markdown card produced pos="heading: Running a course (#running-a-course); ~line 1", and selecting inside a card's structured fields produced pos="frontmatter", both alongside ref=<card path>. The second clause — jumping back to a quoted span from a source chip on an assistant message — I could not exercise: asking the agent to quote a sentence produced a plain quoted line with no source chip attached.

title: Quote a selection from the open card into the composer
story: As a person reading a card in the companion pane, I want to attach a text selection to my next message, so that the agent knows exactly which passage I mean.
evidence: `ChatSelections` renders a pill per attached selection matching a `[selectionN]` token in the textarea, showing full text, source and position; `useCompanionSelection` wires the companion pane's selection into `selections.addSelection`.

verdict.note: FileView.tsx wraps the rendered body in <SelectionCapture onCapture=...> whenever onAddSelection is supplied and calls onAddSelection({ref,text,position}); InteractiveChat-view.tsx passes handleAddSelection into CompanionViewPanel (the companion pane) at line 306, coming from useCompanionSelection (use-companion-selection.ts), which forwards to selections.addSelection (or the native composer command bridge). useChatSelections (InteractiveChat-selections.ts) stores the SelectionItem in the emission store and inserts a `[selection<N>]` token at the caret; SelectionPanel in ChatSelections.tsx renders one pill per selection showing snippet, full text, doc name and position, with a remove button that strips the token. On send, applySelections (lib/selection/serialize.ts:165, used by input/targets/chat-assemble.ts and InteractiveChat-helpers.ts) expands each token into the quoted passage in the outgoing message.

browser.note: Selected a passage in the companion pane; an 'Add selection to message' (+) affordance appeared beside the selection. Clicking it added a removable 'selection1' chip showing the quote and a '[selection1]' token in the composer. On send it reaches the agent as <user-selection ref="/store/courses/Acids_Bases.attach/course-runner.md" pos="...">the exact passage</user-selection>.

title: Read a background task's output file
story: As a person who kicked off a background task from chat, I want to open the output file it wrote, so that I can read the result of work that finished after the message.
evidence: `GET /api/task-output?file=` serves the file as text/plain, refusing anything not under a `/tasks/` path inside `/tmp`; the chat user-message component fetches it by `notification.outputFile`.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/routes/api.ts registers GET /api/task-output with a `file` querystring: it path.resolve()s the value, rejects anything whose resolved path lacks a '/tasks/' segment or does not start with /tmp/ or /private/tmp/ (403), then returns the file body with Content-Type text/plain (404 on ENOENT). The chat side is TaskNotificationMessage in src/frontend/src/components/chat/user-message.tsx, which on expand fetches `${getApiBase()}/task-output?file=` + encodeURIComponent(notification.outputFile) and renders the text. outputFile is populated from the task notification pipeline (core/chat/session/messages.ts sets task.outputFile from msg.output_file; typed in core/chat/message-types.ts and event-bus-schemas.ts), so the entry point is reachable from a chat task notification.

title: Read a transcript with the machinery filtered out
story: As a person reading back a conversation, I want CLI slash-command plumbing and empty acknowledged-only turns hidden and compaction and interruption shown as small markers, so that the transcript reads as the conversation rather than as the agent's protocol.
evidence: `groupMessages` skips `isLocalCommandEntry` entries (bare `<local-command-caveat>`/`<command-name>`/`<local-command-stdout>` text); `buildDataItems` suppresses `isNoResponseOnly` assistant groups while keeping their model markers in order (kept visible in debug view); `CompactionMessage` renders a collapsed "Context compacted" summary and `InterruptedMessage` a "Request interrupted" line.

verdict.note: message-parsing.ts defines isLocalCommandEntry (user entries whose text blocks all start with <local-command-caveat>/<local-command-stdout>/<command-name>) and groupMessages skips them (`if (isLocalCommandEntry(entry)) continue;`). InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx buildDataItems calls isNoResponseOnly(allText) (lib/structured-output-parsing.ts: acks present, all kind 'no-response', nothing left after stripping tags) and, when !debugView, skips the group while still emitting the modelMarkers anchored at that index so order is preserved. ChatMessages.tsx exports CompactionMessage (a <details> with summary 'Context compacted') and InterruptedMessage ('Request interrupted'), both rendered by GroupItem for compaction/interrupted groups.

browser.note: The interruption half is real — 'Request interrupted' rendered as a small centered marker after Stop agent. But no <local-command-*> entries occurred to test the slash-command filtering, no empty acknowledged-only turn appeared, and running Advanced ▸ 'Run /compact' produced a visible '/compact' user bubble and a normal prose reply with no 'Context compacted' marker.

title: Reconnect mid-turn and pick the stream back up
story: As a person whose network or tab dropped while the agent was mid-reply, I want the client to resume the same turn from the last frame it saw, so that I do not lose the text that streamed while I was disconnected or have to wait for the turn to end.
evidence: chat-send-run.ts captures the turn's messages into the server-minted `turnId` buffer (turn-buffer.ts) with monotonic seq numbers; the `turnStream` subscription in events.ts replays `framesAfter(lastEventId)` and yields a `resync` frame when the buffer is gone or has a gap, which chat-actors.ts handles by falling back to a full history refetch — rate-limited by reconnect-refresh-gate.ts.

verdict.note: Verified end to end. callback-box/src/webapp/routes/chat-send-run.ts captureTurn() calls createTurnBuffer(turnId) and pushes every ChatMessage into it (buffer.push), scheduleTurnCleanup on finish. core/chat/turn-buffer.ts assigns monotonic seq, bounds the ring (MAX_FRAMES 4000 / 8MiB), tracks evictedThrough and exposes framesAfter/hasGapAfter with a 60s finished TTL. webapp/trpc/routers/events.ts turnStream takes {turnId, lastEventId}, yields {t:'resync'} when the buffer is missing or hasGapAfter(lastSeq), otherwise replays framesAfter(lastSeq) and yields each via tracked(String(seq)) so wsLink resends lastEventId on reconnect. frontend/src/machines/chat-actors.ts subscribes to events.turnStream and on a 'resync' frame fires STREAM_RECOVER (full history refetch), which reconnect-refresh-gate.ts rate-limits.

title: Recover a chat thread whose session went bad
story: As the boxholder, I want a chat job whose agent session failed to drop that thread's stored session, so that my next message in the thread starts a fresh session instead of failing the same way forever.
evidence: In `processChatJobs`, a successful invocation calls `markSessionUsed(sessions, sessionKey)` while a failure calls `resetSession(sessions, sessionKey)` before `saveChatSessions`; the session key is the job's `thread.ref` (falling back to the job path), so only the failing thread is reset.

verdict.note: src/core/reactor/chat-jobs.ts processChatJobs() computes sessionKey = extractThreadRef(job.content) ?? job.relPath, and after agent.invoke calls markSessionUsed(sessions, sessionKey) on success or resetSession(sessions, sessionKey) on failure, then saveChatSessions(boxRoot, sessions) after the loop. resetSession in src/core/chat/reactor-sessions.ts:116 does `delete store[threadRef]`, dropping only that thread's record from .callback-box/chat-sessions.json, so the next message for that thread takes the getOrCreateSession new-session branch. processChatJobs is reachable from src/core/reactor/cycle.ts:257.

title: Recover dictation lost to an interruption
story: As a person whose phone slept mid-dictation, I want the captured transcript offered back with Send, Continue, or Discard, so that I do not lose what I already said.
evidence: `RecoveredDictation` renders the persisted `useDictationDraft` transcript in a dedicated card; Send commits it as a narration `<speech>` message and Continue moves the text into the composer and restarts the mic.

verdict.note: RecoveredDictation.tsx renders a Card labelled 'Recovered dictation · captured <formatAgo>' with the persisted transcript and Discard / Continue / Send buttons. InteractiveChat-recovery.tsx's useRecoveredDictation pulls recoveredDraft from useDictationDraft (localStorage key from lib/dictation-draft.ts draftKey, written continuously during dictation), surfaces the widget only when idle, and wires handleRecoverSend -> sendVoiceSegment (InteractiveChat-dispatch.ts:97, createVoiceEmission producing a plain <speech> narration emission) and handleRecoverContinue -> inputStore.set(joinTranscript(...)) plus startVoice(). It is rendered through InteractiveChat.tsx lines 243/291, so the path is reachable.

title: Rename a chat and have the automatic titler leave it alone
story: As a person who has titled a conversation myself on its chat card, I want the nightly chat review to detect that the title is mine and stop rewriting it, so that my name for a chat survives every later review pass.
evidence: `resolveTitleOwner` in review/husk-write.ts classifies a husk title as unmanaged/generated/manual by comparing it against the hash of the title the reviewer last wrote and against the transcript-derived snippet title; state.ts persists `titleOwner`, and the transition to `manual` is one-way and re-checked each pass. session-label.ts then prefers the husk's editorial title in both session-list endpoints.

verdict.note: src/core/chat/review/husk-write.ts `resolveTitleOwner` returns 'manual' immediately when storedOwner==='manual' (one-way), classifies by comparing contentHash(currentTitle) against storedHash when a hash exists, and on the first pass compares against the transcript snippet title to distinguish an ensureChatHusk title from a hand-typed one; applyReviewToHusk re-reads the husk under withCardLock and sets writeTitle = titleClean && owner !== 'manual', so a manual title is never overwritten. state.ts persists titleOwner/titleHash (TitleOwnerSchema, defaults unmanaged/null) and run.ts re-derives the owner each pass (lines ~199, ~232). session-label.ts resolves the display label with the husk's editorial title first for both session-list endpoints. Caveat noted but not disqualifying: the `chat-review` schedule in src/core/box/defaults.ts (cron '0 4 * * *', 'Nightly chat review') is seeded enabled:false, so the nightly pass is opt-in per box.

title: Reopen a past Codex chat transcript
story: As a person using the web app, I want the history of a Codex-engine chat to load back, so that resuming that conversation shows what was already said.
evidence: CodexHistoryServer spawns the Codex app-server and speaks JSON-RPC over stdio for the history operations the SDK does not expose, with typed CodexHistoryRpcError/CodexHistoryServerExitError; codex-transcript.ts is the caller.

verdict.note: src/services/codex-history-server.ts spawns the codex app-server child process and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdio, with exported CodexHistoryRpcError and CodexHistoryServerExitError classes. src/core/chat/session/codex-transcript.ts is the caller (constructs CodexHistoryServer, defines threadReadSchema/threadListSchema and readCodexSessionHistory/listCodexThreadMetadata). Web reachability confirmed: load-history.ts resolveChatEngine dispatches to readCodexSessionHistory, and loadSessionHistory is called from the tRPC routers src/webapp/trpc/routers/history.ts and chat-session-procedures.ts, so a web-app chat on the codex engine loads its prior transcript.

title: Reset stuck chat sessions
story: As an operator, I want to wipe the reactor's persisted chat sessions before a run, so that a poisoned or unusable conversation session stops breaking every new message on that thread.
evidence: `runReactor` with `resetSessions` loads the session map, calls `resetAllSessions`, saves it and logs "Chat reactor sessions reset." before any job runs; independently, `processChatJobs` calls `resetSession(sessions, sessionKey)` whenever a thread's agent invocation fails, so the next message starts fresh.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/reactor/engine.ts declares `resetSessions?: boolean` in the options, normalizes it to `shouldResetSessions`, and at line ~120 (after the lock is acquired, before any cycle runs) calls loadChatSessions -> resetAllSessions(sessions) -> saveChatSessions and logs 'Chat reactor sessions reset.'. It is reachable from the CLI: callback-box/src/cli/commands/reactor.ts registers `--reset-sessions` ('Reset all persisted chat reactor sessions') and passes options.resetSessions into runReactor. Independently, chat-jobs.ts line 90 calls resetSession(sessions, sessionKey) in the failure branch of the agent invocation (markSessionUsed on success), matching the 'next message starts fresh' claim.

title: Resume a past conversation
story: As a returning user, I want to reopen a previous chat from a list labeled by its first message, so that I can pick up a thread instead of starting over.
evidence: `chat.sessions` returns each session's label, last-used time and which is most-active from `loadAllSessions`; `SessionListPanel` renders rows (landmark-grouped, never landmark-filtered) linking to `/chat?session=<id>`.

verdict.note: core/chat/session/list.ts `loadAllSessions` returns ChatSessionRow{sessionId, label, mtime,...} most-recently-active first, labels resolved by core/chat/session-label.ts `resolveSessionLabel` (husk title, else the transcript/preview first user message, else id prefix). trpc/routers/chat-session-procedures.ts `sessions` query maps those rows to {label, lastUsedAt, isActive: row.sessionId === mostActive}. Frontend SessionListPanel.tsx fetches via getChatSessions, groups rows with layoutSessionList from session-list-grouping.ts (current landmark first, 'Other chats' after — grouped, not filtered), and renders each as a <Link to={href(`/${boxSlug}/chat`)}> with the session search param; ChatPage.tsx reads `?session=<id>` and bootstraps that session's history. Reachable from the chat bar: ChatBarChrome.tsx renders SessionChip, whose 'Recent chats ›' sub-panel renders SessionListPanel.

browser.note: Session menu ▸ Recent chats listed rows labeled by first message plus id prefix and 'active just now', grouped by landmark ('in Box', 'in Acids & Bases'). Clicking a row navigated to ?session=<id> and rendered that transcript.

title: Run a chat that shows only callouts, not prose
story: As someone configuring a landmark or an agent writing a reply, I want a chat's feature flags (prose, narration) set from the landmark card or changed mid-conversation, and every open tab on that session to follow immediately, so that a place can decide how its chats read without the person touching a menu.
evidence: The `chat-features-changed` bus handler routes through `applyFeaturesChange` into `setChatFeatures`; InteractiveChat-view.tsx passes `proseEnabled={model.chatFeatures.prose !== "off"}` down to `AssistantMessage`, whose `showProse` branch renders only callouts and acks when off; `readLandmarkFeatures` seeds those flags from a landmark card's `navigation.chat-app` mapping.

verdict.note: core/chat/features.ts registers `prose` (default on) and `narration` and parses `<chat-app …>` deltas out of agent output; core/landmark/features.ts `readLandmarkFeatures`/`readLandmarkFeaturesForDir` seed those from a landmark card's `navigation.chat-app` and are called at session creation (webapp/trpc/routers/chat-control-procedures.ts:236, webapp/routes/chat-send-target.ts:46). webapp/routes/chat.ts:159 bridges the session's `features-changed` to the bus as `chat-features-changed`; InteractiveChat-ws.ts:152-154 routes it through `applyFeaturesChange` (InteractiveChat-helpers.ts:149, session-id filtered) into `setChatFeatures`, so every open tab on that session updates live. InteractiveChat-view.tsx:186 passes `proseEnabled={model.chatFeatures.prose !== 'off'}`, and ChatMessages.tsx:117/168 gates the prose groups on `showProse` while still rendering `CalloutStack` (acks render as badges on the user message).

title: Run box chats on Codex instead of Claude
story: As someone configuring a box, I want chats to run on the box's configured harness, with history, labels and deletion working the same, so that choosing Codex doesn't cost me the chat surface.
evidence: `resolveChatEngine` picks the box's `agentEngine` for new chats and the recorded per-session engine for resumes; `codex-transcript.ts` adapts Codex app-server `thread/read`, `thread/list` and delete into the chat history model, and `createCodexAgent` supplies the batch-agent contract with the plugin installed by `ensureCodexPluginInstalled`.

verdict.note: src/core/box/config.ts loadAgentEngine reads config.agentEngine ('claude'|'codex', defaulting to claude), and src/core/chat/session/engine.ts resolveChatEngine returns that for a new chat (sessionId null) or the recorded history entry's engine for a resume. That resolver is consulted across the chat surface: start.ts (buildBackendStartOptions passes engine into ChatBackendStartOptions), load-history.ts, availability.ts, transcript-sync.ts, thread.ts, deliver-user-message.ts, and webapp/trpc/routers/history.ts + chat-control-procedures.ts. codex-transcript.ts implements readCodexSessionHistory (thread/read), listCodexThreadMetadata (thread/list, paginated, used by session/list.ts which resolves labels via resolveSessionLabel) and deleteCodexSession/codexSessionExists (used by session/delete.ts). services/codex-chat.ts is the interactive Codex ChatBackend and core/agent/codex-agent.ts createCodexAgent implements the batch Agent contract, both calling ensureCodexPluginInstalled. No feature flag gates it beyond the box config field.

title: See the agent's background self-notes in the transcript
story: As a person reading a chat, I want notes the agent recorded about its own background work shown as marked records with their ref and commit, so that machine-written entries do not read as things I or the assistant said in conversation.
evidence: `groupMessages` calls `entrySelfNotes` and emits a `self-note` group carrying the parsed notes; `SelfNoteMessage` renders each with a self-note header, the note's `ref` and a shortened commit hash in its own bordered block rather than a user bubble.

verdict.note: message-parsing.ts groupMessages calls entrySelfNotes(entry) (shared/self-note.ts parses <self-note ref=... commit=...> blocks in pure-self-note user entries) and pushes a {type:'self-note', notes} group.
