InteractiveChat-message-items.tsx GroupItem branches on group.type === 'self-note' and renders SelfNoteMessage per note; ChatMessages.tsx SelfNoteMessage draws a bordered left-rule block with a 'self-note' header, the note's ref, and commit.substring(0,7), separate from UserMessage bubbles.

browser.note: No agent self-notes exist in this box's chat history (fresh worktree clone, no background/machine-written entries), so the self-note group with ref + short commit never rendered. Producing one would require triggering background/scheduled work.

title: See the files this conversation touched
story: As a person using the web app, I want the paths the agent read or wrote during this chat surfaced as a recency-ordered list with card summaries, so that I can jump to what the conversation was about.
evidence: collectPaths() walks the session entries for box-path markdown targets, legacy view: refs, ack targets, and tool inputs keyed file_path/notebook_path/target_file/source_file; dedupeRecent() orders most-recent-first and useRecentFiles fetches summaries via trpc files.summarize.

verdict.note: hooks/useRecentFiles.ts collectPaths() walks SessionEntry content blocks, extracting markdown link/image box-path targets, legacy view: refs, ack refs via parseAcks (lib/structured-output-parsing.ts, which defines parseAcks at line 91), and tool_use inputs keyed file_path/notebook_path/target_file/source_file; dedupeRecent() keeps the last occurrence and reverses to most-recent-first, capped at MAX_RECENT_FILES=20, with summaries from trpc.files.summarize. Reachable in the UI: components/chat/RecentFilesPanel.tsx calls useRecentFiles and renders FileEntry rows, and ContextMenuBody.tsx mounts it as the chat context chip's 'Recent files ›' sub-panel with an onPanel jump handler.

browser.note: After the agent read one card, the 'Here:' / Place menu's 'Recent files' submenu listed it as 'Acids Bases Progress' with its card summary ('Probe-seeded progress for the acids/bases learner — ...') and full path. Expanding the row previews the card inline with Card/Source tabs and offers 'Open as side panel' / 'Open as full page'. Empty before any file was touched ('No recent files yet').

title: See what the agent is doing during a turn
story: As a person waiting on a turn, I want tool calls, thinking blocks, and long-running background tasks shown as they happen, so that I can tell the agent is working and on what.
evidence: `activity-rendering.tsx` maps tool calls to one-line human summaries via the toolDescribers table; `useBackgroundTasks` folds TaskEvents from the event stream into a pill strip above the composer showing label, last tool, and elapsed time.

verdict.note: activity-rendering.tsx holds the toolDescribers Map (Read/Edit/Write/Bash/Grep/Glob/TodoWrite/Agent/Task) used by describeToolCall to produce one-line summaries, and renders 'thinking' parts in the collapsible activity group (cases at lines 76/191/221, plus ThinkingCornerMark); message-parsing.ts groups consecutive non-text parts into {kind:'activity'} groups and handles partial-streaming blocks. BackgroundTasks.tsx exports useBackgroundTasks + a TaskPill strip showing description, lastToolName, and formatted elapsed time, folded from TaskEvents via applyTaskEvent in background-tasks.ts; InteractiveChat.tsx wires useBackgroundTasks into InteractiveChat-ws.ts (onTaskEvent on live events) and InteractiveChat-view.tsx renders <BackgroundTasks/> above the composer. The fourth cited file, core/chat/card-activity.ts, is about companion-pane card activity rather than agent activity, but the other three fully implement the story.

browser.note: A tool-using turn rendered '▶ Ran script: Find image files under box/inbox' as a one-line summary while the turn was live, alongside 'Agent is working…'; assistant messages also carry a small 'thought' marker span for thinking. No long-running background task existed to exercise the BackgroundTasks pill strip.

title: See when someone else writes in the same chat
story: As one of several people sharing a box, I want another person's messages and server-delivered messages to appear in my open chat live, so that a shared conversation stays in sync without a reload.
evidence: useChatWs's `chat-user-message` handler dispatches OTHER_USER_MESSAGE when the sender's email differs from the current user, and a plain REFRESH when `user === null` (a delivered upload/capture); `isOtherChatUser` decides how the bubble is attributed.

verdict.note: InteractiveChat-ws.ts's onEvent handles `chat-user-message`: after the session filter, `userMessage.user === null` (server-injected upload/capture delivery) sends `{type:"REFRESH"}`, and otherwise when `currentUser && userMessage.user.email !== currentUser.email` it sends `{type:"OTHER_USER_MESSAGE", message, userName, timestamp}` — both live over the realtime socket, no reload. chat-message-sender.ts `isOtherChatUser` compares senderEmail against currentUserEmail (falling back to name, and false when locallyAuthored), and user-message.tsx line ~155 uses it to render the left-aligned other-user bubble with a name label.

title: See when the agent re-listened to my recording
story: As a person who dictated a message, I want a badge when the agent replaced my transcript with a better pass or listened to the audio to answer a question, so that I can tell what it actually heard.
evidence: The `chat-retranscription` / `chat-audio-consulted` bus handlers write into the per-message audio overlay store (matched with `matchesOwnSession`), and `AudioOverlayBadgeCluster` renders the ear / ear-sparkle badges with the swapped text and the questions asked; `chat-last-audio-request` is answered from this tab's retention store.

verdict.note: InteractiveChat-ws.ts (lines 126-143) handles the `chat-retranscription` and `chat-audio-consulted` bus events, gates each with matchesOwnSession(sessionId, event.sessionId), and writes them into the store from audio-overlay-store.ts via applyRetranscription/applyConsulted (consulted appends deduped questions). user-message.tsx reads that entry with useAudioOverlayEntry and renders <AudioOverlayBadgeCluster> in both layouts (lines 181, 214), and buildAudioBadgeSpecs in audio-overlay-badge.tsx produces an ear badge labeled 'Retranscribed — <service>' whose popover shows the original realtime transcript, plus an ear-sparkle badge 'The agent analyzed this recording' listing the questions asked. Emitters exist server-side in webapp/routes/chat-audio-review-routes.ts (emitTransient for both events), and `chat-last-audio-request` is fulfilled from this tab in the same ws handler (fulfillLastAudioRequest, native-last-audio-request.ts / lib/audio/last-audio.ts).

title: See which dictated words the recognizer was unsure of
story: As a person sending a dictated message, I want low-confidence stretches marked as unsure in what gets sent, so that the agent knows which words to distrust rather than acting on a mishearing.
evidence: `markUnsureWords` (called from `assembleChatMessage`) wraps low-confidence spans in `<unsure>` using the seed/extend thresholds against Deepgram `FinalWord` confidences; `UserMessageText` renders the marked words with a subtle style instead of dropping the tag.

verdict.note: input/unsure-words.ts exports markUnsureWords with UNSURE_THRESHOLD=0.7 (seed) and UNSURE_EXTEND=0.9 (extend/bridge, sentence-stop) applied against FinalWord.confidence from machines/transcription-events, tokenized via unsure-words-tokenize.ts. input/targets/chat-assemble.ts line 79 calls markUnsureWords on the body when emission.origin === 'voice' and emission.words is defined, before applySelections, and the wrapped <speech> body carries the <unsure> tags (stt="deepgram" stamped when words present). assembleChatMessage is reached from input/targets/chat-target.ts, used by components/chat/InteractiveChat-dispatch.ts, so the send path is live. components/chat/user-message-text.tsx parses <unsure>…</unsure> in its tagRe and renders the word with a dotted underline rather than stripping it.

title: Send a message and watch the reply stream in
story: As a person using the box's web chat, I want to type a message, send it, and see the agent's reply appear token by token, so that I get an answer without waiting for the whole turn to finish.
evidence: `POST /api/chat/send` (registerChatSendRoutes) validates the body, resolves a target session and starts an acked run; the session is created with `includePartialMessages: true` (registerChatRoutes in routes/chat.ts) so token deltas reach the client, and the frontend chatMachine's stream actor plus the WS `chat-complete`/`chat-history` subscription in InteractiveChat-ws.ts drive the live bubble.

verdict.note: registerChatSendRoutes in callback-box/src/webapp/routes/chat-send-routes.ts registers `POST /api/chat/send` (line 60). registerChatRoutes in webapp/routes/chat.ts builds the ChatSessionRegistry with buildSessionOptions returning includePartialMessages: true (line 95), which start.ts:142 passes into the SDK query via services/claude-chat.ts:134. The frontend streamActor in frontend/src/machines/chat-actors.ts calls startChatTurn, subscribes to trpcClient.events.turnStream, and on `stream_event` frames emits STREAM_TEXT for each `text_delta` (lines 135-163), suppressing the duplicate final assistant text via sawTextPartial. Token-by-token rendering in the live bubble is therefore real, not just whole-turn delivery.

browser.note: Typed in the composer, pressed Enter, reply appeared without reload. Mid-turn sampling of a 400/700-word essay prompt showed partial prose growing in place with 'Agent is working…' below it, so token deltas reach the client.

title: Send while the agent is still working
story: As a person mid-conversation, I want a message sent during a running turn to be accepted and queued rather than rejected, and to see how many of my messages are waiting, so that I can keep typing without tracking whether the agent is busy.
evidence: chat-send-routes.ts enqueues on a busy session and answers `{queued: true}` with a 200 instead of starting a turn; chatMachine.ts promotes the message to a dimmed pending bubble on that response and arms the missed-chat-complete recovery poll, and TargetStrip.tsx renders the 'N messages queued' banner above the composer.

verdict.note: chat-send-routes.ts lines ~160-170: when chatSession.isBusy() it records the user message and calls chatSession.enqueue(buildSendInput(...)), returning HTTP 200 {queued:true} rather than an error. ChatSession.enqueue (core/chat/session/index.ts:281) pushes onto messageQueue and drainQueue combines them via combineQueuedInputs (session/state.ts:244) after the turn completes. On the client, chat-actors.ts:280 emits STREAM_QUEUED, chatMachine.ts:289 handles it with promoteLastToPending (chat-actions.ts:168) keeping a dimmed pending bubble and InteractiveChat-hooks.ts usePendingMessagePoll arms the recovery poll; InteractiveChat-view.tsx renders TargetStrip with pendingCount, which prints 'N messages queued' (TargetStrip.tsx:37).

browser.note: Sending while a turn was running was accepted: the composer button became 'Queue message (agent is busy)', the new message showed as a dimmed 'queued — waiting' bubble, and a '1 message queued' banner rendered above the composer. The queued message ran after the turn finished.

title: Start a chat about the card I am reading
story: As a person browsing a card in the web app, I want a Chat/New control on the card page that opens a conversation scoped to that card's landmark with the card already docked beside it, so that I can ask about what I am looking at without hunting for the right chat first.
evidence: CardViewPage renders OpenChatControl, which calls the `chat.openForCard` tRPC query (chat.ts) to resolve the nearest enclosing landmark dir plus the most-recent session bound to it, then navigates to /$boxSlug/chat with `?session=<id|new>&contextDir=…&card=<cardPath>`; the 'New' button always forces session=new.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/frontend/src/pages/card/CardViewPage.tsx:36 renders OpenChatControl(boxSlug, cardPath); OpenChatControl.tsx exposes a 'Chat' and a 'New' button, both calling utils.chat.openForCard.fetch({cardPath}). chat.ts openForCard (lines 101-114) resolves nearestLandmarkDir(boxRoot, {cardPath}) plus getLastSessionForDirectory, returning {contextDir, sessionId}. 'Chat' navigates to /$boxSlug/chat with search {session: sessionId, card}; 'New' always navigates with {session: 'new', contextDir, card}. The chat route's validateSearch (router.tsx:117) accepts `card`, documented as the card live-open in the companion pane; the card page itself is the /card/$ route (router.tsx:183-188).

title: Toggle narration and prose for a chat
story: As a person in a chat, I want to turn narration mode or agent prose on and off, so that the conversation behaves the way I want without editing configuration.
evidence: The feature registry defines `narration` and `prose` with closed value sets; `chat.setFeature` validates and stores the change, the session broadcasts `chat-features-changed`, and the snapshot rides each user message as the `<chat-app>` tag the agent can also mutate.

verdict.note: Over-claim on the prose half. core/chat/features.ts does register narration and prose with closed on/off value sets and chat-control-procedures.ts setFeature validates and stores them, but the only user-facing control is narration: VoiceChip.tsx renders the '✓ Narration mode' menu item wired to handleToggleNarration in InteractiveChat-hooks.ts (which calls setChatFeature with feature 'narration' — the only literal feature name any frontend call passes). Grepping the frontend for prose finds only consumption (InteractiveChat-view.tsx proseEnabled={model.chatFeatures.prose !== 'off'}); nothing calls setChatFeature for prose, and FeatureDescriptor.uiKind/listFeatures are referenced nowhere outside features.ts, so no generic settings UI exists. prose is settable only from a landmark card (schemas/landmark.ts prose enum) or an agent <chat-app> delta — i.e. by editing configuration, which the story says the user avoids. The cited VoiceChip-panels.tsx contains no narration or prose code at all (it is the transcription-service sub-panel).

panel.note: The mechanism is live end to end. core/chat/features.ts registers narration and prose with closed value sets and defaults, exporting isKnownFeature/isValidValue/resolveFeatures/mergeSeedFeatures; core/chat/session/features.ts::set() validates against that registry, persists via updateFeaturesForSession, and fires onChange (the features-changed event); webapp/trpc/routers/chat-control-procedures.ts mounts chat.setFeature, which calls target.setFeature and returns the resolved map, with wireSession bridging the change onto the bus. On the client, api-chat.ts exports setChatFeature (re-exported from api.ts), InteractiveChat-hooks.ts calls it for narration behind handleToggleNarration (wired through InteractiveChat-view.tsx -> ChatBarChrome -> VoiceChip's menu), InteractiveChat-ws.ts applies the chat-features-changed broadcast, and InteractiveChat-view.tsx consumes model.chatFeatures.prose !== 'off'; prompts.ts documents and the snapshot emits the <chat-app prose=... narration=.../> tag with agent-side deltas. Two caveats that fall outside this lens: the cited VoiceChip-panels.tsx has no narration/prose code (the toggle lives in VoiceChip.tsx), and no frontend call passes feature 'prose' (listFeatures/uiKind are unreferenced outside features.ts) — so the prose half is settable only via the generic endpoint, landmark, or agent delta, which is a reachability/wording question for the other reviewers.

Narration has a real rendered entry point: VoiceChip.tsx:128 renders a '✓ Narration mode' MenuItem in the voice chip's root panel, wired through ChatBarChrome/InteractiveChat-view.tsx:135 to handleToggleNarration (InteractiveChat-hooks.ts:164-192), which calls setChatFeature -> trpcClient.chat.setFeature (api-chat.ts:105), and that procedure is registered (chat-control-procedures.ts:182, spread into the chat router at routers/chat.ts:80). No flag or config gates it. Prose has no dedicated rendered control -- the frontend only consumes it (InteractiveChat-view.tsx:186 proseEnabled={model.chatFeatures.prose !== 'off'}) -- but a person in the chat still reaches it without editing configuration: prompts.ts:125-127 tells the agent it can toggle prose mid-conversation via <chat-app prose="off"/>, and narration mode itself flips prose off. So the capability is reachable by the stated role; whether 'toggle prose' deserves equal billing with narration is a wording/scope question for another lens.

The registry in callback-box/src/core/chat/features.ts declares both `narration` and `prose` (uiKind toggle, label 'Show agent prose'), but only narration has a user control. The single frontend call site is InteractiveChat-hooks.ts:180, `setChatFeature({ sessionId, feature: "narration", value: next })`, driven by the '✓ Narration mode' menu item in VoiceChip.tsx:135; grepping the whole frontend for prose finds only consumption (ChatMessages.tsx proseEnabled), and listFeatures()/uiKind are referenced nowhere outside features.ts, so no generic feature-settings UI exists. prose can only be set by landmark frontmatter (src/schemas/landmark.ts:87 `prose: z.enum(["on","off"])`) or by an agent `<chat-app>` delta — i.e. by editing configuration or by the agent, which is precisely what the story's 'so that ... without editing configuration' clause promises the person avoids. The story claims a two-feature capability in the web UI where the code delivers one.

browser.note: Narration verified end to end: Voice menu > 'Narration mode' flipped the button label to 'Voice — narration on' and the next turn's envelope changed from <chat-app narration="off" ...> to narration="on", with the reply arriving as a <callout>. There is no separate 'agent prose' control anywhere in the UI (Voice menu = Mute / Narration mode / Voice settings; Session menu > Advanced = Debug View / Run /compact / Restart Subprocess / Stop Process / Delete conversation); prose stayed "on" in every envelope I saw.

triage.reasoning: Narration is fully delivered — VoiceChip.tsx renders the 'Narration mode' item, handleToggleNarration (InteractiveChat-hooks.ts:164-194) calls setChatFeature -> chat.setFeature, and the browser check (browser/chat-2.json) confirmed the toggle flips the next turn's <chat-app narration="on"> envelope. Prose is a real, working feature but has no user control: the only literal feature name any frontend call passes is 'narration' (grep of src/frontend for setChatFeature), the frontend only consumes prose (proseEnabled), and FeatureDescriptor.uiKind / listFeatures() are referenced nowhere outside src/core/chat/features.ts, so the settings UI those fields anticipate does not exist. Prose is changed by asking the agent (prompts.ts:123-127 documents `<chat-app prose="off"/>` as a mid-conversation toggle), by turning narration on (which flips prose off), or by landmark frontmatter. Nothing is broken or unreachable — the story just bills prose as a UI toggle alongside narration when the UI has one toggle. Correct the story to 'turn narration mode on and off' and note prose rides narration / the agent. The unused uiKind+label ('Show agent prose') in the registry is dead metadata, not a user-visible defect.

title: A damaged credential or sync-state file stops the write instead of resetting it
story: As an operator, I want a truncated or unparseable Google token file or connector state file to raise a named error telling me to inspect or delete it, so that a crash mid-write cannot cost me the shared refresh token or a connector's sync cursors by silently starting from defaults.
evidence: loadTransientState returns defaultValue only on ENOENT and otherwise throws TransientStateCorruptError ("Refusing to fall back to defaults — inspect the file, or delete it to resync from scratch"); readTokensForUpdate mirrors it with GoogleTokenStoreCorruptError, failing the write so a single-field update cannot replace the whole token record.

verdict.note: src/connectors/transient-state.ts loadTransientState() returns defaultValue only when errnoCode(e) === 'ENOENT'; any other read error or a JSON.parse failure throws TransientStateCorruptError whose message is 'Refusing to fall back to defaults — inspect the file, or delete it to resync from scratch.' src/connectors/google-token-store.ts readTokensForUpdate() mirrors that: ENOENT -> {}, otherwise GoogleTokenStoreCorruptError ('Refusing to overwrite it — inspect or remove the file by hand, then re-authorize'). Because readTokensForUpdate is called inside the locked RMW just before writeFileAtomic (line ~202), the throw aborts the write, so a single-field update cannot replace the whole token record. Both errors are named classes carrying the offending path (statePath/storePath).

title: A synced Google Doc admits what the export dropped
story: As a box agent, I want a synced Doc's card to tally the content markdown export cannot carry — complex tables, inline objects, equations, footnotes, pending suggestions — so that I know when to open the original instead of trusting the local copy.
evidence: tallyLossyFromDocument walks the Docs API body counting complex tables (isComplexTable: nested tables or multi-paragraph cells), inline objects, equations, footnotes and unresolved suggestion ids; lossyToTemplateItems writes them as `<item type= count=>` entries in the card's `<lossy>` block (comments are excluded — they go to the sidecar), and `cb drive status` prints them as a `Lossy: …` line per mounted file.

verdict.note: src/connectors/drive-handler-docs.ts tallyLossyFromDocument counts inlineObjects (as images), footnotes, paragraph-element equations, unresolved suggestedInsertionIds/suggestedDeletionIds (deduped in a Set), and tables where isComplexTable finds a nested table or a multi-paragraph cell; comments are deliberately excluded from the tally (they go to reconcileCommentsSidecar). lossyToTemplateItems emits {type,count} pairs which pull() passes as createGdocTemplate({lossy}) (src/schemas/gdoc.tsx:133 writes the lossy field, and its schema instructions tell the agent what it means). src/cli/commands/drive.ts:249-264 scrapes <item type=".." count=".."> from mounted cards and prints a 'Lossy: type=n, ...' line in cb drive status. If the documents.readonly scope is missing, tryGetDocument returns null and lossy falls back to emptyLossy(), but the normal scoped path is intact.

title: A view calls a paid provider API without holding the key
story: As a boxholder, I want a view running in my browser to call an external provider API through the box's authenticated adapter, so that a view can use Replicate/OpenAI/Anthropic/Mistral without the key ever reaching the browser or hitting CORS.
evidence: `ViewProps.adapterFetch(adapter, { path, ...RequestInit })` is documented to have the server inject the key from `config/connectors/<adapter>.secret.json` and to accept upstream absolute polling URLs by stripping the origin; `useViewFileHelpers.ts` implements it and `webapp/routes/api-adapters.ts` is the proxying route.

verdict.note: src/webapp/routes/api-adapters.ts registers ANY(GET/POST/PUT/DELETE) /api/adapters/:adapter/* with an ADAPTERS table for replicate, mistral, anthropic, openai; it resolves the key server-side (resolveSecret with a legacy config/connectors/<adapter>.secret.json fallback), injects authorization/x-api-key upstream, forwards only content-type/accept/prefer/anthropic-version (cookies dropped), and streams the response back — so the key never reaches the browser and CORS is bypassed. useViewFileHelpers.makeHelpers.adapterFetch strips the origin from an absolute http(s) URL (new URL(...).pathname + search) and fetches `${apiBase}/adapters/${adapter}${path}`. Route is registered from routes/api.ts (registerApiAdapterRoutes) and the helper is passed into views by AgentViewRenderer.tsx; ViewProps.adapterFetch is declared in core/views/types.ts.

title: An enabled-but-unconfigured mail connector says so instead of looking idle
story: As a box owner, I want Gmail sync to report an error when the box has Gmail turned on but no connector config, so that a box that has quietly stopped importing mail shows a failure rather than a healthy-looking "no new items".
evidence: `readConfig` in gmail.ts throws `MissingGmailConfigError` on ENOENT ("Gmail is enabled for this box but has no configuration") and `parseGmailConnectorConfig` throws on an invalid one; sync returns `{ success: false, error }`, which `reportSyncResult` prints as an error and counts, instead of the earlier degrade-to-empty-config path that let a box go five days without importing mail.

verdict.note: connectors/gmail.ts readConfig reads config/connectors/gmail.json and on ENOENT throws MissingGmailConfigError (message in connectors/gmail-config.ts line 167: 'file not found — Gmail is enabled for this box but has no configuration'); parseGmailConnectorConfig throws GmailConnectorConfigError on invalid config. readConfig is called inside syncUnderLock, whose throw is caught by GmailConnector.sync and returned as { success: false, created: [], updated: [], error: 'Gmail sync failed: …' }. cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts reportSyncResult prints `Error: <error>` to stderr and returns errors:1 (counted into totalErrors) rather than falling into the 'No new items.' branch. The gmail.ts doc comment explicitly cites the five-day silent-degrade incident this replaced.

title: Authorize Google from the CLI
story: As an operator, I want to run `cb google-auth` and complete the OAuth flow in a browser, so that a box gets a Google refresh token without going through the web admin page.
evidence: googleAuthCommand takes --client-id/--client-secret (or the resolved store/env creds), starts an ephemeral Fastify server on port 8976, opens the consent page, exchanges the code, and calls saveGoogleTokens; --reauth forces a re-grant.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/google-auth.ts exports googleAuthCommand ('cb google-auth', registered at src/cli/index.ts:113) with --client-id/--client-secret/--reauth; it falls back to getGoogleClientCreds (src/connectors/google-auth.ts:70), skips when loadGoogleTokens already has a refreshToken unless --reauth, builds the consent URL with access_type=offline/prompt=consent via createOAuth2Client + GOOGLE_SCOPES, starts a Fastify server on 127.0.0.1:8976 serving /oauth/callback, calls open(authUrl), exchanges the code with oauth2Client.getToken, and persists refreshToken/accessToken/tokenExpiry through saveGoogleTokens (src/connectors/google-token-store.ts:225). No web admin page is involved.

title: Auto-mount new files from a Drive folder
story: As a box owner, I want a Drive folder mounted at a local path so new files in it get cards automatically, so that I do not have to add each document by hand.
evidence: loadDriveConfig reads folders[] from config/connectors/google-drive.json; GoogleDriveConnector.syncFolder lists the folder, skips files already carded, and creates `<safeName>.<cardType>.card` under folder.localPath for each handled mimeType.

verdict.note: drive-config.ts defines DriveFolderMount {driveFolderId, localPath} and loadDriveConfig reads config/connectors/google-drive.json. In google-drive.ts the sync loop (step 3, 'Folder mounts — discover new files') calls this.syncFolder for each config.folders entry; syncFolder does service.listFiles(folder.driveFolderId), skips files whose driveId is already in existingDriveIds (collected from existing *.card files) or whose card path already exists on disk, skips mimeTypes with no handler via getHandlerForMimeType, and otherwise creates <safeFilename(name)>.<handler.cardType>.card under folder.localPath then syncs it. Created cards are staged and committed.

title: Be told exactly what is wrong with a hand-edited Gmail config
story: As my box's agent, I want a Gmail config that is ambiguous, incomplete, duplicated or missing to fail the sync with a named error, so that a filter file I edited by hand never quietly collects the wrong mail or no mail at all.
evidence: parseGmailConnectorConfig throws distinct errors — AmbiguousGmailShorthandError (query and labels both set), MixedGmailRuleConfigError, StrayGmailActionError, DuplicateGmailRuleNameError, MissingGmailActionError — and readConfig in gmail.ts turns an absent file into MissingGmailConfigError rather than an empty config, because degrading "looked identical to a healthy connector with nothing to do".

verdict.note: src/connectors/gmail-config.ts defines GmailConnectorConfigError and the named subclasses DuplicateGmailRuleNameError, MixedGmailRuleConfigError, MissingGmailActionError, StrayGmailActionError, AmbiguousGmailShorthandError and MissingGmailConfigError, and parseGmailConnectorConfig throws each at the corresponding condition (query+labels both set, mixed shorthand/rule form, stray action, missing action, duplicate rule name). src/connectors/gmail.ts readConfig throws MissingGmailConfigError on ENOENT rather than returning an empty config, and it is called from syncUnderLock, so a bad or absent config surfaces as a failed sync ({success:false} with the error message) rather than a silent no-op.

title: Be told when the Google authorization dies
story: As a box owner, I want the box to notice that Google revoked or expired its grant and tell me where to reconnect, so that paused Gmail/Calendar/Drive sync does not go unnoticed for days.
evidence: classifyRefreshFailure marks the grant dead on invalid_grant, probeGoogleAuthIfStale forces a refresh about daily, googleAuthHealthChecks emits a `google-auth` health warning with the /<slug>/admin?reconnect=google link, and google-auth-alert.ts sends one notification per breakage via notifyBoxholder.

verdict.note: connectors/google-auth-status.ts: isInvalidGrantError/classifyRefreshFailure call markGoogleAuthDead (google-token-store.ts:253, sets needsReauthSince/reauthReason) only on invalid_grant, and probeGoogleAuthIfStale forces a refresh once PROBE_INTERVAL_MS (24h) has elapsed. webapp/trpc/routers/health-google.ts googleAuthHealthChecks emits an ok:false 'google-auth' warning naming reauthorizeUrl() = /<slug>/admin?reconnect=google, and it is wired into the health router (health.ts:328). core/schedule/google-auth-alert.ts checkGoogleAuthAndAlert probes, then sends one notifyBoxholder alert per breakage using a needsReauthSince latch; it is called from scheduler.ts:276 each tick. The admin UI honors the deep link (frontend/src/components/admin/GoogleServicesSection.tsx:38 reads ?reconnect=google).

title: Browse Drive files and folders
story: As a boxholder, I want the box to look up a Drive file's metadata and list a folder's contents, so that it can follow links into my Drive and know what it is dealing with before fetching.
evidence: getFile(fileId) requests id,name,mimeType,modifiedTime,owners,parents,webViewLink; listFiles(folderId) pages drive/v3 files with q="'<folderId>' in parents and trashed = false".

verdict.note: src/services/google-drive.ts createGoogleDriveService implements getFile(fileId) as GET drive/v3 files/<id> with fields id,name,mimeType,modifiedTime,owners(emailAddress,displayName),parents,webViewLink, and listFiles(folderId) paging drive/v3 files with q="'<folderId>' in parents and trashed = false" (pageSize 100, nextPageToken loop). Both are reachable: src/cli/commands/drive.ts calls service.getFile (lines 71, 130) and service.listFiles (line 280), and src/webapp/trpc/routers/drive.ts constructs the same service. Matches the story's claim as written.

title: Calendar events as .ics files in the box, remote-authoritative on conflict
story: As a box owner, I want each synced event kept as an .ics file that is refreshed from Google, with a genuine local-and-remote edit resolved in Google's favor and noted, so that the box never silently clobbers a change I made in Google Calendar.
evidence: syncCalendar pulls with sync tokens into `store/calendar/{date}_{shortId}.ics`; decideCalendarSync is the single precedence function — no local edit or new remote event → remote-wins, local edit with unchanged remote → local-wins, both changed → remote-wins with a note.

verdict.note: google-calendar-ics.ts eventFilename() builds `${dateStr}_${shortId}.ics` (event.id.slice(-8)) and google-calendar-state.ts calendarDir() resolves to boxRoot/store/calendar. google-calendar.ts sync passes state.syncTokens[calendarId] into syncCalendar (google-calendar-sync.ts), which uses the sync-token delta pull. decideCalendarSync in google-calendar-decide.ts is the single precedence function: untracked or !localEdited -> remote-wins; localEdited && !remoteChanged -> local-wins (tryPushLocalEdit patches Google); localEdited && remoteChanged -> remote-wins, and reconcileEvent then logs a warning and pushes an acc.notes entry with detail 'local edit discarded — event also changed remotely (remote wins)'. Matches the story including the 'noted' qualifier.

title: Calendar sync repairs an expired sync token and isolates one bad calendar
story: As a box owner, I want a lapsed Google sync token to trigger a full re-pull automatically and a calendar that errors to be reported without stopping the others, so that calendar sync keeps working after an outage without me intervening.
evidence: runCalendarSync catches the per-calendar sync failure: on HTTP 410 it deletes `state.syncTokens[calendarId]`, saves state, and re-runs syncCalendar with `syncToken: undefined` (flagging isFullResync); any other status saves state and returns an `error` string for that calendar while the loop continues to the next one.

verdict.note: Read callback-box/src/connectors/google-calendar.ts in full: runCalendarSync catches a syncCalendar failure, and when it is a ky HTTPError with status 410 it deletes state.syncTokens[calendarId], saves state, and re-runs syncCalendar with syncToken undefined, returning a synced full-resync outcome. The isolation half now holds: an ordinary failure restores the incoming token, saves state, and returns a failed member outcome, which the caller records before continuing later calendars and then running processLocalDeletes, pushAndCleanOrphans, the final saveState, and stageAndCommitPaths. Failure remains visible through success false, a sanitized aggregate error, a partial commit message with failed calendars, and wakeup's connector error count and nonzero exit status. The entry point is cb wakeup, which constructs this connector in wakeup-connectors.ts and calls sync.

title: Cap how many threads a mail rule may track by itself
story: As a box owner, I want a rolling ceiling on the threads a track rule creates on its own, tunable per rule, so that a query that turns out to be too broad stops after a handful of cards instead of filling the box.
evidence: A track action carries a `budget: {threads, window}` normalized from DEFAULT_TRACKING_THREADS (25) and DEFAULT_TRACKING_WINDOW ("7d"); remainingAutomaticTrackingBudget counts the rule's recorded tracking timestamps inside the rolling window and evaluateGmailRules only issues track requests while capacity remains. `cb connector gmail track` is explicit and unbudgeted.

verdict.note: gmail-config.ts defines DEFAULT_TRACKING_THREADS=25 and DEFAULT_TRACKING_WINDOW='7d', with a per-rule optional budget {threads, window} normalized by normalizeBudget() into {threads, windowMs} on a track action. gmail-tracking.ts:90 remainingAutomaticTrackingBudget filters the rule state's automaticTrackingEvents timestamps to the rolling window and returns threads - events.length; gmail-rules.ts automaticTrack() (line 157) returns selected:false when remaining===0, and evaluateGmailRules is invoked from connectors/gmail.ts:212 during sync. The explicit path (cli/commands/connector.ts importing trackGmailThread from gmail-track.ts) applies no budget, matching the story's scoping to rule-created tracking.

title: Configure which Gmail, Calendar and Drive content syncs
story: As the box owner, I want to see which calendars and Drive folders are available and set what the box should pull, so that syncing brings in what I care about and nothing else.
evidence: `calendar.available`/`config`/`updateConfig`, `drive.available`/`config`/`updateConfig`, and `gmailConfig`/`updateGmailConfig` (ownerProcedures spread into `adminRouter`) read and write the per-connector configuration.

verdict.note: Calendar and Gmail hold up: trpc calendar.available/config/updateConfig (src/webapp/trpc/routers/calendar.ts) are driven by src/frontend/src/components/settings/CalendarSection.tsx, and admin.gmailConfig/updateGmailConfig (admin-gmail.ts, spread into adminRouter at routers/admin.ts:48) by components/admin/GmailFiltersSection.tsx. Drive does not: src/frontend/src/components/settings/DriveSection.tsx is documented in its own header as 'this view is read-only. Mounting itself is done via CLI (cb drive add)' and calls only drive.config and drive.available — it never calls trpc.drive.updateConfig, so the owner cannot set Drive folders from the web UI. Also drive.available returns service.listSpreadsheets(), i.e. available spreadsheets, not available folders, so 'see which Drive folders are available' is wrong as written.

panel.note: All three cited procedure sets are real and mounted: src/webapp/trpc/router.ts imports and mounts calendarRouter (line 36), driveRouter (line 43) and adminRouter (line 40), and adminRouter spreads gmailAdminProcedures at routers/admin.ts:48, so admin.gmailConfig/updateGmailConfig from admin-gmail.ts are live owner procedures. Calendar and Gmail are also wired to real UI: settings/CalendarSection.tsx calls trpc.calendar.available/config/updateConfig (toggling calendars and the sync window), and admin/GmailFiltersSection.tsx calls trpc.admin.gmailConfig plus trpc.admin.updateGmailConfig, which writes config/connectors/gmail.json through the connector's own parser. drive.config and drive.available are consumed by settings/DriveSection.tsx; drive.updateConfig (routers/drive.ts:45, writes google-drive.json via saveDriveConfig and commits it) has no caller in the frontend or elsewhere in src — it is still a registered procedure on the mounted appRouter rather than unreferenced dead code, but whether the owner can actually reach Drive folder configuration from the web UI is a reachability question outside my lens. On the exists-and-wired lens the story holds.

Calendar and Gmail are reachable: router.tsx:170/176 route /settings -> SettingsPage (renders CalendarSection, which calls trpc.calendar.updateConfig at CalendarSection.tsx:20) and /admin -> AdminPage (renders GmailFiltersSection, calling trpc.admin.updateGmailConfig at line 78). Drive has no web entry point for the 'set what the box should pull' half: DriveSection.tsx is documented as 'Mounting itself is done via CLI (cb drive add); this view is read-only', calls only trpc.drive.config and trpc.drive.available (lines 10-11), and grep over src/frontend/src finds no caller of drive.updateConfig anywhere; the UI instead instructs the owner to run 'cb drive add'. It also lists available spreadsheets, not folders, so a web-UI owner cannot see or set Drive folders. The story as written overclaims reachability for its Drive third; the Gmail/Calendar portions are fully reachable.

The calendar half holds: CalendarSection.tsx calls trpc.calendar.available/config/updateConfig, and GmailFiltersSection drives admin.gmailConfig/updateGmailConfig. The Drive half does not deliver what the story says. src/frontend/src/components/settings/DriveSection.tsx queries only trpc.drive.config and trpc.drive.available and never calls drive.updateConfig; its own header comment says 'Mounting itself is done via CLI (cb drive add); this view is read-only', and the page text tells the owner to run 'cb drive add <url> <path>'. Also drive.available returns service.listSpreadsheets() (routers/drive.ts), i.e. spreadsheets, not folders — the mounted-folder list comes from config only. So for a web-UI story, 'see which ... Drive folders are available and set what the box should pull' over-claims: Drive is view-only in the web UI and the availability listing is of spreadsheets.

browser.note: Neither half could be exercised. On /settings, Calendar and Drive both fail at 'Google auth not configured'; on /admin the Google Services block renders 'Connect Google Account' plus 'Owner access required', so no Gmail/Calendar/Drive configuration UI (available lists, updateConfig) was reachable with this identity and this box's connector state.

triage.reasoning: Two of the three connectors deliver; Drive has no owner-facing way to set what syncs, from the web UI or anywhere else. Verified in code: `src/frontend/src/components/settings/DriveSection.tsx` calls only `trpc.drive.config` and `trpc.drive.available`, its header says 'this view is read-only', and `grep -rn 'drive.updateConfig' src/frontend/src` returns nothing — the mutation at `src/webapp/trpc/routers/drive.ts:45` has no caller anywhere in the repo. The page tells the owner to run `cb drive add <url> <path>`, but that command mounts a single file (`src/cli/commands/drive.ts:123`); `cb drive` has no folder-mount command at all (inspect/add/sync/status/list), so the `folders` list in `config/connectors/google-drive.json` can only be set by hand-editing JSON. Separately `drive.available` returns `service.listSpreadsheets()`, so the UI lists spreadsheets, not folders — the story's 'see which Drive folders are available' is wrong even about the read half. Calendar (CalendarSection.tsx -> calendar.available/config/updateConfig) and Gmail (GmailFiltersSection.tsx -> admin.gmailConfig/updateGmailConfig) are fully reachable. The browser check was inconclusive because the test box has no Google auth, so this rests on the code. This is a product hole rather than a wording problem — the backend mutation exists and is unreachable, and the project's own position is that the CLI is not a user surface — but it is already filed, so it likely folds into the existing issue rather than becoming a second one.

title: Connect a Google account from the admin page
story: As a box owner, I want to connect my Google account by clicking Connect on the admin page and completing Google's consent screen, so that Gmail, Calendar and Drive can sync with my box.
evidence: `googleSetup` (ownerProcedure in admin-google.ts) mints a one-time nonce via createGoogleOAuthState and returns Google's authUrl with GOOGLE_SCOPES and access_type=offline; `GET /auth/google-services/callback` (registerGoogleServicesCallback in routes/admin.ts) consumes the nonce, exchanges the code, saves tokens, and redirects to `/<slug>/<returnPath>?google=connected`. GoogleServicesSection renders the Connect/Re-authorize button.

verdict.note: admin.googleSetup (ownerProcedure, webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts:49) calls createGoogleOAuthState for a one-time nonce and returns generateAuthUrl({access_type:'offline', scope: GOOGLE_SCOPES}). GOOGLE_SCOPES in connectors/google-auth.ts:22 covers calendar.events, gmail.readonly/compose, drive and spreadsheets, matching the Gmail/Calendar/Drive claim. useGoogleServices.ts:93-94 mutates googleSetup and sets window.location.href = data.authUrl from the Connect/Re-authorize button in GoogleServicesSection.tsx (rendered by frontend/src/pages/AdminPage.tsx:40). registerGoogleServicesCallback (webapp/routes/admin.ts:27, wired in webapp/server.ts:199) handles GET /auth/google-services/callback, exchanges the code, saves tokens and redirects to `/<slug>/<returnPath>?google=connected`.

title: Create, edit and delete calendar events by editing files
story: As my box's agent, I want to drop or edit an .ics file in store/calendar (or mark one X-CB-DELETE), so that the next sync creates, updates or deletes the corresponding Google Calendar event.
evidence: pushAndCleanOrphans inserts untracked .ics files via insertEventViaApi (validating the timezone with validateIcsTimezone and honoring X-CB-CALENDAR-ID), processLocalDeletes deletes events marked X-CB-DELETE (capped at 3 per sync), and tryPushLocalEdit patches hash-detected local edits back to Google.

verdict.note: google-calendar.ts syncs .ics files in calendarDir(boxRoot) = path.join(boxRoot, 'store/calendar') (google-calendar-state.ts:47). In sync(), processLocalDeletes() scans tracked files for /^x-cb-delete[:;]/im and deletes via deleteEventViaApi with a MAX_DELETES=3 per-sync cap (google-calendar-push.ts:119-181), then pushAndCleanOrphans() reads untracked *.ics, parses with icsToGoogleEvent, runs validateIcsTimezone (calendar-utils.ts:332), targets apiEvent._calendarId (from X-CB-CALENDAR-ID, google-calendar-ics.ts:363) or the default calendar, and calls insertEventViaApi (google-calendar-state.ts:158). Local edits are detected by content-hash mismatch and PATCHed back in tryPushLocalEdit (google-calendar-sync.ts:88-126). decideCalendarSync in google-calendar-decide.ts gates all three paths.

title: Disconnect the Google account
story: As a box owner, I want to disconnect Google, so that the stored refresh token is removed and no connector can keep reading my account.
evidence: `googleDisconnect` (ownerProcedure) unlinks the centralized CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE and the legacy per-box config/connectors/google.secret.json; googleStatus then reports hasTokens: false.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts:84 defines `googleDisconnect: ownerProcedure.mutation` which fs.unlink()s the path in process.env.CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE (centralized store) and also the legacy per-box `config/connectors/google.secret.json`, ignoring ENOENT. `googleStatus` (line 20) computes `hasTokens: !!(tokens && tokens.refreshToken)` from loadGoogleTokens, which reads exactly those two locations (src/connectors/google-token-store.ts lines 87/95/110), so after the unlink it reports false. The web entry point exists: GoogleServicesSection.tsx renders a 'Disconnect' Button (line 116) bound to handleDisconnect from useGoogleServices.ts:101, which calls trpcClient.admin.googleDisconnect.mutate() then refetches status.

title: Doc sync still works without the Docs metadata scope
story: As an operator, I want a box whose Google grant predates the documents.readonly scope to keep syncing Docs at reduced fidelity with a message naming the fix, so that an older authorization degrades instead of breaking Drive sync.
evidence: tryGetDocument catches the getDocument failure, logs "If this is a 403, run 'cb google-auth' to grant the documents.readonly scope" and returns null; pull then falls back to the Drive file's name, writes an empty lossy tally, deletes state.extra.headRevisionId, and push falls back to modifiedTime alone for divergence detection.

verdict.note: src/connectors/drive-handler-docs.ts tryGetDocument() (line 166) catches any getDocument error, console.warn's "...If this is a 403, run 'cb google-auth' to grant the documents.readonly scope." and returns null. pull() uses it in place of service.getDocument, so on null it uses emptyLossy() (229), falls back to file.name for the title and "" for revision (299-301), and deletes state.extra.headRevisionId (279). push()'s divergence check (385-390) only compares revisionId when both stored and current values exist, otherwise relying on file.modifiedTime !== state.lastModified. src/connectors/google-auth.ts:38 lists documents.readonly among requested scopes, so a pre-existing grant can indeed lack it — sync degrades rather than breaks.

title: Explore the connected mailbox read-only from the CLI
story: As a box agent, I want to run read-only Gmail commands through the box's own Google authorization, so that I can search and inspect mail while writing a rule without the box being able to send or mutate anything.
evidence: `cb connector gmail gws <args…>` calls runReadOnlyGws, which first runs assertReadOnlyGwsArgs (only `gmail …` commands ending in get/list/getProfile or the `+read`/`+triage` helpers, plus help/schema, pass — anything else throws UnsafeGwsCommandError) and only then mints an access token, passed to the pinned @googleworkspace/cli child as GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_TOKEN.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/connector.ts registers `gmailCommand.command("gws")` (cb connector gmail gws [args...]) which resolves the box's Google auth via getGoogleAuth/createGoogleAuthService and calls runReadOnlyGws. In src/connectors/gmail-gws.ts, runReadOnlyGws calls assertReadOnlyGwsArgs BEFORE auth.getAccessToken(): it allows only bare help, `schema gmail.*`, and `gmail ...` commands whose last non-flag word is in READ_OPERATIONS (get/list/getProfile) or READ_HELPERS (+read/+triage); anything else throws UnsafeGwsCommandError. The token is then passed only in the child env as GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_TOKEN to the pinned @googleworkspace/cli run.js spawned with stdio inherit. Matches the story including the no-send/no-mutate qualifier.

title: Fail loudly when a third-party API changes shape
story: As an operator, I want a Google or Telegram response that no longer matches the fields we consume to raise a named error, so that a shape drift shows up as a failed sync instead of cards full of empty values.
evidence: validateResponse(raw, {schema, service, operation}) safe-parses every real Gmail/Calendar/Drive/Telegram response and throws ConnectorResponseError naming service.operation plus the failing field paths, without echoing the payload.

verdict.note: src/services/connector-response.ts defines ConnectorResponseError (message '<service>.<operation>: response did not match expected shape' plus 'path: message' issue lines only, never the payload) and validateResponse(raw,{schema,service,operation}) which safeParses and throws on failure. Real service implementations call it at every .json<T>() boundary: google-gmail.ts (listMessages/getMessage/getThread/getAttachment/listLabels/getProfile/listHistory/createDraft), google-gmail-threads.ts, google-calendar.ts (listCalendars/listEvents/insertEvent/patchEvent), google-drive.ts (getFile/listFiles/getSpreadsheet/getSheetValues/getDocument/listComments), and telegram.ts getUpdates against telegramUpdatesSchema. Schemas in google-gmail-schemas.ts / telegram-schemas.ts cover only consumed fields and ignore extra keys, so a drift in a consumed field throws instead of yielding undefined. (Some non-ingest Telegram calls like getMe/sendMessage are unvalidated, which does not affect the story's claim about consumed sync responses.)

title: Get the box's timezone block for hand-written events
story: As a box agent, I want the box's VTIMEZONE block on demand and a validation error that names the missing TZID, so that an .ics file I write by hand is accepted by the push instead of being silently rejected.
evidence: `cb calendar vtimezone` prints vtimezoneBlock(loadBoxTimezone(boxRoot) ?? the system zone) — generateVtimezone derives STANDARD/DAYLIGHT components for the IANA zone; the push-side validator rejects a timed event with "Non-all-day event missing TZID on DTSTART. Include a VTIMEZONE component and TZID parameter…", and the box skill points authors at the command.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/calendar.ts:87-94 registers `cb calendar vtimezone`, printing vtimezoneBlock((await loadBoxTimezone(boxRoot)) ?? Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone); calendarCommand is wired into the CLI at src/cli/index.ts:114. vtimezoneBlock/generateVtimezone in src/connectors/google-calendar-ics.ts:120-161 builds the VTIMEZONE component for the IANA zone. On the push side, validateIcsTimezone (src/connectors/calendar-utils.ts:332-347) returns exactly 'Non-all-day event missing TZID on DTSTART. Include a VTIMEZONE component and TZID parameter (e.g., DTSTART;TZID=America/Chicago:20260401T140000).' and is called from google-calendar-push.ts:72. src/core/box/skills-content.ts:278-289 tells authors to run `cb calendar vtimezone` and paste the block.

title: Google authorization state as a health check
story: As a box owner, I want a `google-auth` line in the box's health report saying whether the grant is live and when it was last verified, so that I can see the connection's state without triggering a sync.
evidence: googleAuthHealthChecks reads readGoogleAuthStatus and emits either a failing check ("Google authorization expired or was revoked … Reconnect at …") or an ok check with `last verified <duration> ago`, and emits nothing when Google was never configured or connected.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/trpc/routers/health-google.ts defines googleAuthHealthChecks(boxRoot,{now}) which calls readGoogleAuthStatus from src/connectors/google-auth-status.ts and returns [] when !configured || !connected, a failing check ('Google authorization expired or was revoked … — Gmail, Calendar and Drive sync are paused. Reconnect at /<slug>/admin?reconnect=google') when needsReauthSince is set, and otherwise an ok check 'Google authorization is live (last verified <dur> ago)' (or 'not verified yet'). It is named 'google-auth' and is wired into the report: src/webapp/trpc/routers/health.ts:328 pushes its results into runHealthChecks, which cb health (src/cli/commands/health.ts:29) and the healthRouter both consume. It is a pure reader of the token record (authCheckedAt stamped by src/connectors/google-token-store.ts, refreshed by the ~daily probeGoogleAuthIfStale), so no sync is triggered.

title: Import matching mail as thread and message cards
story: As a box owner, I want mail matching a `track` rule to appear in the box as email-thread cards with each message, body and attachment on disk, so that my agent can read and act on the actual mail.
evidence: GmailConnector.sync() discovers changes incrementally through discoverGmailChanges (Gmail history cursor), evaluates rules, then writeThreadCards writes `<subject>.email-thread.card` under box/inbox/email with msg-NNN.email-message.card, body text and attachment files, committed with a narrative message.

verdict.note: GmailConnector.syncWorkingSet (src/connectors/gmail.ts ~L188-235) calls discoverGmailChanges (history cursor), evaluateGmailRules (gmail-rules.ts, which builds trackRequests only for rules whose action.type === 'track', budget-gated by remainingAutomaticTrackingBudget), then refreshThreadSnapshots/writeThreadCards. gmail-threads.ts cardLocation writes new cards to box/inbox/email/<safe subject>.email-thread.card, and writeMessage writes msg-NNN.email-message.card, msg-NNN.body.txt and attachments/<filename> under the card's .attach dir. commitInbound stages the written paths with buildGmailCommitMessage (gmail-commit.ts), which produces a narrative 'Pull N Gmail threads' subject plus New/Updated thread lists. Story matches.

title: Incremental Gmail sync from a history checkpoint
story: As a boxholder, I want the Gmail connector to pull only what changed since its last checkpoint, so that repeat syncs are cheap and nothing already-ingested is re-processed.
evidence: getProfile() returns the mailbox historyId checkpoint and listHistory({startHistoryId}) requests historyTypes=messageAdded/labelAdded from users/me/history; a 404 (expired checkpoint) is converted to NotFoundError so the caller re-establishes a checkpoint instead of listing all mail.

verdict.note: src/services/google-gmail.ts defines getProfile() (validated by gmailProfileSchema in google-gmail-schemas.ts, which carries historyId) and listHistory({startHistoryId,pageToken,maxResults}) that sends historyTypes=messageAdded and historyTypes=labelAdded to users/me/history, and converts an HTTPError 404 into NotFoundError(startHistoryId, 'History'). The reachable caller is discoverGmailChanges in src/connectors/gmail-discovery.ts: with no checkpoint it calls getProfile() and returns zero refs (establishing the checkpoint); with one it pages listHistory and dedupes refs; on NotFoundError it re-establishes from getProfile() and flags historyExpired instead of listing all mail. That is exactly the incremental-since-checkpoint behavior claimed.

title: Keep Google access alive and notice a dead grant
story: As a boxholder, I want every Google call to refresh my OAuth token automatically and to be told plainly when the grant has died, so that connectors keep working and a revoked login surfaces as a reconnect prompt instead of silent failures.
evidence: createGoogleAuthService(client, {boxRoot}) wraps OAuth2Client.getAccessToken() as the single token chokepoint for gmail/drive/calendar, running classifyRefreshFailure() on a refresh error so an invalid_grant is recorded against the token file and rethrown as a typed expiry.

verdict.note: src/services/google-auth.ts createGoogleAuthService(client, {boxRoot}) returns a GoogleAuthService whose getAccessToken() calls OAuth2Client.getAccessToken() (lazy refresh) and, on throw, awaits classifyRefreshFailure(e, {boxRoot}) and rethrows the typed GoogleAuthExpiredError when it is an invalid_grant, else rethrows the original. It is the token source for gmail.ts:164, google-calendar.ts:89, google-drive.ts:100 plus the drive/calendar tRPC routers and CLI commands. classifyRefreshFailure in src/connectors/google-auth-status.ts calls markGoogleAuthDead(), persisting needsReauthSince/reauthReason into the token file, which readGoogleAuthStatus() exposes for the health/reconnect surface (webapp/trpc/routers/admin-google.ts, test/webapp/health-google.doctest.md); probeGoogleAuthIfStale() re-checks daily so an idle box still learns the grant died.

title: Label an existing email in Gmail to pull it into the box
story: As a boxholder, I want applying a Gmail label to mail I already received to make it match a rule and come into the box, so that labelling is a manual send-this-to-my-box gesture and not just a filter on brand-new arrivals.
evidence: refsForPage in discoverGmailChanges collects message refs from BOTH record.messagesAdded and record.labelsAdded, so a message that only gained a label since the last history checkpoint becomes a candidate; evaluateGmailRules then re-queries it with `(<rule query>) rfc822msgid:<id>` and acts on the match, and the config shorthand's `labels: [...]` expands to `label:X OR label:Y`.

verdict.note: refsForPage in callback-box/src/connectors/gmail-discovery.ts (lines 22-31) collects refs from both record.messagesAdded and record.labelsAdded, and discoverGmailChanges' doc comment says 'messages added or newly labelled since the prior checkpoint' — so a previously received message that only gained a label is a candidate. matchesRule in gmail-rules.ts re-queries each candidate with q: `(${rule.query}) rfc822msgid:${messageId}` and, on a match, produces trackRequests/procedure triggers; no recency filter (no newer_than/internalDate cutoff) restricts candidates to new arrivals. gmail-config.ts shorthandQuery maps labels: [...] to `label:X OR label:Y`.

title: Mail attachments land in the box as files beside the message
story: As a box agent, I want a tracked thread's attachments downloaded into an attachments/ directory next to each message and listed on the message card, so that I can read and reuse what was mailed in without going back to Gmail.
evidence: `extractAttachmentRefs` + `service.getAttachment` fetch each part's bytes in gmail-mime.ts, with `safeAttachmentFilename` forcing a whitelisted extension (anything else becomes .bin); gmail-threads.ts writes them under `<message>.attach/attachments/` and emits `attachments:` refs with contentType and size on the message card.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/connectors/gmail-mime.ts has extractAttachmentRefs(payload) (line 183) using safeAttachmentFilename (line 82), which forces a whitelisted extension from CONTENT_TYPE_EXTENSIONS and otherwise appends .bin (lines 47, 92, 96); the fetch loop at line 231 calls service.getAttachment(raw.id, ref.attachmentId) and decodes base64url bytes. gmail-threads.ts writes each message card into the thread's attach dir and, when attachments exist, mkdirs `<basename>.attach/attachments/` and writes each file there (lines 124-140), while the card front matter emits `attachments:` entries with ref `attachments/<filename>`, contentType and size (lines 102-108). Reachable from gmail-track.ts and gmail.ts, which both import writeThreadCards.

title: Mail rules act on new mail, not the archive
story: As a box owner, I want a newly saved Gmail rule to start from the moment I save it and to catch up in bounded chunks, so that turning on a filter never dumps years of old mail into the box.
evidence: discoverGmailChanges returns no refs on the first call — it only records the profile's historyId as the checkpoint — then pages the history API with GMAIL_HISTORY_RECORD_LIMIT and stores a `historyResume` (startHistoryId/pageToken/refOffset) once GMAIL_HISTORY_REF_LIMIT refs are reached; when Gmail reports the cursor gone, `historyExpired` makes syncWorkingSet call resetRuleBaselines and warn "history cursor expired; rule counts were refreshed without importing mail".

verdict.note: discoverGmailChanges in src/connectors/gmail-discovery.ts returns refs: [] and just the profile historyId when startHistoryId is undefined (first call establishes a checkpoint); subsequent calls page listHistory with maxResults GMAIL_HISTORY_RECORD_LIMIT=100 and slice at GMAIL_HISTORY_REF_LIMIT=500, returning a historyResume {startHistoryId, pageToken, refOffset} when more remains. On NotFoundError it re-reads the profile and sets historyExpired: true; src/connectors/gmail.ts line 200-202 then calls resetRuleBaselines(work.state) and warns 'Gmail: history cursor expired; rule counts were refreshed without importing mail'. Per-rule newness is real too: evaluateGmailRules (gmail-rules.ts:195) skips any rule whose baselineAt is undefined for that sync, calling establishBaseline (listThreads maxResults 1, records baselineAt=now and baselineMatches) so a newly saved rule never fires on the existing archive; baselineAt is persisted in gmail-state.ts.

title: Mount a Drive sheet or doc as a card
story: As a box agent, I want to attach a Google Sheet or Doc to the box by URL (or mount a whole Drive folder), so that its contents live in the box as files a card points at.
evidence: `cb drive inspect|add <url-or-id> <path>|sync|status|list` drives the connector, whose two sources are cards carrying a `drive-id` (readDriveIdFromCard) and folder mounts from `config/connectors/google-drive.json`; the sheets handler exports each tab as JSON into the card's attach dir.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/drive.ts registers `cb drive` with subcommands inspect/add <url-or-id> <path>/sync/status/list, and driveCommand is wired into cli/index.ts (line 115). `add` resolves the file id, picks a handler by MIME type, creates `<path>.<cardType>.card`, and delegates to handler.pull() writing into attachDirFor(cardPath). drive-handler-sheets.ts exports one JSON file per tab into that attach dir and records `attach/<file>.json` refs on the card. google-drive.ts documents and implements the two sources: per-card `drive-id` via readDriveIdFromCard (line 54) and folder mounts read from config/connectors/google-drive.json via drive-config.ts (folders?: DriveFolderMount[]), auto-creating cards for new files in a mounted folder.

title: Move a synced Gmail thread or Drive mount anywhere in the box
story: As my box's agent, I want to file a tracked email-thread card or a mounted Drive card into whatever folder it belongs in, so that connector-managed content can be organized with the rest of the box and still keep syncing at its new location.
evidence: findTrackedGmailThreads globs `**/*.email-thread.card` across the whole box (ignoring .git/tmp/trash) and indexes by thread-id, and cardLocation writes refreshes to `tracked.absPath` rather than back to box/inbox/email; GoogleDriveConnector.sync likewise globs `**/*.<cardType>.card` for every handler and syncs whatever path the card sits at.

verdict.note: connectors/gmail-tracking.ts globs TRACKED_THREAD_GLOB = '**/*.email-thread.card' from boxRoot (ignoring node_modules/.git/tmp/.callback-box/procedure/runs) and indexes each card by its thread-id in findTrackedGmailThreads. connectors/gmail-threads.ts cardLocation() returns opts.tracked.absPath (and attachDirFor(absPath)) when a tracked card exists, falling back to box/inbox/email only for brand-new threads, so a moved card is refreshed in place. connectors/google-drive.ts sync() builds patterns `**/*.${h.cardType}.card` for every registered drive handler, globs them box-wide, and syncs each by the driveId read from the card at whatever path it sits.

title: Pick which calendars sync and how far
story: As a box owner, I want to see my Google calendars, toggle which ones sync, and set how many days back and forward, so that only the calendar data I care about lands in the box.
evidence: `calendar.available` lists calendars via fetchAvailableCalendars and marks each `syncing`; `calendar.updateConfig` saves calendars/syncDaysBack/syncDaysForward to `config/connectors/google-calendar.json` and commits it. `cb calendar calendars|add|remove` is the CLI counterpart.

verdict.note: src/webapp/trpc/routers/calendar.ts exposes calendar.available (fetchAvailableCalendars + per-calendar `syncing` computed from loadCalendarConfig), calendar.config, and calendar.updateConfig which accepts calendars/syncDaysBack/syncDaysForward, calls saveCalendarConfig, and commits config/connectors/google-calendar.json (path confirmed at src/connectors/calendar-config.ts:33). The web UI is CalendarSection.tsx (rendered by SettingsPage.tsx): it queries calendar.available, renders a per-calendar checkbox wired to toggleCalendar, and has days-back/days-forward inputs that saveSyncWindow on blur. CLI counterpart exists too: src/cli/commands/calendar.ts defines `calendars`, `add`, and `remove` subcommands.

browser.note: The 'Google Calendar' section renders, but this box has no Google auth, so it briefly shows 'Loading calendars...' and settles on the error 'Google auth not configured. Run: cb google-auth'. No calendar list, sync toggles, or days-back/days-forward inputs could be reached.

title: Preview a Drive file before mounting it, and audit the mounts after
story: As a box agent, I want to inspect a Drive URL for its tabs, comment count and content markdown export would drop before mounting it, and later list every mount with its title, last sync and conflict status, so that I know what a mount will cost and which mounts have gone wrong.
evidence: `cb drive inspect <url-or-id>` calls `service.getFile` plus the mime handler's `inspect()` and prints tabs, a "Lossy content (will not survive markdown push)" tally, comment count, revision id and the card type it would create — without writing anything; `cb drive status` globs every handler's `*.<cardType>.card` and prints title, drive id, last-synced time, non-`synced` status and lossy summary.

verdict.note: cli/commands/drive.ts registers `inspect <url-or-id>` (added to the program via cli/commands/index.ts -> cli/index.ts:115 program.addCommand(driveCommand)). Its action calls service.getFile, getHandlerForMimeType, then handler.inspect(file, service) and prints title/type/id/modified/owner/link, 'Sheet tabs (n)', 'Lossy content (will not survive markdown push)' tallies, 'Comments: n', 'Revision: ...' and 'Card type: <handler.cardType>' — it writes nothing. drive-handler-docs.ts inspect() (line 187) returns details {revisionId, lossy: tallyLossyFromDocument(doc), comments: comments.length}. `cb drive status` globs `**/*.<cardType>.card` for every registered handler and prints path, title, drive id, last-synced (modified), status when not 'synced' (drive-handler-docs.ts sets status="conflict" on a remote-file conflict, line 307) and a lossy summary.

title: Read a synced sheet and its comments in the browser
story: As a box owner, I want a synced spreadsheet card to open as a tabbed table with a link back to the Drive original and its comment threads readable beneath it, so that I can consult synced Drive content in the box instead of switching to Google.
evidence: The gsheet renderer parses the card's `sheets` frontmatter into TabBar tabs, loads each tab's JSON attachment into SheetTable, shows the ExternalLink to the Drive file, and mounts AttachedComments; the comments renderer is registered above the generic `.json` file type so a `<basename>.comments.json` sidecar renders through parseComments/CommentsThread with a toggle back to raw JSON.

AttachedComments.tsx reads `comments.ref` frontmatter, loads the sidecar and shows it in an Accordion via parseComments/CommentsThread. The sync side is real: src/connectors/drive-handler-sheets.ts writes per-tab JSON plus reconcileCommentsSidecar and createGsheetTemplate (schemas/gsheet.tsx sets comments: {ref: attach/<basename>.comments.json}); renderers/comments.tsx matches *.comments.json at priority 50, above json.tsx's 40.

title: Read box history to see what each sync changed
story: As a box owner, I want every connector sync committed with a written summary of the threads pulled or the events added, changed and cancelled, plus which connector and trigger produced it, so that the box's git history explains external changes instead of showing opaque file churn.
evidence: buildGmailCommitMessage renders "Pull N Gmail threads (M files)" plus capped new/updated thread lines; buildNarrativeCommitMessage turns the calendar's SyncNotes (from describeChanges' field-level diffs) into the commit body, falling back to "Sync calendar: no changes (token refreshed)"; both go through stageAndCommitPaths with `Pulled-By`/`Triggered-By` trailers on an explicit changed-file list.

verdict.note: The Gmail/Calendar half checks out: gmail-commit.ts buildGmailCommitMessage builds 'Pull N Gmail thread(s) (M files)' with capped New:/Updated: lines, used by gmail.ts commitInbound (line 178) with Pulled-By: gmail-connector plus optional Triggered-By; google-calendar-notes.ts buildNarrativeCommitMessage counts new/updated/deleted/pushed/cancelled SyncNotes (details from describeChanges' ICS field diffs) and google-calendar.ts line 225-231 commits an explicit changed-file list with the same trailers, falling back to 'Sync calendar: no changes (token refreshed)'. But the story's literal qualifier 'every connector sync ... plus which connector and trigger produced it' overclaims: src/connectors/google-drive.ts line 211-214 commits its sync as `Sync Google Drive: ${parts.join(', ')}` with NO trailers object at all, so neither the connector nor the trigger appears in that commit; telegram-webhook.ts line 70-74 sets only Pulled-By and no Triggered-By. The mechanism is per-connector, not universal.

panel.note: All cited code is live and connected. gmail-commit.ts exports buildGmailCommitMessage (subject 'Pull N Gmail thread(s) (M files)' plus capped New:/Updated: lines), imported by gmail.ts:15 and used in commitInbound (gmail.ts:178-184) inside stageAndCommitPaths with Pulled-By: gmail-connector and conditional Triggered-By. google-calendar-notes.ts exports describeChanges and buildNarrativeCommitMessage, imported by google-calendar.ts:42-43 and used at line 225 to build the message, falling back to 'Sync calendar: no changes (token refreshed)', committed at lines 227-231 over an explicit changed-file list with the same trailer pair. stageAndCommitPaths in src/lib/git.ts really renders the trailers object into the commit body (git.ts:378-381). The connectors are reachable from the CLI: cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts constructs both (lines 37-38), sets connector.triggeredBy = 'cb wakeup' (line 69), and is imported by cli/commands/wakeup.ts; finalize.ts imports them too. The earlier verdict's objection was about universality across other connectors (google-drive, telegram), which is a scope/wording question, not a code-existence one; my lens is satisfied.

The sync path that writes these commits has real, unflagged entry points: `cb wakeup` is registered in src/cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(wakeupCommand)) and runs src/cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts, which sets connector.triggeredBy = "cb wakeup" and calls connector.sync() for every registered connector (Gmail/Calendar register via registerConnector in gmail.ts:299 and google-calendar.ts:296). Additional entry points hit the same code: the registered core command `connector-sync` (src/core/commands/connector-sync.ts registerCommand), `cb drive sync` (cli/commands/drive.ts:202) and `cb finalize` (finalize.ts:82), plus programmatic spawns of wakeup (core/reactor/subprocess.ts:46 runCbSubcommand "wakeup", core/scan/promote.ts spawnCbWakeup). The sync then commits through stageAndCommitPaths with Pulled-By/Triggered-By trailers (gmail.ts:178-183, google-calendar.ts:227), and the output lands in the box's own git history, which the box owner reads directly. Nothing here is behind a default-off flag or unset config beyond the connector's own credentials, so my lens is satisfied; the scope question the earlier verifier raised (google-drive.ts omitting trailers) is an accuracy issue, not a reachability one.

The Gmail and Calendar halves deliver as written: gmail.ts commitInbound (line 178) commits with buildGmailCommitMessage's thread summary plus Pulled-By: gmail-connector and an optional Triggered-By, and google-calendar.ts line 227 commits buildNarrativeCommitMessage's added/changed/cancelled narrative (or 'Sync calendar: no changes (token refreshed)') with the same trailers. But the story's literal scope is 'every connector sync ... plus which connector and trigger produced it', and google-drive.ts lines 208-214 commits `Sync Google Drive: N new, N updated, N pushed` with NO trailers object at all, so neither the connector nor the trigger is recorded for a Drive sync; telegram-webhook.ts line 70-74 sets Pulled-By only, never Triggered-By. Even the Gmail/Calendar path attaches Triggered-By only when this.triggeredBy is set, so the 'which trigger produced it' half is conditional rather than guaranteed. The code delivers a per-connector convention, narrower than the universal claim.

triage.reasoning: The described behavior is real for the connectors the story actually describes; the word 'every' is the part that is wrong, and it is a catalog fix rather than product work. Confirmed: `gmail-commit.ts` `buildGmailCommitMessage` renders 'Pull N Gmail thread(s) (M files)' with capped New:/Updated: lines and `gmail.ts:178` commits it with `Pulled-By: gmail-connector` plus a conditional `Triggered-By`; `google-calendar-notes.ts` `buildNarrativeCommitMessage` turns `describeChanges`' field-level SyncNotes into the body, `google-calendar.ts:225-231` commits an explicit changed-file list with the same trailers and falls back to 'Sync calendar: no changes (token refreshed)'; `src/lib/git.ts:378-381` really renders trailers. The exception is Drive: `src/connectors/google-drive.ts:211-214` commits `Sync Google Drive: N new, N updated, N pushed` with no `trailers` object, even though the class declares `triggeredBy` (line 82); `telegram-webhook.ts:70-74` sets `Pulled-By` only. So every connector sync does get a written summary — the benefit clause ('git history explains external changes instead of opaque file churn') holds across the board — but the connector/trigger attribution is a per-connector convention, not universal. I am not calling the missing Drive trailers a gap: the commit subject already names the connector, so the reader-facing consequence is close to nil; it is a one-line consistency wart worth mentioning to the maintainer, not a user-noticeable break. The catalog entry should be narrowed to Gmail and Calendar.

title: Read Drive comment threads on a synced doc
story: As a person reviewing a synced Google doc or sheet, I want its collaborative comments shown as a readable thread with authors, dates, quoted spans and replies, so that I can see the feedback alongside the document.
evidence: AttachedComments reads the card's comments: { ref }, loads the <basename>.comments.json sidecar and renders CommentsThread inside a "Comments (N)" Accordion; renderers/comments.tsx registers the same thread view above the generic .json renderer for any *.comments.json path.

AttachedComments.tsx reads frontmatter comments.ref, resolves it relative to the card, fetches /files/<path>, and renders CommentsThread inside an Accordion titled 'Comments (N)'; it is mounted by renderers/gsheet.tsx (line 140) and components/MarkdownCardView.tsx (line 231), i.e. synced sheets and gdoc markdown cards. renderers/comments.tsx registers a 'Comments' renderer at priority 50 for any path ending .comments.json and is imported by renderers/setup.ts. The sidecar itself is written by src/connectors/drive-comments-sidecar.ts from the Drive comments API, so the data source exists.

title: Read Drive comments alongside the document
story: As my box's agent, I want a synced Doc or Sheet's comment threads written next to the content, so that the discussion on a shared document is part of what I can read.
evidence: reconcileCommentsSidecar writes `<basename>.comments.json` (content, author, timestamps, resolved state, anchors, replies) from service.listComments on every pull and deletes it when comments drop to zero; both handlers call it and reference it from the card's comments field.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/connectors/drive-comments-sidecar.ts's reconcileCommentsSidecar writes `<basename>.comments.json` into the card's attach scope when comments exist and unlinks it (staging the deletion) when they drop to zero. Both drive-handler-docs.ts (line ~264) and drive-handler-sheets.ts (line ~163) call it with `service.listComments(file.id)` fetched on every pull, and pass `commentsFile` into createGdocTemplate/gsheet template, which the gdoc schema (src/schemas/gdoc.tsx) exposes as the optional `comments: {ref}` field with agent instructions to read it. services/google-drive.ts listComments requests content, author, resolved, createdTime/modifiedTime, quotedFileContent (the anchor) and replies, matching the story's claims.

title: Read Gmail mail, threads, labels and attachments

It is reachable: src/connectors/gmail.ts:164 constructs the service from createGoogleAuthService, gmail-rules.ts:52 calls listThreads({q: rule.query}), gmail-mime.ts:234 calls getAttachment, gmail-track.ts:49 calls listLabels. Matches the story as written.

title: Read the agenda from the box's own copy
story: As a box agent, I want to print upcoming events for today, a few days, or weeks straight from the synced .ics files, so that answering "what's on my calendar" needs no network call and works when Google is unreachable.
