title: Recover when the Gmail history cursor has expired
story: As a boxholder, I want a Gmail sync whose checkpoint has aged out of Google's history window to re-baseline instead of re-importing, so that a box that has been off for a while does not flood itself with mail it already saw or silently miss the gap.
evidence: `listHistory` throws `NotFoundError` for a too-old `startHistoryId`; `discoverGmailChanges` catches it, re-reads `getProfile().historyId` and returns `historyExpired: true` with no refs, and `GmailConnector.syncWorkingSet` then calls `resetRuleBaselines` and warns "history cursor expired; rule counts were refreshed without importing mail". The fake's `oldestValidHistoryId` reproduces the condition.

verdict.note: google-gmail.ts listHistory catches a 404 from Gmail and rethrows `new NotFoundError(opts.startHistoryId, "History")` (line ~195). gmail-discovery.ts discoverGmailChanges wraps the paging loop in try/catch: `if (!(error instanceof NotFoundError)) throw error;` then re-reads `opts.service.getProfile()` and returns `{ refs: [], historyId: profile.historyId, historyResume: undefined, historyExpired: true }` — no refs, so no re-import. GmailConnector.syncWorkingSet (connectors/gmail.ts ~200) does `const state = changes.historyExpired ? resetRuleBaselines(work.state) : work.state;` plus console.warn("Gmail: history cursor expired; rule counts were refreshed without importing mail"), and persistState writes the fresh changes.historyId, re-baselining the cursor. google-gmail-fake.ts has `oldestValidHistoryId` and throws NotFoundError when start < that value.

title: Resolve a Google Doc conflict and resume syncing
story: As my box's agent, I want a conflicted Doc to stop pushing until I merge the upstream copy and delete the .remote.md file, so that resolving the conflict is an explicit act and the card returns to synced only once I have done it.
evidence: docsHandler.push returns early with "Skipping push … unresolved conflict (<basename>.remote.md exists)" whenever the conflict file is present, and pull sets the card's status to `conflict` or `synced` purely from an fs.access check on `<basename>.remote.md` — so deleting that file is what unblocks the push and clears the status.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/connectors/drive-handler-docs.ts: in the push path (~line 363-373) an fs.access on `${cardBasename}.remote.md` in the local attach dir causes an early return logging `[google-drive] Skipping push for <name>: unresolved conflict (<basename>.remote.md exists)`. On divergence the handler writes the upstream body to `<basename>.remote.md` (~line 398). The pull path (~lines 282-307) re-checks the same file and sets `status: hasRemoteFile ? "conflict" : "synced"`, so deleting the file is exactly what unblocks push and clears the status. Story matches.

title: Run outbound connectors
story: As an agent, I want `cb finalize` to run the outbound connectors as a post-processing phase, so that work the box produced actually leaves the box.

It is registered on the CLI at src/cli/index.ts:125 (program.addCommand(finalizeCommand)), so the command is reachable. The header comment confirms the reactor invokes it after job cycles complete.

title: Say why a calendar event was created or deleted
story: As an agent, I want to add X-CB-REASON and X-CB-REF lines to an .ics file, so that the sync commit records why the event exists and which card prompted it while Google never sees the annotation.
evidence: `pushAndCleanOrphans` calls `extractCbAnnotations` to pull `reason`/`ref` out of the .ics, pushes the stripped content and rewrites the local file without the annotations, then attaches them as the SyncNote's `detail`/`ref`; `processLocalDeletes` reads the reason off `X-CB-DELETE` the same way, and `buildNarrativeCommitMessage` renders both into the commit body.

verdict.note: google-calendar-notes.ts exports extractCbAnnotations, which matches ^x-cb-reason and ^x-cb-ref case-insensitively and returns the values plus content with those lines stripped. google-calendar-push.ts pushAndCleanOrphans calls it before insertEventViaApi, rewrites the local .ics with the stripped content on success, and attaches reason/ref as the SyncNote detail/ref; processLocalDeletes reads X-CB-DELETE's reason and an optional X-CB-REF the same way for the delete note. buildNarrativeCommitMessage (notes.ts) renders each note as '- summary — detail [ref: ref]' in the commit body, and google-calendar.ts:225 uses it for the sync commit. Only the mapped fields of icsToGoogleEvent reach the Google API, so the X-CB-* lines are never sent.

title: See what Drive is mounted and what else is available
story: As a box owner, I want the settings page to list the box's Drive folder mounts and the spreadsheets in my Drive with the command to mount one, so that I can see what is synced without running anything.
evidence: DriveSection renders `drive.config`'s folder mounts and `drive.available`'s files (name + modified date, capped in a scrolling list) with `cb drive add <url> <path>` shown as the mount instruction, and "No spreadsheets found in your Drive." when the list is empty; the drive router's `available` throws FORBIDDEN when Drive isn't in the box's googleServices.

title: See why a Google connection attempt failed
story: As a box owner, I want a failed Google authorization to land me back on the admin page with the reason shown, so that I can tell a declined consent from a missing OAuth app instead of just seeing an unchanged Connect button.
evidence: The `/auth/google-services/callback` handler redirects to `${returnUrl}?google=error&message=…` for no-code, "OAuth not configured", and a thrown exchange error, and to `?google=connected` on success; useGoogleServices' mount effect reads the `google` param, sets either successMessage or the `message` text as `error`, and strips the query with history.replaceState.

verdict.note: src/webapp/routes/admin.ts registerGoogleServicesCallback handles GET /auth/google-services/callback and, after nonce validation, redirects to `${returnUrl}?google=error&message=No+code+received` (declined consent yields no code), `?google=error&message=OAuth+not+configured` when getGoogleClientCreds returns null, `?google=error&message=<encoded exchange error>` on a getToken throw, and `?google=connected` on success. returnUrl is `/${boxSlug}/${consumed.returnPath}` with returnPath defaulting to "admin" in admin-google.ts googleSetup, so it lands on the admin page. useGoogleServices.ts has a mount effect reading the `google` param that sets successMessage or setError(params.get("message") || "Authorization failed") and calls window.history.replaceState; GoogleServicesSection.tsx line 135 renders that error.

browser.note: Half-verified. Loading /admin?google=connected rendered 'Google services connected successfully.' inside the Google Services card and history.replaceState stripped the query (location.href came back as the bare /admin), so the callback-return-and-report mechanism works. Loading /admin?google=error&message=OAuth+not+configured stripped the query but showed 'Owner access required' rather than 'OAuth not configured' — useGoogleServices' fetchStatus writes the googleStatus failure into the same `error` state right after the mount effect sets it, and googleStatus is owner-gated for this session. For a real owner googleStatus would succeed and not overwrite, so this is a masking artifact of the non-owner session, not a demonstrated defect.

title: Stop syncing something by trashing its card

title: Track one Gmail thread on demand
story: As my box's agent, I want to promote a single Gmail thread by its thread id, so that a specific conversation becomes a synchronized card without widening any rule.
evidence: `cb connector gmail track <thread-id>` calls trackGmailThread, which fetches the whole thread under the gmail-track file lock, writes the thread/message cards, commits with a Tracked-By trailer, and prints the card path.

No rule/config is touched, so no rule is widened.

title: Turn an agent-written reply into a Gmail draft
story: As a box owner, I want a draft my agent wrote as an email-outbound card to be uploaded to Gmail as a real draft in the right thread, so that I can review and send it from Gmail myself.
evidence: uploadPendingDrafts scans box/inbox/email for unstamped *.email-outbound.card, builds RFC 2822 MIME with In-Reply-To/References resolved from the referenced email-message card, calls service.createDraft, and stamps gmail-draft-id/gmail-draft-url back onto the card; sync() commits the stamped cards.

verdict.note: src/connectors/gmail-drafts.ts `uploadPendingDrafts` walks box/inbox/email/<thread>/ for *.email-outbound.card with status draft and no `gmail-draft-id`, resolves `in-reply-to.ref` to the referenced email-message card via `resolveCardRef`/`readSourceMessage` (message-id + thread-id), builds RFC 2822 MIME in `buildMime` with In-Reply-To/References, and calls `service.createDraft({raw, threadId})`. src/services/google-gmail.ts `createDraft` POSTs users/me/drafts with `{message:{raw,threadId}}`. `stampDraftCard` writes gmail-draft-id and a https://mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#drafts/<id> URL back into the frontmatter, and GmailConnector.uploadDrafts (gmail.ts:247, called from syncUnderLock inside sync()) commits the stamped paths via stageAndCommitPaths.

title: Turn Gmail, Calendar and Drive on or off per box
story: As a box owner, I want to enable only the Google services this box should use, so that a shared Google grant does not give every box access to my mail, calendar and files.
evidence: `handleServiceToggle` writes the box's googleServices policy through admin.updateBoxConfig; each connector's sync() gates on isGoogleServiceAllowed(boxRoot, "gmail"|"calendar"|"drive") and returns a no-op result when the service is off.

verdict.note: useGoogleServices.ts `handleServiceToggle` merges {service: enabled} into status.enabledServices and calls trpcClient.admin.updateBoxConfig.mutate({ googleServices: updated }); admin.ts's updateBoxConfig accepts googleServices (googleServicesSchema) and persists it via webapp/box-config-write.ts into config/box.json. core/box/config.ts exposes isGoogleServiceAllowed(boxRoot, service) returning config.googleServices?.[service] === true (default false). Gmail's sync() (connectors/gmail.ts:270) returns { success: true, created: [], updated: [] } when resolveService() hits the !isGoogleServiceAllowed(boxRoot,'gmail') branch; google-calendar.ts:120 and google-drive.ts:107 return the same empty success result when their service is off. The UI entry point is real: GoogleServicesSection.tsx renders a CheckboxField per GOOGLE_SERVICE_LABELS wired to handleServiceToggle, and AdminPage.tsx renders <GoogleServicesSection />.

browser.note: The Google Services section renders with a 'Server-wide' badge, the copy 'Google account connection is shared across all boxes. Enable specific services per box below.', and a single 'Connect Google Account' button plus 'Owner access required'. No Gmail/Calendar/Drive per-box toggles are shown — no Google account is connected on this box (config/connectors does not exist) and googleStatus is owner-gated, so the toggles could not be exercised.

title: Two cards claiming the same mail thread stop the sync by name
story: As my box's agent, I want the Gmail sync to fail naming both card paths when two live email-thread cards carry the same thread-id, so that a duplicated thread card is fixed rather than left with two copies quietly diverging as snapshots are rewritten.
evidence: findTrackedGmailThreads globs every `*.email-thread.card` (ignoring .git, tmp, procedure/runs and store/trash), indexes by `thread-id`, and throws DuplicateTrackedGmailThreadError(threadId, [existing.relPath, relPath]) on a second claim; it is called at the top of GmailConnector.syncWorkingSet and by trackGmailThread, so the whole sync surfaces the error instead of picking one card.

verdict.note: gmail-tracking.ts findTrackedGmailThreads globs '**/*.email-thread.card' with ignores node_modules, .git, tmp, .callback-box, procedure/runs, store/trash; it parses each card, reads fields['thread-id'], and on a second occurrence throws DuplicateTrackedGmailThreadError(threadId, [existing.relPath, relPath]) whose message names both card paths. It is awaited at the top of GmailConnector.syncWorkingSet (gmail.ts:194, before discoverGmailChanges) and in gmail-track.ts:86 within the track flow (also gmail-threads.ts:262), so the duplicate aborts the sync rather than one card being chosen.

title: Two-way sync a Google Doc as markdown, with conflict and lossy warnings
story: As my box's agent, I want a Doc exported as markdown that I can edit and push back, with a refusal when the doc changed upstream and a count of content markdown would drop, so that I do not silently destroy the original.
evidence: The docs handler exports the body to `<basename>.attach/<basename>.md`, stores headRevisionId/modifiedTime, and on push re-reads remote state — on divergence it sets the card status="conflict" and writes `<basename>.remote.md`; tallyLossyFromDocument counts footnotes, inline objects, equations, suggestions and tables into the card's lossy block.

verdict.note: src/connectors/drive-handler-docs.ts registers a `gdoc` DriveTypeHandler (imported for side effect by src/connectors/google-drive.ts line 39). pull() exports the doc via service.exportFile(file.id, MARKDOWN_MIME) into `<basename>.md` inside the attach dir, stores state.lastModified = file.modifiedTime and state.extra.headRevisionId = doc.revisionId, and sets card status "conflict" when `<basename>.remote.md` exists. push() refuses when the stored revision/modifiedTime diverges from upstream, writing the upstream body to `<basename>.remote.md`, and skips entirely while an unresolved `.remote.md` remains. tallyLossyFromDocument() counts inlineObjects as images plus footnotes, equations, suggestion ids, and complex tables, and lossyToTemplateItems() puts them in the card via createGdocTemplate.

title: Two-way sync a spreadsheet as per-tab JSON
story: As my box's agent, I want each Sheet tab kept as a JSON file with formulas and computed values, and my local edits pushed back, so that I can read and change a spreadsheet as ordinary files.
evidence: The sheets handler pulls FORMULA and FORMATTED_VALUE renderings into `<tab>.json` (buildSheetData/serializeSheetData, one row per line), tracks contentHashes per file, and pushes back tabs whose local hash diverged; the connector globs *.gsheet.card to find mounts.

verdict.note: src/connectors/drive-handler-sheets.ts registers a DriveTypeHandler for mimeType application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet (cardType 'gsheet'). Its pull() fetches each tab twice via service.getSheetValues with valueRenderOption FORMULA and FORMATTED_VALUE, merges them with buildSheetData (formula cells become {f,v}) and writes serializeSheetData output (one JSON row per line) to <safeTabName>.json in the card's attach dir, storing contentHashes per file. push() re-reads each .json, compares contentHash to the stored hash, and on divergence parses it (parseSheetData/sheetDataToValues) and calls service.updateSheetValues for the tab resolved by the stored tabGids gid. google-drive.ts globs `**/*.${h.cardType}.card` (so `**/*.gsheet.card`) and syncFile() calls handler.push() before handler.pull(); service methods exist in src/services/google-drive.ts (getSpreadsheet/getSheetValues/updateSheetValues).

title: Typed cards for externally synced content
story: As a boxholder with connectors on, I want email-thread, email-message, gdoc, gsheet, webpage, extfile and tab-arrangement card types, so that synced mail, Drive documents, captured pages and live external files are ordinary box cards with their untrusted bytes kept in separate files.
evidence: EmailThreadSchema holds subject/participants and refs to its EmailMessageSchema cards (whose body text is a separate .txt reached by an opaque ref); GdocSchema/GsheetSchema carry drive-connector metadata with the content attached, WebpageSchema keeps a markdown body plus a frozen HTML snapshot, and TabArrangementSchema validates a Clerk-captured tab set via validatedArrangementIssues.

verdict.note: All seven schemas exist and are registered in callback-box/src/schemas/registry.ts (EmailThreadSchema, EmailMessageSchema, GdocSchema, GsheetSchema, WebpageSchema, ExtfileSchema, TabArrangementSchema). email-thread.tsx defines subject/participants/date-range and messages as an array of {ref} pointing at child email-message cards; email-message.tsx declares body-file: opaqueContentRef() with instructions saying the untrusted body text lives as a separate .txt in the attach scope. gdoc.tsx/gsheet.tsx describe drive-connector-synced docs/sheets with content attached, webpage.tsx is 'readable markdown body plus a frozen HTML snapshot in the attach scope', extfile.tsx is a live file: pointer with drift stamps, and tab-arrangement.ts has validate: ({fields}) => validatedArrangementIssues(fields) for a Clerk-captured tab set.

title: Use the connector CLI while a scheduled sync is running
story: As my box's agent, I want to run `cb drive add` or a manual sync while the box's own scheduled sync is mid-flight, so that neither process wipes the other's recorded sync state for files or calendars it did not touch.
evidence: updateTransientState runs every state read-modify-write under an in-process card lock plus a cross-process sibling `.lock` file with a ~5s retry budget; commitDriveStateDelta/mergeDriveState and saveCalendarState/mergeSyncTokens then merge only the per-file or per-calendar entries this writer actually changed onto freshly-loaded state, preserving a concurrent writer's entries.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/connectors/transient-state.ts `updateTransientState` wraps every read-modify-write in an OUTER in-process `withCardLock(statePath)` and an INNER cross-process sibling lock at `<state>.lock` via `requestScopedLock`/`acquireLock`, retrying 50 x 100ms (~5s) before throwing TransientStateLockError; fresh state is loaded inside both locks. google-drive-state.ts `mergeDriveState`/`commitDriveStateDelta` start from `{...fresh.files}` and only overwrite driveIds whose FileState differs from the run-start snapshot; google-calendar-state.ts `mergeSyncTokens`/`saveCalendarState` likewise spread `fresh` and only apply calendars whose token changed (and delete ones the writer cleared). cli/commands/drive.ts line 175 (`cb drive add <url> <path>`, registered via cli/commands/index.ts -> cli/index.ts `program.addCommand(driveCommand)`) persists the new file's entry with `update: (fresh) => ({files: {...fresh.files, [fileId]: fileState}})`, so a concurrent server sync's entries survive.

title: Wake a procedure when new mail matches a rule
story: As a box owner, I want a Gmail rule to run a named procedure when it matches, so that new mail can drive an automation without creating a card per thread.
evidence: A `procedure` action carries a config/procedures/<name>.procedure.card ref; procedureTrigger returns a ConnectorProcedureTrigger with a directive pointing at `cb connector gmail pending <rule>`, which sync() returns in SyncResult.procedures for the wakeup loop to run.

verdict.note: gmail-config.ts defines a rule action `{type:"procedure", ref}` validated against /^config\/procedures\/[^/]+\.procedure\.card$/. In gmail-rules.ts the `case "procedure"` branch records a pending summary (no per-thread card) and calls procedureTrigger(rule), returning ConnectorProcedureTrigger{procedureRef, directive: 'Gmail rule <name> has new matching mail. Inspect with: cb connector gmail pending <rule>'}. gmail.ts line 242 puts evaluated.procedures into SyncResult.procedures (declared in connectors/index.ts), and both cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts and core/commands/connector-sync.ts feed them to runConnectorProcedureTriggers, which runs the `procedure-run` command per trigger. story: As an operator monitoring a deployed box, I want a configured API key to reach a whitelisted set of read-only health and debug endpoints, so that a monitor or field-test harness can poll the box without a user session.
evidence: verifyDiagBearerKey timing-safe-compares CB_DIAG_API_KEY, and isDiagnosticBypassRequest lets a GET through only when every comma-separated tRPC procedure in the URL is in DIAG_PROCEDURE_WHITELIST (health.check, debugLog.get, chat.statusAll).

verdict.note: webapp/auth.ts verifyDiagBearerKey reads process.env.CB_DIAG_API_KEY, returns false when unset, and does a length check plus crypto.timingSafeEqual against `Bearer <key>`. isDiagnosticBypassRequest requires method GET, parses the comma-separated tRPC procedure list after /api/trpc/, requires every procedure to be in DIAG_PROCEDURE_WHITELIST (health.check, debugLog.get, chat.statusAll), then the bearer check. server-box-scope.ts calls isDiagnosticBypassRequest in its auth hook and returns early (skipping cookie auth). server-root.ts /healthz uses verifyDiagBearerKey directly and 503s when the key is unset; field-test/run-server.ts mints a per-run key, matching the 'field-test harness' clause.

title: Have a crashed box brought back without me watching it
story: As an operator, I want the hub to relaunch a supervised box that exits, backing off exponentially and giving up after five consecutive failures until I reload it, so that a transient crash doesn't silently take a box's schedules offline and a genuinely broken box doesn't spin forever.
evidence: `crash-backoff.ts` defines `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` (5) and `backoffDelayMs` (1s doubling, capped at 30s); the supervisor tracks `consecutiveFailures` per box, restarts on child exit after that delay, marks the box unhealthy once the budget is spent, and `reloadUnhealthy()` (SIGHUP) resets the counters and retries.

verdict.note: src/hub/crash-backoff.ts exports MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES = 5, BASE_BACKOFF_MS = 1000 and backoffDelayMs(n, base) = min(30_000, base * 2**(n-1)) — exponential doubling capped at 30s. src/hub/supervisor.ts tracks per-box `consecutiveFailures` (incremented at lines 470 and 508, reset to 0 on healthy start at 458), sets `box.status = "unhealthy"` and stops retrying once the count reaches MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES (lines 515-516), otherwise schedules a restart after `backoffDelayMs` (line 521). Supervisor.reloadUnhealthy() (line 394) zeroes consecutiveFailures for unhealthy boxes and is wired to SIGHUP in src/cli/commands/hub.ts line 178, and hub-health.ts maps consecutiveFailures>0 / "unhealthy" into the hub verdict, so the operator-facing `cb hub` path exists.

title: Have every box migrate itself when new engine code ships
story: As an operator, I want each deploy to apply pending script migrations per box and commit them one at a time — skipping a box with a dirty tree, stopping at a migration that needs an agent, and printing nothing when there's nothing to do — so that boxes converge on the current card shapes without me visiting each one.
evidence: `deploy.sh` runs `timeout 600 cb migrate --sweep` per box; `sweepMigrations` applies script-kind migrations under the box git lock with one commit each, returning `current`/`applied`/`skipped-dirty`/`needs-procedure`/`failed`/`commit-failed`, and `runSweep` maps those to a quiet exit 0 or a non-zero 'a human needs to look'.

verdict.note: deploy/deploy.sh (lines ~553-585) loops over /home/callback/boxes/*/content and runs `timeout 600 cb migrate --sweep` per box in the at-rest window, printing only non-empty output and always exiting 0 so one box never fails the deploy. core/migration-sweep.ts sweepMigrations wraps sweepUnderLock in withBoxGitLock, returns 'current' when nothing is pending, 'skipped-dirty' when getStatus is unclean, 'needs-procedure' at a procedure-kind migration, and otherwise runs each script migration and commits it individually ('Apply migration: <name>' with a migration-sweep trailer), rolling the manifest entry back to 'commit-failed' if the commit throws. cli/commands/migrate.ts runSweep maps 'current'/'applied' to exit 0 (and prints nothing at all for 'current') and every human-needed status to exit 1 with a warning.

title: Health names credential files still sitting in the box tree
story: As an operator, I want a health warning listing any `config/connectors/*.secret.json` left behind, so that I can move those credentials into the machine store instead of leaving live secrets in the agent's own working directory.
evidence: `legacySecretFilesCheck` reads `config/connectors/`, filters `*.secret.json` and returns a warning-severity check naming each file ("migrate to the machine store and delete: …"); health.ts pushes it into the box's health checks.

verdict.note: health-secrets.ts exports legacySecretFilesCheck(boxRoot): reads <boxRoot>/config/connectors, filters names ending .secret.json, and returns a HealthCheck named legacy-secret-files with severity 'warning' whose message is 'Legacy secret file(s) — migrate to the machine store and delete: config/connectors/<name>, …' (ok:true with a clean message when none). health.ts line 30 imports it and line 308 does checks.push(await legacySecretFilesCheck(boxRoot)) inside the box health check assembly, so it lands in the operator-facing health output.

title: Inspect the live deployment as its owner
story: As an operator, I want to fetch and browse production pages authenticated as the configured owner and to get a shell on the server, so that I can diagnose a box that only misbehaves in production without going through the browser OAuth wall.
evidence: prod-curl mints and consumes a signed session cookie for `CB_OWNER_EMAIL` on the server (never written locally) and curls a deployed URL; prod-browse hands the same cookie to a real browser; prod-ssh resolves the server via resolve-server-ip.sh. The scripts carry an explicit identity boundary: they authenticate only as the configured owner.

verdict.note: deploy/prod-curl sources resolve-server-ip.sh, ssh's to root@SERVER_IP, sources /home/callback/.env, requires CB_OWNER_EMAIL, mints an HMAC-signed cb_session cookie from /home/callback/.cb-session-secret entirely on the server, and curls http://127.0.0.1:3210<path> with that cookie — nothing written locally. deploy/prod-browse mints the same cookie over ssh and installs it into bin/browse's profile for the deploy/public-url host before opening the page. deploy/prod-ssh execs `ssh -A root@$SERVER_IP` using the same resolve_server_ip helper. Both curl/browse scripts carry an explicit 'IDENTITY BOUNDARY: this authenticates only as CB_OWNER_EMAIL' header, and deploy/README.md:189-222 documents all three.

title: Keep a long-running server from drifting or degrading
story: As an operator, I want the host to recycle the serving process nightly once the box is at rest and to update the agent CLI on its own schedule with a loud failure signal, so that a server left alone for weeks does not accumulate leaked memory or fall behind on its agent runtime.
evidence: setup-server.sh installs `cb-wait-quiet` (polls `cb activity` up to a cap) plus `callback-serve-recycle.service`/`.timer` at 04:00 to restart only callback-serve, and `claude-update.service`/`.timer` running claude-update.sh nightly; the wrapper appends ok/FAIL lines to a persistent log and exits non-zero so `OnFailure=claude-update-failure.service` logs to daemon.err. It also raises Claude Code's transcript retention to 60 days so nightly chat review still has its raw material.

verdict.note: callback-box/deploy/setup-server.sh writes /usr/local/bin/cb-wait-quiet (loops `cb activity` with a 180s deadline, always exits 0), callback-serve-recycle.service whose ExecStart is `cb-wait-quiet; systemctl restart callback-serve`, and callback-serve-recycle.timer at OnCalendar=*-*-* 04:00:00; both it and claude-update.timer (04:00 with RandomizedDelaySec=30m) are enabled+started at the end of the script. claude-update.service runs deploy/claude-update.sh as the callback user with OnFailure=claude-update-failure.service; the wrapper appends timestamped 'starting/ok/FAIL' lines to /home/callback/claude-update.log, logs to daemon.err via logger, and exits with claude's exit code. Lines 140-152 also set cleanupPeriodDays=60 in the callback user's ~/.claude/settings.json for transcript retention. Everything the story claims is present.

title: Keep asset manifests in sync
story: As an operator, I want to verify, migrate, add and overwrite the per-scope asset manifests that track binaries inside .attach directories, so that the box can detect a missing, changed or unclaimed asset instead of silently losing it.
evidence: `executeAttachments` dispatches `verify` (read-only `scanBoxAttachments`, non-zero on errors — used by the pre-commit hook), `migrate` (write mode, claims/refreshes/renames), `add` (claim one file, chmod 444) and `overwrite` (atomic stdin write plus manifest update).

verdict.note: src/core/commands/attachments.ts executeAttachments switches on subcommand: verify -> runVerify (scanBoxAttachments dryRun, prints errors and returns success:false when any), migrate -> runMigrate (write-mode scan reporting claimed/refreshed/renamed), add -> runAdd (loadManifest/computeEntry/saveManifest plus chmod 0o444), overwrite -> runOverwrite using writeAsset's chmod +w -> tmp write -> rename -> chmod 444. src/core/asset-manifest-scan.ts reconciles each `.attach/` scope against its manifest and reports missing-file, hash-mismatch and manifest-malformed errors plus unclaimed/refreshed/renamed sets, with scope discovery in src/lib/attach-scopes.ts (findAttachScopes). All four are reachable as `cb attachments verify|migrate|add <path>|overwrite <path>` in src/cli/commands/attachments.ts. Note the evidence's 'used by the pre-commit hook' is stale (test/core/install-validation-hooks.doctest.md asserts the hook no longer calls it), but that does not affect the story text.

title: Keep my own on/off state on a shipped schedule while still taking its updates
story: As an operator, I want the fields a box owns as state — a stock schedule's `enabled` toggle — to be ignored when deciding whether I customized a template and carried onto the new version, so that disabling a shipped schedule neither parks its future definition updates nor gets silently re-enabled by them.
evidence: installTemplateFile takes `boxOwnedFields`: stripBoxOwnedFields removes those keys before the customized-or-not hash comparison and applyBoxOwnedFields copies the box's values from the local card onto the written (or parked) template. `ScheduledScriptSchema.templateMerge = { boxOwnedFields: ["enabled"] }` (schemas/scheduled-script.tsx) is the one declared policy, passed through by installSchedules in core/box/defaults.ts.

verdict.note: src/core/install-template-file.ts defines InstallTemplateOptions.boxOwnedFields; canonicalize() = stripBoxOwnedFields(normalize(content), boxOwnedFields) is used for BOTH the template hash and the local hash, so a card differing only in an owned key hashes equal to stock and takes the 'overwritten' path. applyBoxOwnedFields({upstream, box}, fields) copies the box's value for those keys onto the template before writing, and is also applied to the parked mirror in config/_template-updates/. src/schemas/scheduled-script.tsx:106 declares templateMerge: { boxOwnedFields: ["enabled"] } (the only templateMerge in src/), typed in src/cards/schema.ts (TemplateMergePolicy, resolved at schema.ts:387), and installSchedules in src/core/box/defaults.ts:332 spreads it into the installTemplateFile call. Matches the story exactly.

title: Keep the box I have open from being stopped underneath me
story: As a person with a box open in a browser tab, I want the app to send a cheap heartbeat while the tab is visible, so that a lazily-started box is woken and its idle timer refreshed instead of being stopped while I am still reading it.
evidence: registerApiRoutes declares `server.head("/api/keepalive")` inside the box scope, answering 204 with `Cache-Control: no-store` and deliberately skipping the health checks, so reaching it through a lazy hub runs `Supervisor.ensureRunning`/`touch` (which resets `lastActivity` and the idle timer). The frontend hook and the tRPC client fetch it with `method: "HEAD"` only from a visible tab, so abandoned tabs still idle out.

verdict.note: The mechanism exists but is dev-only, narrower than the story's "a person with a box open in a browser tab". src/webapp/routes/api.ts:43 does declare `server.head("/api/keepalive")` returning 204 with Cache-Control: no-store, and src/hub/supervisor.ts has ensureRunning/touch resetting lastActivity and re-arming the idle timer (lazy mode only — its header comment says hub children are otherwise resident with no lazy-start or idle-shutdown). But both callers bail out unless `import.meta.env.DEV`: useDevWorktreeKeepalive (src/frontend/src/hooks/useDevWorktreeKeepalive.ts:26 `if (!import.meta.env.DEV) return;`) and wakeDevBox in src/frontend/src/lib/trpc/index.ts:56. In a production build the app sends no heartbeat at all, and the hook's own doc scopes it to the monorepo dev router/worktrees.

panel.note: All four cited pieces are live and connected. `registerApiRoutes` (callback-box/src/webapp/routes/api.ts:43) declares `server.head("/api/keepalive")` returning 204 with Cache-Control: no-store, and that registrar is mounted per-box at src/webapp/server-box-scope.ts:260. The frontend hook useDevWorktreeKeepalive is imported and called inside AppLayout (src/frontend/src/app-shell.tsx:23,49), which router.tsx uses as the app's layout route, and it HEAD-fetches `${getApiBase()}/keepalive` on mount, on a 60s interval, and on visibilitychange, skipping hidden tabs. src/frontend/src/lib/trpc/index.ts:55-80 defines wakeDevBox() hitting the same endpoint and awaits it inside the wsClient `url` thunk before each socket open. Supervisor.ensureRunning/touch (src/hub/supervisor.ts:247,291) reset lastActivity and re-arm the idle timer. The DEV-only guards in both callers are a reachability question, outside my lens; the code exists and is wired.

The entry points exist end to end with no config to set. src/frontend/src/app-shell.tsx:49 calls useDevWorktreeKeepalive() unconditionally inside AppLayout, the wrapper every box page renders under, and the hook fires a HEAD to `${getApiBase()}/keepalive` immediately, on visibilitychange, and every 60s while document.visibilityState === 'visible'; src/frontend/src/lib/trpc/index.ts:80 awaits the same wakeDevBox() before each WebSocket open. That request lands on the box-scoped route registered at src/webapp/routes/api.ts (`server.head("/api/keepalive")` -> 204, Cache-Control: no-store), and routing it through a lazy hub runs Supervisor.ensureRunning/touch (src/hub/supervisor.ts:247, 291) which resets lastActivity and re-arms the idle timer. The only gate is `import.meta.env.DEV`, which is on by default in the dev-router build where lazy start/idle-stop actually exists -- so a person with a box open in a tab reaches it without setting anything; whether the story's phrasing overreaches by not saying 'dev' is a scope question for another lens, not reachability.

The story is unqualified about who benefits ('a person with a box open in a browser tab', 'I want the app to send a cheap heartbeat'), but both senders are gated on the dev bundle: useDevWorktreeKeepalive.ts:26 returns immediately unless `import.meta.env.DEV`, and wakeDevBox in src/frontend/src/lib/trpc/index.ts:56 does the same ('This stays dev-only; production hubs keep their existing upgrade behavior'). The server side is general — src/webapp/routes/api.ts:43 registers `server.head("/api/keepalive")` inside the box scope returning 204/no-store — and lazy idle-stop is a real production hub config (src/hub/hub-config.ts:71 `lazy`, `idleMs` defaulting to 5 minutes, plus keepRecent), so a production build viewing a lazily-started box sends no heartbeat at all and can still be idle-stopped mid-read. The hook's own docstring scopes it to 'the monorepo dev router' and worktrees, one special case rather than the general capability the story asserts.

triage.reasoning: Code is fine; the story's scope is wrong. The server half is general (webapp/routes/api.ts registers `server.head("/api/keepalive")` inside the box scope, 204 + no-store, skipping health checks) and Supervisor.ensureRunning/touch do reset lastActivity and re-arm the idle timer. But both senders are gated on the dev bundle: useDevWorktreeKeepalive.ts returns immediately unless `import.meta.env.DEV`, and wakeDevBox in lib/trpc/index.ts does the same with the comment "This stays dev-only; production hubs keep their existing upgrade behavior". That gate is not a defect: lazy start / idle-stop is the dev router's model (hub-config.ts `lazy` defaults to false, and docs/implemented-plans/boxes-as-packages-v2.md records that production hub.json keeps `lazy: false` because schedulers and webhooks want children resident, with supervisor.ts's header saying the same). So in every configuration that ships, the only environment with an idle timer to refresh is the one where the heartbeat runs. The story's 'a person with a box open in a browser tab' should read 'a developer with a worktree box open in the dev router'; there is nothing to build. (A hub deliberately configured `lazy: true` in production would send no heartbeat, but that is an unused opt-in config, not the shipped path.)

title: Live box dashboard
story: As a boxholder, I want one dashboard page showing my box's name, git cleanliness, version and creation date that refreshes itself as things happen, so that I can see the state of the box without reloading.
evidence: DashboardPage queries status.status/health.check and subscribes via useBusSubscription, invalidating on file-change/card-created/wakeup-complete. HeaderStrip renders box name, a connected dot, and a clean/dirty git button opening a staged/modified/untracked popover; SystemInfo shows boxVersion, created date and the deployed commit.

verdict.note: pages/DashboardPage.tsx runs trpc.status.status + trpc.health.check queries and a useBusSubscription whose onEvent invalidates status/scheduler caches on file-change, question-answered, card-created and wakeup-complete — self-refreshing without reload. components/dashboard/HeaderStrip.tsx renders the box name (last segment of status.boxRoot), a connected/disconnected dot, and a clean/dirty button toggling GitStatusPopover listing staged/modified/untracked files. components/dashboard/SystemInfo.tsx renders v{status.boxVersion}, 'Created: ' + status.created, git clean/modified-untracked counts, and the deployed commit hash/time from health.check version. Route /$boxSlug/dashboard is in router.tsx and reachable from the nav menu (components/PlacePill-panels.tsx MenuItem 'Dashboard', lib/nav-menu-entries.ts).

browser.note: Dashboard renders a header strip with the box name/path, a green 'Connected' dot, and a 'dirty (93 files)' button; SystemInfo footer shows 'v1.0.0', 'Created: 1/30/2026', and 'Git: 8 modified, 85 untracked'. Live refresh verified without reloading: while the page sat open, the git counts changed (85→86→85 untracked) and two new commits ('Answer question…', 'Dismiss question…') appeared at the top of Recent Activity on their own. Caveat: the box name shown is 'content' (the content dir basename), not 'test1'.

title: Live updates degrade rather than exhausting the server on a huge box
story: As an operator running an unusually large or high-churn box, I want the live-update file watcher to skip churny trees and stop adding watches at a fixed ceiling, logging once when it does, so that UI freshness quietly degrades instead of the box process running out of file descriptors and failing to spawn the agent at all.
evidence: core/box/file-watcher.ts watches directories (never individual files), excludes `HIGH_CHURN_DIRS` (`procedure/runs`, `store/trash`), caps live watches at `MAX_WATCHED_DIRS` (1024) and queued bookkeeping at `MAX_NOTIFICATION_WORK`, and emits a one-per-watcher `[box-watcher] directory watch limit … reached` warning when it stops adding watches; events are coalesced per `(event, path)` over `COALESCE_MS`.

verdict.note: src/core/box/file-watcher.ts watches directories only (fs.watch(current, ...) on dirs, header comment explains the per-file FD cost on macOS), skips HIGH_CHURN_DIRS = ["procedure/runs", "store/trash"] plus dot segments in ignored(), and bounds live watches at MAX_WATCHED_DIRS = 1024 and queued coalescing windows at MAX_NOTIFICATION_WORK = 1024 via reserveDir()/entryBudgetExhausted(). reportWatchLimit() logs `[box-watcher] directory watch limit of N reached for <boxRoot>; live updates below <rel> are disabled` exactly once per watcher (limitReported guard). COALESCE_MS = 50 throttles per (event, path). Reachable in the app: webapp/trpc/routers/events.ts calls ensureBoxWatcher and webapp/server-box-scope.ts calls closeBoxWatcher, with events emitted onto core/event-bus.ts.

title: Maintain the box manifest
story: As an operator, I want to add, remove and list the boxes in the shared manifest, so that serve and the scheduler know which boxes exist on this machine.
evidence: `boxesCommand` has add/remove/list against boxes.json; the older `cb scheduler add|remove|list` subcommands remain as deprecated aliases.

verdict.note: The add/remove/list half checks out: `boxesCommand` in callback-box/src/cli/commands/boxes.ts registers add/remove/list against ~/.config/cb/boxes.json via addBoxToManifest/removeBoxFromManifest/loadBoxesConfig (core/box/boxes-config.ts), it is registered in src/cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(boxesCommand)), and cli/commands/scheduler.ts keeps `add|remove|list` as deprecated aliases that print a deprecationNotice. But the story's 'so that' clause is contradicted by the code: the module comment in src/cli/commands/serve.ts says 'The ~/.config/cb/boxes.json manifest ... feeds the SCHEDULER only -- cb serve never reads it', and serve.ts line ~121 repeats 'The boxes.json manifest is never consulted here'; grep for loadBoxesConfig shows no call in serve.ts or webapp/server.ts. Multi-box serving uses `cb hub` with its own hub.json. Only the scheduler (plus activity.ts and secrets/migrate.ts) reads this manifest, so the claim that serve learns which boxes exist is an over-claim (the stale `boxesCommand` .description() string is the only place saying otherwise).

panel.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/boxes.ts defines boxesCommand with add/remove/list subcommands calling addBoxToManifest, removeBoxFromManifest and loadBoxesConfig, all real exported functions in core/box/boxes-config.ts (lines 85-121) that read/write the boxes.json manifest. The command is wired into the CLI: cli/index.ts imports it at line 64 and calls program.addCommand(boxesCommand) at line 142. cli/commands/scheduler.ts still registers add/remove/list as live deprecated aliases (lines 49-95) that print a deprecationNotice and delegate to the same manifest helpers. Nothing here is dead code; the earlier verifier's objection was about the story's 'so that' clause (serve never reads the manifest), which is a wording/accuracy question outside this lens.

The entry point is the installed `cb` binary (callback-box/package.json bin: {"cb": "./bin/cb"}): src/cli/index.ts line 142 does program.addCommand(boxesCommand), and src/cli/commands/boxes.ts registers the `add`, `remove`, and `list` subcommands with unconditional actions calling addBoxToManifest/removeBoxFromManifest/loadBoxesConfig from core/box/boxes-config.ts. No flag, env var, or config gates any of them. The deprecated aliases are also reachable: src/cli/index.ts line 127 adds schedulerCommand, whose add/remove/list subcommands (scheduler.ts lines 62-95) print a deprecation notice and delegate. The earlier verifier's objection was about the story's 'so that' clause (serve never reads boxes.json), which is an accuracy question, not a reachability one; my lens is satisfied.

The add/remove/list half is fully delivered: boxes.ts registers add/remove/list over ~/.config/cb/boxes.json via addBoxToManifest/removeBoxFromManifest/loadBoxesConfig in core/box/boxes-config.ts, and scheduler.ts still exposes the same three as deprecated aliases. But the 'so that' clause names serve as a consumer, and the code says the opposite: serve.ts's header states 'The ~/.config/cb/boxes.json manifest (cb boxes add/remove/list) feeds the SCHEDULER only — cb serve never reads it', repeated at line 121 ('The boxes.json manifest is never consulted here'), and a grep for loadBoxesConfig across src shows callers only in scheduler.ts, activity.ts, secrets/migrate.ts and boxes.ts — none in serve.ts or webapp/server.ts (multi-box serving uses cb hub with its own hub.json). The benefit clause therefore promises an outcome the code does not produce.

triage.reasoning: The capability half is fully delivered: cli/commands/boxes.ts registers add/remove/list over ~/.config/cb/boxes.json via addBoxToManifest/removeBoxFromManifest/loadBoxesConfig (core/box/boxes-config.ts:85-121), is wired in cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(boxesCommand)), and scheduler.ts keeps the same three as deprecated aliases. The story's 'so that' clause is the wrong part: `cb serve` never reads the manifest. serve.ts's module comment says so ('feeds the SCHEDULER only — cb serve never reads it') and repeats it at the resolution site (line ~121); I grepped every loadBoxesConfig call site — scheduler.ts, activity.ts, secrets/migrate.ts, boxes.ts — and none is in serve.ts or webapp/server.ts. Multi-box serving is `cb hub` with its own hub.json (hub/hub-config.ts). So the code is fine and the story's benefit clause is stale; correct it to 'so that the scheduler knows which boxes to run' (activity.ts and secrets migrate also read it). One cosmetic loose end worth a one-line fix while someone is there, not a gap: boxesCommand's own .description() still reads 'Manage the box manifest used by serve and scheduler', which is the only place in the tree still claiming serve consumes it — the module doc-comment directly above it already contradicts it.

title: Migrate a box past the cards that will not convert
story: As an operator migrating a large box, I want a migrator that could not convert some individual cards to still count as applied and let the remaining migrations run, while a hard precondition failure stops the whole pass and leaves the manifest untouched, so that one malformed card does not strand the box on an old data shape.
evidence: The apply loop in src/cli/commands/migrate.ts treats exit code 2 as a soft per-card failure — records the manifest entry, collects the name into softFailures, continues, and finally tells the operator to run `cb validate` — while any other non-zero code prints "failed hard", skips the manifest entry and exits with that code.

verdict.note: Read the apply loop in callback-box/src/cli/commands/migrate.ts (~lines 307-355). It documents the shared exit-code convention: code 2 = per-card soft failure, any other non-zero = hard failure. On `code !== 0 && code !== 2` it prints `Migration "X" failed hard (exit code N). Manifest not updated for this entry. Subsequent migrations not run.` and `process.exit(code)` before appendManifestEntry, so the manifest is untouched and later migrations don't run. On code 2 it still calls appendManifestEntry, pushes to softFailures, prints the continue warning, and at the end tells the operator to `Run \`cb validate\``. src/core/migration-run.ts is the sweep-side counterpart and echoes the same hard-failure message (line 168).

title: Migrate in-tree connector secrets into the store
story: As an operator, I want to move every box's `config/connectors/*.secret.json` into the machine store in one planned pass, and to copy one box's grants to another, so that adding a box no longer means copying credential files around.
evidence: core/secrets/migrate.ts plans a migration across every manifest box (mapping legacy filenames to store names, deduping identical values into one entry with per-box grants) and applies it under one store lock without printing values; `cb secrets migrate` and `cb secrets copy-grants` (cli/commands/secrets-migrate.ts, `copyBoxGrants`) expose it.

verdict.note: src/core/secrets/migrate.ts enumerates legacy config/connectors/*.secret.json across manifest boxes (migrationBoxRoots reads the manifest; enumerateLegacySecrets), planSecretMigration maps legacy filenames to store names and dedupes identical values into one entry with per-box grants (PlannedEntry.grants; conflicting values parked as <name>/<slug>), and applySecretMigration re-plans and writes inside a single store lock. src/cli/commands/secrets-migrate.ts exposes migrateCommand and copyGrantsCommand (the latter calling copyBoxGrants in src/core/secrets/lifecycle.ts), both added to secretsCommand (secrets.ts lines 366-367), which is registered in src/cli/index.ts — so `cb secrets migrate` and `cb secrets copy-grants` are reachable. printPlan prints names, grants, conflicts and skips only, never secret values; note the originals are left in place (copy, not delete), which the command output states explicitly.

title: Migrate retired view: links to plain box paths
story: As an operator, I want a one-time command that rewrites stored `view:` links in box content to plain box paths, so that older boxes stop rendering dead links.
evidence: migrateBoxViewLinks() rewrites `](view:…)` targets (dropping the retired `?zoom`) across box markdown/cards; `cb migrate-view-links --dry-run` reports what would change.

verdict.note: core/views/link-migration.ts exports migrateBoxViewLinks(boxRoot,{dryRun}), globbing **/*.md and **/*.card and rewriting `](view:…)` targets via rewriteViewTarget, which strips the `view:` scheme and drops the retired `zoom` query flag while keeping other params. cli/commands/migrate-view-links.ts registers the `migrate-view-links` command with a --dry-run flag that prints 'Would rewrite N view: link(s) in M file(s)'; it is wired into the CLI at cli/index.ts:109 (and exported from cli/commands/index.ts), so `cb migrate-view-links` is reachable.

title: One shared Google grant across every box on the server
story: As an operator, I want the refresh token kept in one centralized file rather than per box, so that a single authorization serves every box and a corrupt or contended token file fails loudly instead of being silently overwritten.
evidence: centralTokenPath() reads CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE with the per-box `config/connectors/google.secret.json` as legacy fallback; writes go through a cross-process file lock and throw GoogleTokenStoreCorruptError rather than starting from `{}` when the existing file can't be parsed.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/connectors/google-token-store.ts implements exactly this: centralTokenPath() returns process.env.CB_GOOGLE_TOKENS_FILE or null, googleTokenWritePath() falls back to the per-box config/connectors/google.secret.json, and loadGoogleTokens() reads central-first with legacy fallback. updateGoogleTokens() wraps every read-modify-write in withCardLock plus a cross-process requestScopedLock on <tokens>.lock (LOCK_RETRIES/LOCK_RETRY_MS, GoogleTokenLockError on exhaustion), and readTokensForUpdate() tolerates only ENOENT — any other read/parse failure throws GoogleTokenStoreCorruptError instead of merging into {}. The env var is propagated to per-box child processes under the hub (src/hub/child-env.ts allowlist line 63), so the one file really is shared across boxes.

title: Park agent work when the provider quota is exhausted
story: As someone maintaining boxes on a machine, I want a quota-exhausted engine to be recognized and held until its reset time, so that scheduled runs stop burning retries and I hear about it once.
evidence: `engine-unavailability.ts` recognizes per-provider quota signals and derives `retryAt` (parsed or a bounded fallback hold); `applyEngineUnavailability` records it from a failed run into the machine-level advisory store, which keeps `episodeStartedAt`/`notifiedAt`/`notifiedRetryAt` per provider, self-expires at `retryAt`, and fails open on a corrupt file.

verdict.note: core/agent/engine-unavailability.ts recognizes per-provider quota signals (CODEX_LIMIT_RE, CLAUDE_LIMIT_RE/CLAUDE_EPOCH_RE), parses a reset time or applies FALLBACK_HOLD_MS=1h, yielding `retryAt`/`retryAtSource`. engine-unavailability-apply.ts `applyEngineUnavailability` (called from core/agent/run.ts:266 and codex-run.ts:141/150 on failed runs) records it via engine-availability-store.ts `recordEngineUnavailability`, which keeps episodeStartedAt/notifiedAt/notifiedRetryAt per provider in ~/.local/share/cb/engine-availability.json, fails open on unreadable/invalid JSON, and expires records at retryAt in `liveEngineUnavailability`. The 'held until reset' and 'heard once' claims hold: cli/commands/tick-utils.ts:96, tick-helpers.ts:134, and core/reactor/engine.ts:156 consult boxEngineUnavailability to defer scheduled work, and notifyEpisode + markEngineUnavailabilityNotified latch the boxholder notification per episode.

title: Pick a box at the root
story: As a user with more than one box on a server, I want the root URL to list my boxes (or go straight in when there is only one, or prompt me to sign in when there are none), so that I land somewhere useful.
evidence: BoxRedirect uses useBoxes; with one box it navigates to /$boxSlug with replace, with none plus authRequired it shows the sign-in prompt, otherwise it renders a BoxActionsTile per box.

verdict.note: frontend/src/router.tsx line 44-48 wires path "/" to BoxRedirect (re-exported from app-shell.tsx, defined in pages/BoxSelection.tsx). BoxRedirect uses useBoxes() (hooks/useBoxes.ts, a shared react-query over fetchBoxes from lib/boxes.ts); a useEffect navigates to /$boxSlug with replace when boxes.length === 1, renders the 'Sign in to access your boxes.' screen with <SignInLink> when boxes.length === 0 && authRequired, and otherwise renders a <BoxActionsTile> per box. On the hub side hub/box-picker.ts serves this SPA route at `/` (registerBoxPicker is called at hub-server.ts:344), with a server-rendered list fallback when the frontend bundle is absent.

title: Probe a running server from an uptime monitor
story: As an operator, I want a diagnostic-key-gated server endpoint that reports box count, version, template drift, schema load failures and engine mismatch, so that monitoring alarms on a degraded deployment instead of me finding out by hand.
evidence: `registerRootInfoRoutes` serves `GET /healthz`, requiring `CB_DIAG_API_KEY` via `verifyDiagBearerKey`, and returning `templateDrift`, `schemaLoadFailures`, `engineVersionMismatch` and the open-access flag; `GET /api/build-info` is the unauthenticated minimal build-hash probe.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/server-root.ts registerRootInfoRoutes() (line 136) registers GET /healthz: it returns 503 {status:'unconfigured'} when CB_DIAG_API_KEY is unset, 401-style rejection via verifyDiagBearerKey(request) (src/webapp/auth.ts:68, timing-safe bearer compare against CB_DIAG_API_KEY), and on success returns {status, open: request.server.openAccess, boxCount, version, templateDrift:{total,byBox}, schemaLoadFailures:{total,byBox}, engineVersionMismatch:{total,byBox}}. GET /api/build-info in the same function is unauthenticated and returns only {buildHash, open}. registerRootInfoRoutes is wired at src/webapp/server.ts:202, so the route is reachable on a running server.

title: Reach a box privately over a tailnet
story: As an operator who doesn't want to publish a box to the internet, I want the admin page to hand me the exact `cb tailscale setup` command for this box's port and link to the box's tailnet URL once it's exposed, so that I can reach it from my own devices only.
evidence: TailscaleSection fills --target from the loopback port in the browser's own URL and queries admin.tailscaleBaseUrl, which uses deriveTailscaleBaseUrl/parseServeConfig; cb tailscale status/setup/stop run the serve configuration on the host.

verdict.note: TailscaleSection.tsx is rendered by AdminPage.tsx (line 45). useLocalTargetPort() reads window.location.port on loopback hosts (excluding dev-router 3210) and renders the literal `cb tailscale setup --target <port>` string; otherwise it shows the auto-detecting `cb tailscale setup`. It also calls trpc.admin.tailscaleBaseUrl (admin.ts:288, ownerProcedure) which shells `tailscale serve status --json` and runs parseServeConfig/deriveTailscaleBaseUrl (src/services/tailscale.ts:274,313), rendering an ExternalLink to baseUrl + boxPathPrefix() only when exposed. src/cli/commands/tailscale.ts registers status/setup/stop subcommands with --target. Matches the story as written.

title: Read a hub-run box's own output after it misbehaves
story: As an operator, I want each box the hub spawns to have its stdout and stderr appended to a per-box rolling log file, so that a chat turn's error detail is still recoverable after the moment has passed instead of vanishing with the child process.
evidence: `supervisor.ts` calls `forwardChildOutput({ child, logFile: <boxRoot>/.callback-box/hub-child.log })` for every spawned child; child-output-log.ts buffers each stream into whole lines and appends them timestamped and stream-tagged via `appendRollingLog`, because piped-but-unread child output is otherwise discarded on exit.

verdict.note: src/hub/supervisor.ts:446, inside the private launch() used for every managed box, calls forwardChildOutput({child, logFile: path.join(boxRoot, '.callback-box', 'hub-child.log')}) right after spawning. defaultSpawnChild in src/hub/child-spawn.ts uses stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe'], so both streams are piped and otherwise unread. src/hub/child-output-log.ts forwardStream buffers chunks, splits on newlines (holding a partial line back), and appends each line as '<ISO timestamp> [stdout|stderr] <line>' via appendRollingLog, which src/lib/rolling-log.ts implements as mkdir+append with truncate-to-last-half past 100_000 bytes — a per-box rolling file that survives the child's exit.

title: Rebuild the running server from its own checkout
story: As an operator, I want one command to fast-forward the server's checkout, reinstall, rebuild the CLI bundle and frontend and restart the hub and scheduler in place, so that I can bring a server current without running the full commit-pinned rsync deploy from my machine.
evidence: deploy/rebuild.sh execs prod-ssh /root/rebuild-server.sh; rebuild-server.sh does `git pull --ff-only` in /opt/callback/callback-box, pnpm install, node scripts/build-cli.mjs (dist/cli.mjs + dist/cards), a frontend build, then `systemctl restart callback-hub callback-scheduler` and reports is-active for both. Documented at deploy/README.md:181.

verdict.note: callback-box/deploy/rebuild.sh is a two-line wrapper that execs deploy/prod-ssh /root/rebuild-server.sh. deploy/rebuild-server.sh runs `git pull --ff-only` in /opt/callback/callback-box, `pnpm install`, `node scripts/build-cli.mjs` (dist/cli.mjs + dist/cards), then pnpm install + pnpm build in src/frontend, then `systemctl restart callback-hub callback-scheduler` and prints systemctl is-active for both. deploy/README.md:181 documents it as '### rebuild.sh — Pull latest code and rebuild', distinct from deploy.sh's rsync path.

title: Reconcile a box's migration ledger without re-running a migration
story: As an operator holding a box that is already in a migration's post-state — it was migrated out of band, or the migrator has since been retired — I want to record that migration as applied without running it, either one name at a time or seeding the whole manifest, so that a legacy box stops being told it has pending work it must not do.
evidence: `cb migrate` declares --mark-applied <name> and --mark-all-applied; markMigrationApplied() in src/cli/commands/migrate.ts refuses an unknown MIGRATIONS name or a manifest-less box, no-ops when already recorded, and otherwise appends the config/migrations.jsonl entry.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/migrate.ts defines migrateCommand with both --mark-applied <name> and --mark-all-applied options, and it is registered in src/cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(migrateCommand)). markMigrationApplied() returns 'unknown-migration' when the name is absent from MIGRATIONS, 'no-manifest' when readManifest() is null, 'already-applied' as a no-op, otherwise appends to MANIFEST_PATH = 'config/migrations.jsonl' (src/core/migrations.ts:130) without running the migrator. --mark-all-applied writes an entry per MIGRATIONS entry but refuses to overwrite a non-empty existing manifest. Matches the story.

title: Register a box with the hub without hand-editing config
story: As an operator, I want `cb hub add-box <slug> <path>` to plan and validate the routing-table edit before writing it, so that adding a box cannot leave the hub with a config it refuses to load.
evidence: The `add-box` subcommand calls `planAddBoxToHubConfig`/`describeAddBoxPlan`/`applyAddBoxPlan`, which validate the resulting config through the hub's own loader; `deploy/add-box.sh` drives it twice, once with `--dry-run` as a preflight.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/hub.ts registers `hub add-box <slug> <path>` (hubCommand is added to the program in src/cli/index.ts:102) with a `--dry-run` option; the action calls planAddBoxToHubConfig, prints describeAddBoxPlan, and only writes via applyAddBoxPlan when not dry-running. src/hub/hub-config-edit.ts builds the candidate config, runs it through parseHubConfig (the same validator hub-config.ts applies at startup, catching reserved/malformed slugs and duplicate box paths) before anything is written, and applyAddBoxPlan writes atomically after re-checking baseText. deploy/add-box.sh invokes `cb hub add-box … --dry-run` in the preflight (line ~210) and the real `cb hub add-box` later (line ~435), matching the story's two-pass claim.

title: Repair a box's git-annex configuration
story: As an operator, I want a doctor that checks a box's git-annex setup and fixes what it can, so that asset storage keeps working without me remembering the remedy for each misconfiguration.
evidence: `cb doctor annex` (cli/commands/doctor.ts) runs runAnnexDoctor, which repairs by default and reports only what it cannot fix — narrowing .git/info/attributes to the asset extensions (with the coverage safety check) and reinstating the post-checkout/post-merge `git annex smudge --update` hooks.

verdict.note: cli/commands/doctor.ts registers `cb doctor annex` (with --check/--json/--box) and calls runAnnexDoctor(createGitAnnexService(), {repoRoot: shape.packageRoot, boxRoot, options:{check}}), printing formatAnnexDoctor and exiting 1 when unhealthy; repair is the default and --check is the read-only mode. core/annex/doctor.ts runs checks binary/initialized/gitignore-assets/thin/largefiles/annexed-coverage/attributes/content-present/journal/smudge-hooks/hook, emitting statuses ok|repaired|failed, i.e. it fixes what it can and names the remedy for the rest. info-attributes.ts writes the scoped assetAnnexAttributes() rendering and provides uncoveredAnnexedPaths as the coverage safety check gating the narrowing; smudge-hooks.ts checkAnnexSmudgeHooks reinstalls the post-checkout/post-merge `git annex smudge --update` hooks (status "repaired"). services/git-annex.ts is the shelled-out GitAnnexService the doctor drives. Also invoked from cb init and the health-annex tRPC router.

title: Restart a box server without leaving a second one behind
story: As an operator restarting a box server, I want the new process to kill the previous one for each box it serves and to exit when its own parent dies, so that a restart never leaves two servers writing to one box or an orphan holding the port.
evidence: startServer resolves boxes, then for each writes `<boxRoot>/.cb-serve.pid` after calling `killPreviousServer(pidFile)` (server-lifecycle.ts: SIGTERM, one-second grace, then SIGKILL, tolerating a stale pid file); SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP and a 2s `process.ppid` orphan check all funnel into one idempotent `shutdown` that unlinks the pid files and force-closes connections.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/webapp/server.ts startServer calls resolveBoxes(options) then, for each box, killPreviousServer(path.join(box.boxRoot, '.cb-serve.pid')) before creating the server, and afterwards writes process.pid into each box's .cb-serve.pid. server-lifecycle.ts killPreviousServer reads the pid, probes with signal 0, SIGTERMs, waits 1000ms, then SIGKILLs if still alive, swallowing a stale/missing pid file. The single `shutdown` unlinks every pid file, calls server.server.closeAllConnections() and server.close(); SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP go through fireShutdown (guarded against overlapping shutdowns), and a 2000ms setInterval comparing process.ppid to initialPpid fires the same shutdown on orphaning.

title: Route a fleet of boxes behind one hub
story: As an operator running several boxes, I want a hub that owns login once and proxies each request to the right box's child process with a hub-signed identity header, so that boxes never hold the session secret and can't forge each other's sessions.
evidence: hub-server.ts strips client-supplied `x-cb-*` headers, resolves identity from the session cookie, injects `x-cb-authenticated-email` + `x-cb-hub-secret` (or `x-cb-hub-auth: off`), and proxies `app.all("/*")` to the endpoint; `buildChildEnv` is a fail-closed allowlist that keeps `CB_SESSION_SECRET` out of children.

verdict.note: src/hub/hub-server.ts createHubServer registers the fleet's login routes at the hub (registerAuthSurface), then app.all("/*") calls stripHubHeaders (deletes every client-supplied `x-cb-*` header) and decideHubAuth, which resolves identity from the session cookie via resolveRequestIdentity and injects HUB_SECRET_HEADER plus `x-cb-authenticated-email` (or `x-cb-hub-auth: off` only under openAccess, which no CLI path sets), failing closed with 401/login-redirect otherwise, before proxy.web to the resolved Endpoint (src/hub/endpoints.ts). src/hub/child-env.ts buildChildEnv is an exact-name + prefix allowlist that CB_SESSION_SECRET is not on, and supervisor.ts:434 spawns children with only that env plus CB_HUB_SECRET, so children cannot mint sessions. Routing table comes from hub-config.ts's parseHubConfig boxes map.

title: Run a migration that needs the agent's judgment
story: As an operator, I want a migration entry that names a procedure instead of a script to be run by driving the box agent through that procedure, and to be refused outright unless the procedure ends in an abort-severity shell check, so that a judgment-shaped data change is still recorded as applied only when a machine confirmed it actually happened.
evidence: migrations.ts defines ProcedureMigration/isProcedureMigration and registers { name: "view-card-shape", procedure: "view-card-shape" }; migrate.ts's apply loop calls assertProcedureHasGate (requiring a step with validate.severity "abort" and non-empty validate.shells, else ProcedureGateError) then spawns `cb procedure run`.

verdict.note: src/core/migrations.ts defines ProcedureMigration/isProcedureMigration ('procedure' in m) and the registry includes { name: 'view-card-shape', procedure: 'view-card-shape' }. In src/cli/commands/migrate.ts the --apply loop branches on isProcedureMigration, calls assertProcedureHasGate (parses config/procedures/<name>.procedure.card and requires some step with validate.severity === 'abort' and validate.shells.length > 0, else ProcedureGateError → process.exit(1)), then runProcedure spawns `cb procedure run <name>`, which drives the box agent (src/cli/commands/procedure.ts → core command 'procedure-run'). The manifest entry is appended only after a 0/2 exit. templates/procedures/view-card-shape.procedure.card does carry a severity: abort step with shells. src/core/migration-sweep.ts documents that the unattended sweep is script-kind only and stops on procedure migrations for a human.

title: Run under a path prefix without breaking URLs
story: As an operator serving a box behind a path prefix, I want the router base, API base, and WebSocket URL all derived from that prefix, so that the same build works at / in production and at /<worktree>/<box>/ behind the dev router.
evidence: joinBaseAndPath/withBase prefix hardcoded paths with import.meta.env.BASE_URL, getApiBase() derives /<prefix>/<box>/api from the first path segment after the base, and getWebSocketUrl() builds the wss URL from it; createAppRouter passes the stripped base as TanStack's basepath, and useDevWorktreeKeepalive HEADs the box-scoped wake endpoint each minute while visible so the dev router does not idle-stop a worktree being watched.

verdict.note: api-core.ts defines `joinBaseAndPath`/`withBase` (prefix hardcoded paths with import.meta.env.BASE_URL), `getApiBase()` which strips the Vite base then takes the first path segment as the box to build `<prefix>/<box>/api`, and `getWebSocketUrl()` which builds ws/wss from window.location.host + getApiBase() + "/trpc". router.tsx `createAppRouter` reads BASE_URL, strips the trailing slash and passes it as TanStack's `basepath` (undefined at "/"). hooks/useDevWorktreeKeepalive.ts HEADs `${getApiBase()}/keepalive` immediately, every 60s, and on visibilitychange, only when DEV and document visible. All three claims hold.

title: See box problems on the dashboard
story: As a boxholder in the web app, I want the dashboard to surface failed health checks and box-growth warnings with actions to acknowledge them, so that I learn about a broken credential or runaway growth without running a CLI.
evidence: `HealthWarnings` renders `health.check` output only when there are issues and exposes acknowledge / expect-rates handlers for box growth; `SystemInfo` shows the deployed commit recorded in deploy-info.json.

verdict.note: DashboardPage.tsx (src/frontend/src/pages/) queries trpc.health.check plus health.acknowledgeBoxGrowth / health.expectBoxGrowthRates mutations and renders <HealthWarnings>. HealthWarnings.tsx returns null when health.status === "healthy" or no failing checks, otherwise lists failing checks by severity and renders 'Acknowledge this growth' / 'Expect these rates' buttons when check.actions includes acknowledge-box-growth / expect-box-growth-rates and the viewer is the owner. src/webapp/trpc/routers/health.ts assembles the checks (googleAuthHealthChecks for broken Google credentials, API-key checks, boxGrowthHealthCheck) and defines the HealthCheck.actions union; src/core/box-growth/actions.ts implements acknowledgedGrowthState / rate expectations used by health-box-growth.ts. SystemInfo is also rendered on the same page from deploy-info.json read by readVersionInfo.

browser.note: The dashboard does surface failed health checks: a 'Box warnings' panel lists the pending-migrations warning and the legacy-secret-files warning, rendered only because there are issues. The acknowledge-growth actions and the deploy-commit line in SystemInfo were not observable (no growth warning active; no deploy-info.json in this dev checkout).

title: See what a box is made of
story: As a person using the box, I want an inventory of my box broken down by card type, file count and bytes — including how much lives in git-annex — so that I can see where the box's content and storage actually are.
evidence: scanBoxInventory() walks the box (excluding .git/.callback-box/node_modules) summarizing per-type counts and bytes, with box-repository-stats.ts adding annexed-vs-regular storage via `git annex find`; the inventory tRPC router caches it for 15 minutes and InventoryPage.tsx renders the table.

verdict.note: scanBoxInventory (src/core/box-inventory.ts) walks the box excluding .git/.callback-box/node_modules and returns per-type direct/grouped summaries with count+bytes plus repository stats; box-repository-stats.ts computes checkout/git disk bytes and an annexed-vs-regular StorageBreakdown from `git annex find` output (annexFindLine bytesize). The inventoryRouter (src/webapp/trpc/routers/inventory.ts) exposes summary with a 15-minute cache, and the /inventory route in src/frontend/src/router.tsx renders InventoryPage → InventoryContent (Git storage stats, annexed percentage, StorageTable of annexed vs regular for All/Linked/Unlinked) and InventoryTable (type, count, formatted bytes).

browser.note: /inventory shows 'Inventory summary' with whole-box totals (1,303 physical files, 111 MB content size, 1,070 grouped items), a 'Git storage' section (269 MB repository footprint, 120 MB Git storage, 99.0% logical content annexed) with an Annexed vs Regular Git table broken out by All/Linked/Unlinked showing size + file count per cell, a treemap area view (toggles All/Linked/Unlinked, Grouped/Direct, By count/By size — verified By size switches the map to '.capture-session.card 106 MB'), and a full per-type table with Type/Count/Size rows including card types (.capture-session.card 11 / 106 MB, .intake-job.card 609 / 347 KB, .question.card 39 / 22 KB, .md 115 / 230 KB, 'Orphaned .attach/' 40 / 41 KB, etc.). Card-type breakdown, file counts, bytes, and the git-annex split are all present.

title: Seed cards for a new box
story: As an operator, I want a fresh box to come with default procedures, a personality card, a briefing, a root landmark, a todo view and the default scheduled scripts, so that the box is usable immediately rather than empty.
evidence: core/box/defaults.ts installs procedure templates from PACKAGE_ROOT/templates/procedures plus createInitialPersonalityTemplate, createBriefingTemplate, createLandmarkTemplate, createTodoViewTemplate and createScheduledScriptTemplate, each through installTemplateFile.

verdict.note: core/box/defaults.ts exports installProcedures (copies PACKAGE_ROOT/templates/procedures), installGuides, installPersonality (createInitialPersonalityTemplate -> config/main.personality.card), installBriefing (briefing.briefing.card), installRootLandmark (Box.landmark.card), installTodoView (store/plate.todo-view.card), and installSchedules which installs the built-in defaults (check-email, check-calendar, refresh-maps, gc-procedure-runs, process-retrospective, chat-review) via createScheduledScriptTemplate. Each goes through installTemplateFile from core/install-template-file.ts. cli/commands/init.ts imports and calls all of them, so `cb init` is the reachable operator entry point.

title: Serve many boxes from one supervised process
story: As an operator, I want `cb hub` to spawn, route to, and restart each registered box with crash-loop backoff, so that a multi-box server keeps every box reachable under one front door.
evidence: `Supervisor` implements `EndpointProvider`, spawning per-box children on allocated ports with readiness probes and `crash-backoff.ts` limits; `createHubServer` proxies by slug prefix using the boxes in `hub.json` loaded by `loadHubConfig`.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/hub.ts is registered as hubCommand in src/cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(hubCommand)); its default action loads hub.json via loadHubConfig (src/hub/hub-config.ts, default ~/.config/cb/hub.json), constructs `new Supervisor({config, hubSecret})` and passes it as `endpoints` to `createHubServer` (src/hub/hub-server.ts). Supervisor (src/hub/supervisor.ts) `implements EndpointProvider`, spawns per-box children with readiness probes (defaultCheckReady/waitForHttp), tracks `restarts`/`restartTimer`, and imports MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES/BASE_BACKOFF_MS/backoffDelayMs from src/hub/crash-backoff.ts for restart backoff. hub-server.ts routes by `/<slug>/...` (slugForPath, plus /webhook/<slug>) and proxies via http-proxy-3 to the resolved endpoint, with ensureRunning for lazy spawn.

title: Serve several boxes from one server under slug prefixes
story: As an operator, I want one server process to serve every box I've configured, each mounted at its own URL prefix, so that I can run a household's boxes from a single deployment.
evidence: `createServer`/`startServer` in server.ts resolve boxes via `resolveBoxes` (server-lifecycle.ts) and call `registerBox` per box, which registers the box's routes, tRPC and static frontend inside a Fastify scope with `prefix: /${box.slug}`.

verdict.note: src/webapp/server.ts createServer resolves boxes via resolveBoxes (server-lifecycle.ts, returning options.boxes when supplied) and loops calling registerBox per box; server-box-scope.ts registers the box's routes/tRPC/static frontend inside Fastify scopes with prefix `/${box.slug}` (lines 297-317, plus /webhook/<slug>). The CLI entry is src/cli/commands/serve.ts, which accepts multiple box dirs (`cb serve [dirs...]`), resolves each to a slug via its own resolveBoxes, and passes the BoxSpec[] to startServer. Note the boxes.json manifest is deliberately not consulted by serve (it feeds the scheduler; `cb hub` has its own manifest), but one process serving several boxes each under its slug prefix is exactly what the code does.

title: Ship an exact commit to the server
story: As an operator, I want the deploy to build from a clean checkout of a resolved commit sha and rsync from there, so that what runs in production always matches a commit rather than someone's working tree.
evidence: deploy.sh resolves `--ref` to a full sha, checks out detached into the shared `.deploy-checkout` with `git clean -fdx` (preserving node_modules unless the lockfile or patches changed), rsyncs from that checkout, and records the shipped hash in deploy-info.json for rollback.

verdict.note: callback-box/deploy/deploy.sh resolves --ref (default HEAD) to a full sha with `git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${RAW_REF}^{commit}"` and aborts if it doesn't resolve (line ~127), then `git -C "$CHECKOUT" checkout --detach --quiet "$SHA"` into the shared $MAIN_ROOT/.deploy-checkout plus `git clean -fdx -e node_modules -e .deploy-last-sha` (line ~227), wiping node_modules only when pnpm-lock.yaml or patches/ differ between the last and current sha (lines ~239-253). Every rsync source is "$CHECKOUT/..." (lines ~343-349 and the main sync), never the invoking working tree, and the shipped hash/subject are read from the checkout at $SHA (lines 505-506) and written to $INSTALL_DIR/callback-box/deploy-info.json (line 516), with the header documenting rollback via `deploy.sh --ref <old-sha>`.

title: Ship by committing, and read back what shipped
story: As a maintainer, I want a commit on main to launch the deploy by itself only when it touched a path the deploy actually ships, pinned to that commit's sha, with its own timestamped log I can tail, so that shipping is not a separate remembered step and two overlapping deploys cannot overwrite each other's output.
evidence: The root post-commit hook runs only on branch `main`, skips merge commits (post-merge covers those), and greps the commit's file list for `callback-box|agent-doctest|personal-vibe-check|patches` or the root pnpm files before deploying; it pre-flights `deploy/server-ip`, captures the trigger-time sha and passes it as `deploy.sh --ref`, and writes each run to `deploy/.deploy-logs/<ts>-<sha8>.log` with `.last-deploy.log` repointed as a relative symlink and the log dir pruned to 20.
