verdict.note: Read .husky/post-commit and .husky/post-merge in full. post-commit gates on BRANCH=main, skips merge commits (HEAD^2 check, delegating to post-merge), and greps `git diff-tree --name-only -r HEAD` for '^(callback-box|agent-doctest|personal-vibe-check|patches)/' or the root pnpm files before deploying; it pre-flights callback-box/deploy/server-ip, captures SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) and runs deploy.sh --ref "$SHA" backgrounded into callback-box/deploy/.deploy-logs/<UTC-ts>-<sha8>.log, with .last-deploy.log relinked as a relative symlink and `ls -1t | tail -n +21` pruning to 20. post-merge mirrors this for fast-forward/merge cases (fail-open on an uncomputable diff). deploy.sh accepts --ref and resolves it to a full sha (usage line at deploy.sh:42, parsing at ~line 105).

title: Stand up a box server from nothing
story: As an operator, I want one script to create the cloud VM, point DNS at it, and provision the host — packages, Node, Claude Code, the serve and scheduler services, and the nginx front door — so that a box fleet can be rebuilt from scratch rather than from a hand-tended machine.
evidence: create-server.sh provisions the `hcloud` server, registers the SSH key, writes the Cloudflare DNS record for the box hostname, then uploads and runs setup-server.sh, which apt-installs the media/PDF toolchain (including qpdf, which the scan routes hard-require), installs Node and the native Claude Code CLI for root and the `callback` user, writes and enables `callback-serve.service` and `callback-scheduler.service`, and installs the nginx reverse-proxy site.

verdict.note: callback-box/deploy/create-server.sh registers the SSH key with `hcloud ssh-key create`, creates the Hetzner server, writes deploy/server-ip, then updates/creates the Cloudflare A record for CF_DOMAIN via the API (and sets SSL flexible), waits for SSH, scps setup-server.sh and runs it. setup-server.sh line 22 apt-installs nginx, poppler-utils, imagemagick, ffmpeg, pandoc and qpdf (the PDF validator used by src/core/scan/validate.ts), installs Node via NodeSource (lines 30-38), installs the native Claude Code CLI for root and the callback user (lines 135-136), writes /etc/systemd/system/callback-serve.service and callback-scheduler.service (lines 201, 227) and enables/starts them (358-359), and writes plus enables the nginx reverse-proxy site (362-395). deploy/README.md documents the flow.

title: Start boxes on demand and stop idle ones
story: As an operator with many boxes on one machine, I want boxes to cold-start on their first request and stop when idle — except ones holding pending chat timers — so that a fleet fits on modest hardware without dropping scheduled work.
evidence: `Supervisor` implements `EndpointProvider.ensureRunning` with lazy start, `evaluateIdle` (which keeps a box alive when `boxHasPendingSchedules` or it's in the `keepRecent` set persisted in hub-state.json), and crash-loop backoff via crash-backoff.ts.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/hub/supervisor.ts implements ensureRunning(slug) (lazy cold-start on first request, dedup of concurrent launches; a no-op get() on non-lazy hubs), armIdleTimer -> evaluateIdle(slug) returning "stopped"|"kept"|"kept-schedule", where kept-schedule comes from boxHasPendingSchedules (pending-schedules.ts, which resolves the box root and calls loadChatSchedules — the same loader `cb serve` re-arms from, counting overdue entries) and "kept" from the keepRecent most-recently-active set backed by hub-state.ts (hub-state.json, slug->lastActivity). crash-backoff.ts supplies MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES=5 and exponential backoff. Lazy mode is opt-in via hub-config.ts `lazy` (default false), but that is exactly the operator-set knob the story's operator would turn on, and keepRecent>0 requires lazy:true.

title: Stop committing a box's binaries without losing them
story: As an operator, I want the already-tracked assets dropped from the git index only after every one of them is covered by a manifest, so that switching a long-running box to manifest tracking cannot delete a binary nothing else records.
evidence: `runUntrackAssets` (dispatched from `executeAttachments`'s `untrack-assets` case) lists tracked files matching the gitignore, skips those outside `.attach/` scopes, checks each remaining one against its scope's `loadManifest`, and refuses with "Run 'cb attachments migrate' first" when any is uncovered; otherwise it removes them from the index and reports that working-tree files are preserved.

verdict.note: src/core/commands/attachments-gitignore.ts:424 runUntrackAssets lists tracked-but-ignored files via listTrackedIgnored, partitions with partitionTrackedIgnored (reporting/skipping files outside .attach/ scopes), then findUncoveredAssets (line 356) loads each scope's manifest with loadManifest from core/asset-manifest.js and collects any file whose relative key is absent (an unreadable/missing manifest is treated as empty, so its files are uncovered). If uncovered.length > 0 it returns success:false with 'Run cb attachments migrate first'; otherwise gitRmCached drops them from the index and it prints 'Working-tree files are preserved.' Reachable: src/cli/commands/attachments.ts:46 registers `untrack-assets`, dispatching to executeAttachments' case at attachments.ts:83.

title: Summarize box state
story: As an agent, I want `cb status` to print the box's version, git cleanliness, engine-version match, inbox and schema-load problems, so that I can tell at a glance whether the box is in a sound state.
evidence: `statusCommand` calls getSystemState, getEngineVersionReport, listParkedTemplateUpdates and listSchemaLoadFailures and prints each section, with -v for detail.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/status.ts defines statusCommand ('cb status', -v/--verbose) and prints boxRoot + state.boxVersion from getSystemState (src/core/state.ts:127), an Engine line from getEngineVersionReport (src/core/engine-version.ts:61) including a MISMATCH note, 'Git: clean' / 'Git: uncommitted changes' with staged/modified/untracked counts under -v, inbox count, questions, parked template updates via listParkedTemplateUpdates, and schema load failures via loadBoxSchemas + listSchemaLoadFailures (plus legacy schema files). It is registered at src/cli/index.ts:96 (program.addCommand(statusCommand)).

title: Take upstream template updates without losing local edits
story: As a boxholder, I want re-running init to refresh shipped templates only when I have not edited them and park the new version for review when I have, so that engine updates reach my box without clobbering my customizations.
evidence: `installTemplateFile` hashes the local file against `config/template-versions.json`; a match overwrites with the new template, a divergence writes the new version to `config/_template-updates/<path>`, with `normalize` and `boxOwnedFields` handling volatile and box-owned fields.

verdict.note: src/core/install-template-file.ts installTemplateFile hashes the local file's canonical form (normalize + stripBoxOwnedFields) against config/template-versions.json; a match with the recorded hash (or one of priorStockHashes) overwrites via applyBoxOwnedFields (outcome "overwritten"), a divergence writes the new template into config/_template-updates/<relpath> (outcome "parked") without updating the recorded hash. src/core/template-stock-hashes.ts supplies TEMPLATE_STOCK_HASHES[...].superseded as priorStockHashes; src/core/box/templates.ts calls installTemplateFile for guides/procedures/schedules, and src/cli/commands/init.ts (`cb init`, initCommand, description "Initialize or update a callback box") invokes installProcedures/installGuides/installSchedules on every re-run.

title: The box mirrors itself to a git remote as it works
story: As a box agent, I want each wakeup to push the box's new commits to its configured upstream and report why it did not, so that a box with a remote keeps an off-machine copy of its whole history without a failed push ever aborting the cycle.
evidence: pushToRemote() returns a PushResult instead of throwing — `skipped` with a reason for no remote / no tracking branch / already up to date, `commitsPushed` from `status.ahead`, or `error` when the push itself fails. `cb wakeup` calls it as its final step and offers `--skip-push` to suppress it.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/lib/git.ts:474 pushToRemote() returns a PushResult (interface at line 458) rather than throwing: {skipped:true, reason:'no remote configured'} when git.getRemotes() is empty, 'no upstream tracking branch' when status.tracking is falsy, 'already up to date' when status.ahead===0, otherwise git.push() with commitsPushed=status.ahead, and a caught error returned as {error: errorMessage(err)}. callback-box/src/cli/commands/wakeup.ts defines pushChanges() (line ~144) as Step 6, logging the failure/skip-reason/pushed-count, and the action body at line 257-260 runs it last, guarded by `if (!options.skipPush)`; the flag is declared at line 166 as `--skip-push`. Nothing rethrows, so a failed push logs '⚠ push failed: …' and the wakeup completes.

title: Upgrade a box's engine as one revertible unit
story: As an operator, I want `cb upgrade --to <spec>` to bump the engine dependency, run migrations, sync templates and typecheck in one reviewable commit, so that a rollback reverts code and data together.
evidence: upgrade.ts refuses a dirty tree (`DirtyWorkingTreeError`), snapshots HEAD, bumps the dependency and installs, then spawns the newly installed `node_modules/.bin/cb` for migrate/template-sync/typecheck and commits once; rollback is a single `git reset --hard` at the package root.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/upgrade.ts defines `upgradeCommand` (`cb upgrade --to <spec>`, requiredOption --to), registered at src/cli/index.ts:95 via commands/index.ts. runUpgrade() does exactly the claimed sequence: getStatus() clean check throwing DirtyWorkingTreeError, getHead() snapshot, bumpCallbackBoxDependency() + `pnpm install`, then spawns packageRoot/node_modules/.bin/cb for `migrate --apply` and `init`, then node_modules/.bin/tsc -p ., then stageAll+commit once with an Upgraded-To trailer. Failure path revertUpgrade() calls revertToSnapshot (reset --hard + clean) at the package root so code and migrated box files revert together. core/migration-run.ts exists and backs `cb migrate`.

title: Upstream templates and hooks reach every box after a deploy
story: As an operator, I want the doc-generation pass that runs at the start of each reactor cycle to re-install upstream procedures, guides, schedules, card rules and git validation hooks whenever the running callback-box build has changed, and commit just those files, so that a deploy reaches existing boxes without me running `cb init` on each one and without dirtying their working trees.
evidence: `getCallbackBoxVersion` (core/docs-gen/index.ts) combines the `deploy-info.json` commit hash with the source git HEAD so `canSkipGeneration` misses after a deploy; the regeneration path then runs `syncTemplatesFromSource` (installProcedures/Guides/Personality/Briefing/Schedules, installSchemasGuide/installViewsGuide, generateRules, installValidationHooks, pruneStaleTemplateUpdates) and `commitTemplateSyncChanges` commits only paths matching `isTemplateManagedPath` as "Sync templates from upstream".

verdict.note: core/reactor/cycle.ts refreshDocsStage ("Stage 2: refresh agent docs") calls generateDocs(boxRoot) every cycle. In core/docs-gen/index.ts, getCallbackBoxVersion() joins `deploy:<hash>` read from deploy-info.json at PACKAGE_ROOT with `git:<HEAD>`, and canSkipGeneration() only skips when that combined string matches the marker from the previous run — so a deploy (which advances deploy-info.json but not the server's git HEAD) forces regeneration. The regeneration path calls syncTemplatesFromSource(), which runs installProcedures/installGuides/installPersonality/installBriefing/installSchedules (core/box/defaults.ts; installSchedules writes config/schedules/*.scheduled-script.card from createScheduledScriptTemplate), installSchemasGuide/installViewsGuide (core/box/templates.ts), generateRules (core/init-rules.ts, .claude/rules/ from card schemas), installValidationHooks (core/install-validation-hooks.ts, .claude/settings.json + .git pre/post-commit hooks) and pruneStaleTemplateUpdates. commitTemplateSyncChanges() then takes the box git lock, filters staged/modified/untracked paths through isTemplateManagedPath (install-template-file.ts) after toBoxRelativePath normalization, and commits only those with message "Sync templates from upstream" — matching the story's no-`cb init`, no-dirty-tree claim.

title: Verify a deploy actually left the fleet serving
story: As an operator, I want the deploy to check the hub's health verdict and cold-start one real box through a canary route, so that a fleet-wide startup break is caught by the deploy rather than by a user.
evidence: `GET /healthz` serves the `hubVerdict` derived from per-box statuses (503 when any box is broken) and `GET /healthz/canary` calls `ensureRunning` then fetches the box's own authenticated `/healthz`; both are gated on `CB_DIAG_API_KEY`, and deploy.sh polls them after restarting services.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/hub/hub-health-routes.ts registerHealthRoutes defines GET /healthz (serves getHealth(), replying 503 when status==="unhealthy") and GET /healthz/canary, which calls endpoints.ensureRunning(slug) then fetches ${endpoint.origin}/healthz with the CB_DIAG_API_KEY bearer and requires 200; both go through requireDiagKey (503 unconfigured / 401 wrong key). hub-health.ts hubVerdict()/isBoxBroken() derive the verdict from BoxRuntimeStatus[] (unhealthy if any box broken). callback-box/deploy/deploy.sh (~lines 590-692) reads CB_DIAG_API_KEY from /home/callback/.env, polls localhost:3210/healthz for up to ~180s judging the parsed status, then curls /healthz/canary and fails the deploy on a non-ok status, dumping /healthz for context. Story matches.

title: Verify annexed file bytes against their keys
story: As an operator, I want a paced, read-only integrity pass over the box's annexed content that names any objects git-annex quarantined as bad, so that silent bit-rot in attachments is found instead of discovered when a file is opened.
evidence: `GitAnnexService.fsck(repoRoot, { incrementalScheduleDays })` runs `git annex fsck` and returns an `AnnexFsckReport` (`clean`, `badPaths`, raw `output`); `cb doctor annex-fsck` (annexFsckSubcommand in cli/commands/doctor.ts) calls it, prints "annex fsck: no bad content" or lists the quarantined paths. It is read-only on purpose so it can be scheduled independently of wakeup, unlike the config-checking annex doctor.

verdict.note: src/services/git-annex.ts defines AnnexFsckReport {clean,badPaths,output} and GitAnnexService.fsck(repoRoot,{incrementalScheduleDays}) which runs `git annex fsck --incremental-schedule=<n>d` (paced), treats exit code as authority, and collects paths from lines matching 'Bad file content'/'No known copies exist'. src/cli/commands/doctor.ts registers annexFsckSubcommand as `cb doctor annex-fsck` (--days default 30, --box), printing 'annex fsck: no bad content' when clean or listing bad paths plus 'Quarantined under .git/annex/bad/'. doctorCommand is wired into the CLI at src/cli/index.ts:99. fsck is read-only and documented as schedule-run, separate from the config-checking `doctor annex` subcommand, matching the story.

title: Warn when a box grows unexpectedly
story: As a person using the box, I want a health warning when my box's file, directory or commit counts jump beyond what its history suggests, and a way to say 'this is expected', so that a runaway connector or automation is caught before it buries the box.
evidence: measureBoxGrowthIfDue() is called hourly from core/schedule/scheduler.ts; evaluateBoxGrowth() applies BOX_GROWTH_THRESHOLDS (absolute and per-hour, with connector-specific rates) and boxGrowthHealthCheck() returns actions acknowledge-box-growth / expect-box-growth-rates, which HealthWarnings.tsx renders as buttons wired to health-box-growth.ts.

verdict.note: core/box-growth/health.ts exports measureBoxGrowthIfDue (called from core/schedule/scheduler.ts:202 on the hourly tick, BOX_GROWTH_MEASUREMENT_INTERVAL_MS = 1h) and boxGrowthHealthCheck, which runs evaluateBoxGrowth (policy.ts) against BOX_GROWTH_THRESHOLDS covering absolute file/directory counts, per-hour file/directory/commit rates, and connector-specific rates, with the accepted-baseline multiplier deriving limits from the box's own prior measurement. When findings exist it returns actions acknowledge-box-growth / expect-box-growth-rates; HealthWarnings.tsx renders those as 'Acknowledge this growth' and 'Expect these rates' buttons (gated on canManageBoxGrowth, passed as isOwner from DashboardPage.tsx) wired to the mutations in webapp/trpc/routers/health-box-growth.ts (acknowledgeCurrentBoxGrowth / expectCurrentBoxGrowthRates). Commit-count findings confirmed via kind 'rate-commits' in policy.ts:165-170.

browser.note: The 'Box warnings' section renders health-check warnings (2 pending migrations; legacy secret files) but no box-growth warning is currently firing on this box, so I could not see the growth measurement or the 'this is expected' affordance. Reaching it would require making the box grow past thresholds.

title: Ask whether the box is quiet
story: As a script or field-test harness, I want one query reporting every live session's running/busy state, so that I can wait for the box to go idle before checking results.
evidence: `chat.statusAll` returns `registry.snapshotAll()` plus a box-wide `busy` flag, and answers `{initialized:false}` rather than throwing for a box whose chat runtime never started — the quiescence gate the field-test harness polls.

verdict.note: chat-control-procedures.ts:144 `statusAll: publicProcedure.query` returns `{initialized:false, busy:false, sessions:[]}` when getChatRuntime(ctx.boxRoot) is null, otherwise `{initialized:true, busy: sessions.some(s=>s.busy), sessions}` from registry.snapshotAll(). registry.ts:190 snapshotAll maps every held entry plus pending sessions to {sessionId, running, busy}. It is reachable to scripts: webapp/auth.ts:103 lists "chat.statusAll" on the diagnostic-key whitelist, and src/field-test/quiescence.ts:72 polls GET /api/trpc/chat.statusAll as its chat quiescence gate.

title: Audit what a box agent actually knows
story: As a maintainer, I want to run prompts against a real box agent and check what it demonstrably knows, so that I can tell whether guidance I wrote actually reached it.
evidence: `pnpm knowledge-audit run|list|eval` (src/dev/knowledge-audit.ts) executes the YAML-defined audits via createAgent against --box, parses transcripts for behaviour, and writes a markdown report; box-guard.ts refuses a box nested inside another repo before the between-test git reset runs.

verdict.note: callback-box/package.json has "knowledge-audit": "tsx src/dev/knowledge-audit.ts"; that file is a commander program with list, run and eval subcommands. run loads src/dev/knowledge-audits.yaml via loadTests(), calls assertStandaloneBox() from dev/lib/box-guard.ts (which refuses a box nested in an enclosing git repo precisely because runTest does `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fd`), regenerates docs, then runTest() in dev/lib/test-runner.ts executes each prompt against a real box agent via createAgent and parses the session transcript for files read/searches, and generateReport() from dev/lib/report.ts writes a markdown report.

title: Author a field-test scenario as a validated directory
story: As a maintainer, I want to author a field test as a directory of persona, checklist, check scripts, assets and email fixtures that is fully validated before a run starts, so that a typo in a scenario fails at load with every problem listed instead of halfway through a run that has already spent a box, a server and an operator session.
evidence: `loadFieldScenario` parses scenario.yaml against a strict zod schema (name, description, startTime, models, checklist of id/brief/pre/cleanup/checks/questions), requires persona.md, and `referenceProblems` collects every cross-file failure in one pass — duplicate checklist ids, a check that is not a bare filename in checks/, an asset reference in a brief that escapes or misses assets/, and an inject-email fixture with no emails/<name>.yaml.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/field-test/scenario.ts: ScenarioFileSchema is a zod strictObject over name (kebab id), description, startTime (ISO w/ offset), optional models.operator/chat, and checklist of strictObject{id,brief,pre,cleanup,checks,questions}; readPersona() makes persona.md mandatory; referenceProblems() accumulates every cross-file failure in one pass — duplicate checklist ids, a check that is not a bare filename (path.basename !== check) or missing from checks/, an assets/... brief reference that escapes assetsDir or does not exist, and an inject-email pre action with no emails/<fixture>.yaml — then loadFieldScenario throws FieldScenarioInvalidError with the whole problems list. loadFieldScenario is the first statement of runFieldScenario (src/field-test/run.ts:186) and is also invoked directly by the `cb field-test` command (src/cli/commands/field-test.ts:105), so validation precedes any box/server spin-up. field-tests/spine/ and field-tests/onboarding-first-days/ exist with persona.md, checks/, assets/ (and emails/ for the latter).

title: Be told when the pinned document extractor has gone stale
story: As an operator, I want a watch that compares the pinned Docling release against PyPI and speaks up only when a settled newer release exists, so that a deliberate pin does not rot silently while extraction output stays reproducible.
evidence: `DOCLING_VERSION` in docling-version.ts is the single pin, parsed (not imported) by `bin/check-docling-update.ts` (`pnpm check-docling-update`), which prints one line only when PyPI's newest release is above the pin and older than the settling window; it exits 0 always and is wired into the daily maintenance log.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/services/docling-version.ts holds `export const DOCLING_VERSION = "2.117.0"` and is the single pin — imported by src/services/docling.ts (uvx --from docling==VERSION) and text-parsed by deploy/setup-server.sh and bin/check-docling-update.ts. That script regex-parses the pin, fetches https://pypi.org/pypi/docling/json, and exits 0 silently unless compareVersions(latest,pinned) > 0 AND the release is older than SETTLING_DAYS=14; otherwise it prints the available-version line plus a manual-upgrade instruction line. It is wired as `check-docling-update` in the root package.json and invoked from bin/update-agent-sdk-scheduled.sh:110 (daily maintenance), and documented in callback-box/docs/maintenance.md lines 17 and 76.

title: Browse prompts and watch them grow
story: As a maintainer, I want the prompt-browser page's data regenerated — inventory, assembled situations, duplication report and a size ledger — so that I can see overlapping prompt text and whether prompt size is creeping up.
evidence: `pnpm prompt-viewer --box <path>` writes dev/prompts/data.json and appends to the tracked dev/prompts/size-ledger.jsonl when the numbers changed; duplication.ts reports contiguous shared spans of >= 12 words between fragments.

verdict.note: callback-box/package.json line 63 defines the script `prompt-viewer: tsx src/dev/prompt-viewer.ts`. prompt-viewer.ts parseArgs accepts --box/--no-ledger, calls buildViewerData() and writes dev/prompts/data.json, then compares the last line of dev/prompts/size-ledger.jsonl and only appends a LedgerLine when {situations,fragments} changed (else prints 'ledger unchanged'). prompt-viewer-data.ts builds `situations`, `inventory`, `duplication`, and `fragmentIndex` into the ViewerData; dev/prompts/ contains the hand-written index.html plus the tracked size-ledger.jsonl. duplication.ts uses 8-word shingles with MIN_SPAN_WORDS = 12 and reports maximal same-diagonal (contiguous in both fragments) runs of >= 12 words.

title: Browser CSP violations are collected and digested
story: As an operator, I want the app to ship one Content-Security-Policy for both dev and prod and log the violations browsers report against it, so that I can see what a policy would break before promoting it from report-only to enforcing.
evidence: `buildCspPolicy({mode, reportPath})` is the single policy shared by the Fastify `onSend` hook (`registerCspReportingHeaders`, which only stamps `text/html` responses and yields to routes with their own CSP) and the Vite dev server; `routes/api-csp-report.ts` is the unauthenticated root-level sink that normalizes both the legacy and Reporting-API wire shapes into a capped rolling JSONL log that `src/dev/csp-digest.ts` reads back by cursor.

verdict.note: src/lib/csp.ts `buildCspPolicy({mode, reportPath})` is the single builder (COMMON_DIRECTIVES + mode-specific script/style) used by both src/frontend/vite.config.ts:40 (dev, Report-Only) and registerCspReportingHeaders in src/webapp/server-root.ts:100, whose Fastify onSend hook stamps Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only + Reporting-Endpoints only on text/html responses and skips replies that already set a CSP. src/webapp/routes/api-csp-report.ts registerCspReportRoute is registered root-level and unauthenticated at PROD_CSP_REPORT_PATH (server.ts:210), normalizing both application/csp-report and Reporting-API array shapes into a capped, rolling-truncated JSONL log at <box>/.callback-box/csp-reports.log. src/dev/csp-digest.ts (npm script `pnpm csp-digest`) reads that log incrementally via a per-box cursor and reports what an enforcing policy would break.

title: Build on callback-box as a package
story: As a box author writing card schemas or embedding the server, I want callback-box to expose its validator dependencies, its server entry point and its view widgets as declared package exports, so that a box depends on callback-box alone rather than pinning zod and yaml itself.
evidence: package.json's `exports` map names `./schema` (re-exporting `z` and yaml parse/stringify), `./server` (`createServer`/`startServer`/`DEFAULT_PORT`, side-effect-free), `./cards` and `./view-widgets` (CardLink/CardRef/NodeViewHostProvider types).

verdict.note: callback-box/package.json has an `exports` map with ./cards, ./schema, ./server, ./view-widgets (and ./tsconfig.base.json). src/exports/schema.ts re-exports `z` from zod and `parse as parseYaml`/`stringify as stringifyYaml` from yaml, with a docblock stating boxes import z from here rather than declaring their own zod/yaml deps. src/exports/server.ts re-exports createServer/startServer/DEFAULT_PORT from ../webapp/server.js (all three confirmed exported at server.ts:54, :89, :271) plus BoxSpec/ServerOptions/ServerContext types, and is a pure re-export with no side effects (the side-effectful boot stays in webapp/server-main.ts). src/exports/view-widgets.d.ts declares CardLink, CardRef and NodeViewHostProvider component types.

title: Capture full agent prompt traffic and session provenance for debugging
story: As someone debugging a box, I want to log an agent run's full API traffic and to see which session id belongs to which task, so that I can inspect what the agent was actually told.
evidence: With `CB_LOG_PROMPTS=1`, `setupRunEnv` starts `startPromptLogger` and points the run's `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at the local proxy writing `.callback-box/logs/<hint>.log`; independently, each agent's first invoke calls `appendSessionManifest` to record `{sessionId, task, timestamp}` in `store/usage/session-manifest.jsonl`.

verdict.note: src/core/agent/run.ts `setupRunEnv` reads `process.env.CB_LOG_PROMPTS === "1"`, calls `startPromptLogger(boxRoot, filenameHint)` and, when it comes up, sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: http://localhost:<port>/` in the SDK env. prompt-logger.ts spawns `npx claude-code-logger start --verbose --log-body --merge-sse` and streams to `<boxRoot>/.callback-box/logs/<hint>.log`. Independently, src/core/agent/index.ts (and codex-agent.ts) call `appendSessionManifest` on the first session id, writing `{sessionId, task, timestamp}` JSONL to `store/usage/session-manifest.jsonl` (manifest.ts). CB_LOG_PROMPTS is allowlisted in script-env-allowlist.ts / hub/child-env.ts so an operator can set it.

title: Dev harness pages for chat surfaces
story: As a developer, I want dev-build-only routes that render the composer's states, capture mode against a fake API, and the speech replay menu against mock TTS, so that I can inspect and script those surfaces without a device or backend.
evidence: router.tsx adds devSpeechRoute (/dev/speech), devComposerStatesRoute (/dev/composer-states) and devCaptureModeRoute (/dev/capture-mode) only when import.meta.env.DEV; the harnesses render the real components — ComposerStatesHarness the cross-product of composer axes with `?state=` isolation, CaptureModeHarness the overlay over an in-memory CaptureApi, SpeechTestHarness the SpeechMenu with window.__speechTestLog for an external driver.

verdict.note: router.tsx lines 208-227 define devSpeechRoute (/dev/speech), devComposerStatesRoute (/dev/composer-states) and devCaptureModeRoute (/dev/capture-mode), spread into the box layout children only under `(import.meta.env !== undefined && import.meta.env.DEV)` (line 269). All three harness files exist under src/frontend/src/pages/dev/components/: ComposerStatesHarness.tsx renders the real ChatComposerSection/ChatInputArea/MobileTextareaRow across a declared axis cross-product with `?state=<key>` isolation (data-state attribute at line 254); CaptureModeHarness.tsx mounts CaptureOverlay/CaptureBubbleView/CaptureChip inside a CaptureApiProvider wrapping an in-memory fake CaptureApi (line 284); SpeechTestHarness.tsx renders the real SpeechMenu + useSpeechPlayback against the backend mock TTS and installs window.__speechTestLog/__speechState for an external driver.

browser.note: All three dev-only routes exist and render under the dev (vite) build: /dev/composer-states shows the 37-combination composer gallery (idle/typing/recording/paused/speaking x narration x muted x streaming, plus idle-keyboard, typing-keyboard, and the -locked variants, plus recording-empty) with the 8 impossible muted+speech combos listed and explained; ?state=<id> isolates a single card (e.g. ?state=idle-keyboard renders only that composer, no gallery header or impossible list). /dev/capture-mode renders the pending-capture bubble across its captions against in-memory data with no backend. /dev/speech renders the SpeechMenu harness with mocked slow TTS (500ms delay, 80ms/chunk), Play all / Reset log controls, a live isPlaying/segment/remaining state line, and states it records events on window.__speechTestLog. All are real components, not mockups.

title: Drive the app from a headless browser
story: As an agent or script driving the app, I want the page to advertise when it has finished fetching and to expose stable provenance attributes on rendered content, so that automation can wait for readiness and know which card a region came from.
evidence: TrpcProvider sets body.dataset.cbLoading from useIsFetching/useIsMutating (starting 'true' at module load) and clears React's onclick trap that pollutes the accessibility tree; cbSource()/cbSourceItem() emit the data-cb-source provenance attributes; useDocumentTitle sets and restores the page title.

title: Invoke any box command over HTTP with its output streamed back
story: As a script or agent driving a box remotely, I want to list the box's registered commands and run one over HTTP or tRPC while its output streams back line by line, so that anything the CLI can do can be driven from outside the box host without a shell.
evidence: `registerCommand`/`listCommands`/`runCommand` in core/command-runner.ts hold one registry that CLI, other commands, and the web share; `commandsRouter` (trpc/routers/commands.ts) exposes `list`, `get` and `executeSync` and is mounted in trpc/router.ts, while `registerCommandRoutes` (webapp/routes/commands.ts, wired in server-box-scope.ts) runs the same command through `executeCommandStreaming`, emitting `{type:"output"}` lines as SSE and a final `{type:"result"}`.

verdict.note: The streaming-over-HTTP half does not exist. src/webapp/routes/commands.ts defines executeCommandStreaming(), but a repo-wide grep for that symbol finds only its own definition — no caller, no test — and registerCommandRoutes() (the function wired in server-box-scope.ts:262) registers exactly one route, POST /api/upload, which writes an uploaded file to the box tmp dir. There is no SSE or any other HTTP route that runs a command, and no route emitting {type:"output"} lines. What actually exists is the tRPC commandsRouter (src/webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts, mounted at trpc/router.ts:38) with list/get/executeSync, and executeSync is non-streaming: it buffers ctx.write/writeLine into outputLines and returns them only in the final response.

panel.note: The registry and the non-streaming tRPC surface exist and are wired: src/core/command-runner.ts holds registerCommand/listCommands/runCommand, and commandsRouter (src/webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts) exposes list/get/executeSync and is imported and mounted at src/webapp/trpc/router.ts:8,38. The streaming-over-HTTP half is not wired: registerCommandRoutes (src/webapp/routes/commands.ts:79), the function called from server-box-scope.ts:262, registers exactly one route — POST /api/upload, which writes an uploaded file to the box tmp dir — and no route in src/webapp/routes/ sets text/event-stream or invokes a command. executeCommandStreaming is exported from that same file but a repo-wide grep finds importers only in test/core/command-streaming.doctest.md and test/webapp/routes/ls-format.doctest.md; nothing in src/ calls it, so no HTTP path emits the {type:"output"} lines the story describes. executeSync buffers ctx.write/writeLine into outputLines and returns them only in the final response, so it is not a line-by-line stream either.

Half the story is reachable, half has no entry point. commandsRouter (webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts) exposes list/get/executeSync as publicProcedures and is mounted at trpc/router.ts:38 (`commands: commandsRouter`), so a remote script can enumerate the registry filled by the ~20 registerCommand() calls in core/commands/* and run one — but executeSync buffers ctx.write/writeLine into `outputLines` and returns them only in the final mutation response, so nothing streams. The streaming path has no entry point at all: executeCommandStreaming() in webapp/routes/commands.ts:38 has zero callers repo-wide (grep finds only its own definition), and registerCommandRoutes() — the function wired at server-box-scope.ts:262 — registers exactly one route, POST /api/upload, which writes an uploaded file to the box tmp dir. There is no SSE or other HTTP route that runs a command or emits {type:"output"} lines, so 'run one over HTTP ... while its output streams back line by line' is unreachable as written.

The story's core qualifier -- running a command over HTTP/tRPC 'while its output streams back line by line' -- is not delivered. registerCommandRoutes() in callback-box/src/webapp/routes/commands.ts registers exactly one route, POST /api/upload; the exported executeCommandStreaming() in the same file has no caller anywhere in the repo (grep for the symbol returns only its own definition), so no SSE or other route emits {type:'output'} lines. The only reachable path is trpc/routers/commands.ts executeSync, which buffers ctx.write/writeLine into an outputLines array and returns it all in the single mutation response -- batched, not streamed. The benefit clause also over-claims: ~22 registerCommand() call sites back the shared registry against ~61 .command( definitions in src/cli, so 'anything the CLI can do' is not what the registry exposes.

triage.reasoning: All three lenses refuted, and the code agrees. The registry half is live: registerCommand/listCommands/runCommand in core/commands/, and commandsRouter (webapp/trpc/routers/commands.ts) exposing list/get/executeSync, mounted at webapp/trpc/router.ts:38 — a remote script really can enumerate and run commands. The streaming half does not exist: registerCommandRoutes (webapp/routes/commands.ts), the function wired at server-box-scope.ts:262, registers exactly one route, POST /api/upload; a repo-wide grep for text/event-stream in src returns nothing; executeCommandStreaming is still exported from that file but its only importers are test/core/command-streaming.doctest.md and test/webapp/routes/ls-format.doctest.md. executeSync buffers ctx.write/writeLine into an outputLines array and returns it in the single mutation response — batched, not line-by-line. The SSE route was deliberately deleted (3fd5e4c9 removed the web-UI bare-command buttons and the execute SSE route; 898699ab removed the remaining raw /api/commands handlers as superseded by tRPC), and nothing calls the streaming helper, so no user or caller is broken. The story should be rewritten to the surviving capability (list/get/run over tRPC, output returned in the response) and drop both 'streams back line by line' and 'anything the CLI can do' (~22 registerCommand call sites vs far more CLI .command( definitions). Separately worth a code-quality note, not a product issue: executeCommandStreaming is now exercised only by two doctests for a route that no longer exists.

title: Land extracted site nuggets only when their quotes are real

title: Read diagnostics for a send or scroll problem that only happens on a phone

title: Trace which generated doc reached the prompt
story: As a maintainer, I want generated docs stamped with DOCID markers when I ask for it, so that I can tell which generated file contributed a line of an agent's context.
evidence: `withDocId` (core/docs-gen/shared.ts) prepends `<!-- DOCID:<path> -->` to each generated file; `setDocIdDebug` writes/removes the `.callback-box/docid-debug` marker, driven by `cb init --docid-debug` / `--no-docid-debug` (cli/commands/init.ts).

verdict.note: core/docs-gen/shared.ts withDocId returns `<!-- DOCID:<relativePath> -->\n<content>` when debug is set, and is applied to every generated file in docs-gen/index.ts (agent guide, cb-commands.md, connectors.md, card docs, etc.) and compile.ts. index.ts defines DOCID_DEBUG_MARKER = ".callback-box/docid-debug", a stat-based check that defaults the debug flag, and setDocIdDebug to write/remove it. cli/commands/init.ts imports setDocIdDebug, exposes `--docid-debug` (line 249), calls it at line 182 when the option is set, then regenerates docs and prints the DOCID-enabled notice. Off by default, opt-in per the story's "when I ask for it".

title: Track always-on context size over time
story: As a maintainer, I want each audit run to record the box's baseline and peak loaded context against both git HEADs, so that trimming a box's context shows up as a trend rather than a number I eyeball.
evidence: context-usage.ts sums input + cache_creation + cache_read tokens per assistant turn to get real loaded context; context-history.ts appends a dated entry keyed by box basename and audit id, stamped with the box and monorepo HEADs, into the committed context-history.yaml.

verdict.note: context-usage.ts loadedContextTokens() sums input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens per assistant turn, and summarizeContextUsage() reduces to initialTokens (baseline) / peakTokens / addedTokens / turnCount. context-history.ts recordRun() loads src/dev/context-history.yaml, appends ContextHistoryEntry{date, boxCommit, repoCommit, initial, peak, added, turns} keyed by box basename -> audit id, and writes it back. The caller is src/dev/knowledge-audit.ts (the `knowledge-audit run` command, lines ~148 and ~201): it captures boxCommit = gitHead(resolvedBox) before doc regeneration and repoCommit = gitHead(PACKAGE_ROOT), so both HEADs are stamped. The committed yaml already carries multi-date series per audit id, and report.ts consumes priorHistory to show deltas; audit-box.ts is the box-identity helper rather than the appender, but it is one of several implementing files.

title: Track token usage
story: As a maintainer, I want session logs synced into a queryable usage database, so that I can ask in SQL what the box's agent work is costing.
evidence: `usageCommand` offers --sync (session manifest + Claude Code session logs into SQLite), --sql <query> printed as an aligned table, and --schema.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/usage.ts defines usageCommand with --sync, --sql <query> and --schema, registered in src/cli/index.ts (program.addCommand(usageCommand)). It delegates to syncUsage/queryUsage/USAGE_SCHEMA_DESCRIPTION in src/core/usage.ts, which opens a better-sqlite3 DB, reads store/usage/session-manifest.jsonl for task attribution and parses ~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/<sessionId>.jsonl logs into a usage table of input/output/cache token counts. --sql auto-syncs then prints rows via printTable (aligned table); the default invocation syncs and prints a per-task/model token summary.

title: View the generated site without remembering to rebuild it
story: As a maintainer, I want the dev router to serve the site at /<worktree>/site/ and rebuild it on request whenever the sources no longer match what dist was built from, so that I can look at the front door mid-edit and never be shown a stale build.
evidence: router-site.ts resolves a request under `/<name>/site/` to a file in `site/dist/`, calls `ensureBuilt`, which consults `isStale(siteDir, distRoot)` against the content-hash input manifest `dist/.inputs.json` and runs `pnpm --dir site build` when it drifts; builds are serialized per site dir by a `buildLocks` map and a failure surfaces as a 500 carrying the build's error text.

verdict.note: bin/router.ts:1237-1245 dispatches /<name>/site and /<name>/site/... to serveSite() in bin/router-site.ts, which sets Cache-Control no-store, resolves rel under repoRoot/site/dist via resolveSiteTarget (traversal guard, index.html for dirs, 301 to trailing slash), and calls ensureBuilt() before serving. ensureBuilt consults isStale(siteDir, distRoot) from site/sources.ts, which compares dist/.inputs.json (schema-validated, content sha256 hashes of package.json, top-level *.ts, and everything under content/) against a fresh hashSources(); missing/unparseable manifest or any read error returns true (rebuild). Builds are serialized per siteDir by the buildLocks Map and the default runner is execa('pnpm', ['--dir','site','build']); a SiteBuildError is surfaced as a 500 containing the build's stderr/stdout.

title: Ambient todo line in agent context
story: As the box's agent, I want a one-line count of on-plate todos injected into my prompt when there are any, so that I mention outstanding work without being asked to go look for it.
evidence: `computeTodoAmbientLine` (core/todo/ambient-summary.ts) returns "N open todos on the plate (M escalated) — `cb todos`" or null when empty; it is consumed by the reactor prompt and the chat per-turn snapshot rather than persisted.

verdict.note: core/todo/ambient-summary.ts exports computeTodoAmbientLine(boxRoot), which calls collectTodos (core/todo/collect.ts), filters plateState 'escalated'|'on-plate', returns null when empty, and otherwise returns `N open todos on the plate (M escalated) — \`cb todos\``. It is called in core/session-context.ts:266 (set as out.todos on the per-turn chat snapshot, computed fresh each send, not persisted) and in the reactor prompts via core/reactor/batch-jobs.ts:42 and chat-jobs.ts:50, both passing ambientLine into buildReactorUserPrompt. Only-when-nonzero behavior matches the story's 'when there are any'.

title: Attach a guide to a kind of job
story: As the box's agent, I want a guide card to declare which job types it applies to and have that produce a rule keyed on those job cards, so that the right guidance loads when I pick up that kind of work instead of me having to know which guide to read.
evidence: `compileConfigGuides` (core/docs-gen/compile.ts) compiles each `config/*.guide.card` to `docs/generated/<name>-guide.md` and builds a jobType→guides map from the card's `jobTypes`, writing one `.claude/rules/guides-for-<jobType>.md` per type whose frontmatter `paths` is `**/*.<jobType>.card` and whose body lists each guide with its `appliesTo` line and compiled path.

verdict.note: core/docs-gen/compile.ts compileConfigGuides scans config/*.guide.card, compiles each to `docs/generated/<name>-guide.md` (DOCS_DIR from shared.ts), and accumulates jobTypeMap from parsed.jobTypes (guide-parse.tsx maps the card field 'job-types' to jobTypes, 'applies-to' to appliesTo). For each job type it writes `<boxRoot>/.claude/rules/guides-for-<jobType>.md` with frontmatter `paths: - "**/*.<jobType>.card"` and a body listing `- **config/<file>.guide.card> — <appliesTo>` plus the compiled reference path. compileGuides (compile.ts:112) is called from generateDocs at core/docs-gen/index.ts:506, so the rules are produced on normal doc generation.

title: Be steered off a move that would break the box's links
story: As the box's agent, I want to be told mid-run when a `git mv` on box content would leave inbound refs dangling, so that I reach for `cb mv` and the box's links keep resolving after a reorganization.
evidence: `gitMvNudgeHook` (core/sdk-hooks.ts) is a PreToolUse Bash matcher that detects `git mv` touching a `store/` path or a `.card` and injects `GIT_MV_NUDGE` as additionalContext — advisory, never blocking. It is installed on every background agent run (`hooks: { PreToolUse: [gitMvNudgeHook()] }` in agent/run.ts buildQueryOptions) and on every chat run (services/claude-chat.ts:128).

verdict.note: src/core/sdk-hooks.ts defines `gitMvNudgeHook()` with `matcher: "Bash"`, returning early unless hook_event_name is PreToolUse and `isGitMvOnBoxContent(command)` matches (`git mv` plus a `store/` path or `.card` token); it returns hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext = GIT_MV_NUDGE, which recommends `cb mv` because git mv doesn't rewrite inbound refs — no deny/block decision, so it is advisory. It is installed unconditionally at src/core/agent/run.ts:90 (`hooks: { PreToolUse: [gitMvNudgeHook()] }`) and src/services/claude-chat.ts:128. `cb mv` exists (src/cli/commands/move.ts, `new Command("mv")`).

title: Briefing Markdoc rendered into agent context
story: As a box agent, I want Markdoc-tagged card bodies such as the briefing emitted as plain markdown, so that guidance I am given through CLAUDE.md reads correctly in a harness that has no Markdoc awareness.
evidence: emitBodyAsMarkdown() (core/markdoc/emit.ts) walks a parsed Markdoc body via emit-nodes.ts and renders the briefing vocabulary tags (purpose, key-person, correction, property, project-phase, see-also) in emit-tags.ts; schemas/briefing.tsx calls it when compiling the briefing.

verdict.note: emitBodyAsMarkdown (src/core/markdoc/emit.ts:43) parses the body with Markdoc.parse and walks it via emitNode (emit-nodes.ts), deliberately avoiding Markdoc.format; emit-tags.ts renders universal tags (quote, source, todo, see-also) plus briefing tags purpose/correction and the recipe vocabulary, with unknown tags falling back to inner text. schemas/briefing.tsx:165 calls it inside compileBriefing, and core/docs-gen/compile.ts compileBriefings writes the result to briefing.md 'so CLAUDE.md can include them'. One evidence nit that does not affect the story: key-person/property moved to briefing frontmatter (emitted as **Label:** lines by compileBriefing, not emit-tags) and project-phase was retired (emit-tags.ts:146-149).

title: Build a course out of linked card types
story: As a boxholder building a learning experience, I want course, concept-map, exposition-plan, lesson-plan, progress and figure card types that reference one another, so that the topic graph, how to present it, the delivery order, and each learner's evidence-backed understanding are separate, checkable cards.
evidence: CourseSchema is the manifest binding a concept-map, exposition-plan, lesson-plan, material and progress; ConceptMapSchema validates its node/edge graph via conceptMapErrors, LessonPlanSchema tags segments interactive vs material against concept-map nodes, and templates-courseware.ts registers a create template for each.

verdict.note: src/schemas/course.ts defines CourseSchema with ComponentRef fields concept-map, exposition-plan, lesson-plan, material and progress; concept-map.ts has conceptMapErrors() wired as CardSchema.validate for the in-card node/edge graph plus an orphan-node warning; lesson-plan.ts defines SegmentMode = enum(['interactive','material']) with a `concepts` list of concept-map node ids and material refs; progress.ts records per-node status/basis with evidence: z.array(z.string()).min(1). All six schemas (including FigureSchema) are imported and listed in schemas/registry.ts, and templates-courseware.ts registerTemplate()s create templates for concept-map, course, exposition-plan, lesson-plan and progress.

title: Card-type rules loaded on edit
story: As a box agent, I want each card type's instructions to auto-load as a `.claude/rules/` file when I open or edit a matching card, so that I follow the right conventions for that card type without reading a global guide.
evidence: generateRules() in core/init-rules.ts emits one path-scoped rule per card schema carrying `instructions`, plus connector file rules; refresh-derived-rules.ts recompiles guide- and exposition-plan-derived rules from the `cb validate` PostToolUse hook so an edit refreshes the rule in-session.

verdict.note: core/init-rules.ts generateRules() iterates built-in cardSchemas plus loadBoxSchemas() box-local schemas, and for each type with `instructions` writes .claude/rules/card-<type>.md with frontmatter `paths: - "**/*.<type>.card"`, so Claude Code path-loads it when a matching card is read/edited; it also writes the connectorRules files. It is invoked from cli/commands/init.ts:169 and core/docs-gen/index.ts:270. core/refresh-derived-rules.ts refreshDerivedRules() is called from the cb validate PostToolUse hook (cli/commands/validate-hook.ts:111) and recompiles guide/exposition-derived rules on edit, matching the supporting evidence.

title: CLAUDE.md that stays wired up but stays mine
story: As a boxholder, I want my box's CLAUDE.md created if absent and kept pointing at the generated agent guide and my current briefing files — adding what's missing at the top and dropping includes for briefings that no longer exist — so that I can hand-write box guidance in that file without the generator ever overwriting it.
evidence: `ensureClaudeMdIncludes` seeds a new CLAUDE.md with `@.callback-box/agent-guide.md` plus each compiled briefing path, otherwise splices only the missing `@` lines in after the existing leading includes and filters out stale briefing includes, rewriting the file only when something changed. `ensureAgentContext` is called from `generateDocs`.

verdict.note: src/core/docs-gen/index.ts:518 calls ensureAgentContext(boxRoot, briefingPaths) inside generateDocs; ensureAgentContext (src/core/docs-gen/claude-md.ts:14) calls ensureClaudeMdIncludes. That function builds requiredIncludes = ['@.callback-box/'+AGENT_GUIDE_FILE, ...briefingPaths.map(p=>'@'+p)]; when CLAUDE.md is missing it writes a seed file of just those lines, otherwise it splices any missing include in after the leading run of '@' lines, filters out '@...briefing....md' lines not in requiredIncludes, and writes back only if `changed`. Hand-written prose below the includes is never rewritten.

title: Generated agent guide and reference docs
story: As the box's agent, I want the box to compile its guides, personality, briefings, procedures and card-type instructions into an always-loaded agent guide plus on-demand reference docs, so that I start every run knowing this box's rules and commands.
evidence: `generateDocs` (core/docs-gen/index.ts) — called from `cb init` and the reactor — writes `.callback-box/agent-guide.md` and `docs/generated/*.md` (cb-commands, procedures, triage, connectors, views, per-card-type docs), compiles guides/personalities/briefings via compile.ts, and keeps CLAUDE.md's @-includes pointed at them (claude-md.ts) behind an mtime+source-commit skip cache.

verdict.note: core/docs-gen/index.ts generateDocs writes .callback-box/agent-guide.md (via generateAgentGuide from core/agent-guide/index.ts, composed from laws.ts/cards.ts/box-shape.ts/sections.ts) and docs/generated/*.md — connectors.md, views.md (core/views/doc.ts), procedures.md, triage.md, cb-commands, narration-mode/python-tools/reducing-claude-md, plus one card-<type>.md per schema built from the schema's `instructions` field (src/cards/schema.ts) through generateCardDoc. compile.ts supplies scanProcedures/compilePersonalities/compileGuides/compileBriefings feeding the guide; claude-md.ts ensureAgentContext keeps the '@.callback-box/agent-guide.md' include in CLAUDE.md. It is called from cb init (cli/commands/init.ts:213), the reactor cycle (core/reactor/cycle.ts:105) and chat start-run, behind an input-mtime + source-commit skip cache keyed on .callback-box/docs-generated-at.

title: Give a Codex chat the box's own guidance
story: As a boxholder running chats on Codex, I want the box's CLAUDE.md and the files it @-includes folded into the Codex session's developer instructions, so that a Codex chat follows the same box guidance a Claude chat gets from the harness reading CLAUDE.md itself.
evidence: Before the first turn, codex-chat.ts finds the box root and runs `expandClaudeIncludes({claudePath: join(boxRoot, "CLAUDE.md"), packageRoot})`, joining the result onto `opts.systemPrompt`; `CodexSdkSession` passes that combined string to the SDK as `new Codex({config: {developer_instructions: ...}})`.

verdict.note: The mechanism is narrower than the story states. src/services/codex-chat.ts:47-54 does call expandClaudeIncludes({claudePath: join(boxRoot,'CLAUDE.md'), packageRoot}) and joins the result onto opts.systemPrompt, which CodexSdkSession passes as `new Codex({config:{developer_instructions: options.systemPrompt}})` (src/services/codex-sdk-session.ts:174-175). But src/core/agent-context-includes.ts's expandClaudeIncludes reads CLAUDE.md ONLY to harvest `@file.md` include lines: `sections` accumulates the contents of the included files, never the body of CLAUDE.md itself, so the box's CLAUDE.md text is NOT folded into developer_instructions. CLAUDE.md is expected to reach Codex through a generated AGENTS.md symlink (src/core/agent-context-mirrors.ts mirrorClaudeDocs), and the primary test box ~/src/boxes/test1 has no AGENTS.md at all, so the story over-claims what the cited code does.

panel.note: The chain is live end to end: src/services/claude-chat.ts:386 wires createCodexChatBackend into createChatBackend and dispatches engine==="codex" to it; codex-chat.ts:47-58 imports expandClaudeIncludes from src/core/agent-context-includes.ts, calls it with {claudePath: join(boxRoot,'CLAUDE.md'), packageRoot: (await getBoxShape(boxRoot)).packageRoot}, joins the result onto opts.systemPrompt, and hands it to createCodexSdkSession, whose constructor (codex-sdk-session.ts:174) does new Codex({config:{developer_instructions: options.systemPrompt}}). Nothing here is dead code. The prior verifier's objection is semantic (expandClaudeIncludes accumulates only the @-included files' bodies, not CLAUDE.md's own text, which instead reaches Codex via the generated AGENTS.md symlink in src/core/agent-context-mirrors.ts mirrorClaudeDocs, itself wired through src/core/docs-gen/claude-md.ts) — that is a question of what the code means, not whether it exists and is connected, so it falls outside this lens.

The path is fully wired for a boxholder in the web UI: AdminPage (route /admin in src/frontend/src/router.tsx:172-176) renders AgentEngineSection's RadioGroup with a 'Codex' option, which calls trpc admin.updateBoxConfig({agentEngine}) (src/webapp/trpc/routers/admin.ts:229-251, z.enum(["claude","codex"])). That config is read by loadAgentEngine (src/core/box/config.ts:112-119) via resolveChatEngine (src/core/chat/session/engine.ts) into ChatBackendStartOptions.engine (src/core/chat/session/start.ts:123-140), and createChatBackend dispatches engine==="codex" to createCodexChatBackend (src/services/claude-chat.ts:383-390), whose run calls expandClaudeIncludes({claudePath: join(boxRoot,'CLAUDE.md')}) and joins it into the systemPrompt passed to CodexSdkSession's developer_instructions (src/services/codex-chat.ts:46-58). Nothing here sits behind an off-by-default flag; the only default is agentEngine='claude', flippable from the rendered control. The earlier verdict objects to what expandClaudeIncludes actually folds in, which is an accuracy question, not a reachability one.

The story says the box's CLAUDE.md AND the files it @-includes are folded into the Codex session's developer instructions; the code folds in only the @-included files. expandClaudeIncludes (callback-box/src/core/agent-context-includes.ts) reads CLAUDE.md solely to match ^@file.md lines and pushes only each included file's contents into `sections`, returning sections.join("\n\n") — the CLAUDE.md body is never appended. codex-chat.ts:47-54 joins that string onto opts.systemPrompt, and codex-sdk-session.ts:175 passes it as config.developer_instructions, so the developer instructions carry the includes but not CLAUDE.md's own text. The other half of opts.systemPrompt is not a substitute: resolveSystemPrompt (core/chat/session/start.ts:68-73) returns CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT + tzContext + NARRATION_OVERLAY. CLAUDE.md's body is instead expected to reach Codex out-of-band via the AGENTS.md mirror (core/agent-context-mirrors.ts:53), which is a different mechanism than the one the story claims.

triage.reasoning: The story misnames the channel; the capability is delivered by design. `expandClaudeIncludes` (src/core/agent-context-includes.ts) reads CLAUDE.md only to match `^@file.md` lines and pushes just the included files' bodies into `sections` — CLAUDE.md's own text is never appended — so codex-chat.ts:47-58 folds the includes, not CLAUDE.md, into `developer_instructions` (codex-sdk-session.ts:174). That split is deliberate: Codex reads AGENTS.md natively, and `mirrorClaudeDocs` (src/core/agent-context-mirrors.ts:50-61) symlinks AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md beside every CLAUDE.md in the package; what Codex does NOT do is resolve Claude's `@file.md` includes, which is exactly the hole expandClaudeIncludes fills. I verified the mirror is live and self-healing: generateAgentContextMirrors is called from ensureAgentContext (src/core/docs-gen/claude-md.ts:16), and generateDocs runs at chat start (src/core/chat/session/start-run.ts:116) and in the reactor loop; the worktree box ~/src/box-worktrees/user-stories-refresh/test1 has the AGENTS.md -> CLAUDE.md symlink at package root, and the chat cwd (boxRoot = <package>/content, start.ts:122) sits under it. So a Codex chat does get the box's CLAUDE.md plus its includes — just not both through developer_instructions. The story should be corrected to name both halves (the @-included files go into developer instructions; CLAUDE.md itself reaches Codex through the generated AGENTS.md mirror). No product change is warranted. Aside, not a gap: the long-idle ~/src/boxes/test1 has no AGENTS.md because docs-gen has not run there since the mirror landed; it would be created on the next chat start.

title: Have the weekly retrospective actually change what the agent believes
story: As a boxholder, I want the retrospective's integrate step to drain every pending report's observations into the personality and guide cards under an evidence model — turning changes that contradict my stated beliefs into question cards instead of silent edits — so that lessons the box observed become how it behaves, with an audit trail.
evidence: The stock `process-retrospective` procedure's `integrate` step prechecks for reports still marked `_Pending integration._`, feeds the full observation ledger (`.callback-box/retro/observations.jsonl`) and the current belief cards to an agent in one pass, requires one `Retro-Run:` commit trailer per drained report, and routes authoritative/conflicting changes to question cards; the `process-retrospective` default schedule runs it weekly.

verdict.note: templates/procedures/process-retrospective.procedure.card's `integrate` step precheck greps store/reviews/retro/*.md for '_Pending integration._', exits CHECK_SKIP when none, and dumps the full ledger (.callback-box/retro/observations.jsonl), every pending report, config/main.personality.card and config/*.guide.card into one agent prompt (pass-output: true). The prompt's STEP 3 forbids editing user-stated beliefs and routes conflicts to question cards, STEP 5 finalizes each report, STEP 6 requires one `Retro-Run:` trailer per drained report, and the validate shell aborts if any report is still pending. src/core/retro/ledger.ts owns that jsonl path; `cb retro scan` exists in src/cli/commands/retro.ts. The default schedule in src/core/box/defaults.ts:274 is cron '0 7 * * 1' (weekly) but seeded enabled:false — opt-in per box, so the automatic weekly run requires the boxholder to enable it; the story's claim is about the integrate step itself, which the card implements.

title: In-box authoring guides
story: As a box agent, I want box-local guides for writing schemas, views and tricks installed in the box, so that I can author new card types and views from documentation that lives beside the code I am editing.
evidence: installSchemasGuide / installViewsGuide / installTricksFiles in core/box/templates.ts write the embedded SCHEMAS_CLAUDE_MD and views guide into the box (schemas guide via the template tracker so it refreshes when unmodified).

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/box/templates.ts defines SCHEMAS_CLAUDE_MD/SCHEMAS_CLAUDE_MD_V2, VIEWS_CLAUDE_MD and TRICKS_CLAUDE_MD_V2 and exports installSchemasGuide (writes ../src/schemas/CLAUDE.md), installViewsGuide (../src/views/CLAUDE.md) and installTricksFiles (../src/tricks/scripts/CLAUDE.md plus tricks package.json), each via installTemplateFile with priorStockHashes from TEMPLATE_STOCK_HASHES so an unmodified copy refreshes and a customized one parks under config/_template-updates/. src/core/box/index.ts lines 198-204 calls all three during box init/update, and src/core/docs-gen/index.ts:265-269 re-installs the schemas and views guides, so the guides really land inside the box beside the schema/view/trick source. defaults.ts is the weaker of the two cited files (it installs guide CARDS and personality, not these CLAUDE.md guides), but templates.ts plus its callers fully implement the story.

title: Keep a living theory of the user that compiles into agent instructions
story: As a box, I want guide cards holding triage rules, named actions, experiments and reactions with confidence levels, compiled down to concise actionable markdown, so that job-processing agents act on settled beliefs while the learning record keeps its evidence.
evidence: GuideSchema in guide-elements.tsx declares triage-rules/actions/experiments/reactions with ConfidenceLevel and BeliefSource; parseGuide() normalizes the on-disk shape and compileGuide() emits the stripped markdown, dropping hypothesis-level rules and concluded experiments.

verdict.note: guide-elements.tsx defines GuideSchema with optional arrays 'triage-rules', actions, experiments, reactions plus default-action, and ConfidenceLevel/BeliefSource enums defaulted on rule fields; guide-parse.tsx parseGuide()/parseGuideCard() maps the kebab-case on-disk frontmatter into the camelCase ParsedGuide. guide-compile.tsx compileGuide() emits markdown that filters triageRules to confidence !== 'hypothesis', keeps only experiments with status 'active' or 'proposed', and drops context notes with duration 'past'. guide.tsx is the re-export surface and guide-templates.tsx supplies createInitialGuideTemplate. It is reachable: GuideSchema is in src/schemas/registry.ts and compileGuide/parseGuideCard are consumed by src/core/docs-gen/compile.ts (compileGuides, writing docs/generated) and src/core/commands/scan-guide-context.ts, so the full card stays the learning record while the compiled markdown feeds job agents.

title: Keep directory MAP.md indexes current
story: As a box agent, I want to be told exactly which directories' MAP.md files went stale since they were generated, and have the CLAUDE.md includes and state stamps updated after I rewrite them, so that the box's directory indexes stay accurate without rewriting all of them.
evidence: precheck() diffs each mapped directory's immediate-children set at its recorded commit (.cb-maps-state.json) against disk and emits a MapBrief; `cb refresh-maps --brief` feeds it to the agent and `--finalize` ensures each dir's CLAUDE.md `@MAP.md` include and re-stamps state; precheck-ignore.ts supports a box's `.cb-maps-ignore`.

verdict.note: src/core/maps/precheck.ts walks mappable dirs and compares each directory's immediate-children set at the commit recorded in `.cb-maps-state.json` (MAP_STATE_FILE in src/core/maps/state.ts, listChildrenAtCommit vs listChildrenOnDisk) producing MapTask{action,added,deleted,children} inside a MapBrief. src/cli/commands/refresh-maps.ts (`cb refresh-maps`, registered in src/cli/index.ts) prints that brief as JSON under --brief and persists it; --finalize replays the saved tasks through src/core/maps/finalize.ts, which inserts the `@MAP.md` include into each dir's CLAUDE.md and re-stamps state only for maps mapWasRewritten() proves changed (git diff/status against task.head), so untouched maps are not marked current. src/core/maps/precheck-ignore.ts loads a box's `.cb-maps-ignore` on top of the built-in patterns.

title: Managed box skills
story: As a box agent, I want the box to ship with skills for calendar, drive, email, location, schedules, tricks, views and course-building, so that I can invoke a worked procedure for those tasks instead of improvising.
evidence: buildBoxSkills() in core/box/skills.ts writes each constant from skills-content.ts (BUILD_COURSE_SKILL, CALENDAR_SKILL, DRIVE_SKILL, EMAIL_SKILL, LOCATION_SKILL, SCHEDULES_SKILL, TRICKS_SKILL, VIEWS_SKILL) to `<box>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, discovered by the agent SDK's settingSources.

verdict.note: buildBoxSkills() in core/box/skills.ts returns exactly build-course, calendar, drive, email, location, schedules, tricks, views, each with content from a corresponding constant in skills-content.ts (BUILD_COURSE_SKILL, CALENDAR_SKILL, DRIVE_SKILL, EMAIL_SKILL, LOCATION_SKILL, SCHEDULES_SKILL, TRICKS_SKILL, VIEWS_SKILL, all present as exports). generateSkills(boxRoot) writes each to <packageRoot>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (build-course also gets figure-examples.md), and is called from cli/commands/init.ts:175 during `cb init`, so every initialized box ships them. The file header documents that the agent SDK discovers box-level .claude/skills via settingSources.

story: As the boxholder, I want a question that declares a learning destination to carry that destination into its follow-up job when I answer, so that answering teaches the box a lasting rule instead of only fixing the one item.

title: Deliver browser push notifications and prune dead subscriptions

title: Keep getting notifications after the browser rotates my subscription
story: As a device subscribed to a box's notifications, I want the browser's replacement push subscription re-registered automatically with the boxes I had opted into carried across, so that proactive alerts keep arriving without me revisiting the settings page.

title: Let the agent decide not to answer a group message
story: As a boxholder with the box in a group chat, I want the agent to end its turn with either exactly one reply entry or a `kind: seen` marker, so that it can stay quiet on chatter that isn't for it instead of replying to everything, and the connector still knows the messages were processed.
evidence: The schema's `instructions` require exactly one trailing entry — an agent message or a `kind: seen` acknowledgement ("When in doubt, acknowledge rather than respond") — and describe scanning backward to the last seen/agent entry to find new messages; `sendOutbound` (telegram-outbound.ts) globs `*/thread.chat-thread.card`, uses `findUnsentAgentMessages` to deliver only unsent agent entries and `stampSentMessage` to record `sent`/`id`, so a `seen`-only turn sends nothing; agent-guide/commands.ts points agents at the `kind: seen` entry's `text:` for notes while processing a chat-thread card.

verdict.note: src/schemas/chat-thread.ts defines a `kind: z.literal('seen')` entry variant and its instructions state 'You MUST leave exactly one trailing entry' — either an agent message or a seen entry 'to acknowledge without responding', with 'When in doubt, acknowledge rather than respond' and the scan-backward rule ('The last kind: seen or kind: message with sender: agent marks the boundary'). connectors/telegram-outbound.ts globs '*/thread.chat-thread.card' under the chat dir, calls findUnsentAgentMessages (chat-utils.ts:153, which collects only entries with kind==='message' && sender==='agent' && sent===undefined) and stampSentMessage to record sent/id — so a seen-only turn produces no outbound send while the boundary still advances. core/agent-guide/commands.ts line ~50 tells agents to put notes in the `text:` of the `kind: seen` entry.

title: One call to reach the boxholder on every channel
story: As a box agent, I want a single call that notifies the boxholder over every configured channel, so that proactive alerts reach them without each producer wiring up push and Telegram separately.
evidence: notifyBoxholder() writes a durable `web-push` card always and a `telegram-message` card when config/box.json's healthAlerts.telegramChat is set, delivered by their connectors at `cb finalize` (or immediately with deliver: true); telegram-send.ts is the direct Bot API send.

verdict.note: callback-box/src/core/notify-boxholder.ts exports notifyBoxholder(boxRoot, input), which loads config/box.json via loadBoxConfig, writes a `web-push` output card (createWebPushTemplate) when the box has push subscriptions (endpointsForBox) and a `telegram-message` card (createTelegramMessageTemplate) when healthAlerts.telegramChat is set, commits them to box/output, and with deliver:true flushes them immediately via sendOutputPushCards/sendOutputCards. src/core/telegram-send.ts and src/core/send-push.ts both exist as the channel-level senders. The story's claim (one call fans out to every configured channel so producers don't wire push and Telegram separately) matches; only the evidence blurb's 'always' for web-push is slightly off — the card is written only when a device is subscribed, which is still 'configured channel'.

title: Receive Telegram messages by webhook or polling
story: As a boxholder, I want the box to receive my Telegram messages either through a registered webhook or by catching up on missed updates, so that messages reach the box whether or not it is publicly addressable.
evidence: setWebhook(url, {secret_token, allowed_updates})/deleteWebhook/getWebhookInfo and getUpdates({offset,limit,timeout}) wrap the Bot API; connectors/telegram.ts deletes the webhook before catching up via getUpdates and re-registers afterwards.

verdict.note: services/telegram.ts declares and implements setWebhook(url,{secret_token, allowed_updates}), deleteWebhook({drop_pending_updates}), getWebhookInfo(), and getUpdates({offset,limit,timeout}) over grammy's bot.api. connectors/telegram.ts sync() runs Phase 1 catchUpPolling — which calls tg.deleteWebhook({drop_pending_updates:false}) before looping tg.getUpdates({offset,limit:100,timeout:0}) and advancing offset = update_id + 1 — then Phase 2 setupWebhook() re-registers via tg.setWebhook(<publicUrl>/webhook/<slug>/telegram, {secret_token, allowed_updates}). The inbound webhook route exists at webapp/routes/telegram.ts, and setupWebhook's MissingPublicUrlError is caught in sync(), so polling still works for a box without a public URL.

title: Send something out of the box by writing a card
story: As an agent, I want to drop a telegram-message, web-push or email-outbound card in the box's output directory, so that the box reaches the boxholder (or drafts them an email) without me calling a messaging API directly.
evidence: TelegramMessageSchema is "an outbound Telegram message queued in box/output/ — the connector sends it on sync and deletes the card on success"; WebPushSchema declares title/body/url/severity with instructions to create the card in box/output/, and EmailOutboundSchema uploads as a Gmail draft for review.

verdict.note: Two of the three card types match, the third does not. telegram-message.ts and web-push.ts both instruct writing the card into box/output/ with status: pending, and connectors/output-cards.ts deliverPendingOutputCards reads OUTPUT_DIR = 'box/output', delivers, deletes on success and stamps status: failed otherwise. But email-outbound cards are NOT written to box/output/: EmailOutboundSchema's own 'Placement' instructions say reply drafts go in box/inbox/email/thread-X.attach/ and new emails in a fresh directory under box/inbox/email/, and connectors/gmail-drafts.ts findDraftCards only reads boxRoot + 'box/inbox/email' — it never looks at box/output. A card dropped in the output directory as the story describes would never be uploaded as a Gmail draft.

panel.note: All three schemas exist and are registered: schemas/registry.ts imports and lists TelegramMessageSchema, WebPushSchema and EmailOutboundSchema. connectors/output-cards.ts deliverPendingOutputCards is the shared box/output scanner and has two live callers — connectors/telegram-output-cards.ts sendOutputCards (called from connectors/telegram.ts:149 during sync and core/notify-boxholder.ts:146) and connectors/push.ts sendOutputPushCards (core/notify-boxholder.ts:141). email-outbound has its own live uploader: connectors/gmail-drafts.ts uploadPendingDrafts, imported and invoked by connectors/gmail.ts:247 on sync, plus a box-facing 'email' skill in core/box/skills-content.ts. Nothing here is dead code; the earlier verdict's objection is about which directory email-outbound cards go in (box/inbox/email vs box/output), a wording/accuracy matter outside my lens.

The entry point is the registered `cb finalize` CLI command (src/cli/index.ts:125 -> src/cli/commands/finalize.ts), which constructs the gmail, telegram and push connectors (lines 56-60) and calls sync() on each; docs/glossary.md notes finalize also closes every reactor cycle, so an agent-written card is flushed without any manual step. telegram.ts:149 calls sendOutputCards and push.ts:37 calls sendOutputPushCards, both of which run deliverPendingOutputCards over OUTPUT_DIR = 'box/output' (connectors/output-cards.ts:21) and delete on success; gmail.ts:247 calls uploadPendingDrafts for email-outbound cards. No feature flag gates any of these paths — only ordinary per-box connector credentials (bot token, VAPID keys, Gmail auth). Whether email-outbound cards belong in box/output/ is an accuracy question outside my lens; every card type named has a real, agent-triggerable entry point.

The story claims one mechanism -- drop a telegram-message, web-push or email-outbound card in the box's output directory -- but the code delivers that for only two of the three named types. connectors/output-cards.ts sets OUTPUT_DIR = "box/output" and deliverPendingOutputCards is imported by exactly two callers, connectors/push.ts (web-push) and connectors/telegram-output-cards.ts; nothing routes email-outbound through it. EmailOutboundSchema's own Placement instructions put reply drafts in box/inbox/email/thread-X.attach/ and new emails in a fresh dir under box/inbox/email/, and connectors/gmail-drafts.ts findDraftCards walks only path.join(boxRoot, "box/inbox/email"). schemas/email-message.tsx:70 states the opposite of the story outright: drafts go next to the message, "not in `box/output/`". So the story's benefit clause ('or drafts them an email') is unreachable by the placement the story specifies -- a general claim where the code covers a narrower case.

triage.reasoning: The story merges three card types under one mechanism the code only implements for two, and the third's real mechanism is deliberate and documented. connectors/output-cards.ts sets OUTPUT_DIR = "box/output" and deliverPendingOutputCards has exactly two callers — telegram-output-cards.ts and push.ts — so telegram-message and web-push match the story. email-outbound does not: connectors/gmail-drafts.ts findDraftCards walks only path.join(boxRoot, "box/inbox/email"), EmailOutboundSchema's own Placement section puts reply drafts in box/inbox/email/thread-X.attach/ and new mail in a fresh dir under box/inbox/email/, and schemas/email-message.tsx:70 says drafts go next to the message "not in `box/output/`". The product is self-consistent — the schema instructions an agent actually reads say the right thing — so nothing is broken; the catalog entry should be split (output-dir cards: telegram-message + web-push; email drafts: their own placement) or drop the email clause.
