title: A phone voice message is upgraded to a better transcript after it is sent
story: As a person dictating a message in the phone app, I want the live transcript sent immediately and then replaced by a high-quality pass the box runs, retried across app launches if it does not finish, so that I am not made to wait for accuracy before the message goes out.
evidence: `prepareVoiceMessage` in NativeComposerView.swift posts the retained recording to `ChatAPI.transcribeAudio` (the box's `POST /api/chat/transcribe-audio` HQ route) and resolves the final text via `VoicePreparationResolver`, falling back to the live dictation with "HQ transcription failed; sending live dictation."; `PendingEmissionStore.voicePreparations` persists and is replayed by `resumeVoicePreparations` on launch, with `finishVoicePreparation` committing the upgraded text.

verdict.note: The HQ path in NativeComposerView.swift (sendVoiceKeywordMessage -> case .hq) does NOT send the live transcript first. It calls pendingStore.stageVoicePreparation, which stores a VoicePreparation (not a PendingEmission); no emission exists until resumeVoicePreparation -> prepareVoiceMessage returns and finishVoicePreparation builds the PendingEmission with the resolved text. PendingEmissionStore.rebuildDeliveries even applies a `preparationBarrier` that withholds later pending emissions created after the oldest outstanding preparation, so nothing is delivered while the HQ pass is outstanding. The launch-replay half of the story is real (voicePreparations is persisted and resumeVoicePreparations re-runs it), but the message goes out only after the HQ pass finishes or fails, which is the opposite of 'sent immediately and then replaced' / 'not made to wait for accuracy before the message goes out'.

panel.note: Every cited piece is live and connected. NativeComposerView.swift's .hq branch calls pendingStore.stageVoicePreparation, then resumeVoicePreparation -> prepareVoiceMessage, which posts the retained recording via ChatAPI(box:).transcribeAudio (ChatAPI.swift:108, POST <apiURL>/chat/transcribe-audio) and resolves text through VoicePreparationResolver.text (SpeechKeywords.swift:329), with the literal 'HQ transcription failed; sending live dictation.' fallback. The backend route exists and is mounted: registerChatAudioRoutes in callback-box/src/webapp/routes/chat-audio-routes.ts:53 registers POST /api/chat/transcribe-audio and is imported and called from routes/chat.ts:40,203. The cross-launch replay is real too: PendingEmissionStore persists via ComposerDraftRepository.saveVoicePreparations/loadVoicePreparations, restores voicePreparations on activate(), and NativeComposerView's .onChange(of: pendingStore.voicePreparations) fires resumeVoicePreparations, with finishVoicePreparation committing the upgraded text. Whether the message truly goes out before the HQ pass (the preparationBarrier in rebuildDeliveries) is a behavior-accuracy question outside this lens.

The path has real entry points. RootView.swift renders NativeComposerView as the chat's bottom safeAreaInset in the shipping app (line ~301), and NativeVoiceKeywordSendPlan.make (SpeechKeywords.swift:365) selects the .hq branch whenever narrationEnabled is on (set from the web chat via ChatWebView's narration bridge message) or the spoken phrase matches sendHqPatterns ("clean up and send" / "send and clean up"), so an ordinary dictating user reaches sendKeywordIntent -> stageVoicePreparation -> resumeVoicePreparation. Launch/replay is on by default: NativeComposerView's `automaticallyResumeVoicePreparations` defaults to true and only the fixture screen passes false, and the .onChange on pendingStore.voicePreparations fires with the restored list. The box-side endpoint is registered for real: registerChatAudioRoutes (chat.ts:203, reached from server-box-scope.ts registerChatRoutes) declares POST /api/chat/transcribe-audio, which ChatAPI.transcribeAudio calls. My lens is satisfied; the earlier verifier's objection is about ordering (message withheld until the HQ pass finishes), not reachability, which is another reviewer's call.

The story's central claim — live transcript "sent immediately and then replaced by a high-quality pass" — is not what the code does. In NativeComposerView.sendKeywordIntent, the `.hq` branch calls pendingStore.stageVoicePreparation, which only writes a VoicePreparation record plus the copied audio; no PendingEmission and no delivery exists at that point. The emission is constructed inside PendingEmissionStore.finishVoicePreparation, i.e. only after prepareVoiceMessage returns the HQ text (or the fallback after "HQ transcription failed; sending live dictation."), and rebuildDeliveries additionally applies a preparationBarrier that withholds any later pending emission created after the oldest outstanding preparation — so nothing leaves the phone while an HQ pass is in flight. The persistence/retry-across-launch half is real (voicePreparations manifest + resumeVoicePreparations on change/launch), but the "so that I am not made to wait for accuracy before the message goes out" benefit is the opposite of the implemented behavior.

triage.reasoning: The story's headline behavior is the inverse of an intentional design, and the code is coherent. In NativeComposerView.swift the `.hq` branch does not enqueue anything: it calls `pendingStore.stageVoicePreparation`, which writes a VoicePreparation record plus a copy of the audio and nothing else. The PendingEmission is built only in `PendingEmissionStore.finishVoicePreparation`, after `prepareVoiceMessage` returns HQ text (or the 'HQ transcription failed; sending live dictation.' fallback). `rebuildDeliveries` additionally applies `preparationBarrier = voicePreparations.map(\.createdAt).min()` and skips any pending emission created after it, so later messages are held too rather than jumping the queue — ordering is deliberately preserved. Only the `.live` branch (narration off) enqueues the realtime transcript immediately. The persistence/replay half of the story is accurate (voicePreparations persist via ComposerDraftRepository, restore on activate(), and `resumeVoicePreparations` re-runs them on launch). So the catalog entry should be rewritten to what the app does — a keyword HQ send holds the message until the better transcript lands, retrying across launches — rather than 'sent immediately and then replaced'. No product defect: nothing is broken, and 'send now, correct later' would be a design change, not a fix.

title: Follow an outside link from the phone app without carrying my box credential
story: As someone tapping a link in the companion app, I want anything outside my box's own origin to open in the system browser instead of the app's webview, so that a foreign page never runs where the app injects my box's device token.
evidence: decidePolicyFor cancels any main-frame navigation whose origin(from:) differs from allowedOrigin and hands the URL to openExternalURL; newWindowDestination routes target=_blank the same way; and both injected document-start scripts (the localStorage callbackbox.mobileAuthToken write and the session observer) bail unless window.location.origin equals the paired box's origin.

verdict.note: ios-app/CallbackBox/Views/ChatWebView.swift decidePolicyFor (line ~403) allows a main-frame navigation only when ChatWebView.origin(from: url) == allowedOrigin or scheme is about:, otherwise calls decisionHandler(.cancel) then openExternalURL(url) (UIApplication.shared.open). createWebViewWith routes target=_blank through handleNewWindowRequest → newWindowDestination (line 857), which returns .browser for any non-matching origin. startupScript() builds both injected document-start scripts with an allowedOrigin guard: the session observer returns early unless window.location.origin === allowedOrigin, and the localStorage 'callbackbox.mobileAuthToken' write is inside the same origin check, so the device token is never written on a foreign page.

Re-pair it before using Capture.' for ownerless devices. title: Install the box on my phone as its own app
story: As someone using the box from a phone browser, I want to add it to my Home Screen and have it open standalone with its own icon, so that it behaves like an app — and so that iOS will let me enable push for it at all.
evidence: index.html links manifest.webmanifest (display: standalone, 192/512 icons) and main.tsx registers withBase("/sw.js"), whose pass-through fetch handler exists specifically to keep the app installable; NotificationsSection returns needs-install on iOS until display-mode: standalone or navigator.standalone is true.

verdict.note: src/frontend/index.html line 11 links /manifest.webmanifest; the manifest has display "standalone", start_url "./", name/short_name, and 192/512 png icons present in src/frontend/public/icons/. main.tsx lines 29-33 register withBase("/sw.js"), and sw.js installs a deliberate pass-through fetch handler commented as being there to keep the app installable. NotificationsSection.tsx detectSupport (lines 34-52) returns {kind: "needs-install"} on iOS when neither matchMedia("(display-mode: standalone)") nor navigator.standalone is true, and the render branch at line 143 tells the user to Add to Home Screen before enabling notifications.

browser.note: Verified against the running app: the served HTML links <link rel="manifest" href="/user-stories-refresh/manifest.webmanifest">, that manifest returns 200 application/manifest+json with display: standalone, start_url ./, theme/background colors, and 192x192 + 512x512 icons (both icon URLs return 200 image/png). /user-stories-refresh/sw.js is served, and in the live page navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() reports scope http://localhost:3210/user-stories-refresh/ with active: true. The Home-Screen install gesture itself and the iOS 'needs-install' branch of the Admin Notifications section are device-only (headless Chrome shows the plain 'Enable notifications' control), so the install act was not performed — every installability prerequisite the app serves was checked and is correct.

title: Interrupt the box's speech by starting to talk on the phone
story: As a person on the phone app, I want pressing record while the box is speaking to stop the speech immediately, so that I can barge in on a spoken reply.
evidence: `nativeSpeechCommandFromDetail` parses the shell's `{version:1, action:"stop"}` command and `useNativeBridges` calls `stopSpeech`; the page posts narration, speech-playback and response state back over the `callbackboxNarrationState` / `callbackboxSpeechPlaybackState` / `callbackboxResponseState` channels.

verdict.note: native-speech-command.ts `nativeSpeechCommandFromDetail` accepts exactly {version:1, action:"stop"}; use-native-bridge.ts `useNativeSpeechCommandBridge` drains `window.callbackboxNativeSpeechCommandQueue` and calls `stopSpeech()` on a valid command, and `useNativeBridges` (wired in InteractiveChat.tsx:236 with `stopSpeech: voice.handleStopSpeech`) installs it. The same module posts callbackboxNarrationState / callbackboxSpeechPlaybackState / callbackboxResponseState via native-post.ts. iOS side closes the loop: NativeComposerView.applyVoiceTurn case `.startDictationInterruptingSpeech` opens the mic and calls onInterruptSpeech, RootView sets a NativeSpeechStopRequest, and ChatWebView.deliverSpeechStopRequest evaluates `window.callbackboxNativeSpeechCommand(...)` with NativeSpeechCommand.stop.

title: Keep one box's phone session from touching a sibling box on the same host
story: As an operator running several boxes behind one hub origin, I want each box to sign and verify its own mobile session cookie and to try every `cb_mobile` value a request carries, so that a cookie planted under one box can neither authenticate against nor deny service to another.
evidence: `mobile-session.ts` signs with a per-box secret at `.callback-box/mobile-session.secret` (explicitly not `CB_SESSION_SECRET`, so no cross-box forgery is possible), verifies with a length-checked `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, and fails closed when no secret exists; `resolveMobileRequestAuth` iterates `parseCookieHeaderAll(...)[MOBILE_COOKIE_NAME]` over every value rather than the first, so a junk `cb_mobile` set at `Path=/` by a sibling box cannot mask the real one.

verdict.note: core/mobile/mobile-session.ts signs/verifies cb_mobile with an HMAC key read from <boxRoot>/.callback-box/mobile-session.secret (per-box, header comment explicitly rejects CB_SESSION_SECRET for the cross-box forgery reason), verifyMobileSession returns null when expectedSignature is null (no secret = fail closed), and signaturesEqual does a length check before crypto.timingSafeEqual. core/mobile/request-auth.ts:63-66 does parseCookieHeaderAll(headers.cookie) — lib/cookies.ts:40 returns Record<string,string[]> collecting every value per name — and loops over cookies[MOBILE_COOKIE_NAME] calling verifyMobileSession on each, so a junk sibling-box cookie earlier in the header cannot mask a valid one. resolveMobileRequestAuth is reachable from webapp/server-box-scope.ts:104/213 and routes/chat-helpers.ts:199.

title: Keep several boxes on the phone and switch between them
story: As someone with more than one box, I want the companion app to hold several paired boxes — added by QR pairing or by typing a box URL — and to switch the app between them, so that one phone serves every box I own without re-pairing each time.
evidence: PairedBoxStore keeps a list of boxes with a selectedBoxID and a per-box credential; PairBoxView offers both pairScannedCode and addManualBox(label:baseURL:sessionID:), RootView's "Choose Another Box" menu calls store.select, and the web PlacePill hides its own box switcher inside the shell via webBoxSwitchingAvailable(isNativeShell()).

verdict.note: ios-app/CallbackBox/Storage/PairedBoxStore.swift holds a [PairedBox] array with selectedBoxID, per-box authToken persisted via PairedBoxCredentialStore, addManualBox(label:baseURL:sessionID:), pair(from:) for callbackbox://pair URLs, select(_:) (line 164) and remove. PairBoxView.swift offers both 'Scan Pairing QR' (QRScannerView -> pairScannedCode) and a manual Label/Base URL/Session ID form calling addManualBox, plus a 'Paired Boxes' list. Switching is reachable in normal use from ComposerActionsView.swift's 'Boxes' section (store.select(box) with a checkmark on the current one) and from RootView.swift:434 'Choose Another Box' on the locked screen. Web-side webBoxSwitchingAvailable(isNativeShell()) in native-shell-navigation.ts is consumed by PlacePill.tsx to suppress the web switcher inside the shell.

title: Keep the composer above the on-screen keyboard
story: As a person using the web app on a phone, I want the app shell sized to the visible viewport while the keyboard is up, and the app installable as a standalone PWA, so that typing does not push the composer off screen.
evidence: useVisualViewportHeight mirrors window.visualViewport.height into --app-height only while the layout/visual gap exceeds 150px (keyboard up), dropping the override otherwise so URL-bar collapse cannot jitter the shell; main.tsx registers the service worker at withBase('/sw.js'); webBoxSwitchingAvailable() hides web box switching inside the native shell.

verdict.note: hooks/useVisualViewportHeight.ts sets --app-height from window.visualViewport.height only when window.innerHeight - vv.height > 150 (KEYBOARD_GAP_PX), removing the property otherwise; index.css line 14 sets the shell height to var(--app-height, 100dvh) and app-shell.tsx line 50 calls the hook, so the shell tracks the visible viewport with the keyboard up. main.tsx line 30 registers navigator.serviceWorker.register(withBase('/sw.js')); public/sw.js is a real worker (skipWaiting/clients.claim, a pass-through fetch handler kept explicitly for installability, plus push handling) and public/manifest.webmanifest declares display:"standalone" with 192/512 icons, linked from index.html. native-shell-navigation.ts's webBoxSwitchingAvailable(nativeShell) => !nativeShell exists as cited (peripheral to the claim, but the cited file is real).

browser.note: The page ships <link rel=manifest> to /manifest.webmanifest with display:"standalone", name/short_name, theme/background colors and 192/512 icons, plus apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes and width=device-width viewport. The shell is a single .h-app column sized to the viewport (height: var(--app-height, 100dvh)); at a 390×780 viewport it measured exactly 780px with the composer pinned at the bottom. The keyboard-up case itself (--app-height tracking visualViewport) is a device behavior a headless browser cannot raise.

title: Keep the phone's session alive through webview reloads
story: As someone using the companion app, I want the embedded web page to re-establish its session from the device token after the webview reloads itself, so that a back-navigation or content-process crash doesn't leave the app stuck on an authentication error.
evidence: refreshMobileSession() posts the stored bearer to /api/pairing/session, which resolves the device identity and calls setMobileSessionCookie to mint a path-scoped cb_mobile; renewMobileSessionCookie re-checks revocation past the cookie's half-life and clears it for a revoked device.

verdict.note: frontend/src/lib/mobile-auth.ts's refreshMobileSession() POSTs the localStorage bearer to `${apiBase}/pairing/session`; webapp/routes/pairing.ts registers POST /api/pairing/session, re-resolves identity via resolveMobileBearerIdentity (core/mobile/pairing.ts), 401s if invalid/revoked, and otherwise calls setMobileSessionCookie (webapp/mobile-cookie.ts) which signs a cb_mobile scoped to path /<boxSlug> with MOBILE_SESSION_TTL_MS. The caller is trpcFetch in frontend/src/lib/trpc/index.ts: on a 401 with a stored mobile token it refreshes once and retries the request, and the WS client's url thunk refreshes before opening a socket. renewMobileSessionCookie in the same file only re-checks the device store past half the TTL and clearCookie()s cb_mobile for a device that isMobileDeviceActive rejects.

title: Leave the app and have the capture keep uploading
story: As a person capturing on my phone, I want the media already recorded to keep uploading after I switch apps or the app is killed, retried with backoff and reported when it resumes, so that walking away does not strand a capture's bytes on the device.
evidence: `CaptureBackgroundSession.configuration()` builds a `URLSessionConfiguration.background(withIdentifier:)` with `sessionSendsLaunchEvents = true` and `isDiscretionary = false`; `CallbackBoxAppDelegate.application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:)` hands the relaunch completion handler to `CaptureBackgroundEvents.shared`; `CaptureUploadCoordinator` retries up to `CaptureStore.maximumUploadAttempts` and emits `.retryScheduled`, which `NativeCaptureController` shows as "Upload interrupted. Retrying in N seconds."

verdict.note: CaptureAPI.swift:138 `CaptureBackgroundSession.configuration()` builds URLSessionConfiguration.background(withIdentifier: "app.callbackbox.ios.capture-upload-v1") with sessionSendsLaunchEvents=true and isDiscretionary=false, so uploads continue after app switch/kill and relaunch the app on completion. CallbackBoxAppDelegate.application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:) forwards the completion handler to CaptureBackgroundEvents.shared, and the delegate is installed via @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor in CallbackBoxApp.swift. CaptureUploadCoordinator.handle failure path calls CaptureStore.recordUploadFailure, which retries while uploadGeneration < CaptureStore.maximumUploadAttempts (4) with exponential delay `1 << (generation-1)`, emitting .retryScheduled; NativeCaptureController.swift:479 renders 'Upload interrupted. Retrying in N seconds.' CaptureUploadRuntime.shared is wired from CallbackBoxApp.swift and NativeCaptureController.

title: Lock a paired box behind Face ID or the device passcode
story: As someone with a sensitive box on my phone, I want to require device authentication before that box opens in the companion app, and to have to authenticate again to turn the requirement off, so that whoever picks up my unlocked phone still cannot read the box.
evidence: PairedBox.requiresDeviceUnlock is toggled per box in PairBoxView (turning it off runs authenticateForLockRemoval first); RootView shows a lock screen with Unlock / Retry / "Open Anyway" when the device has no passcode, and the share extension refuses a locked box that hasn't been unlocked this session.

verdict.note: PairedBox.requiresDeviceUnlock exists and BoxLockManager.swift wraps LAContext .deviceOwnerAuthentication (Face ID / passcode) with isLocked(box), unlock(box), openWithoutPasscode, and authenticateForLockRemoval(). PairBoxView.swift line 71 renders a 'Require Device Unlock' Toggle whose setter turns it on directly but routes turning it off through `await boxLockManager.authenticateForLockRemoval()` before store.setRequiresDeviceUnlock(false, ...), with a 'no passcode' escape alert. RootView.swift computes `boxLockManager.isLocked(box)` and shows a lock screen with Unlock / Retry / 'Open Anyway' (the last only in the .passcodeNotSet case). ShareViewController.swift line 145 guards on `metadata.requiresDeviceUnlock, unlockedBoxIDs.contains(metadata.id) == false` and prompts LAContext before sharing.

title: Open, lock, and close the phone keyboard
story: As a person on a phone whose composer is a voice-first button bar, I want to open a typing row for one message and optionally lock it open, so that I can type occasionally without the keyboard taking over the screen for the rest of the conversation.
evidence: `typingMode`/`typingLocked` state in InteractiveChat.tsx gates the `sm:hidden` MobileTextareaRow; the layout's floating lock button toggles `typingLocked` (aria-pressed) and the ✕ closes both, while `handleSend` clears `typingMode` after a send unless it is locked; `useTextareaFocus` focuses the row when typing mode opens.

verdict.note: InteractiveChat.tsx:179-180 holds typingMode/typingLocked; InteractiveChat-view.tsx passes onKeyboard={() => setTypingMode(true)} to ChatInputArea, whose mobile-only (sm:hidden) keyboard button in InteractiveChat-composer.tsx:281-289 opens the row, and hideMobile={typingMode} hides the button bar. InteractiveChat-layout.tsx:168-200 renders the sm:hidden MobileTextareaRow when typingMode||isTranscribing, with a floating lock button toggling typingLocked (aria-pressed, title 'Lock open'/'Unlock (close after send)') and an ✕ that clears both. handleSend in InteractiveChat-actions.ts:83-85 clears typingMode after a send only when !typingLocked, and useTextareaFocus (same file, ~227) focuses the textarea when typingMode opens.

browser.note: Verified on the real chat page at a 390x844 viewport (the harness cards are static, so the interaction was driven against /test1/chat). Idle phone composer is the voice-first bar: Add, Capture, 'Type a message', 'Voice input'. Clicking 'Type a message' replaces the bar with the typing row - textarea (focused automatically: document.activeElement was the TEXTAREA), Send (disabled while empty), a lock button titled 'Lock open' with aria-pressed=false, and a 'Close keyboard' button. Clicking the lock flips it to aria-pressed=true with title 'Unlock (close after send)'. Clicking 'Close keyboard' while locked returns to the button bar (closes both typing mode and the lock). The harness mirrors this: ?state=idle-keyboard / typing-keyboard have aria-pressed=false, ?state=idle-keyboard-locked / typing-keyboard-locked have aria-pressed=true. Not exercised: the 'send clears typing mode unless locked' half - that needs an actual send, which would trigger an agent run (excluded as destructive).

title: Pair a phone by scanning a code
story: As a box owner, I want Settings to show a QR code and deep link that pairs my phone's companion app with this box, so that I can set up the app without typing a URL or copying a credential by hand.
evidence: pairing.createTicket (ownerProcedure) calls createMobilePairingTicket for a single-use 10-minute token; CompanionPairingSection renders it as callbackbox://pair?baseURL=…&label=…&pairingToken=… with a generated QR SVG, which PairedBoxStore.pair(from:) parses.

verdict.note: SettingsPage.tsx renders <CompanionPairingSection/>, which calls trpc.pairing.createTicket (ownerProcedure in webapp/trpc/routers/pairing.ts -> createMobilePairingTicket in core/mobile/pairing.ts: random token, single-use `used` flag, DEFAULT_PAIRING_TTL_MS = 10 min). The component builds `callbackbox://pair?baseURL=&label=&pairingToken=` via pairingDeepLink(), renders it as an inline QR SVG with qrcode-generator (qrSvg) plus a Copy Link button and the literal link text. On the iOS side PairBoxView.swift has a 'Scan Pairing QR' button opening QRScannerView, and PairedBoxStore.pair(from:) parses the callbackbox://pair URL and redeems the pairingToken (redeemPairing). No typing or manual credential copy required.

browser.note: The 'iOS Companion' section is present with the copy 'Pair the native app with this box using a short-lived QR code.' and a 'Create QR' button. Clicking it returns 'Owner access required' inline (pairing.createTicket is an ownerProcedure and the browse identity is not the owner), so no QR SVG or callbackbox:// deep link was ever rendered. The control exists; the payload could not be reached without owner credentials.

title: Pair the phone by opening a link instead of scanning
story: As someone pairing a phone while already reading the settings page on that same phone, I want to copy the pairing link and open it, so that pairing works when there is no second screen to scan a QR code from.
evidence: `pairingDeepLink` builds `callbackbox://pair?baseURL=…&label=…&pairingToken=…` and `copyLink` writes it to the clipboard; the app registers the `callbackbox` URL scheme in Info.plist and both `.onOpenURL` and the `PairingURLInbox` fed by `application(_:open:options:)` call `store.pair(from: url)`.

verdict.note: CompanionPairingSection.tsx has pairingDeepLink() building `callbackbox://pair?baseURL=&label=&pairingToken=` (lines 29-35) and a 'Copy Link' Button wired to copyLink(), which does navigator.clipboard.writeText(ticket.deepLink) — shown whenever a ticket exists, alongside the QR. ios-app/CallbackBox/Info.plist registers CFBundleURLSchemes = ['callbackbox'] under CFBundleURLName app.callbackbox.ios.pairing. CallbackBoxApp.swift handles both .onOpenURL { store.pair(from: url) } and .onReceive(pairingURLInbox.$pendingURL...) { store.pair(from: url) }, with CallbackBoxAppDelegate.application(_:open:options:) feeding PairingURLInbox.shared.accept(url). PairedBoxStore.pair(from:) parses scheme/host 'callbackbox'/'pair', reads baseURL/label/pairingToken and redeems the ticket. Same-device copy-then-open works.

browser.note: The copy-the-link path lives inside the same ticket result as the QR, and no ticket could be created (owner-gated), so no pairing link or copy control was rendered. Nothing to copy and no clipboard behavior to observe.

title: Quote a card passage from inside the native app
story: As a person reading a card in the phone app, I want a selection I attach to reach the native composer and be told when it isn't accepted, so that quoting works the same on the phone as in the browser.
evidence: Under `nativeComposer`, `useCompanionSelection.handleAddSelection` routes to `useNativeComposerCommands.addSelection`, which posts an `add-selection` command and waits up to 15s for an acknowledgement, surfacing a rejected one as the dismissible `nativeCommandError` banner.

verdict.note: use-companion-selection.ts's useCompanionSelection.handleAddSelection branches on the nativeComposer flag and calls useNativeComposerCommands.addSelection instead of the web addSelection. use-native-composer-commands.ts posts a version-1 add-selection command via postNativeComposerCommand (native-post channel callbackboxComposerCommand), registers a 15s timeout (ACK_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000) that sets 'The native composer did not confirm the selection. Add it again.', and drains ack details through nativeComposerCommandAcknowledgementFromDetail, setting error to the rejection reason. InteractiveChat-view.tsx InteractiveChatBody renders that value through ChatStatusBanners (error={nativeCommandError ?? error}) with onDismissError calling dismissNativeCommandError, and handleAddSelection is wired to CompanionViewPanel's onAddSelection (the card pane). ChatPage.tsx sets nativeComposer from ?nativeComposer=1 or isNativeShell(), and ios-app decodes NativeComposerCommand, so the native path is real.

title: Record from the native app in its own audio format
story: As a person recording in the native mobile app, I want each recording uploaded as a single AAC/M4A file rather than browser WebM chunks, so that native recording works without pretending to be a browser MediaRecorder.
evidence: `StagingSegment.format` carries `webm-opus` or `m4a-aac`; `addAudioChunk` rejects a format change mid-segment (`StagingAudioFormatMismatchError`) and a second file in an `m4a-aac` segment (`M4ASegmentFileCountError`), and `writeAudioCards` names the media `.m4a` vs `.webm` accordingly while concatenating only WebM chunks within a segment.

verdict.note: src/core/capture/audio-format.ts defines CaptureAudioFormatSchema = z.enum(["webm-opus","m4a-aac"]) plus StagingAudioFormatMismatchError and M4ASegmentFileCountError. In src/core/capture/staging-store.ts, addAudioChunk() defaults to webm-opus, throws StagingAudioFormatMismatchError when a later chunk's format differs from the segment's first, and throws M4ASegmentFileCountError if an m4a-aac segment already has a chunk. src/core/capture/write-cards.ts picks extension "m4a" vs "webm" from segment.format, re-checks chunks.length === 1 for m4a, and concatenates chunks only within a segment (concatSegmentChunks). The path is reachable end-to-end: src/webapp/routes/capture-upload.ts parses the `x-capture-audio-format` header (default webm-opus) into addAudioChunk, the session route advertises acceptedAudioFormats ["webm-opus","m4a-aac"], and ios-app/CallbackBox/Services/CaptureAcquisition.swift records kAudioFormatMPEG4AAC and CaptureAPI.swift sets X-Capture-Audio-Format.

title: Record through a Bluetooth headset without wrecking playback afterwards
story: As a person recording into the phone app with a headset on, I want the audio session switched to a recording configuration that uses the headset mic and then returned to a full-quality playback configuration when recording stops, so that captures pick up the mic I am wearing and the box's replies do not come back quiet and speaker-bound.
evidence: AudioSessionRouting.configuration(role:highQualityBluetoothAvailable:) returns one of exactly two AVAudioSession configurations — .playback for .idle, a recording category/mode/options set for .recording; SystemAudioSession.activateRecording() installs the recording one and deactivate() restores idle via prepareIdle(). CaptureAcquisition and SpeechDictation both call activateRecording() through the AudioSessionControlling protocol, and CallbackBoxAppDelegate calls prepareIdle() at launch.

verdict.note: ios-app/CallbackBox/Services/AudioSessionRouting.swift defines AudioSessionRouting.configuration(role:highQualityBluetoothAvailable:) returning exactly two AVAudioSessionConfiguration values: .playback/.default/[.mixWithOthers] for .idle, and .playAndRecord/.default with [.duckOthers, .defaultToSpeaker, .allowBluetoothA2DP, .allowBluetoothHFP] (+ .bluetoothHighQualityRecording on iOS 26) for .recording. SystemAudioSession.activateRecording() applies the recording role and setActive(true); deactivate() calls setActive(false, .notifyOthersOnDeactivation) then prepareIdle(), restoring the playback configuration. CaptureAcquisition.swift (lines 736/753/768) and SpeechDictation.swift (309/418) hold an AudioSessionControlling and call activateRecording()/deactivate(); CallbackBoxAppDelegate.swift:17 calls SystemAudioSession().prepareIdle() at launch. The comments explicitly name the quiet/speaker-bound playback defect this prevents.

title: See and revoke paired devices
story: As a box owner, I want a list of the devices paired to my box with when each was paired and last used, and a button to revoke one, so that a lost phone stops reaching the box.
evidence: pairing.devices returns listMobileDevices() (label, createdAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt) and pairing.revokeDevice calls revokeMobileDevice; DeviceRow renders the Revoke button, and resolveMobileRequestAuth refuses a revoked device on the next request.

verdict.note: src/webapp/trpc/routers/pairing.ts exposes devices (ownerProcedure -> listMobileDevices) and revokeDevice (-> revokeMobileDevice, NOT_FOUND if missing). core/mobile/pairing.ts listMobileDevices strips tokenHash and returns records with label/createdAt/lastUsedAt/revokedAt; revokeMobileDevice delegates to TokenStore.revoke, which stamps revokedAt and makes verify skip the record. CompanionPairingSection (rendered from src/frontend/src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx) lists devices under 'Paired devices' with 'Paired <date> - last used <date>' and a destructive Revoke button per unrevoked DeviceRow. Bearer auth via resolveMobileRequestAuth/token-store rejects revoked devices; the signed cb_mobile cookie has a documented at-most-one-TTL renewal window (isMobileDeviceActive fails closed), which is a bounded lag, not a missing capability.

browser.note: A 'Paired devices' subheading is rendered under iOS Companion, but its body is 'Owner access required' — pairing.devices returns 403 FORBIDDEN for this identity (verified with a direct fetch). No device rows, paired/last-used timestamps, or Revoke buttons could be observed.

title: See the boxes my phone is paired to without a browser sign-in
story: As a paired phone on a host serving several boxes, I want the box listing to answer with exactly the boxes my device credential opens, so that the app can resolve and open its box without anyone signing in through the browser.
evidence: `listMobileAuthorizedBoxes` in hub-server.ts (mirrored in server-root.ts around line 256) runs `verifyMobileRequest(box.boxRoot, headers)` against every configured box and, when any pass, returns just those slugs from `/api/boxes` — before the cookie-session identity resolver is consulted at all.

verdict.note: In callback-box/src/webapp/server-root.ts the GET /api/boxes handler (line ~247) checks verifyBrowseKey, then calls listMobileAuthorizedBoxes({boxes, headers}) (defined line 347) which runs verifyMobileRequest(box.boxRoot, headers) over every configured box and returns only the passing slugs; if that list is non-empty it returns immediately, before resolveRequestIdentity (the cookie-session resolver) is called. hub-server.ts mirrors this in respondHubBoxes (listMobileAuthorizedBoxes at line 166, used at line 196, again ahead of resolveRequestIdentity). verifyMobileRequest in core/mobile/request-auth.ts:83 wraps resolveMobileRequestAuth, which accepts a device cookie session or a mobile bearer token, so a paired phone gets exactly its boxes with no browser sign-in.

title: Send the leftovers of a capture as a follow-up
story: As a person on the phone whose capture ended with items still unsent, I want the app to open a fresh capture session and move the unacknowledged photos and clips into it, so that the leftovers go to the box as a follow-up capture rather than being stranded on the device.
evidence: `sendRemainingAsFollowUp` cancels in-flight uploads for the old session, creates a new session via `CaptureAPI.createSession`, calls `store.moveUnacknowledgedItems(from:to:)` and deletes the old capture before resuming the active session; `submitResumable` likewise cancels background transfers before finalize so bytes are not spent on a sealed session that would 409.

verdict.note: NativeCaptureController.sendRemainingAsFollowUp() (ios-app/CallbackBox/Views/NativeCaptureController.swift:297) cancels in-flight uploads via uploadRuntime.cancel for the old session, calls CaptureAPI.createSession(targetSessionID:) (Services/CaptureAPI.swift:225), createManifest for the new session, store.moveUnacknowledgedItems(boxID:from:to:) (Storage/CaptureStore.swift:350 — moves items in .local/.failed state, refusing while any item is .uploading), deletes the old capture, and resumes with beginActiveSession(). It is reachable from the UI: NativeCaptureView.swift:323 renders a 'Send Remaining Items as a Follow-up' button wired through onSendFollowUp to this method.

title: Share into the box from another iOS app
story: As a person reading something in another app, I want to share it to a chat or a save destination in my box, so that it is captured without switching apps and re-typing it.
evidence: ShareViewModel loads the shared item and a destination list per paired box, offering a Selection of .chat(ShareChatRow) or .save(ShareDestinationRow) and submitting through ShareExtensionAPI.

verdict.note: ios-app/CallbackBoxShareExtension exists as a real appex target (referenced in CallbackBox.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj as CallbackBoxShareExtension.appex, embedded in Foundation Extensions). ShareViewController.swift's ShareViewModel loads the shared item plus the paired-box list from SharedSelectedBoxStore (SharedSelectedBoxSnapshot.swift), fetches per-box destinations via ShareExtensionAPI.destinations() (GET trpc/share.destinations), and offers Selection .chat(ShareChatRow) / .save(ShareDestinationRow); submit() posts to chat/send or trpc/share.saveTextual. Backend counterparts exist in webapp/trpc/routers/share.ts (destinations, saveTextual as authedProcedure). Capture happens inside the share sheet without leaving the source app.

title: The phone screen stays awake while a capture is recording
story: As a person recording a capture on my phone, I want the screen kept awake for as long as the microphone is open, so that a silent room does not let iOS lock the screen, suspend the app, and kill the recording.
evidence: ScreenAwakeHold holds a set of ScreenAwakeReason (.captureRecording, .voiceTurn, .speechPlayback) and writes UIApplication's idle-timer flag only on the aggregate edges; NativeCaptureController.applyScreenAwake() sets .captureRecording from the recording state on each phase change and clears it on disappear, and NativeComposerView holds the composer's reasons over a voice turn.

verdict.note: ios-app/CallbackBox/Services/ScreenAwake.swift defines ScreenAwakeReason (.voiceTurn, .speechPlayback, .captureRecording), ScreenAwakeState.set() returning whether the aggregate isHeld flipped, and ScreenAwakeHold as the single writer of UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled on those edges. NativeCaptureController.swift:747 applyScreenAwake() sets .captureRecording active when scenePhase == .active && controller.surfaceState.isRecording, and it is re-derived on .onAppear, on scenePhase change, and on surfaceState.isRecording change, with .onDisappear clearing only .captureRecording. NativeComposerView.swift (screenAwakeReasons ~line 901, applyScreenAwake ~922) holds the composer's reasons over a voice turn and clears them at line 180. Story matches.

title: Unpair a box from the phone and take its data with it
story: As someone retiring a box from my phone, I want unpairing to delete that box's stored device token and its retained voice recordings before the pairing entry goes, so that removing the box leaves no credential or audio behind on the device.
evidence: `PairedBoxStore.removeBoxes` calls `deleteTokensFirst` (keychain delete per box id) then `VoiceAudioRetentionStore.forgetSynchronously(boxID:)` before dropping the entry and re-selecting another box; `PairBoxView` calls `store.remove(box)` from the box list.

verdict.note: PairedBoxStore.swift: both remove(_:) and remove(at:) funnel into removeBoxes(), which first calls deleteTokensFirst(for:) (per-box credentialStore.deleteToken, the keychain delete declared in PairedBoxCredentialStore.swift line 84, with rollback re-persisting on failure), then loops VoiceAudioRetentionStore.forgetSynchronously(boxID:) for each box, and only then removes the entries, re-selects boxes.first when the selected box was removed, and save()s. PairBoxView.swift line 66 calls store.remove(box) from the box list and line 82 wires .onDelete to store.remove. Order and scope match the story as written.

title: Upload a camera roll from the phone while still typing
story: As a person sending dozens of photos from my phone, I want them copied to disk and uploaded as a batch with a live 'Uploading photos — n of m' status while I keep writing the message that introduces them, so that a large selection neither exhausts memory nor makes me wait to type.
evidence: `loadPhotos` routes a selection past `BulkPhotoThreshold.shouldBatch` into `uploadPhotoBatch`, which stages picks as file representations copied into app-owned storage (BulkPhotoStaging), reports `Preparing n of m photos…` then `Uploading photos — n of m`, and deliberately does not gate the text field. BulkUploadOutcome distinguishes `.delivered`/`.accepted` (the seal is the hand-off, box owns recovery) from never-sealed, where the caller keeps the user's text to try again.

verdict.note: NativeComposerView.loadPhotos() (ios-app/CallbackBox/Views/NativeComposerView.swift:1031) routes selections past BulkPhotoThreshold.shouldBatch into uploadPhotoBatch(), which sets statusText "Preparing n photos…"/"Preparing n of m photos…" then shows batchProgressText "Uploading photos — done of total" (line ~341), which outranks other composer status. BulkPhotoStaging.stage() imports one item at a time via a PickedPhotoFile FileRepresentation copied into the app-owned caches staging root, explicitly to avoid holding all bytes in memory. isTextEntryLocked = isPreparingSend || !draftStore.isReady, and uploadPhotoBatch never sets isPreparingSend, so the text field stays writable; the note is read on the main actor at seal time. BulkUploadCoordinator.run returns .delivered/.accepted (staging discarded, composer text cleared) vs .failed (text kept, "try again").

title: Be stopped when a doc cannot be made self-contained
story: As an agent drafting a publication, I want the render to fail when the source or an image lies outside the box, is missing, or is an annex pointer whose bytes are not present locally, so that I never ship a page with a broken or box-escaping reference to the public internet.
evidence: render-docs.ts defines and throws `ImageEscapesBoxError` and `ImageContentNotPresentError` (the latter telling you to `git annex get` the bytes) while inlining or copying every image; draft.ts throws `SourceEscapesBoxError` before rendering, and `cb pub draft`'s catch turns each into an `Error:` message with exit 1, so no bundle is committed.

verdict.note: src/publish/render-docs.ts localizeImage() resolves each against boxRoot and throws ImageEscapesBoxError when the resolved path leaves the box, ImageNotFoundError when readFileSync fails, and ImageContentNotPresentError ('fetch it with `git annex get`') when the bytes parse as a git-annex pointer; otherwise it inlines a data: URI or emits assets/.. draft.ts draftPublication() does the same box-confinement check on the source path and throws SourceEscapesBoxError before calling renderDocsPublication. src/cli/commands/pub.ts's draft action wraps the call in try/catch that prints `Error: ${errorMessage(error)}` and process.exit(1) before any commit, so the throw aborts the draft.

title: Bound what a publication's drop box will accept
story: As a boxholder with a submit form on a publication, I want the edge to enforce the manifest's per-submission size and per-day count, a hard 1MB body ceiling and an optional per-IP rate limit, and to refuse a form on a fully public page at all, so that a shared page cannot be flooded into my box by whoever finds the URL.
evidence: handleSubmit in pub-worker/src/submit.ts checks HARD_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES before parsing, returns forbidden() when manifest.tier === "public" or no submit block exists, enforces submit.maxSubmissionBytes, calls countSubmissionsSince against submit.maxPerDay (tooManyRequests), and calls env.SUBMIT_RATE_LIMITER.limit keyed by `${pubId}:${ip}`. maxPerDay/maxSubmissionBytes come from submitBlockSchema in src/publish/manifest-edge.ts.

verdict.note: handleSubmit in callback-box/pub-worker/src/submit.ts is reached from index.ts (matchSubmitPath on POST /__submit/<id>). It checks HARD_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES = 1MB against both Content-Length and the buffered bytes before parsing, returns forbidden() when manifest.tier === 'public' or manifest.submit is null/undefined, enforces submit.maxSubmissionBytes on the raw body, calls countSubmissionsSince against submit.maxPerDay returning tooManyRequests(), and calls env.SUBMIT_RATE_LIMITER.limit({key: `${pubId}:${ip}`}) only when that optional binding exists. submitBlockSchema in src/publish/manifest-edge.ts (lines 51-59) defines maxSubmissionBytes and maxPerDay as positive ints; field validation comes from validateSubmissionFields in src/publish/submission.ts.

title: Catch secrets in a bundle before it is committed
story: As an agent, I want the draft step to leak-scan the rendered bundle for home paths, stray emails, credential shapes and external URLs and block on unaccepted findings, so that an obvious secret never reaches git or the edge.
evidence: `scanBundle` emits stable-id findings by kind (`home-path`/`email`/`credential`/`external-url`); a `leaks-blocked` draft result prints each id and exits 1, and the CLI notes the draft was written for preview but NOT committed. `--accept-leak <id>` waves a specific false positive through.

verdict.note: src/publish/leak-scan.ts exports scanBundle(files, {ownerEmail, allowedEmails}) with LeakKind = 'home-path'|'email'|'credential'|'external-url', HOME_PATH/EMAIL_RE/EXTERNAL_URL_RE and a CREDENTIAL_PATTERNS table, each finding carrying a stable id = sha256(kind\0file\0match).slice(0,12). draftPublication in src/publish/draft.ts runs scanBundle on the rendered bundle, splits findings by the acceptLeaks set, writes the draft dir to disk, and when blocking.length > 0 returns {ok:false, reason:'leaks-blocked', …} BEFORE calling commit(). src/cli/commands/pub.ts registers '--accept-leak <id>' (repeatable via collect) and on 'leaks-blocked' prints each '--accept-leak <id> (kind: match)' line plus 'The draft was written to disk for preview but NOT committed', then process.exit(1).

title: Choose who can reach a publication
story: As a boxholder, I want to draft a publication at a chosen access tier with an expiry, a viewer email allowlist, or a human slug, so that a page can be public, capability-secret, or restricted to named accounts.
evidence: `cb pub draft` takes `--tier` (validated against `tierValues`), `--expires` (ISO or duration), `--emails` (accounts tier) and `--slug` (public tier); the values land in the publication manifest and are projected to the edge manifest by `toEdgeManifest`.

verdict.note: cli/commands/pub.ts `draft` has --tier (required, validated against tierValues via TIER_SET/isTier), --expires <iso|duration>, --emails <csv> parsed into an array, --slug, all passed to draftPublication. publish/manifest-edge.ts exports tierValues = ["public","secret","accounts","any-account"]; publish/draft.ts checkFlagCombo rejects a slug on non-public tiers and returns "invalid-expires" for bad expiry, and writes slug/allowedEmails into the manifest. publish/manifest.ts toEdgeManifest (line 164) projects to the edge manifest, used by publish/go.ts on upload. access-setup.ts is supporting plumbing for the accounts tier rather than the core, but the claim holds against the other cited files.

title: Collect replies from a published page
story: As a reader of a publication with a submit block, I want to post a form on the page, so that I can send the boxholder a reply without an account or an email round trip.
evidence: `POST /__submit/<pub-id>` is matched by `matchSubmitPath` and handled by `handleSubmit`, which validates each field against the manifest's `submit` block and writes `submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json` with the Access-verified viewer email (null on the secret tier) and a country-only attribution.

verdict.note: The edge half exists — pub-worker/src/index.ts routes matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit (pub-worker/src/submit.ts), which validates fields against the manifest submit block, enforces maxSubmissionBytes/maxPerDay, and writes submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json with viewer email (null on secret) and coarseCountry. But nothing produces a page with a form: src/publish/draft.ts (draftPublication, the only manifest-assembling path, driven by `cb pub draft` in src/cli/commands/pub.ts) never sets a `submit` field and has no flag for one, and src/publish/render-docs.ts emits Markdoc HTML with no <form> element at all (grep for '<form' across src/ and pub-worker/src finds only login/invite/password pages and frontend React forms). The submit block is only a schema shape in manifest.ts/manifest-edge.ts; a reader can never encounter a form on a published page, so the story over-claims a user-reachable capability.

panel.note: The cited code is real and fully wired on the receiving side: pub-worker/src/index.ts:34,66-67 imports and dispatches matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit from pub-worker/src/submit.ts, which parses the urlencoded body, validates against the manifest submit block via validateSubmissionFields/submissionSchema in src/publish/submission.ts, enforces size/volume limits, and writes submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json; src/connectors/publish-submissions.ts consumes those objects and is registered live (createPublishSubmissionsConnector is called in src/cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts:41). The submit block is not merely schema decoration either: manifest.ts's toEdgeManifest (lines 176-189) carries submit into the edge manifest that src/publish/go.ts uploads. Nothing here is dead code. I did confirm the earlier verifier's point that no code emits a <form> (grep for '<form' across src/publish and pub-worker/src finds none, and draft.ts never sets submit), but a missing reader-facing entry point is the reachability lens's call, not mine; on existence-and-wiring the story holds.

The edge endpoint exists (pub-worker/src/index.ts routes matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit), but a reader has no way to arrive at it. handleSubmit (pub-worker/src/submit.ts:100-105) returns 403 unless manifest.submit is non-null, and no code path ever sets that field: draftPublication (src/publish/draft.ts:202-217) is the only manifest assembler and its rawManifest has no `submit` key, and `cb pub draft` (src/cli/commands/pub.ts:80-100) exposes no flag for one. Nor is a form ever rendered — src/publish/render-docs.ts just emits Markdoc HTML, and `grep -rn '<form' src/publish pub-worker/src` returns nothing. `submit` exists only as a zod shape in manifest.ts/manifest-edge.ts, so the reader-facing entry point in the story ('post a form on the page') does not exist.

Taking existence/reachability of the form as given (the other reviewer's lens), the scope claim holds. pub-worker/src/submit.ts handleSubmit accepts POST /__submit/<pubId>, validates every submitted field against the manifest's submit block via validateSubmissionFields (src/publish/submission.ts), enforces maxSubmissionBytes/maxPerDay/per-IP limits, and writes submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json; src/connectors/publish-submissions.ts pulls those objects on `cb wakeup`, safeParses them, and lands each as a pub-submission card in box/inbox/ — so the 'so that' clause (reply reaches the boxholder with no email round trip) is actually produced end to end. The 'without an account' qualifier is narrower than the general wording: resolveSubmitter returns viewer:null only for the `secret` tier, while `accounts`/`any-account` require a Cloudflare Access assertion (and, for `accounts`, allowlist membership). That is a soft narrowing rather than an over-claim — on the account tiers the reader has already authenticated just to view the page, so the accountless promise is about the secret-tier case the code does deliver.

triage.reasoning: The receiving half is fully built and live, and the producing half does not exist, so the capability is unreachable for any reader. Confirmed directly: pub-worker/src/index.ts dispatches matchSubmitPath -> handleSubmit; handleSubmit (pub-worker/src/submit.ts:100-105) returns 403 unless manifest.submit is non-null; and nothing ever sets manifest.submit — draftPublication (src/publish/draft.ts:200-217) is the only manifest assembler and its rawManifest has no submit key, `cb pub draft` (src/cli/commands/pub.ts) exposes no flag for one, and `grep -rn 'submit:' src pub-worker/src` finds submit only as a zod field in manifest.ts / manifest-edge.ts and the read in submit.ts. There is also no form: `grep -rn '<form' src/publish pub-worker/src` returns nothing and render-docs.ts emits Markdoc HTML only. So the whole downstream pipeline (validateSubmissionFields, submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json, the publish-submissions connector wired at wakeup-connectors.ts:41, the pub-submission card schema) can never fire in production. This is not a wording problem: the plan (docs/plans/publish-pages.md Track F) intends a real form on submit-enabled pubs, and the resume issue's step 2 assumes a reader can submit — so the missing authoring path and form is an actual hole in a feature that is otherwise complete.

title: Flip a draft live behind a human confirmation
story: As a boxholder, I want `cb pub go` to re-show the file-by-file preview and require me to type the pub-id at an interactive terminal before uploading, so that no agent can put box content on the public internet on its own.
evidence: `goPublication` re-runs the leak scan on the on-disk bundle and calls a `ConfirmFn` defaulting to `defaultTtyConfirm`, which requires a TTY and the typed pub-id; a non-TTY stdin returns `not-confirmed` rather than auto-flipping. Uploads bundle objects first, edge manifest last.

verdict.note: The confirmation half checks out: goPublication in callback-box/src/publish/go.ts re-runs scanBundle, then calls deps.confirm ?? defaultTtyConfirm, which returns false immediately when !process.stdin.isTTY and otherwise requires the typed pub-id; a false answer yields {ok:false, reason:'not-confirmed'}, and uploads go bundle objects first then manifestKey last. But the 'file-by-file preview' clause is an over-claim: defaultTtyConfirm prints only tier/expiry/allowlist/slug and a count line (`bundle files: N`) — it never enumerates the files. The per-file printPreview(result.files, result.scan) in cli/commands/pub.ts is invoked on the `go` path only in the leaks-blocked branch, i.e. when the flip is refused, not as part of the confirmation.

panel.note: callback-box/src/publish/go.ts exports goPublication and defaultTtyConfirm: it loads/validates the local manifest via lifecycle.ts, re-runs scanBundle on the on-disk bundle, calls deps.confirm ?? defaultTtyConfirm (which returns false when !process.stdin.isTTY and otherwise requires the typed pub-id via readline), returns reason 'not-confirmed' on refusal, and on confirm puts every bundleKey object before manifestKey(toEdgeManifest(...)) and then the slug pointer. It is wired end-to-end: cli/commands/pub.ts imports goPublication at line 31, defines goCommand ('go') calling it at line 220 with no injected confirm (so the TTY prompt is the real default), and adds goCommand to pubCommand, which cli/commands/index.ts exports and cli/index.ts registers on the program (line 135). lifecycle.ts (loadLocalManifest, bundleKey, manifestKey, slugKey, persistAndCommitManifest) and manifest-edge.ts are live imported modules, not dead code. The prior verdict's objection concerned what the confirmation prompt prints (count vs file-by-file enumeration) — a wording/accuracy question outside this lens; on existence and wiring the story is satisfied.

The entry point is the registered CLI command `cb pub go <pub-id>`: callback-box/package.json exposes bin `cb`, src/cli/index.ts imports pubCommand and calls program.addCommand(pubCommand) (line 135), and src/cli/commands/pub.ts builds `new Command("go")` at line 206 and attaches it via pubCommand.addCommand(goCommand) (line 253ff). The action handler resolves the box root and publish store, then calls goPublication(...) with no `confirm` dep, so src/publish/go.ts line 177 falls through to defaultTtyConfirm — the TTY/typed-pub-id gate the story describes is on the ordinary operator path, not behind any flag or env toggle. The only precondition is having run `cb pub setup` (resolvePublishStore returning null yields an 'unconfigured' error), which is normal operator configuration rather than an unreachable gate. My lens is satisfied; the earlier verifier's objection was about the preview wording, which is another reviewer's lens.

The confirmation half is fully delivered: goPublication (callback-box/src/publish/go.ts) re-reads the on-disk bundle, re-runs scanBundle, refuses unaccepted findings, then calls deps.confirm ?? defaultTtyConfirm, which returns false when !process.stdin.isTTY and otherwise requires the answer to equal the pub-id exactly; a false answer short-circuits to {ok:false, reason:'not-confirmed'} before any store.put, so the 'so that' clause (no unattended flip) holds. The 'file-by-file preview' clause does not: defaultTtyConfirm receives the per-file `preview` array but prints only tier/expiry/slug/allowlist plus a count line `bundle files: ${args.files.length}` and a leak-finding count -- it never enumerates paths, sizes, or hashes. The actual file-by-file listing lives in printPreview() in callback-box/src/cli/commands/pub.ts, and on the `go` path it is called only in the leaks-blocked failure branch (line 228), i.e. when the flip is refused, never as part of the confirmation the operator answers. So the operator confirms against a summary, not a re-shown file-by-file preview; the story claims more than the code does on that qualifier.

triage.reasoning: The safety gate the story exists for is intact and correctly described everywhere but one clause: goPublication (publish/go.ts) reloads the manifest, re-reads the on-disk bundle, re-runs scanBundle, refuses unaccepted findings ('leaks-blocked'), then calls deps.confirm ?? defaultTtyConfirm, which returns false outright when !process.stdin.isTTY and otherwise requires the answer to equal the pub-id exactly; a false answer short-circuits to reason 'not-confirmed' before any store.put, and uploads put bundle objects first with manifestKey last. cli/commands/pub.ts's goCommand injects no confirm, so the TTY prompt is the real default path. The false clause is 're-show the file-by-file preview': defaultTtyConfirm prints tier, expiry, slug, allowlist, `bundle files: N` and a leak-finding count — it never enumerates paths, sizes or hashes. The per-file printPreview() in pub.ts runs on the `go` path only in the leaks-blocked branch, i.e. when the flip is already refused. This matches the design rather than falling short of it: docs/plans/publish-pages.md:148 puts the file-by-file listing (path, bytes, sha256) on `cb pub draft`, and line 150 puts the eyeball surface on the authed /publish-preview/<pub-id>/ route. So the code is fine and the story over-specifies; correct it to 'shows the publication's tier/expiry/allowlist and file count and requires the typed pub-id at a TTY'. One inaccurate in-code comment feeds the same misreading and is worth a one-line fix, not an issue: pub.ts's comment above the goPublication call says the default confirm 'displays the preview + tier/expiry/allowlist'.

title: Generate the project's public front-door site
story: As a maintainer, I want one build to turn the site's markdown sources into a static site with a machine-facing .md twin per page and an llms.txt index, failing the build on a broken internal link or malformed frontmatter, so that the public front door can never ship stale, broken, or half-rendered pages.
evidence: `pnpm --dir site build` runs build.ts, which reads `site/content/*.md` through the local Markdoc pipeline, writes HTML plus a `<stem>.md` twin and `llms.txt` into `site/dist/`, link-checks every internal link against the emitted output, and throws `BuildError` on an unknown flag, bad frontmatter, or a broken link; `--base` (derived from the git branch, or `/callback-box/` in the Pages workflow) rewrites the URL prefix. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` runs that build on every push to main.

verdict.note: site/package.json defines "build": "tsx build.ts". site/build.ts main() collects site/content/**.md (collectContent), parses frontmatter via parseSource from render.ts (which throws FrontmatterError on a missing fence, invalid YAML, or a failing zod field), renders through Markdoc (renderBody), writes <stem>.html plus a <stem>.md twin (twinMarkdown) to site/dist/, then link-checks every collected internal linkTarget against the emitted set and throws BuildError('broken internal link(s)') otherwise, and finally writes llms.txt (renderLlmsTxt) plus a source manifest. parseArgs throws BuildError on an unknown flag; resolveBase falls back to baseFromBranch(git branch). .github/workflows/pages.yml runs on push to main and executes `pnpm --dir site build --base /callback-box/`, uploading site/dist as the Pages artifact.

title: Keep a shared page out of search indexes and edge caches
story: As a boxholder sharing a page by secret or account-gated link, I want every publication response served noindex, no-store, no-referrer and under a no-egress CSP, so that a link I gave one person does not turn up in a search engine, does not keep serving from a CDN cache after I revoke it, and cannot call out to anything.
evidence: withSecurityHeaders in pub-worker/src/headers.ts sets X-Robots-Tag: noindex, Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, nosniff, COOP and a CSP of default-src 'none' / connect-src 'none' / form-action 'self'; handle() in pub-worker/src/index.ts routes every response — 200, 404, 410, thank-you page — through it exactly once.

verdict.note: callback-box/pub-worker/src/headers.ts defines SECURITY_HEADERS = X-Robots-Tag: noindex, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Cache-Control: no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin, plus a CSP of default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; media-src 'self'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; connect-src 'none'. withSecurityHeaders copies the Response and sets them. pub-worker/src/index.ts has a single exit: handle() at line 52 returns withSecurityHeaders(await route(...)), and the default fetch export delegates to handle — so 200 asset responses, notFound(), gone() (revoked/expired manifests), the account-gated 401/403 paths and submit/thank-you responses all pass through it once. Secret-prefix and account-tier gating are in serveByTier.

title: Learn who opened an account-gated publication
story: As a boxholder, I want each signed-in view of an account-gated publication recorded at the edge and delivered into my box as a digest memo, so that I know which of the people I shared a page with actually read it.
evidence: The Worker writes one `access-log/<pubId>/<id>.json` object per `any-account` view carrying `{ ts, pubId, email }`; the publish-submissions connector downloads those objects, safeParses them, and renders an access-log digest as a memo card with `source: "publish-access-log"`, treating the edge-supplied emails as untrusted, and leaves malformed objects in R2 for inspection.

verdict.note: pub-worker/src/index.ts case "any-account" calls logAccess() after authenticateAccess(), and access-log.ts writes one PUB_INGEST object `access-log/<pubId>/<id>.json` holding {ts,pubId,email} (write failures swallowed so a viewer is never denied). connectors/publish-submissions.ts declares produces = ["pub-submission","memo"], lists that prefix, safeParses each object with accessLogEntrySchema, warns and leaves malformed objects in R2 for inspection, and writes an `Access-Log-Digest-<ts>.memo.card` into the inbox with source: "publish-access-log", noting the emails are untrusted edge-supplied values. The connector is reachable: cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts calls createPublishSubmissionsConnector(boxRoot).

title: Mint a narrowly scoped submissions credential
story: As an operator, I want `cb pub setup --mint-connector-token` to mint an R2 token scoped to only the ingestion bucket and store it in the machine secret store, so that a box compromise cannot rewrite published content or allowlists.
evidence: connector-secret.ts mints via `CloudflareTokensClient` with `R2_BUCKET_ITEM_GROUPS` scoping and stores the JSON under `publish/<box-slug>` with `shareable: false` through `setAndGrantSecret`; pub-setup.ts prints the one-time value for a second machine.

verdict.note: src/cli/commands/pub-setup.ts registers the --mint-connector-token option, resolves a setup-only bootstrap token, and builds a CloudflareTokensClient passed to setupPublishing; src/publish/setup.ts step 7 calls ensureConnectorSecret with bucketName: config.ingestBucketName. ensureConnectorSecret (src/publish/connector-secret.ts) checks R2_BUCKET_ITEM_GROUPS ('Workers R2 Storage Bucket Item Read'/'Write'), mints via tokens.createR2BucketToken, and stores JSON {accountId,bucket,apiToken} under publish/<box-slug> via setAndGrantSecret with access 'server', owningBox and shareable:false. createR2BucketToken in src/services/cloudflare-tokens.ts scopes the policy to resource key com.cloudflare.edge.r2.bucket.<account>_default_<bucket>, i.e. that one ingestion bucket. printSetupSuccess prints the JSON once for a second machine.

title: Provision publishing infrastructure in one command
story: As an operator, I want `cb pub setup` to provision the Cloudflare R2 buckets and deploy the publication Worker off my existing wrangler login, so that publishing works without hand-clicking through the Cloudflare dashboard.
evidence: `pubSetupCommand` in pub-setup.ts resolves auth via `resolveCloudflareAuth` (wrangler login or env) and calls `setupPublishing`, which creates the content and ingestion buckets, deploys the worker, and reports `workerName`/`bucketName`/`hostname`; it is documented as idempotent and re-runnable.

verdict.note: pubSetupCommand (cli/commands/pub-setup.ts) is registered on the `cb pub` command (cli/commands/pub.ts:255), resolves auth via resolveCloudflareAuth (publish/cloudflare-auth.ts — env CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN pair else the `wrangler login` identity via wrangler.whoami/wranglerBearer), and calls setupPublishing. publish/setup.ts ensures both the content and ingestion R2 buckets (lines 167-169 via client.bucketExists/createBucket), resolves the workers.dev hostname, and runs `wrangler deploy` (line 203-207), returning workerName/bucketName/ingestBucketName/hostname which printSetupSuccess prints. Bucket creation is guarded by bucketExists and the header documents idempotent reruns, so the one-command, re-runnable claim holds. Access and connector-token provisioning are optional extra flags, not required for the story's claim.

title: Publish box content as external pages
story: As a boxholder, I want to draft a doc into a publication, review it, then deliberately flip it live or revoke it, so that sharing box content outside the box is a two-step, reversible act.
evidence: `pubCommand` has draft (renders and leak-scans, --expires/--emails/--slug/--accept-leak), ls, go (interactive human-only flip), revoke (edge-side tombstone), plus setup (Cloudflare R2/Worker/Access provisioning) and status (drift between committed and deployed Worker).

verdict.note: callback-box/src/cli/commands/pub.ts defines pubCommand with subcommands draft (--expires/--emails/--slug/--accept-leak, calls draftPublication which renders + leak-scans and refuses to commit on blocking findings), ls, go, revoke; pub-setup.ts adds setup (Cloudflare R2 buckets + Worker deploy + optional Access via wrangler login) and status (flags drift between the committed and deployed Worker). goCommand calls goPublication whose default ConfirmFn (src/publish/go.ts defaultTtyConfirm) requires an interactive TTY and the typed pub-id, refusing on non-TTY stdin; revokeCommand calls revokePublication which writes an edge-side tombstone (next request 410s) and deletes bundle objects. pubCommand is registered at src/cli/index.ts:135, so the draft -> review -> go/revoke two-step reversible flow is reachable as written.

title: Pull publication submissions into the box
story: As a boxholder, I want the publish-submissions connector to pull buffered submissions and access logs into my inbox as cards on wakeup, so that replies to a published page show up as ordinary box content.
evidence: The registered connector downloads `submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json` and `access-log/<pubId>/*.json`, safeParses each, writes a `pub-submission` card into `box/inbox/` and commits it before deleting the remote object (land-then-delete, dedup by submission id).

verdict.note: src/connectors/publish-submissions.ts defines PublishSubmissionsConnector (registerConnector via createPublishSubmissionsConnector, invoked from src/cli/commands/wakeup-connectors.ts line 41, i.e. on `cb wakeup`). pullSubmissions lists submissions/<pubId>/<id>.json via PublishRemoteStore (src/services/publish-remote-store.ts), safeParses with submissionSchema (src/publish/submission.ts), writes a `pub-submission` card (src/schemas/pub-submission.ts createPubSubmissionCard) into getBoxDir(boxRoot,'inbox'), skipping ids whose card file already exists; pullAccessLogs validates access-log/<pubId>/*.json entries into one memo digest. sync() commits all created cards before iterating deleteKeys and calling store.delete — land-then-delete as claimed. Credential resolves from config/connectors/publish.secret.json or CLOUDFLARE_* env; no-op if unconfigured, which is a normal unconfigured-connector case, not a gate.

title: Index refresh at query time
story: As the box's agent, I want the search index to re-diff the filesystem on every query and rebuild only what changed, so that results reflect shell moves, connector writes and uncommitted edits with no hooks to maintain.

No hooks are involved — the diff is filesystem mtime/size based, so shell moves and uncommitted edits are picked up.
